who_can_apply: Must be 14 to 21 years old at the start of employment. No prior professional experience is required.
how_to_apply: Complete the in-person application and interview during the scheduled Application and Interview Weekend.
notes: The organization's Gallery Fellowship (ages 16 to 24) and 10-month Mural Studio job are separate programs. The old ArtWorks web address now redirects to 1001colors.org. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

who_can_apply: Sophomores (80 to 90 credits) and juniors (140 to 150 credits by January) with a 2.0 GPA or higher, good attendance, Algebra I or Integrated Math I done, and currently in Geometry or higher.
how_to_apply: Register for the Evergreen Valley College placement test at (408) 274-7900 x6636, attend a recruitment and info meeting to get the application, then mail it or hand-deliver it to the Roble Building mailroom at Evergreen Valley College.
notes: Page lists no age rule and no 2026-27 meeting dates; call the coordinator (Kathleen Leal, (408) 274-7900 x6881) for the schedule. Must also be taking biology, chemistry and physics and English 2 (sophomores) or English 3 (juniors).

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21, currently in high school or college. Alameda County program. No income or residency rule is listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Contact a regional provider: Eden Area ROP in Hayward, (510) 293-2900, or Tri-Valley ROP in Livermore, (925) 487-4153. Main ACWDB line: (510) 259-3842.
notes: Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 use the Future Force program instead: La Familia (Eden Area) (925) 935-2643, Ohlone College (Tri Cities) (510) 742-2323, International Rescue Committee (North Cities) (510) 857-6884. The county page names only two providers, Eden ROP (Hayward) and Tri-Valley ROP (Livermore), and says to contact the one near you.

who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Chicago and attend a Chicago high school. Most programs are ages 14 to 18 (14 by Sept 28, 2026 for the fall session). Outreach Assistantships need age 16+.
how_to_apply: Apply online (up to six programs, ranked). Save your Application ID for the Teen Dashboard. Most programs require an interview; offers must be accepted within 72 hours. A parent/guardian consent form is required after you accept.
notes: One program per session. A Social Security number or ITIN is not required for every program; teens without one should contact ASM. Applying again each session needs a new application. The fall page says the application is open, but programs began Sept 28, so confirm spots remain. Work permit rules for under-16 not stated on ASM pages.

who_can_apply: Must be 16 or older for Discovery Station and Astronomy volunteering (18 for most other roles). Commit to at least 8 hours a month for one year, preferably in 3-hour shifts.
how_to_apply: Click 'Apply Now' on the volunteer page, create an account in the museum's volunteer system, complete the orientation and online training, and sign a Program Volunteer Agreement.
notes: The Astronomy Education volunteer role (also 16+) was marked 'not recruiting at the moment'. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Girls in 11th grade who are selected and sponsored by a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit. Each high school may have only one delegate. If a school has no sponsoring Unit, a student can apply as a Department (statewide) alternate applicant. Age rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor or contact a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit (the site has a spreadsheet to find one). Each Unit picks a delegate and two alternates. Students at schools with no sponsoring Unit can use the START HERE online application as Department alternate applicants.
notes: Separate from the coed American Legion California Boys State (Boys & Girls State) program, which has its own card on this site. The FAQ says a student may apply to either American Legion CA Boys State or American Legion Auxiliary CA Girls State, but not both. Selection criteria, grade-school rules beyond the 11th grade note, and cost are not stated on the pages read.

who_can_apply: Ages 10 and up. Teens 15 to 17 may volunteer on their own. Under 15 needs an adult (1 adult for every 5 youth).
how_to_apply: Book shifts on the volunteer calendar or email volunteer@accfb.org, phone 510-635-3663 ext. 308.
notes: 7900 Edgewater Dr, Oakland. Wear closed-toe shoes that cover your whole foot. BART to Coliseum, then AC Transit 98.

who_can_apply: Ages and requirements vary by role and are shown on the portal. Not stated on the page I read.
how_to_apply: Browse and apply on the library's Better Impact volunteer portal. Phone 510-745-1500. The application link is on the official page.
notes: The teen page is thin. Ask the Fremont Main Library which roles take teens.

who_can_apply: Teens. The TAG page does not state an age or grade. Other teen volunteer roles on the same page use grades 7 to 12 or ages 12 to 17.
how_to_apply: Complete the online TAG registration form on the library page. Questions: refdesk@alamedaca.gov or (510) 747-7777.
notes: Meets at the Main Library in the Stafford Room. The page states no age rule, so ask the library if you are younger than 12 or older than 17. See also Alameda Free Library Teen Volunteers (Book Reviewers and Coding with LEGO) for volunteer roles such as book reviews and LEGO coding.

who_can_apply: Teen Book Reviewers: grades 7 to 12. Coding with LEGO: ages 12 to 17.
how_to_apply: LEGO program: email Fernanda Nunez at fnunez@alamedaca.gov. Book reviews: use the Teen Book Reviews page. Questions: refdesk@alamedaca.gov or 510-747-7777.
notes: Book reviews are limited to one a month. No coding experience needed for LEGO. See also Alameda Free Library Teen Advisory Group (TAG) for the advisory role, where teens suggest ideas for library events and projects.

who_can_apply: Local youth, especially students in Alameda Unified School District career technical education programs.
how_to_apply: No sign-up is listed; admission is free. Contacts: Jennifer Padilla (City) 510-747-6852; Amanda Vigil (AUSD) 510-337-7091.
notes: Held at Encinal Jr/Sr High, 210 Central Ave, Alameda. It is an annual fair, but the 2027 date has not been posted.

who_can_apply: Teens can volunteer. The internship page gives no age or school rule and lists colleges, so ask if high schoolers can intern.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. Then meet a staff member for an interview and training. Interns use a different form. Teen Advisory Board members use their own form.
notes: Alive says it runs free drop-in hours after school and over the summer, plus teen-led clubs. Locations named on the site are Naperville, Aurora and Hanover Park. The internship page lists college affiliated schools, so ask about high school interns.

who_can_apply: Rising 11th graders, 12th graders and post-secondary students. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Apply during the window; the process includes an interview. The page encourages students to attend a performance and check back next year. Contact: collision.project@alliancetheatre.org or 404-733-4700.
notes: Free thanks to the Palefsky family. Exact dates were not printed on the application page, only the January to mid-April range. The Alliance also lists a year-long Teen Ensemble, but its current page was not read so it is not listed.

who_can_apply: In-person volunteer roles are for ages 16 and up. At-home projects are a good option for anyone under 16. Vet clinic support is 18 and up. School service roles need an agreement signed by a parent and a teacher.
how_to_apply: Register on the volunteer page for the role you want. You also complete virtual Safety and Protocols training and pay the $35 membership fee. For school hours, sign up on the School Service page.
notes: Animal care roles ask for at least six months. The page says Shelter Support is not eligible for court-ordered service hours. Sites include South Elgin, Bloomingdale Petco, Algonquin Petco and Geneva Petco. Others are the St. Charles office and Elburn Forest Preserve.

who_can_apply: Anyone 14 or older. Ages 14 to 17 need a signed permission slip from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. After review you are contacted with details on signing up for a required volunteer orientation, then you pick shifts.
notes: Library does not offer court-ordered community service. Older library posts mention a summer teen volunteer program, but the current page only describes the year-round program. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older to volunteer alone at the warehouse or Community Kitchen. Younger kids can come with an adult. The warehouse takes ages 8 and up. The kitchen takes ages 12 and up.
how_to_apply: Create a user account with Individual Registration and sign up for shifts in advance; no walk-ins. If you need school hours signed or an observer will attend, call the volunteer coordinator first.
notes: Not teen-specific, but a steady way for teens 14 and up to earn volunteer hours. Warehouse work involves moderate lifting. Groups of four or more use a separate group form. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

who_can_apply: The page says community volunteers include high school and college students, corporate partners and retirees. It does not state a minimum age. Ask before you apply.
how_to_apply: For the Hands-On Museum, email volunteer@aahom.org. For wildlife volunteering at Leslie Science & Nature Center, fill out the application linked on the page. Or email volunteer@lesliesnc.org.
notes: The page is short. It gives no age rule, hours, training or start dates, so email first. The Hands-On Museum's old address (aahom.org/volunteer) now sends you to this page. The Leslie wildlife application link goes to a file named Adult_Volunteer_Application.pdf, so ask Leslie before a teen applies for wildlife work.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 to 17 (must be 12 before registering). Those about to turn 18 within 6 months may prefer the adult orientation.
how_to_apply: Online registration only, which opens about 30 days before each session. You must attend all six classes; there are no make-ups, refunds or transfers. A waitlist is available.
notes: Demand is higher than space, so you may wait months. After training you volunteer without a parent present. Inactive for 6 months or more means retaking the training. Shelter is at 3100 Cherry Hill Rd, Ann Arbor. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

who_can_apply: The course is open to ages 15 and up. The page says you are prepared to be a lifeguard when you turn 16. Fifteen year olds who finish the course can join the city's Lifeguard in Training Volunteer Program.
how_to_apply: Register for the course by calling 734-794-6237 or at Mack Indoor Pool (715 Brooks St., inside Ann Arbor Open School). Pool jobs are applied for online through the city's job board when posted.
notes: The lifeguard certification page says 15 year olds can join the Lifeguard in Training Volunteer Program. The recertification section says 15 year olds can be eligible for a city lifeguard job. These two statements differ. Ask the pool at 734-794-6237 what age you can be hired. Michigan says minors must get a work permit before starting a job unless exempt. The permit comes through a Michigan school. See the state youth employment page. You get no refund of the course fee if you fail the course.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up for most roles. Survey Squad is 16 and up. Ushers must be 18. The page says 12 and 13 year olds may volunteer with an adult volunteer. Volunteers work under the supervision of festival staff.
how_to_apply: Pick a volunteer role and a night on the A2SF volunteer sign-up page. Questions: call 734-994-5999.
notes: Seasonal: shifts are in the summer festival only. Usher spots for 2026 were closed. Check the page in spring for 2027 sign-up.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 when programming begins (you must turn 16 by June 1 of the program year) AND you live in, or attend school in, Washtenaw County. Participants may take part for up to three years.
how_to_apply: Online application (opens January): your contact info, parent or guardian contact, approximate household income, possible summer conflicts, and one reference who is not a relative. Accepted minors need a parent or guardian signature.
notes: A paid internship is not guaranteed: the site says a subset of participants is selected, though staff aim to match everyone. After acceptance you need I-9 identification documents and a bank account in your name for pay (this is for payroll, not a fee). Professional development is Tuesday or Wednesday evenings online, then Fridays 10am to 2pm in person from June. Michigan requires a work permit for minors under 18 to work; as of Oct 2, 2026 permits are issued through the state's Youth Employment Permit Portal, not schools. Contact: mail@summerworks.info.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Ann Arbor and Livingston volunteer page (the link goes to the hospital's volunteer system at stjoemercyann.vsysweb.com). Then an interview, paperwork, health screening and a required orientation.
notes: Requirements listed for volunteers: interview, two TB skin tests, proof of varicella and MMR immunity, Tdap, this year's flu shot, health clearance form, one non-relative reference, and orientation; background checks apply to volunteers 18 and over. Also on the same page: The Farm at Trinity Health takes volunteers age 15 and up (no background check under 18). The Apply Now link is http, not https, so it is not in the apply_url field. Volunteer office phone is on the page. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

who_can_apply: The Youth Volunteer Corps is for teens ages 11 to 17. Ages for the other youth volunteer roles are not stated on the page. Youth sports coaches must be at least 14.
how_to_apply: Use the Begin your application button on the volunteering page. Questions: volunteer@annarborymca.org.
notes: The page's own link to a Youth Volunteer Corps page was a dead link when checked, so details of YVC projects and dates are not confirmed. The Y also lists other volunteer roles that appear aimed at adults. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 16. Applicants complete an online application and an on-site interview, then required trainings. Both a parent and the teen sign liability forms.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application during an open window, attend an interview, then the online and on-site training days.
notes: Spring and Fall sessions are weekends only; Summer shifts run seven days a week. The Aquarium also lists other youth roles for ages 11 to 18 (Ocean Neighbors, Teen Science Cafe Volunteer, Student Eco-Ambassadors). The Education Volunteer role is for ages 16 and up with at least 100 hours in six months.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 living in Cherokee, Clayton, Douglas, Fayette, Gwinnett, Henry or Rockdale County. In-school or out-of-school youth who face a barrier such as offender history, homelessness, foster care, parenting, disability or being a basic-skills-deficient or English learner diploma holder.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe an application. Contact the provider for your county. Clayton: 770-997-4511 (640 Hwy 138 SW, Riverdale). Gwinnett: 404-913-0769 (3805 Crestwood Pkwy NW, Suite 300, Duluth). Cherokee: 770-345-5483. Henry: 404-913-0769. Douglas: 770-997-4511. Fayette: 770-910-7733. Rockdale: 770-991-7608.
notes: This is the only Gwinnett and Clayton county youth workforce program found. The City of Atlanta, Fulton, DeKalb and Cobb are not on this page's county list; see their own entries. Providers named on the page: Cherokee Youth Works and Hearts to Nourish Hope. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16. Re-read on 2026-10-09: the page says nothing about cost or pay, so the card is not in the paid group.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at Center, Del Campo, El Camino Fundamental or Inderkum High School who meet federal rules for financial need and/or being first in the family to go to college, and want to go beyond high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Upward Bound application, then staff review eligibility and interview the student and family if eligible. Contact arctrioub@arc.losrios.edu or (916) 484-8033 (Mon to Fri, 9 am to 6 pm).
notes: Only for students at the four listed partner schools. Summer participation is required. The dedicated application page did not show details when read. Ask staff for current dates.

who_can_apply: Summer Volunteer Squad is for teens going into grades 7 to 12. You must live in Arlington Heights.
how_to_apply: Use the volunteer application link on the library volunteer page. New Middle School Panel members sign up on the page.
notes: There is also a Tween Advisory Group for grades 4 to 6, which is for younger kids.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 14 and a half years old. The page lists this rule for all volunteers and links a separate Teen Volunteer Application.
how_to_apply: Complete the Teen Volunteer Application (Google form on the page). Questions: armc-volunteers@armc.sbcounty.gov or Volunteer Management, 400 N. Pepper Avenue, Colton, CA 92324.
notes: Minimum age is 14 and a half. The page lists no application deadline or start dates.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18 who start tasks on their own. You like the arts and feel at ease with kids.
how_to_apply: Use the Learn More and Sign Up link on the volunteer page, which opens a Google Form.
notes: Hours and session dates are not on the page. The Armory's Fall Studio 2026 classes are on a separate page.

who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 18 years old. Students can join one week, all six or any number of weeks.
how_to_apply: Register for classes through the registration link on the Teen Academy page. Questions: Office of Engagement.
notes: Courses change every week. Students agree to the handbook rules when they sign up. The page mentions scholarships; ask the Office of Engagement for details.

who_can_apply: Adults 18 and up. Teens must be at least 16 years old when they apply.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. Then go to an interview. You also need a health screening and a criminal background check. You need orientation papers and training on site. Phone: 847-437-5500.
notes: You need at least 50 volunteer hours before you can ask for written proof of hours (for school or court). Uniform and ID badge are required whenever you volunteer.

who_can_apply: Adults 18 and up. Teens must be at least 16 years old when they apply.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. Then go to an interview. You also need a health screening and a criminal background check. You need orientation papers and training on site. Phone: 847-755-8708.
notes: You need at least 100 volunteer hours before you can ask for written proof of hours (for school or court). Uniform and ID badge are required whenever you volunteer.

who_can_apply: High school students 16 or older by June 2 of the summer.
how_to_apply: Submit the online SPEAK application and have a non-relative adult submit a recommendation form. Attend a 2-hour group interview and the mandatory training day. If you also apply to the paid internship, only the internship application is needed.
notes: Application window usually closes March 1 (2026 pattern). Check the Garden volunteer page in December and January for the 2027 cycle.

who_can_apply: 16 or older by June 2 of the summer, and a rising sophomore, junior or senior at a Metro Atlanta Title I school. Must be eligible to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Submit the internship application and have a non-relative adult (teacher, mentor or boss) submit the recommendation form. Group interview at the Garden, then virtual orientation with a guardian. Questions: lboren@atlantabg.org.
notes: Only for students at Metro Atlanta Title I schools. Work is outside in all weather and includes lifting 40 lbs. Applying here also covers the SPEAK volunteer program. The Garden's Gainesville site has its own separate teen program.

who_can_apply: Atlanta Public Schools students. For dual enrollment, you must be on track to graduate and have a 2.0 GPA. Early College Essentials and Cybersecurity need a 2.6 HOPE GPA and grade 11 or 12.
how_to_apply: Take the YouScience career quiz (recommended). Talk to your school counselor. Then submit the online application. Students with an IEP or 504 plan also need a team review.
notes: Career paths include HVAC, Culinary Arts, Dental Science and Patient Care. Atlanta Technical College runs the dual enrollment paths. They include Carpentry and Cybersecurity. The page lists more. You can be denied if there is no room or you miss the minimums.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Participating sites listed: Adams, Bessie Branham, C. T. Martin, Dunbar, Grove Park, Martin Luther King Jr., Peachtree Hills, Pittman, Rosel Fann, Thomasville, William Walker, Zaban, @Promise South and @Promise MLK. Residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Register for the Atlanta Teen Leader Program. The catalog lists atlantaga.gov/iparcs as the City registration site for its programs. Confirm the steps with your nearest participating recreation center.
notes: Source is the City's 2026 summer catalog, so it does not say which summer the Dec 31, 2026 registration cutoff is for. Ages and pay for the actual summer jobs are not stated. Georgia requires a work permit for any job under 16. The City's iParcs page blocked automated reading.

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors at an APS high school that offers the Mentorship and Internship classes. You do not have to be labeled gifted. Your school picks the students.
how_to_apply: There is no separate form on the page. Ask your guidance counselor whether your school offers the class, or call the gifted office at 404-802-7585. The coordinator matches you using a career survey from early fall.
notes: The coordinator matches students to internships after a career survey in early fall. Students and families arrange their own rides. You must finish the fall Mentorship course first.

who_can_apply: Atlanta Public Schools students. The district page does not list grade, age or GPA rules, so ask your school counselor or the CTAE office.
how_to_apply: The page does not give steps. Call or email the Work-Based Learning contact, or ask your school counselor.
notes: The phone on the page is (404) 802-5878. The page also lists CTAE career paths. They include Engineering Drafting, Allied Health, Cybersecurity and Culinary Arts. Students in other districts use their own district.

who_can_apply: Atlanta youth ages 14 to 24. Documents asked for: original birth certificate, proof of City of Atlanta residency, state or school photo ID, original Social Security card, and a work permit for anyone under 16.
how_to_apply: Register online on the city's SYEP sign-up page with an email address you check daily. Upload your documents in the SYEP portal when asked. You are matched to openings, invited to orientation, and sent an offer letter. Some employers interview first.
notes: A work permit is needed only for ages 14 and 15 (Georgia requires one under 16). You start it after you have a job offer, through your school district. Not guaranteed: the city says selection is competitive. Questions: syep@atlantaga.gov or (404) 546-3000. The registration list asks for an original Social Security card; this is the official city program, so upload documents only inside the SYEP portal and never send them by email or text. The city's atlantaga.gov pages blocked automated reading, so confirm the 2027 timeline with the SYEP team.

who_can_apply: Aurora residents ages 14 to 18 who are in high school.
how_to_apply: Check that you meet the rules, then fill out the BEO Interest Form (Google form).
notes: The page does not name the employers or say if internships pay. For city help, call 311 or 630-256-4636. The City's Summer Youth Programs page said summer 2026 programs are closed and to look for summer 2027.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not give an age or grade range or a residency rule. Ask the teen librarians.
how_to_apply: Write to the Teen Librarians. Ask how to join and what the steps are. The email is teens@aurorapubliclibrary.org.
notes: The library's teen volunteer page said summer reading volunteers for 2027 apply in the spring. It also lists outside groups that take teen volunteers, with their own age rules.

who_can_apply: Aurora residents ages 15 to 24. The page lists separate planning sessions. They are for Aurora high school students, college students and nonprofits.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application form. Staff office hours are Tuesdays 2 to 4 p.m. (630-256-3416) and Wednesdays 10 a.m. to noon (630-256-3402) during the window. Email youthservdiv@aurora.il.us.
notes: The page says about 10 to 40 projects will be funded. Co-design sessions were September 8 and 10, 2026, so they have passed. Ages up to 24 are allowed, so high school students compete with older applicants.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 17 who are in good standing at school and live in Aurora or North Aurora. A signed waiver is required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application and the waiver using the link at the top of the Youth Court page. Print and sign the waiver and bring it to your first session. Contacts on the page: rodriguezs@aurora.il.us or sarmientos@aurora.il.us.
notes: Training dates are not listed on the page. The page says Youth Court is for youth who committed first time offenses. Teens serve as jurors.

who_can_apply: Austin, TX residents who attend an Austin-area high school, ages 15 to 18 when applying, available for the whole program with no more than 3 days absent.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application (link posted on the program page) with an essay. Choose your preferred track on the application. Email SummerHSIntern@austintexas.gov with questions.
notes: Separate from the Austin ISD / Austin Chamber paid internship. Placements depend on site access and career interest.

who_can_apply: Teens age 15 to 17 living in Central Texas who will be a sophomore, junior or senior in the coming fall (homeschoolers welcome). Must be able to work legally in the U.S., or be willing to waive pay on a student-only visa. About 10 teens are hired each year.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Foundation's Teen Library Fellowship page when the application opens. Questions go to the Teen Librarian at kathleen.houlihan@austintexas.gov.
notes: Fellows must attend a mandatory monthly Sunday afternoon retreat at the Central Library; travel stipends are available. The Foundation page says ages 15-17 and $21 per hour; library pages say $22 per hour and one library page says ages 15-18, so confirm when applications open.

who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 17 (no younger than 13 and no older than 17 by Aug 1 for fall, Dec 1 for spring, or May 1 for summer). Must pass a background check (fingerprinting for ages 15+ who lived outside Texas in the last seven years) and attend a mandatory orientation.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application posted on the Teen Volunteer Program page during the window. There may be an interview with the volunteer coordinator; you get three business days to accept an offer. Not every applicant gets a placement.
notes: Placement depends on the library branch and supervisor, and the library gets more applicants than placements. Contact: APL.Volunteers@austintexas.gov. Limit of two absences per season.

who_can_apply: High school students living in Central Texas, ages 16 to 18 (or turning 16 in the year they apply), interested in creative careers and Latinx issues, and able to work legally in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Submit a personal application, a portfolio and teacher recommendations, then do one-on-one and panel interviews. Questions: caminos@austintexas.gov.
notes: About 10 to 12 teens per cohort. Competitive. Dates for the next application window are not posted.

who_can_apply: Lifeguard training and hiring starts at age 15 with no upper age limit. You need a physical Social Security card and Texas-issued ID for the in-person paperwork.
how_to_apply: Step 1: fill out the online lifeguard job application. Step 2: visit the Aquatic Office in person at 2818 San Gabriel St. with your Social Security card, Texas ID and any hiring paperwork emailed to you. Questions: 512-974-9330.
notes: The 2026 posting also offered a $200 stipend for guards trained and working 40 hours before July 4, 2026. One library list says age 16+; the Parks page (dated March 20, 2026) says 15. Texas hour limits apply to 15 year olds.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 16 to 20 who live in the City of Austin or its extraterritorial jurisdiction and are eligible to work legally in the U.S. No academic requirements.
how_to_apply: Online application (about 1.5 hours), short-answer questions, and one reference who completes a recommendation form. Accepted members become City of Austin employees and must verify work eligibility.
notes: Meetings are held at locations around Austin and transportation help may be available.

who_can_apply: At least 16 years old, and enrolled in high school or college (or enrolled within the past 12 months). A community group must sponsor your placement.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply to BART directly. Ask a community organization or your school to sponsor you and have them email workforcedevelopment@bart.gov.
notes: Sponsor organizations fund the placements. Build a relationship with a community group and ask them to contact workforcedevelopment@bart.gov.

who_can_apply: Berkeley High students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe enrollment. Contact CTE Manager Wyn Skeels, WynSkeels@berkeley.net, (510) 644-8727, or your counselor.
notes: Pathway classes meet the a-g college entry requirements. Middle schoolers get a STEM exploration track.

who_can_apply: Age 12 or older. Ages 12 to 15 must have a parent or guardian with them 1 to 1. Age 16 and up can volunteer alone with a release form.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a General Volunteer Orientation online, read the manual, attend orientation. Contact volunteer@berkeleyhumane.org, (510) 845-7735.
notes: Internships need 18 or older (10 to 20 plus hours a week for 3 months or more).

who_can_apply: Finished 10th or 11th grade, 3.0 GPA, 16 by June 21 (2026 rule).
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Pre-College Scholars site. The 2026 window opened Feb 2, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
notes: Very expensive. Aid is limited. Also needs a 3.0 GPA and good standing at your school.

who_can_apply: Teen volunteer: fill out the application. No age is stated. Youth Worker: ages 14 to 25. No experience is needed. A work permit is required if under 18.
how_to_apply: Volunteers: complete the Teen Volunteer Application form. Paid work: go through Berkeley YouthWorks (2180 Milvia St, 510-981-4970); see the YouthWorks page for the current interest form.
notes: The library page also lists other groups that take teen volunteers. Berkeley YouthWorks may require Berkeley residency.

who_can_apply: Bay Area high school students. A new group starts at the beginning of each school year.
how_to_apply: Join the Teen Council mailing list on the Teen Council page, or email teencouncil@berkeleyrep.org.
notes: No grade or age rule is listed beyond high school. Competitive: only 10 to 15 spots.

who_can_apply: Berkeley residents (proof of residency at onboarding). Priority for youth facing barriers, such as foster care or legal system involvement, English learners, young parents, and students with IEPs or 504 plans. The page states no age rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online YouthWorks interest form. Chosen candidates get an email for a 15 to 20 minute interview. Contact: youthworks@berkeleyca.gov, (510) 981-4970.
notes: An interest form does not guarantee a placement. Berkeley Public Library lists the Youth Worker age as 14 to 25. Berkeley residents only.

who_can_apply: Current and former foster youth in Alameda County, per the homepage (it says it serves over 500 each year). The age range and intake steps are not stated on the pages read.
how_to_apply: Call 510.980.9010 or email info@beyondemancipation.org (both from the site footer). Staff connect youth to coaching, training and job resources.
notes: Corrected on 2026-10-07. The site loaded this time (the earlier certificate error is gone). The homepage and employment page say who is served and what coaching covers, but do not state an age range, costs or an intake process, so those are left null or not stated. This is a coaching service rather than a paid job, so the type is the closest available. The employment page lists outside job boards and training partners (Civicorps, Oakland Private Industry Council, EASTBAY Works), which are separate organizations. The jobs page is for B:E staff openings, not youth jobs. Call before relying on it.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. The page does not say which clubhouse hosts each Industry Club or whether you must be a member first.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Industry Clubs interest form on the page, or email membership@bgcncil.org or call the South Elgin office at (847) 608-5017. Teen membership (middle and high school) is free and signs up through MyClubHub (bgcncil.org/join/).
notes: The organization runs Elgin and South Elgin clubhouses (administrative office at 735 Martin Dr, South Elgin) plus Aurora, Batavia and a Schaumburg Teen Center, but the Industry Clubs page does not say where each session meets. Ask before you sign up. Elgin clubhouses follow the School District U-46 calendar.

who_can_apply: Keystone Club is for ages 14 to 18. Youth of the Year is for ages 10 to 18. You must be a Club member. Teen membership (middle and high school) is free, and you must meet the local residency or school district rules.
how_to_apply: Create an account in MyClubHub, pick your clubhouse and fill out the membership application. Staff will email next steps and a start date. Contact for Youth of the Year: cmaxwell@bgcelgin.org.
notes: Age limits can differ by clubhouse. The Industry Clubs (paid career programs for teens) are a separate listing. A Schaumburg Teen Center page exists but only shows a calendar.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who have been Club members for 2 or more years and meet academic requirements. The page does not list the academic requirements.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Ask staff at your Clubhouse. The site lists a 3300 High Street address.
notes: The same Teens page lists Keystone Clubs (ages 14 to 18) and Youth of the Year (ages 16 to 18, a $20,000 scholarship opportunity, not a job). They are not separate cards because the page gives no joining steps. Staff openings are posted on LinkedIn (the careers page does not list them). Season, pay rate, hours and deadlines are not stated, so confirm with the Club before a teen applies. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Girls ages 7 to 18 for workshops. A separate College and Careers Community serves ages 18 plus.
how_to_apply: Check the community events page for current workshops: community.wearebgc.org/events.
notes: The home page did not name a Bay Area chapter, prices or workshop dates. Check the events page for what is open now. Code Along videos are free on YouTube. Home page shows no workshop price, so the card is not in the paid group.

who_can_apply: Community and project clubs are for ages 9 through 18. The home school Senior club is ages 14 to 19. Clubs have size limits and fill first come, first served, and they depend on volunteer leaders.
how_to_apply: Email one of the Extension 4-H staff on the page. They are Kendra Young kkyoung@vt.edu, Lesa Miller lvmiller@vt.edu and Margarita Palomino mrpalomi@vt.edu. Or call the Montgomery County Extension office at 540-382-5790. Staff pass your request to the club leaders.
notes: The clubs page does not give an age rule or meeting time for the Teens for a Better Tomorrow club, so ask staff. This is a youth club, not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Enrolled senior 4-H members in Virginia. The page says the event is for 4-H youth ages 14 to 18. You must be signed up as a member through 4-H Online.
how_to_apply: Join 4-H first. Your county 4-H office can help. Then register through your family profile in 4-H Online. Your county 4-H agent handles unit delegations.
notes: You must already be a 4-H member. Part of the page still shows last year's details, so check the newest page. Statewide event that happens to be in Blacksburg, so it may also be listed as a Virginia-wide card.

who_can_apply: Current 8th or 9th grade students at a Virginia middle, high, home-school or private school. You must be a Virginia resident and a U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident, with at least a C+/B- average (2.7 GPA) and a desire to explore STEM. The program is meant for students without STEM experience.
how_to_apply: Use the online application on the BLAST page. Pick one session. A recommender and a school counselor must also submit forms online before the deadline.
notes: This is a state program with sessions at five universities, so it may also be listed as a Virginia-wide card. The page says applicants must be a current 8th or 9th grader in one place. It describes rising 9th and 10th graders in another place. That means the same thing, since you apply in the school year before. The Feb 1 close date comes from the 'December 1 to February 1' window. The page does not tie it to a year.

who_can_apply: Rising 8th and 9th grade students. Any student who might like cybersecurity is welcome. You do not need any previous experience.
how_to_apply: Use the application link on the CyberSpark page. Phone: 540-231-4312.
notes: Mostly for younger teens (rising 8th and 9th graders). Cost and whether it is a day camp or overnight are not stated, so ask the program. Camp, not a job.

who_can_apply: Virginia residents entering grade 10, 11 or 12. You must be a first generation college student. That means neither parent graduated from a four year college in the U.S. or abroad.
how_to_apply: Send in the Pathways application linked on the program page. Contact Perry Martin at pathways@vt.edu with questions.
notes: Only for Virginia residents who would be first generation college students. The pages do not say whether the summer program is free. The eligibility text on the page mentions students entering grades in the fall of 2025, so it may be out of date. Check the application link before you plan.

who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th grade students, per the Virginia Tech engineering pre-college list. The camp pages read do not give more rules.
how_to_apply: There are two parts. One is a student application. It has activities, short essays of 120 words or less each, and a transcript. The transcript does not need to be official. The other is a parent form. It has consent and a financial statement used for scholarships. The application is shared with the C-Tech2 camp. You can choose either camp or both.
notes: Costs money and is a camp, not a job. The pages read are partly out of date (they mention the 2025 application), so check the newest page and confirm dates with the program. The Virginia Tech C-Tech2 camp has its own card in this guide.

who_can_apply: Ballet intensive: ages 13 to 18, admitted by a filmed prescreen of a classical variation. Contemporary intensive: ages 14 to 18, must have completed grade 8, no screening.
how_to_apply: Online registration form and $100 fee; ballet applicants upload a private YouTube link to a classical variation. Do not pay tuition until accepted. Then submit the Participant Agreement Form.
notes: Intense schedule (Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM). The student pays; this is not a job.

who_can_apply: Intermediate to advanced string, wind and percussion students in grades 8 to 12. Jazz band requires an audition on the first day.
how_to_apply: Online registration form plus the $100 registration fee, tuition by the payment deadline, then a Participant Agreement Form. Contact: musicsp@iu.edu.
notes: Costs and dates are from the 2026 session page. The student pays; this is not a job. The Jacobs Academy also lists other pre-college summer programs.

who_can_apply: Any high school student. Only 50 team spots are available.
how_to_apply: Apply online. It is first come, first served.
notes: The page shows the August 28 and October 3 dates without a year; the date has already passed this fall. Travel costs are not discussed on the page. Expect it to repeat in fall 2027 but confirm.

who_can_apply: High school students with a cumulative GPA of 3.5 or higher on a 4.0 scale. The page says the experience is open to all students. Selective, seats are limited.
how_to_apply: Online application: 100-word statement, 250-word response, GPA and business-related activities. No exceptions for missed deadlines.
notes: The page lists weekday dates (for example 'Wednesday April 7') that match 2027, and a fall 2026 virtual session (Oct 13 and 20, 2026) whose application closed Sept 25, 2026. Applications are not reviewed until after the deadline.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 who want to explore cybersecurity. Students with little or no technical background are encouraged to apply.
how_to_apply: The page does not give steps. Contact the summer camp team at luddycmp@iu.edu or Joshua Streiff at jostre@iu.edu.
notes: Costs money. It is a camp, not a job. The page does not say whether it is residential or a day camp. Ask the summer camp team.

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 10 to 12. No experience is needed. Students are grouped by skill level.
how_to_apply: Applications open in January 2027 through the Luddy high school programs page. Contact the summer camp team at luddycmp@iu.edu or Joshua Streiff at jostre@iu.edu.
notes: Costs money. It is a camp, not a job. The same page lists the Luddy Cybersecurity Immersion Camp, which has its own card.

who_can_apply: High school juniors or seniors with a GPA of at least 3.0, recommended by a principal or guidance counselor, living with a parent or guardian within commuting distance of campus. IU GPA of at least 2.5 is also required once enrolled.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor, then email openprgm@iu.edu for the form and instructions.
notes: Only for students who live close enough to commute to Bloomington. Costs are real college credit fees. Not a job.

who_can_apply: High school students interested in sustainability and the environment. Need a computer, internet access and time for group work during the program.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the 2027 application opens in January 2027. Questions: essi@iu.edu.
notes: Entirely online, so students anywhere can join. The page shows quotes from 9th, 10th and 11th grade alumni. Participants receive a certificate of completion.

who_can_apply: Youth in grades 3 to 12 can enroll in regular 4-H. You must enroll every year.
how_to_apply: Enroll online in 4HOnline (the 'Click here to enroll' link on the county page). Call Purdue Extension Monroe County at 812-349-2575 for help.
notes: County 4-H camp is for grades 3 to 8, so older teens do not use it. The Extension office is at 3400 S Walnut St, Bloomington, IN 47401. This is a youth club, not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Teens entering at least 7th grade in the fall of the next school year. Teens apply with the Teen Volunteer Application; adults 18 and over use a separate form.
how_to_apply: Submit the Teen Volunteer Application (online form linked on the Become a Volunteer page), then register for a volunteer orientation. Contact: Volunteer Manager, 812-337-1337 ext. 221.
notes: Middle and high school volunteers work alongside college students and adults. Some roles (parties, outreach) need prior museum experience and training. Outreach events require your own transportation.

who_can_apply: Teens entering 9th through 12th grade, or the home-school equivalent. Graduating seniors may also apply. Required training is held at University Elementary School.
how_to_apply: Apply with the Teen Volunteer Application on WonderLab's Become a Volunteer page, choosing the WonderCamp internship; special training sessions are listed on the application form. Contact: 812-337-1337 ext. 221.
notes: Unpaid. The Become a Volunteer page says WonderCamp interns must be entering grade 9 in the fall of the next school year, while the internship page says entering grades 9 to 12; use the stricter reading (grade 9 or older) unless WonderLab says otherwise.

who_can_apply: Teen members of Boys & Girls Clubs of Boston, which serves ages 6 to 18 at clubs in Boston and Chelsea. The page gives no age rule for the workforce program itself.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how teens are placed. Find your nearest Club on the Find Your Club page and ask about the Ready to Work program and the Club's Employment Specialist. General contact page: bgcb.org/contact-us.
notes: Confirm first: ages, hours and how to apply are not on the page. Under Massachusetts law (M.G.L. c.149 s.86) a child employed needs a work permit from the superintendent of schools, so ask the Club how permits are handled. The Clubs' home page said membership fees were waived for the 2025 to 2026 school year; ask about this year's fee. Teen centers: Mildred C. Hailey Teen Center (Jamaica Plain) and Josh Kraft Mattapan Teen Center. See permit.html?state=ma for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Email volunteer@bpl.org or call 617-859-2304 to ask about openings and apply.
notes: Sites: Brighton, Central Library, Teen Central, Codman Square, East Boston, Grove Hall, Hyde Park, Mattapan, Roslindale, Shaw-Roxbury and West Roxbury. Workshops include resume building, privacy training and know your rights in the workplace.

who_can_apply: Students entering their junior or senior year of high school in fall 2027. Juniors need to be in Honors and/or AP courses.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with transcript, a 500 to 750 word personal statement and one academic teacher recommendation. The student must apply, not a parent or counselor.
notes: Expensive. 2027 dates are pending approval and may change. Standardized test scores are optional for summer 2027. Contact: summerhs@bu.edu.

who_can_apply: Cambridge residents who are 14 through the summer after finishing high school and eligible to work in the U.S. Priority goes to students eligible for free or reduced lunch and lower-income families.
how_to_apply: Apply online through Trax, the Department of Human Service Programs enrollment system. All applications go on a waitlist for review, which does not mean the program is full. Staff then schedule hiring paperwork (original ID and Social Security card needed).
notes: Questions: youthemployment@cambridgema.gov. The page does not mention a work permit; Massachusetts requires one for workers under 18 (M.G.L. c.149 s.86; Boston youth worker rights page written with the state Attorney General's Office). Participants may not miss more than 5 program days. There is no fixed maximum age on the page; eligibility ends after the summer following high school graduation.

who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18. The Massachusetts Wing site lists Become a Cadet as ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: The squadron page does not describe a visit process. Use the Contact Us and Join CAP pages on the Massachusetts Wing site. The wing phone is 781-225-6540 and its email is hq@mawg.cap.gov (these are the wing's, not the squadron's).
notes: The Massachusetts Wing also lists a Hanscom squadron (MA-043). The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 19 years old at the start of the internship, with a sincere interest in wildlife, education and environmental justice. About 6 to 8 interns are accepted.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application by December 9. Some applicants are invited to an in-person group interview. Email Ana Shapiro, Youth Programs Manager, at ashapiro@zoonewengland.org (no phone calls).
notes: Unpaid, so the work permit question is left open. Spring and summer teen internships are also planned; the page links a calendar of internship periods. The fall internship application is closed.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18. Paid ZooTeen roles are only for teens who live in Boston and Cambridge; volunteer roles are also offered.
how_to_apply: The program page does not give application steps. The school-year ZooTeen page lists the Youth Programs Manager, Ana Shapiro, at ashapiro@zoonewengland.org for questions, and an interest form for application updates.
notes: Work permit flag applies to the paid roles only (state rule: M.G.L. c.149 s.86 and the Boston youth worker rights page, written with the Attorney General's Office); volunteers do not need one. Dates and pay were not on the page, so confirm with the zoo.

who_can_apply: Youth jobs are for ages 14 to 18 (leader jobs for 19 to 24). Must be 14 by the start of the job, have finished 6th grade, and be legally permitted to work in the U.S. Most opportunities are limited to full-time Boston residents; some have extra requirements.
how_to_apply: Browse the futureBOS catalog, apply to at least three jobs, then get an offer and finish onboarding (work permit if under 18, proof of identity and work authorization, proof of school enrollment). City of Boston agency jobs can be onboarded in one visit to the YEO office at 1483 Tremont Street.
notes: Questions: futurebos@boston.gov or 617-635-4202. Under-18 workers need a Massachusetts work permit for the specific job (a doctor must sign for ages 14 and 15); the city page explains the steps. The $15 rate is quoted from the city FAQ. The state minimum wage statute (M.G.L. c.151 s.1) says a wage of less than $15.00 per hour is presumed oppressive and unreasonable; the current 2026 minimum wage page from the state Department of Labor Standards could not be read (403), so confirm the rate in your job offer. The work permit rule is M.G.L. c.149 s.86.

who_can_apply: High school students who will graduate and enter college in 2027, 2028 or 2029. You must be at least 16 by June 13, 2027. You must not turn 19 before July 31, 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply online at Harvard Summer School when the application opens December 1, 2026. Financial aid is requested during the application.
notes: Expensive and selective. Residential financial aid is limited to U.S. citizens and permanent residents.

who_can_apply: Teens of all skill levels and interests. The page does not give an age range, grades or a residency rule. Admission to the ICA is free for anyone 18 and under.
how_to_apply: Email teens@icaboston.org to get involved. The Teen Arts Council and Teen Exhibitions pages mention an application, but the programs page does not explain how to submit it. Phone: 617-478-3100.
notes: Confirm first. Ages, pay amount and deadlines are not on the pages we could read. Boston Public School students from participating high schools can earn school credit for taking part. Other ICA teen programs had no dates set. They are the Teen Digital Cooperative, and the music and photo break intensives. Paid work for people under 18 in Massachusetts needs a work permit (employment permit). See permit.html?state=ma for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Sophomores at the Edward M. Kennedy Academy for Health Careers, Revere High School, Chelsea High School or any Boston public school. A 3.0 GPA is required to apply.
how_to_apply: Ask your school guidance counselor (or PIC career specialist) in the fall and watch the program page for the spring application link. For summer jobs, contact your school's PIC career specialist.
notes: Combines the old Mass General Youth Scholars and Brigham Student Success Jobs programs. Sites include Mass General Hospital, Brigham and Women's, Faulkner Hospital and Mass Eye and Ear. Paid jobs under 18 need a Massachusetts work permit (state rule: M.G.L. c.149 s.86 and the Boston youth worker rights page; not on the MGB page).

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 10, 11 or 12 who are City of Boston residents or attend Boston Public Schools, and who can attend Thursday sessions 4 to 6:30 p.m. all year.
how_to_apply: Check the MFA Teen Programs page for the next application. This cycle's application is closed.
notes: Paid job, so teens under 18 need a Massachusetts work permit (not mentioned on the MFA page; see M.G.L. c.149 s.86 and the Boston youth worker rights page). The MFA also offers Teen Studio Art Classes for ages 12 to 17.

who_can_apply: Students who live or attend high school in the United States and finish the online course and the separate summer application. You must be in the US for the July program. The page lists no age or citizenship rule.
how_to_apply: Sign yourself up through the Formstack link on the Summer Program Application page. No nomination is needed. Or have a teacher or mentor nominate you. Later you need three essays of 500 words or less each. You need a teacher or mentor recommendation. You need parent or guardian information with an electronic signature. You also need to finish the online prerequisite course. Contact: bwsi-admin@mit.edu.
notes: Competitive. The cost wording on the page leaves the $200,000 to $200,001 range unclear, so ask BWSI if you are near that line. The online course is free and stays open to independent learners.

who_can_apply: Public school students from Boston, Cambridge or Lawrence, MA in 7th, 8th, 9th or 10th grade who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents (green card). Exceptions are not made.
how_to_apply: Create a profile in the MITES application portal and submit the MITES Saturdays application (separate from the Summer and Semester application).
notes: Students are expected to keep A and B grades; no minimum GPA to apply. The program encourages applicants who are underrepresented in STEM or from lower-income families or the first in their family to attend college.

who_can_apply: High school juniors who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents with a current green card. You can be from anywhere in the country, at a public, private or homeschool.
how_to_apply: Create a profile in the MITES application portal. MITES Summer and MITES Semester (a six-month STEM experience for rising seniors) share one application. Short-answer responses and recommendations from recent teachers are needed.
notes: Competitive and focused on students from underserved or under-resourced backgrounds. Residential on campus.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores and juniors who live in the United States. Students from Greater Boston can meet on campus. Other students can apply to PRIMES-USA. It meets with mentors online. Local and non-local students use the same portal.
how_to_apply: Use the online application portal linked on the MIT PRIMES how to apply page. It has an online questionnaire. It asks for two or three recommenders. Math teachers or camp counselors are ideal. It asks for a personal statement of up to 2 pages. It asks for lists of math books, courses, camps and computing skills. It also asks for solutions to the PRIMES 2027 Math Problem Set. Apply if you solve at least 70 percent. Upload solutions as one PDF with your name only in the file name.
notes: Competitive and heavy on math. There is also PRIMES Circle, a spring math enrichment program. It is for students within commuting distance of Boston. It has its own apply page at https://math.mit.edu/research/highschool/primes/circle/apply-circle.html, which was not read. Phone: (617) 253-4381.

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 19. You must be in high school or an equivalent program.
how_to_apply: Watch the museum's internship job board. Use View Internships on the Museum of Science internships page. Apply to the youth internship posting when it opens.
notes: The museum pages do not say if the internships are paid, so ask before you apply. Massachusetts law (M.G.L. c.149 s.86) says a child needs a work permit from the superintendent of schools to be employed. The museum also has Youth Volunteers, ages 14 to 19 and in high school. The volunteer page gives no application steps beyond a general interest form. See permit.html?state=ma for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 and older. Most internships are open to residents of Boston and Cambridge.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the application opens (expected next March). Interns also attend a weekly professional development course and an ocean advocacy course. Questions: teens@neaq.org.
notes: Paid job, so teens under 18 need a Massachusetts work permit (the aquarium page does not mention it; M.G.L. c.149 s.86 and the Boston youth worker rights page, written with the state Attorney General's Office, cover the permit rule). The aquarium also runs ClimaTeens (ages 13 and up, 2026-27 applications due October 18, 2026).

who_can_apply: High school rising juniors and seniors from the US and around the world. (The 17 or older rule on the page applies only to the London program.)
how_to_apply: Send in the online application. Add an unofficial high school transcript or report card. Add a personal statement of up to 250 words. A teacher or counselor reference is optional. You ask for financial aid inside the application.
notes: Expensive. The program page says the Summer 2027 offerings were still being finalized and will be posted later this fall. For a free Northeastern option for Massachusetts juniors see the Young Scholars Program card.

who_can_apply: Current juniors. You must be a permanent Massachusetts resident. That means you live and go to school in MA all year. You must live within commuting distance of campus. You must be a US citizen or permanent resident, with no exceptions.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Online Student Application. It takes 60 to 90 minutes. You cannot save it or restart it. So write the essay answers ahead of time. You also need two teacher recommendations. A STEM teacher is best. Enter the recommenders' email addresses in the application.
notes: Free, but only for Massachusetts residents who are US citizens or permanent residents. Late applications are not accepted. Read the program FAQ before emailing the coordinator. The same page also has a line saying applications are due March 2nd, 2026, which conflicts with the March 1, 2027 close date. Confirm the 2027 date with the program before you plan around it.

who_can_apply: Must be 15 on or before the first day and not turn 19 during the program. U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident. You must live locally. You should enjoy working with kids who are 7 to 12 years old.
how_to_apply: In 2026: download the YCC application form from the park page, add 1 or 2 references, scan it and email it to npb_youthprograms@nps.gov. Applications for 2026 are closed.
notes: Paid. Mon to Fri. No housing. Work includes safety duties with young campers and training on public land management. This is a federal job, so ask the park how the Massachusetts permit rule applies. Watch the park page in early 2027. Paid work for people under 18 in Massachusetts needs a work permit (employment permit). See permit.html?state=ma for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Children and teens ages 6 to 18 may apply at each location. Each Club has its own enrollment.
how_to_apply: Use 'Register for Membership Here' on the join page, which goes to the BGCMA parent portal (bgcma.org/local-clubs/parent-portal). Use the Find a Club page to pick a Club. Headquarters phone: 404-527-7100.
notes: This is a general club membership, not a job or internship. The pages read do not describe teen specific programs or teen jobs, so call your nearest Club and ask what is offered for teens.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 10-12 at a NYC high school, with a parent's signed consent, available 3 to 6 hours a week outside school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application or mail a print application to the Librarians of Tomorrow Internship Program, 10 Grand Army Plaza, Brooklyn, NY 11238. Questions: LOT@bklynlibrary.org or 718-230-2406.
notes: Library teen page lists ages 15-18; the program page requires grades 10-12 in NYC. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 10-12 at a NYC high school, with a parent's signed consent, available 3 to 5 hours a week outside school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Selected applicants are contacted for an interview. Questions: storyteen@bklynlibrary.org.
notes: Funded through the NYC Council's City's First Readers initiative. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16-19, with a parent's signed consent for 75 hours of intern service outside school, available to meet weekly.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application. All applicants get a follow-up email and some are invited to interview.
notes: The page does not say which library branches host councils. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: The site says it recruits college and high school students as teaching interns. No age or grade rule is posted. Middle school students can also join as program students.
how_to_apply: Use the Teaching Intern application link on breakthroughsac.org (online account login). Questions: BSAC@BreakthroughSac.org or 916-234-3905.
notes: Age minimum, pay and dates are not posted on the site, so call or email before applying. Training is two weeks (80 hours) on site.

who_can_apply: Young people who are at least 12 and have not reached 19. Have your health card ready when you register.
how_to_apply: Choose Sea, Army or Air Cadets. Find a unit near you in the Corps and Squadron Directory. Register with the Online Registration Tool. Have your health card and your parents' contact details ready. Then unit staff contact you to check ID and welcome you.
notes: This is a Canada-wide program. The units in British Columbia come from the national directory. The British Columbia work rule is not verified for this card. A youth program, not a paid job.

who_can_apply: British Columbia youth ages 15 to 24 who want to work, go to school or start a training program and face barriers to doing so. You must be legally entitled to work in BC. You should not already be working, in school or in training, or be working less than 15 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Sign yourself up with the online Foundry Work & Education form linked on the Foundry services page. Or find a Foundry centre near you.
notes: Foundry also gives free and confidential mental health and wellness services for youth ages 12 to 24. WorkBC also lists this program. The British Columbia work rule is not verified for this card.

who_can_apply: Students in high school. The pages read give no grade or age rule. Check the Youth Train in Trades Guide and your school for rules.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school's career educator or work experience coordinator. Train in Trades uses a program guide and a registration form. Work in Trades signs you up as an apprentice with an employer sponsor. It uses a Youth Apprentice and Sponsor Registration Form.
notes: The British Columbia work permit rule for these jobs is not verified. Other ways to find an apprenticeship listed on the site include job boards, WorkBC centres and hiring fairs. Youth Explore the Trades lets you sample several trades.

who_can_apply: Students who are active at a school or college. Your teacher, instructor or career coordinator must sign you up. The exact rules are in the provincial rules document.
how_to_apply: Talk to your teacher, instructor or career coordinator. They sign you up through the Skills Canada BC registration page. It needs a password. You get it from the organization or your regional coordinator.
notes: Students cannot sign themselves up. Regional registration goes through a teacher login. The provincial rule document at skillscanada.bc.ca/competitions/rules-and-regulations/ lists exact eligibility. The British Columbia work rule is not verified for this card.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 8. Letters of recommendation are not needed but are welcome.
how_to_apply: Fill out the yearly application during an open window. You share your interests and recent wins. You also share your goals for college and a career.
notes: For younger teens. Eighth graders are encouraged to apply to King Scholars at the high school level. Cost is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in grade 9, 10, 11 or 12 when they apply. Spring applicants must be in grades 9 to 11. A parent or guardian must attend onboarding.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the fall or spring window. Check the King Scholars page for the application and how to prepare.
notes: The Brookfield Zoo volunteer page says its regular volunteer forms are for adults. It says this program is its chance for high school students. Grade 8 graduates can join KCLA Transitions. Grade 12 students are not accepted in spring. Scholars who take part a lot can apply for seasonal jobs.

who_can_apply: Residents of Brookhaven or nearby areas, ages 14 to 18 or 19. The page says both, so confirm. You need passing grades and a clean background check. You cannot have criminal convictions or Juvenile Court referrals.
how_to_apply: Download the Cadet Application Packet and the Cadet Agreement Waiver (both PDFs) from the page. The page does not describe the steps after you turn them in.
notes: Meets at Brookhaven Police Department, 1793 Briarwood Road. The page lists ages 14 to 18 in one place and 14 to 19 in another. There is a community service requirement. Contact Officer Hawkins through the page or call 404-637-0600. Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 19 who live in or around Brookhaven. No grade is listed. Seats are limited.
how_to_apply: Reserve a spot with the online form on the program page, or contact the department. The page says early sign-up is encouraged.
notes: Held at Brookhaven Police Department, 1793 Briarwood Rd, Brookhaven, GA 30329. Call Officer Angela Hawkins at 678-296-1904. You can also call the Community Engagement Unit. The number is 404-637-0600, Option 8. This is unpaid, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 16 years old who can volunteer at least six hours a month and is excited about Texas history and welcoming visitors.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. If it is approved you are contacted for an interview, then attend a New Volunteer Orientation.
notes: Only 16 and older. Younger teens should look at the Austin Public Library youth volunteer program (ages 13 to 17).

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18 (the Virginia Wing page says to be at least 12 and not yet 19, and a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident). The squadron has both teen and adult members.
how_to_apply: Email va-130info@vawg.cap.gov or call (703) 239-4530 to ask about a meeting. The Virginia Wing steps are to visit with your parents. Then go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the cadet application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Meetings are at Irving Middle School, 8100 Old Keene Mill, Springfield, VA 22152, but the location can change for school events, and in August they meet elsewhere. Meetings are cancelled on the same days Fairfax County Schools cancels. The squadron page says it won a 2021 Virginia Wing Squadron of Merit award.

who_can_apply: High school students who completed junior year and have a semester left. There is no application. Your school recommends you. A local American Legion Post interviews and sponsors you. Girls State (below) is a separate program.
how_to_apply: Tell your counselor in junior year you are interested, or contact a local American Legion Post (use Find-A-Post on calegion.org). The Post chooses delegates; the delegate then registers online.
notes: Two separate programs. This one has been coed since 2023. California Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary, cagirlsstate.org) is its own program. It ran June 22 to 27, 2026 for 11th graders sponsored by a local Auxiliary Unit, one delegate per school. You can apply to only one. An old note about a 2020 article and a Sanger phone was out of date.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 21, per the 2026 Explorer competition packet. This is the competition age rule. Post membership rules such as GPA or background checks are not stated on the pages read.
how_to_apply: Email CHPExplorers@chp.ca.gov or call (916) 843-3210 (both listed in the 2026 packet) to ask how to join a post near you.
notes: Both official pages were read on 2026-10-07. The program page covers the statewide competition and does not say how to join a post. The 2026 packet is the source for the 15 to 21 age rule, which it states for the competition. Whether a post near you has room, and any background check or GPA rule, must be asked of CHP. The CHP East Sacramento post page returns 403 to automated reads, so use the email or phone above. See also CHP Explorer Post (East Sacramento) for a local post. Ages differ by source: the 2026 competition packet says 15 to 21, while the CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers.

who_can_apply: California law says an apprentice must be at least 16 (Labor Code 3077, in the state child labor guide). Each registered program sets its own minimum age, education and tests, shown in the DAS search, and may set a higher age.
how_to_apply: Use the Apprenticeship Search on the DAS site, check each program's minimum age and requirements, and apply the way the listing says.
notes: The DAS homepage states no age rule. The 16 minimum comes from the 2013 DLSE child labor guide, which also says apprentices need a school-issued work permit. DAS's How to Become an Apprentice page says search results list each program's minimum age. DAS runs a youth apprenticeship grant and reports 5,776 registered pre-apprentices on its homepage.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 15 to 25 who need extra help to finish school or find work. Examples listed are offense history as a minor and teen parent. Others are foster care or no stable housing, and gang involvement or risk. Minority group, low income, and disability or reading difficulty are also listed. You may still qualify if you do not match these.
how_to_apply: The page has no separate enrollment steps. Use the YEOP Contact Information page. It helps you reach a YEOP specialist in your area. Or contact your local America's Job Center of California.
notes: The page says clearly: this is not a job placement program. It is help and coaching toward school and work.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 24 who meet certain requirements. The EDD page does not list the requirements. It points to the Youth Employment Opportunity Program page and fact sheet for criteria.
how_to_apply: Find your local America's Job Center of California with the EDD Office Locator (edd.ca.gov/en/Office_Locator/). The page also suggests building a resume in CalJOBS and visiting the center to ask about internships, apprenticeships and training.
notes: The EDD page does not say the youth services are free. It says Job Centers connect employers with job seekers at no cost. Eligibility criteria are not on the EDD page read; it links to the YEOP services and eligibility criteria. Teens under 18 who take a paid job in California need a work permit from their school (CDE page).

who_can_apply: Under 18 needs written parent or guardian permission. Specific age minimums vary by park.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the State Parks volunteer portal or print a paper application and mail it to the park you want. Questions: Volunteer.inparksprogram@parks.ca.gov or (916) 653-9069. The application link is on the official page.
notes: A criminal background check may be required. Park-level age minimums were not on the page, so ask the park. Student volunteer or intern roles are mentioned only as a general possibility at local parks. No Junior Ranger details were on this page.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 30 on the first day of service. You must meet at least one of: foster care, justice involved, mental health or substance abuse system, low income, hard time finding work, or unemployed and/or out of school.
how_to_apply: Pick your local program from the partner list on the state page and apply through its link. Or use the state interest form. State office: info@californiavolunteers.ca.gov (say Youth Service Corps) or (916) 323-7646.
notes: Partner list on the page: Anaheim, Antioch, Bakersfield, Chula Vista, Fresno, Irvine, La Puente, Long Beach, Los Angeles, Oakland, Rancho Cucamonga, Riverside, Sacramento, San Francisco, San Diego, San Jose, Santa Cruz, South Gate, Stockton, Marin County, Monterey County, Mechoopda Band of Chico Rancheria and Ramona Band of Cahuilla. California requires a work permit for minors in paid jobs (CDE page), so under 18 you will need one. The state page does not say whether each city requires you to live there, so check the local program.

who_can_apply: Your school district must run an approved WEE program. Exploratory WEE students can be as young as 12 and do not need a work permit. General WEE usually needs a work permit. Career Technical WEE needs a job related to a career technical class you take.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor or CTE/work experience coordinator whether your district has a WEE program and what class goes with it.
notes: The 2013 state child labor guide says students must be 16 to enroll in WEE, with exceptions in the Education Code (14 and 15 year olds can get permits in some cases). The CDE page says Exploratory can start at 12. Programs exist only where the district chose to run one. Use the three current names above.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors interested in engineering, robotics or AI. Bonita Unified School District students get priority.
how_to_apply: Email the RASIM Center at rasim@cpp.edu to sign up during the January to April window.
notes: The page's sample schedule is labeled Summer 2027 but gives no exact dates. Confirm by email.

who_can_apply: Kids and teens join through a county 4-H program. Check your county page for age rules and fees.
how_to_apply: Find your county 4-H office from ucanr.edu/sites/ca4H.
notes: The 4-H site blocked automated access on 2026-10-07 (403 and a bot check), so age rules and fees could not be read. Ages, fees and teen roles must be confirmed with your county 4-H office. Re-checked on 2026-10-09: the 4-H page returned HTTP 403 again, so it could not be read and the card stays snippet-only.

who_can_apply: Students at a school that runs a California Cadet Corps unit. Participation is voluntary. The pages read do not say how a student enrolls beyond being at a host school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school whether it has a Cadet Corps unit. The program site says schools that want to start one should email Recruiting@cacadets.org. The site's Contact Us page is cacadets.org/about/contact.
notes: Pages read did not include a school finder, so the best first step is to ask your school office or email the program. The program site says more than 7,000 students are in over 100 schools.

who_can_apply: Students at a California school with an FBLA chapter. The FAQ says FBLA is open to students enrolled in a Career and Technical Education (CTE) business program.
how_to_apply: Ask whether your school has a chapter: email hello@cafbla.org or call (714) 824-4489. If not, fill out the FBLA Interest Form so staff can help your school affiliate; that needs your school administration.
notes: You join through a school chapter, so you need a business pathway or class at your school. If your school has no business program, the FAQ says starting one has to be started with school administration.

who_can_apply: Join through a school that has an agricultural education program; chapters are chartered in schools with ag classes. California reports over 103,000 members. Age and grade rules were not on the pages I read.
how_to_apply: Take an agriculture class at a school with an FFA chapter.
notes: Not every school has an FFA chapter. Ask your counselor or ag teacher. Age and grade limits and dues were not on the California or National FFA pages I read.

who_can_apply: Students at schools that host an academy. Each academy sets its own application. Search the school's website for 'Partnership Academy'.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor if your school has an academy. The CDE page links a directory of academies (a spreadsheet updated September 2026). The page does not say how students apply.
notes: Read the CDE page on 2026-10-09. It confirms a three-year program for grades 10 to 12, structured as a school-within-a-school, with academics plus career technical education, business partnerships, mentoring and internships. It posts only school and district grant dates, not student application dates, and does not say whether students from other districts may transfer in. Academies are run by individual schools, so ask your counselor. Fremont Unified says some CTE courses sit inside Partnership Academies.

who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled in a Pasadena Unified School District (PUSD) high school. Grade and age rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: The page has no form. Use the email link for the program contact (Mitch Aiken) on the Summer Research Connection page.
notes: Only for PUSD students. Contact early in the school year because spots fill by early spring.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 in Wake and Johnston counties per the Capital Area youth page. The NextGen site says the program serves young adults facing barriers such as legal issues, home problems or missed education, and lists Wake, Johnston, Chatham, Lee and Orange counties. Exact eligibility rules and income limits are not stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form for your county at capitalareanextgen.org, or use the Request More Information form on the Capital Area youth page.
notes: This is the federal workforce (WIOA) style youth program for Wake County. Durham is covered by a different workforce board and is not listed. The pages do not say whether 14 to 17 year olds qualify in every case; ask the career center.
