who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

who_can_apply: Rising high school sophomores, juniors and seniors (grades 10 to 12) interested in art and design.
how_to_apply: Register online and pay the $250 registration fee. Scholarship applicants submit a form, a 300 to 500 word personal statement, three artwork samples and a NACAC fee waiver.
notes: Fees shown are the 2026 prices. Meals are included on weekdays. Refunds: tuition balance less the registration fee is refunded in full if withdrawn by June 15, 2026 and half by June 29, 2026.

who_can_apply: High school students who meet at least one criterion, such as low income, foster youth, system-involved, homeless, pregnant or parenting, English learner, below grade level in math or reading, or an IEP.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Referral Form (online form linked on the CCCOE page) or call: West County (925) 296-1507 or 296-1504; East County (925) 296-1505 or 296-1506.
notes: The out-of-school program is for ages 18 to 24, so only the in-school program fits most teens. Help can include transportation, interview clothes and school supplies.

who_can_apply: High school students in the summer before junior or senior year, at least 16 on the first day of camp (no exceptions). A government photo ID is needed for CDC security. Non-Atlanta residents may apply but must arrange housing and travel. Non-U.S. citizens may apply with the documents asked for.
how_to_apply: The pages read do not describe the application steps. The camp page says the application is found through the FAQ page when it opens, and to check back in January 2027.
notes: Very competitive in past years, but numbers were not on the pages read. Sessions are fixed, campers cannot arrive late, leave early or miss days.

who_can_apply: Students 14 to 18 enrolled in high school with a transcript showing at least a 3.2 GPA. New volunteers and one parent or guardian must attend a mandatory in-person Teen Information Session.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with your transcript, finish the online volunteer orientation, complete health screening and flu vaccine (flu season Nov 1 to Apr 30), and attend the Teen Information Session (Monday, Jan 11, 2027, 5:30 to 7:00 p.m.).
notes: Spots are limited and fill fast, so apply the day the window opens. Shifts run Monday to Sunday. Teens who want research should look at Cedars-Sinai's separate INSPIRE Internship Program (not checked here). Questions: TeenVolunteerProgram@cshs.org or 310-423-8044.

who_can_apply: Current high school students. Each semester you complete a Chabot application and the concurrent enrollment packet. You can take any class except basic skills and PE.
how_to_apply: Apply to Chabot, pick a class, complete the IDE Enrollment Form, then register through MyPortal. Questions: cc-earlycollege@chabotcollege.edu or 510-723-6701.
notes: Also offers CCAP classes at your high school and a Summer Academy. Middle schoolers have a separate Bridge to College program.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page encourages students of all backgrounds to apply, especially Oakland public and charter school students. No skills, experience or GPA is needed. Admission is competitive: an initial review, then an information session for applicants and families. Age and residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Online application from February 1 to March 31, then an initial review and an information session for applicants and families. The page also has an interest survey to get application updates.
notes: Corrected on 2026-10-07 after reading the program's own page. The old chabotspace.org/volunteer/ link now returns 404, so the card points to the Galaxy Explorers page. This is a fee-based program ($1,500 a year tuition) unless the family qualifies for Career Access, which is based on need and census tract data. Floor shifts are 2 per month in the school year and 3 per month in summer. Whether paid Interns need a California work permit is not stated, so needs_work_permit is null.

who_can_apply: High school volunteers must be 14 or older. Students must provide up-to-date immunization records.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button under 'Students (college/teen)' on the Carle Foundation Hospital volunteer page (opens an online application) and send immunization records.
notes: The next listed deadline is the spring term deadline of November 15; confirm the year and current rules with Carle Volunteer Services. Other Carle sites list their own teen age ranges.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 who meet at least one condition, such as low family income, a disability, being a school dropout, homeless or foster youth, or needing extra help to finish school or get a job.
how_to_apply: The page gives no workNet address or walk-in hours. General CCRPC office: 1776 E Washington St, Urbana, IL 61802, (217) 328-3313.
notes: Eligibility rules apply, so not every teen qualifies. Call to ask about summer paid placements. The workforce site may be updated separately at eciwork.net. Illinois requires an employment certificate under age 16 (see the Illinois rules on this site).

who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 17. Candidates are picked through an application and interview.
how_to_apply: Email or call Stacey Clementz at the Homer Lake Interpretive Center, (217) 896-2455, or use the online volunteer application on the page.
notes: Youth program volunteers (school programs, September to May) and public program volunteers are also listed on the page; age rules for those are not stated. The District also has public volunteer events that need no application.

who_can_apply: The page says 15 year olds can apply for lifeguard and swim instructor. Minimum ages for other jobs are not stated; check each posting.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the District's job listings (linked from the Employment Opportunities page). Aquatics questions: Ryan Hays, ryan.hays@champaignparks.org. HR: hr@champaignparks.org.
notes: Lifeguard classes are run by the District in Champaign-Urbana. Concession workers get a paid-for Food Handler's certification. Illinois requires an employment certificate under age 16 (see the Illinois rules on this site).

who_can_apply: Teens at least 13 years old who are enthusiastic, hardworking and willing to learn. Teen volunteers may work at most 25 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Champaign Park District Volunteer Portal, then view opportunities. Questions: volunteer@champaignparks.org.
notes: Some roles (for example Prairie Farm) run only part of the year.

who_can_apply: At least 15 years old, attending an area high school or home-schooled, with course prerequisites and assessment requirements met. For high school credit you also need your school's approval and good standing.
how_to_apply: Use the How to Apply page under Dual Credit. Early College Services: 217-353-2663, earlycollege@parkland.edu (office U214).
notes: Early College students do not qualify for financial aid. Credit and grades go on a permanent Parkland transcript. The Early College page also lists an Early College and Career Academy with programs such as Automotive Technology, Certified Nurse Assistant and EMS.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. If you are 16 or 17 you need a signed waiver from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Complete the online volunteer application, then schedule the required interview. Contact: Eva Liu, Volunteer Coordinator, volunteer@champaign.org, 217-403-2000 x3.
notes: Open roles change, so look at the current listings on the page. The Douglass Branch's Club Fred program is a summer role.

who_can_apply: Pre-college students entering the listed grades in the fall. The page does not mention international students.
how_to_apply: Camp application (with the scholarship application inside it). See the Camp FAQs for the process.
notes: Costs do not include travel to campus. Some camps are EAGER or IDEA camps focused on broadening participation, open to all to apply. Use the WYSE mailing list for next year's dates.

who_can_apply: Rising 10th to 12th graders who live in Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Missouri, Iowa or Wisconsin. No international applicants. No course prerequisites.
how_to_apply: Online application with student information, two personal statements and a teacher, mentor or counselor recommendation form (emailed after you submit). Join the Summer Program Notifications mailing list for next year's dates.
notes: Competitive: applications are ranked together, not first come first served. Housing is for selected students who do not live locally. Students get no course credit.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15 who have completed 7th grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the CIT application (PDF or online form on the Teen Programs page). Questions: Cathy Schneider (contact link on the page).
notes: Because pay is not stated, ask whether CITs are paid before applying. Illinois requires an employment certificate under age 16 (see the Illinois rules on this site).

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12. A parent or guardian must complete the Volunteer Waiver first.
how_to_apply: Show up. A guardian signs the Volunteer Waiver and emails it to Connor Ross (cjross@urbanaparks.org, 217-384-4062) or brings a printed copy on the day.
notes: Meets about every two weeks at different parks (Victory, Meadowbrook, Weaver, Crystal Lake, Busey Woods). The same page lists a free Teen Hangout Zone for grades 6 to 12 on select Fridays at Phillips Recreation Center.

who_can_apply: The library's volunteer interest form offers the age choices 14-17 and 18 and older. The page does not state a separate minimum age.
how_to_apply: Read the position descriptions, then fill out the volunteer interest form on the library's Volunteer with us page and pick Youth Event Support Volunteer.
notes: The 14 to 17 range comes from the age options on the interest form, not from a written rule. Call 919-968-2777 or email library@chapelhillnc.gov to confirm the minimum age and hours. The library also has a Teen Room for ages 13 to 18; no teen advisory board was listed on the pages read.

who_can_apply: Children ages 12 to 17 may volunteer if a parent or guardian is with them for each shift. In the Food Recovery Area, ages 12 to 16 need a parent or guardian at each shift. Volunteers ages 17 and older may work there without an adult after an initial shift with an adult. Youth groups ages 12 to 15 need one adult chaperone for every 3 children. Youth groups ages 16 and 17 need one adult for every 6 youth. Volunteers must be 18 or older at the Winchester warehouse.
how_to_apply: Create your own account on the online volunteer calendar. It is required for safety and communication. Then register for a shift. If you do not get a confirmation email, the registration did not go through. Contact the volunteer team at volunteer@brafb.org. Group sizes are 4 to 8 people at most locations. They are up to 10 at the Verona warehouse. Everyone needs their own account.
notes: A parent or guardian must be at every shift for ages 12 to 17, so this works best for families. The page lists the front desk as (540) 268-3663. The footer lists 540-248-3663. Confirm which number is right. The page we read names the Winchester and Verona warehouses. It does not name the Charlottesville warehouse. Confirm which age rule applies there.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 and older. The page welcomes volunteers ages 14 and up. Groups with people under 18 need at least one adult chaperone for every 10 children.
how_to_apply: Use the Schedule Orientation or Volunteer Application link on the SPCA volunteer page to choose an orientation date and fill out the volunteer application. Orientation comes before you take on tasks. Contact: volunteer@caspca.org or 434-973-5959 ext. 314.
notes: The pages do not say if 14 to 17 year olds need a parent signature. They do not say if there are limits on which animals teens can work with. Ask at orientation. The apply link goes to the SPCA's event calendar on a third party site.

who_can_apply: Classes are free for Charlottesville City Schools and Albemarle County Public Schools students. The pages read do not list grade levels. They do not list the steps to enroll.
how_to_apply: The pages do not describe an enrollment process. Ask your school counselor. Contact CATEC at 434-245-2419 or catecinfo@charlottesvilleschools.org. The 2026 to 2027 Program of Studies PDF is linked from the CATEC high school program of studies page.
notes: Confirm first. Grade levels and enrollment steps are not on the pages read. For 2026 to 2027, CATEC does not offer some academic courses. They are Biology II, English 12, USA Government, and Economics and Personal Finance. EMT and Fire Science are no longer dual enrollment through CVCC. Students still earn CTE credits. Address: 1000 East Rio Road, Charlottesville.

who_can_apply: Charlottesville-area youth 14 to 21 (14 by the start of the CAYIP Academy). City of Charlottesville residents get priority. Parent or guardian must also complete paperwork for youth under 18.
how_to_apply: Submit the CAYIP application (questionnaire, inventory and agreement to participate) during the session window, then a one-on-one interview. Accepted youth attend the mandatory paid CAYIP Academy. Contact: cayipinquiries@charlottesville.gov, 434-987-0018.
notes: Applications are only accepted during a session window. Transportation is not provided. Interns may miss at most 5 days per session. Virginia's labor department says 14 and 15 year old workers must get an Employment Certificate before any work; the program page does not mention it, so ask CAYIP staff how it is handled.

who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18. The Virginia Wing site lists Become a Cadet as ages 12 to 18. The national Civil Air Patrol page says cadets can join at ages 12 through 18.
how_to_apply: Send the squadron a message on Facebook or email 091.pa@vawg.cap.gov and they will be in touch. The Virginia Wing headquarters number on the page is 804-454-7356.
notes: Confirm first: the squadron page gives no street address, so ask for the exact meeting location before you go. The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.

who_can_apply: Listed for ages 15 and up. Everyone must pass the in-water pretest or be removed from the class.
how_to_apply: Register through the city's Registration & Tickets system. Within 72 hours of registering, email swimprograms@charlottesville.gov with the subject Lifeguard Pretest to book the pretest at least 8 days ahead.
notes: The page does not say the class leads to a job. The city lists seasonal and variable-hour jobs on governmentjobs.com; none were open on 2026-10-09. Virginia's labor department says 14 and 15 year old workers need an Employment Certificate before any work.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 10 to 12. You send an application and two references who are not relatives. You also do a 15-minute interview.
how_to_apply: New LITs fill out the online application and have two references send the reference form. Returning LITs use a separate form. Then a 15-minute interview.
notes: This costs money and is not a paid job. You must attend at least 85% of your session. Dates shown are from summer 2026.

who_can_apply: High school and college students. The page lists no ages or grades.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the Water Warriors page. You can also sign up there for emails about Water Warriors news and events.
notes: In summer, high school students can test water samples, check CASSI units and clean trash traps with staff. Contact: Jillian Griffin, jgriffin@chattahoochee.org, or 404-352-9828.

who_can_apply: Teens in the Chicago area. The page does not list an age, grade or city rule.
how_to_apply: Watch the Youth & Teen Programs page and join the Adler youth email list (Sign Up on the page). Questions: youthprograms@adlerplanetarium.org.
notes: New program, described as a first group to shape it. Pay, age limits and time commitment are not stated, so confirm with the Adler before you plan around it.

who_can_apply: Teens in the Chicago area. The page does not list an age, grade or city rule.
how_to_apply: Watch the Youth & Teen Programs page and join the Adler youth email list (Sign Up on the page). Questions: youthprograms@adlerplanetarium.org.
notes: Real citizen-science style research with the Far Horizons team. Age limits, pay and hours are not stated on the page, so confirm with the Adler.

who_can_apply: Teens in high schools in the Chicago area.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Apply form linked on the Opportunities for Teens page when the next call opens.
notes: Chicago teens under 18 get free museum admission. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

who_can_apply: Chicago high school teens who will be at least 16 at the start of the internship.
how_to_apply: Apply through After School Matters when the spring window opens.
notes: Run with After School Matters. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

who_can_apply: Chicago Public Schools students going into grade 11 or 12.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link in the College First section of the Science Career Continuum page.
notes: The page lists "Tuesday, April 15" with no year. April 15 fell on a Tuesday in 2025, so this looks like an older date. Check the page for the next deadline. The program runs at the Chicago Botanic Garden; transportation is provided.

who_can_apply: Chicago Public Schools students going into grade 9 or 10.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link in the Science First section of the Science Career Continuum page.
notes: The page lists "Tuesday, April 15" with no year. April 15 fell on a Tuesday in 2025, so this looks like an older date. Check the page for the next deadline. The program runs at the Chicago Botanic Garden; transportation is provided. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules; the page does not say whether one is needed here.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18. Courses are open to all experience levels.
how_to_apply: Register on the Summer at Columbia page when it opens. Use the Registration tab. Questions: summer@colum.edu.
notes: Costs money and is not a job. Earn college credit toward a Columbia degree if you enroll there later.

who_can_apply: High school students from the Chicago area. The page does not list an age or grade rule. Only 15 are chosen.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page in early 2027 for the application. If you have questions, write to digitalstudio@fieldmuseum.org.
notes: Interns work on site at the Field Museum on a set schedule. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

who_can_apply: Students ages 15 to 22 who live in Chinatown, Bronzeville, Little Village, Pilsen or nearby. You want to link your area to the south lakefront. That is McCormick Place to 47th Street.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the program page. Check the Keller Science Action Center page linked from the Field Museum teen page.
notes: Open to ages 15 to 22, so younger teens and college-age students may be in the same group. Confirm dates and pay before relying on this.

who_can_apply: Current high school students. The page does not list an age rule.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page for the application to open in early 2027. Questions: teens@fieldmuseum.org.
notes: The Field Museum says its youth programs may give stipends, public transit vouchers and free admission. Check each program.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 11 to 18. The page describes participants as middle and high school artists ages 11-18.
how_to_apply: Use the "Register for programs here" button on the Programs page. Questions: programs@freespiritmedia.org.
notes: Older teens 18 and up can look at the Creative Pathways job program (ages 18 to 25). The page does not say if sign-up is still open for fall, so contact the program. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16. It refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

who_can_apply: Ambitious high school juniors at schools that partner with Genesys Works. Must be on track to graduate, able to work in the U.S., and able to have a lighter class schedule senior year for internship hours.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the Application Process page. Choose the site nearest you. If you are accepted, you are invited to interview. Ask your school counselor if your school is a partner.
notes: Genesys Works only works with certain partner schools, so check with your counselor first. The Chicago page lists 225 high school internships and 65 company partners. The homepage says students can earn $10,000 to $13,000 in the senior year. The FAQ says $10,000 to $12,000. The pages do not say if a work permit is needed. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16. It refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 18 in the Chicago area. A video audition is part of the application.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Upload a self-tape with an intro, a 1-minute monologue and a 16 to 32 bar song cut. Questions: summerprograms@goodmantheatre.org.
notes: Auditions are by self-tape. Held at the Goodman, 170 N. Dearborn St. The main youth page calls it a four-week program; the program page says five weeks, and the dates shown are five weeks. Confirm the length for 2027.

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 18 in the Chicago area. A video audition is part of the application.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Upload a self-tape with an intro, a 1-minute monologue and a 30 to 60 second wild card. Questions: summerprograms@goodmantheatre.org.
notes: The main youth page calls it four weeks and the program page says five weeks; the dates shown are five weeks. Confirm the length for 2027.

who_can_apply: Chicago Public Schools students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Write to the Goodman and ask about the next application. The email is Education@GoodmanTheatre.org.
notes: The page still shows the 2025/26 school year, so confirm the 2026/27 plan with the Goodman. Meetings are at 170 N. Dearborn St.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not list an age or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Use the Details and registration links on the RISE page. Questions: Contact Us form on the page.
notes: The museum website is now griffinmsi.org. The regular museum volunteer program is for adults 18 and over, so RISE is the teen route. The structured 12-week session may lead to internships, the page says. Also offers a drop-in option with no long commitment.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 12 in the Chicago metro area, guided by a teacher. The Senior Division is grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Work through your teacher: the teacher files the Intent to Participate form, your school registers, then you register your project in zFairs. See the Dates and Deadlines page.
notes: School-based, so you need a teacher or school to sign up. Dates are subject to change, the museum says. The museum congratulates students on results at Illinois State History Day and National History Day. Not a job; good for building research and speaking skills.

who_can_apply: Teens entering grades 9 to 13 who are 13 to 18 years old by the June start date. The page does not list a city or school rule.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Application link on the program page. Two Zoom info sessions were held in Feb and March in 2026.
notes: Camp days run 8 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., Monday to Friday. Required training days are in April, May and June. Teens also get up to 15 Professional Development Sessions and Teen Bonding Nights.

who_can_apply: You must live in the city of Chicago and go to a Chicago high school. You must be at least 16 by the program start. You must be able to come to all program dates.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the After School Matters website and apply there. Use an email you check often. Interviews follow.
notes: Meetings are on Saturdays with a few extra dates. No meetings over CPS spring break. Two absences per semester may be allowed if told in advance. The page does not say whether the board is paid. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

who_can_apply: You must live in the city of Chicago and go to a Chicago high school. You must be at least 16 by June 1. You must be able to come to all program dates.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the After School Matters website and apply there. Rank "Lincoln Park Zoo - Nature Buds" as your top pick.
notes: Outdoor work. Shifts are four days a week. Pay rate is from the 2026 page and may change. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

who_can_apply: Must live in the city of Chicago, be entering grades 11 to 12 (or a college freshman) in the fall, be 16 to 18 by the June start, and be legally allowed to work in the U.S. with proof of identity. No research experience needed.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the zoo SlideRoom link on the program page. The zoo invites strong applicants to a half-day group interview in March.
notes: Introductory research program, so teens with no lab or field experience are welcome. Apprentices do not work directly with animals. You need a way to get to the zoo each day. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

who_can_apply: You must live in the city of Chicago. You must be going into grades 10 to 12 (or be a college freshman) in the fall. You must be 16 to 18 by the June orientation date. You must be allowed to work in the U.S. and have proof of identity.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the zoo SlideRoom link on the program page. Invited applicants go to a half-day group interview at the zoo in March. The zoo also held two Zoom info sessions in late Feb and early March in 2026.
notes: Interns do not work directly with animals. You need a reliable way to get to the zoo each day. You can apply to several zoo teen programs at once. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules. Contact is listed on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18 from across the Chicago area. Parents are not allowed at the events.
how_to_apply: Register for each event with the Register Now button on the Zoo Teens page.
notes: Going to an event adds you to the list for news about the zoo's internships and other teen programs. Parking is at 2400 N. Cannon Drive for events at the zoo.

who_can_apply: Chicago residents ages 16 to 18 by July 1 of the program year. You have taken at least one Marwen course. You can commit to the full schedule. You have a Social Security number or an employment tax ID.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the spring window opens. Selected teens get a 30-minute Zoom interview with Marwen staff in May.
notes: You must have taken a Marwen course first. Marwen classes are no-cost for Chicago students in grades 6 to 12 who face barriers to arts programs. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

who_can_apply: Chicago teens. The page says ages 14 to 19 in one place and 15 to 19 in another, so confirm the age rule with the museum.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply to TCA form (Airtable) on the MCA Teens page when it opens. Questions: Ahmad Bracey, abracey@mcachicago.org, 312-397-4020.
notes: Free museum entry for anyone 18 and under. Teens can also send projects to 21Minus each winter. It is free for ages 21 and under. The page does not say if a work permit is needed. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16. It refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

who_can_apply: Chicago Public Schools students ages 16 to 18. You care about making CPS schools better.
how_to_apply: Recruitment for 2027 starts in the spring. Watch the Mikva Challenge program application page or email inquiries@mikvachallenge.org. Phone: (312) 863-6340.
notes: A city-wide teen council. The program page gives ages 16 to 18; the application page says Citywide Youth Councils are for current 9th to 11th graders.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 20 who live in Chicago or Cook County.
how_to_apply: Recruitment for 2027 starts in the spring. Watch the Mikva Challenge program application page or email inquiries@mikvachallenge.org. Phone: (312) 863-6340.
notes: The council includes young people affected by the juvenile justice system. The age range here is 16 to 20, so some members are over 18 and teens work alongside older youth.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors in Chicago. Mikva staff recruit through teachers.
how_to_apply: Ask your teacher or school about Mikva Challenge student election judges. Or write to inquiries@mikvachallenge.org. You can also call (312) 863-6340.
notes: Mikva says it recruits 2,000+ juniors and seniors in Chicago and DC each election cycle. Mikva says it works with local election boards. The Chicago Board of Election Commissioners website blocked our reader, so pay, age and sign-up rules there were not checked. Confirm with Mikva or the Board.

who_can_apply: About 50 young people after their senior year. Cook County youth, through the state youth program. Age limits not stated.
how_to_apply: Recruitment for 2027 starts in the spring. Watch the Mikva Challenge program application page or email inquiries@mikvachallenge.org. Phone: (312) 863-6340.
notes: For young people after their senior year. The page does not state an age limit. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

who_can_apply: Chicago youth ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: Recruitment for 2027 starts in the spring. Watch the Mikva Challenge program application page or email inquiries@mikvachallenge.org. Phone: (312) 863-6340.
notes: Good fit if you want to work in health or public health. The page lists a partnership with the Lurie Children's Center on Childhood Resilience.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15 who live in Chicago.
how_to_apply: Contact the staff at the park you are interested in to start the application. The process is an application, an interview, a mentoring curriculum and performance check-ins.
notes: Re-read on 2026-10-09: ages 13 to 15, Chicago residence, the apply step (contact the park) and the 2026 session dates all match the page. The page says RIT is a job readiness program and participants are not Park District staff. It does not mention pay, so the pay type was changed from stipend to no pay stated. The next sessions are posted online about a month before each starts.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 and older for lifeguards, recreation leaders, special recreation leaders and junior laborers. The page does not state a residency rule, so check with the Park District.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Park District job site. Use the Learn More and Apply Now links on the Summer Jobs page. Or go to a Teen Opportunity Fair. Applications must be in by the closed date on each job posting.
notes: Work permit: Illinois requires employment certificates only for minors under 16 (Illinois Dept. of Labor FAQ). All of these jobs start at 16. Teens 13 to 15 should see the Recreation Leader in Training program. Fair email: teensinthepark@chicagoparkdistrict.com.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 17 years old who can give four hours a week, Monday to Friday between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m., for at least six months in a row. Needs TB test and MMR and chickenpox records.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application on the page. Rush replies by email in 5 to 7 business days. The email has steps for orientation and a health screening. Contact: volunteer_services@rush.edu, (312) 942-5574.
notes: No summer-only volunteering. No weekend or evening shifts. Internships and externships are not offered through Volunteer Services. Under 17 does not qualify here. The page lists separate phone numbers for Rush Copley and Rush Oak Park.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 18. The 1.0 college-credit option is for juniors and seniors ages 15 to 18.
how_to_apply: Sign up for courses on the Early College Program page. For the Smith Scholarship, fill out the scholarship form. Upload your household 1040 and send in three pieces of art to SlideRoom. For need-based aid, say yes at sign-up and upload the 1040 in DocuSign.
notes: Costs money unless you win the Smith Scholarship or aid. Aid is first come, first served.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18 who have completed their sophomore year by the time of the program. Merit scholarships are open to all students; need-based aid is for US residents.
how_to_apply: Register online when sign-up opens November 1. When you sign up, you can also apply for a merit scholarship or need-based aid.
notes: The page says registration opens November 1 but gives no year. It probably means this coming November for summer 2027, so confirm. The site menu also lists an online version (ECPOSI). Its details were not on the page read.

who_can_apply: High school students from the Chicago area. The page lists no age or school rule.
how_to_apply: Watch the Young Adult Council page for the next application. Questions: teenprograms@steppenwolf.org.
notes: Members see Steppenwolf plays and many Chicago plays for free. Steppenwolf also runs free Step In theatre workshops and Teen Takeover nights, which have cheap tickets to shows. Join the teen email list on the Teen Programs page for updates.

who_can_apply: You must have been in CPS this year and last year. You will be a junior or senior. You have a strong record in the hardest courses you can take. You are ready for college work.
how_to_apply: Fill out an online application. It has short essays, a graded work sample, a teacher recommendation and transcripts. It also has an online interview in mid-August. For the $0 tuition option, you need financial aid papers.
notes: UChicago classes do not follow the CPS calendar, so you attend even when your high school is on break. Many students stop after Winter Quarter.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors or seniors who are at least 16 by June 14, 2027 and live in Cook, Lake, Will or DuPage counties in Illinois or Lake County, Indiana. College freshmen and sophomores can also apply. Must commit to both summers.
how_to_apply: Fill out the common Pathway Programs online application (REDCap). Two people must send in recommendations. At least one must be a teacher or professor. Up to 12 applicants are accepted.
notes: You must find your own housing and ride to UChicago. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16. It refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules. One application covers all the UChicago cancer pathway programs that fit you.

who_can_apply: Full-time high school students who live in Cook, Lake, Will or DuPage counties in Illinois or Lake County, Indiana, and can attend every weekday, 4 hours a day. Up to 20 students per year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the common Pathway Programs online application (REDCap). Two people must send in forms for you. At least one must be a teacher or professor.
notes: Virtual program run with Kentucky, Michigan, Penn and UT Austin. No minimum age is listed. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed for the stipend.

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old (some roles need 18+). Must interview, pass health screening, a drug screen and a background check, and not hold certain visas (B-1, B-2, H-1B, H-4).
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Volunteer application. Do it when a recruiting window is open. The form is in Volgistics. Then you talk with Volunteer Services in an interview. For questions, write to vservices@uchicagomedicine.org. You can also call 773-702-4421.
notes: The page says student volunteers must be at least 16, and some opportunities need 18 or older. The summer program opens in early March 2027. One summer block says applicants must be 18 at submission, while the FAQ says the summer rules match the others (16). Confirm the summer age rule.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who live in Illinois or Lake County, Indiana, are at least 16 by June 14, 2027, and can commit to all 8 weeks. Max 30 students across all sites.
how_to_apply: Fill out the common Pathway Programs online application (REDCap). Pick your site: UChicago, UIC, UIUC, Northwestern downtown or Rush. Two people must send in forms for you. At least one must be a teacher or professor.
notes: No housing or ride is provided, so pick only sites you can reach. The application asks for your GPA and a transcript. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16. It refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

who_can_apply: High school students. The application shows which programs you are eligible for based on your current grade. Chicagoland students can choose to commute for Career Insight and Immersion.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for a profile, transcript, writing sample, supplement and one recommendation letter. It also needs a parent okay and the $75 fee. Test scores are not required. You may rank up to four program choices but can be admitted to one.
notes: Expensive, not a job. Apply by the priority deadline if you need financial aid. Aid is limited and first come, first served.

who_can_apply: The page says the program includes 25 neighborhood high school teens, run with After School Matters. The page does not list an age or school rule.
how_to_apply: Use the How to Apply link on the Youth Farm page (an online form). Questions: Aurea France, Manager of Education and Wellness, per the page.
notes: Run in partnership with After School Matters. Confirm ages, dates and pay before relying on this. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

who_can_apply: City of Chicago residents. The program covers ages 14 to 24, but most summer jobs are for ages 16 to 24 (14 and 15 year olds: see Chicagobility). Under 18 needs a parent or guardian consent form if offered a job.
how_to_apply: Complete the online Chicago Youth Works application (about 20 minutes, can be saved) plus any partner applications for jobs you choose. Online only. Partners contact applicants for interviews. More applicants than jobs, and you can accept only one position.
notes: The FAQ says youth 16 and older do not need a work permit. Some pages on the site are leftovers from old years, so trust the FAQ and the City press release for 2026. Questions: hotline 312-743-0208. Applicants with DACA need a Social Security number for City-funded jobs. Year-round Chicago Youth Service Corps (ages 16 to 24) is also part of this program.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 and 15 who live in Chicago. At least half of participants come from priority groups (for example youth with disabilities, English learners, youth in foster care or experiencing homelessness).
how_to_apply: Apply through the online Chicago Youth Works application. Youth under 18 need a parent or guardian consent form if offered a position. Partner agencies contact applicants directly.
notes: The Chicago Youth Works FAQ says youth under 16 may be required to have a work permit; Illinois law requires one for most under-16 jobs, issued through the school district or ISBE. Ask the program whether a stipend program needs one. The FAQ says the Chicago Housing Authority, After School Matters and DFSS each also have a limited number of slots for 14 and 15 year olds.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18. You must be at least 15 by the program start date (June 8 in 2026).
how_to_apply: Read the Volunteer Manual, pass the online volunteer assessment with at least 80 percent to unlock the application, then upload immunization records, photo ID copy, forms and the name of a non-family recommender. Steps may change for 2027.
notes: Mandatory training in early June with no make-up. Needs MMR, chickenpox, Tdap and current flu shot proof and willingness to get a TB blood test. The page also lists an Explorer career program (high school, no patient contact) that is being updated with no details yet, and a Youth Advisory Council for current and former patients ages 13 to 17.

who_can_apply: The CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers; the East Sacramento post page snippet says ages 15 to 21.
how_to_apply: See the CHP Explorer post locator and contact the East Sacramento post.
notes: The CHP site blocked WebFetch (403) and a browser tab loaded blank, so ages come from search results and are unconfirmed. CHP has other posts. Confirm age limits and meeting times with the post. See also California Highway Patrol Explorer Program for the statewide competition. Ages differ by source: the CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers, while the post page snippet says 15 to 21. Re-checked on 2026-10-09: the CHP post page returned HTTP 403 again, so it could not be read and the card stays snippet-only.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: Complete the Junior Volunteer Application, submit a school recommendation form from a teacher, counselor or administrator, interview, finish health screenings, pass the orientation quiz and attend the mandatory orientation.
notes: The hospital's general volunteer program is age 16 and up. Perks listed include free parking, a food voucher, a free uniform and a free TB test. The next cycle should be the December 30 spring deadline, but the page gives no year, so confirm.

who_can_apply: There is a separate application for ages 16 to 17. Animal care and docent roles are 18 and up. Animal care also needs 100 hours of earlier volunteering.
how_to_apply: Submit the 16-17 volunteer application. Then go to the next orientation. They tell you about it by email.
notes: The center does not take court-ordered community service right now. If you have questions, write to volunteers@thelivingcoast.org.

who_can_apply: Volunteer team applicants should be in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer team form linked on the 10x10 Teen Art Expo page when applications open. Teen artists (age and grade rules for artists are not stated) can submit art when submissions open in mid November 2026. Museum phone: 513-721-2787.
notes: The museum has other volunteer groups. They are docents, visitor service aides, REC volunteers and CAM Cruiser volunteers. The main volunteer page does not state ages for them. Ask the museum before applying to those.

who_can_apply: The Clubs are open to youth ages 5 to 18 across Greater Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky. All youth are welcome, with no income rules. The page does not give an age range for the teen Workforce Development program itself.
how_to_apply: Click Enroll Today on the Join the Clubs page (it goes to the Club portal), or contact your preferred Club for help with the application. After acceptance, families get any extra forms. Phone: 513-421-8909. Email: info@bgcgc.org. Main office: 1205 Dewey Ave., Cincinnati, OH 45205.
notes: Confirm first. The pages do not list teen ages, teen hours, or any teen jobs. No Junior Staff program is mentioned. Clubs are at Price Hill, Avondale, Eastgate and East Westwood in Ohio. They are at Newport and Covington in Kentucky. There is also a Western & Southern Workforce Development Center.

who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 15 and have finished 9th grade. Seniors still in high school in spring must use the high school application.
how_to_apply: Submit the application packet by the posted due date, then attend a parent information session, an in-person interview and an orientation. Medical screening and a background check are required.
notes: Competitive: only the highest scoring applicants are accepted. Volunteers must complete at least 80 percent of their scheduled shifts. The hospital does not arrange job shadowing or senior capstone hours through Volunteer Services.

who_can_apply: Lifeguards must be 15 or older, hold current American Red Cross Lifeguard Training/First Aid and CPR for the Professional Rescuer/AED certifications, and pass a water skills test. The page does not give an age for gate or pool monitors.
how_to_apply: Register for the required lifeguard course screening on the page, then apply to the open positions. Questions: CRC Aquatics, 513-357-7665.
notes: Lifeguards also attend pre-season and on-site pool training and pass an annual water skills review. Check the page for current screening dates. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

who_can_apply: Live in the City of Cincinnati or a surrounding community and be 14 to 24. A limited number of positions are for ages 14 and 15. Under 18, a parent or guardian signs the hiring forms; under 16 you need a work permit.
how_to_apply: Create a free account at governmentjobs.com, then apply to the Y2WK job at agency.governmentjobs.com/cincinnati. Only online applications are accepted. Applicants are contacted by phone or email for an interview.
notes: Very competitive: WVXU reported more than 1,000 teens applied last year and about 6 percent were hired. The CRC page says ages 14 to 24 and residents of the city or surrounding communities; an older City HR FAQ says only City residents ages 14 to 18, so confirm. The CRC FAQ still lists 2019 start dates, so ignore those. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. Adults can volunteer too. Groups of 10 or more can volunteer together. Great Parks supports Eagle Scout, Gold Award and senior capstone projects.
how_to_apply: Watch the Great Parks volunteer page for the March 2027 information sessions and use the Email Volunteer Engagement link on that page to ask about the teen steps. The page does not show a teen application link. Group projects use the Request a Project Match form.
notes: Confirm first: the page gives no teen application steps or time commitment. Great Parks also lists one day volunteer projects; the page read did not state a minimum age for them.

who_can_apply: Age 12 or older, able to commit to an ongoing schedule of 2 to 6 hours a week for three months or longer. A background check applies at age 18 and older. Court-mandated volunteers are not accepted.
how_to_apply: Fill in an application in the library's online volunteer system and pick a listing. Questions: 513-369-6968.
notes: Each branch listing sets its own details, so check the age on the listing you choose. The page also mentions meal-service and tutoring roles. It lists a separate Friends of the Library volunteer line at 513-369-6035.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18, from public, private, parochial, charter and homeschool backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Use the youth application link on the Youth Programs page when recruitment opens. Email youthprograms@cincymuseum.org to be notified.
notes: The program started in 1989. In the first summer teens shadow the Museum of Natural History and Science, The Children's Museum and the Cincinnati History Museum.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18. The page says the program helps students meet service hour requirements for high school graduation and honor societies. Leader in Training is for ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Volunteer Application linked on the Youth Volunteer Opportunities page when recruiting reopens. Questions: volunteer@cincynature.org or (513) 965-3348. The youth opportunities page lists the main phone as (513) 831-1711.
notes: The pages read do not give the street address. Check the Nature Center site for the location. Group service days, including for local high schools, remove invasive plants. The youth opportunities page we read says ages 13 to 18 may apply. It did not repeat the closed for 2026 wording. Check the status before you plan around it.

who_can_apply: High school students.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Groundwork ORV Green Team page. Contact info@groundworkorv.org or 513-301-0310.
notes: Work sites named by the City include Mt. Echo Park, Mt. Airy Forest, Mt. Storm, Caldwell Nature Preserve and Kennedy Heights Park. Pay, hours and the application window are not on the pages, so ask Groundwork ORV. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

who_can_apply: High school and college students ages 15 and older. The page does not list grade levels.
how_to_apply: Email one message to job_shadows@trihealth.com. Include these items. The Job Shadow Instructions. Your Application. The Risk and Release form. The Authorization to Treat Minors form. Your immunization records. The team does not match you to a department. Look at TriHealth's services and locations first.
notes: The TriHealth volunteer page says Good Samaritan and Bethesda North hospitals use adult and teen volunteers. It does not give a teen age or steps. Email volunteer@trihealth.com or call 513-862-2368 to ask. The job shadowing page does not mention a background check.

who_can_apply: High school students from rising 9th grade through rising 12th grade who like technology. In person camp only, and only domestic students are accepted right now.
how_to_apply: Use the Register Here link on the Early IT Summer Camp page. Tell them in your application if cost or lack of resources could keep you from taking part. Questions: ucearlyit@ucmail.uc.edu. There is a parent or guardian orientation on Zoom.
notes: Drop off is at Teacher-Dyer Complex, Room 160 (University Circle), between 8:30 and 10 a.m. with pick up 4:00 to 4:30 p.m. The FAQ says the camp runs over two weeks in one answer and the page says three weeks, so confirm the length.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors who are 16 or older by August 1 of the program year (in 2026 that date was August 1, 2026). Previous research experience is not required.
how_to_apply: Send in the online application form. You also upload a 1 page resume style summary of your school work and activities. You upload a 1 page personal statement. You rank the session you prefer. Contact: Michele Glassmeyer, Michele.Glassmeyer@uc.edu, (513) 558-6351.
notes: Costs money. The price, session dates and age cutoff above are from the 2026 page and may change for 2027.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17. The page words the age rule as 13 to 17 on May 1, 2026, which looks like a leftover date for a 2027 season, so confirm.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application with essays, attend one group interview and two orientations, and set up an online profile to log hours.
notes: Orientation 1 is an online course with a guardian plus a session on April 24 or 25, 2027; Orientation 2 is all day at the Zoo on May 22 or 23, 2027. The Zoo says to contact them if the fee is a hardship. Third-year and older ZooTeens have a lower 70 hour requirement.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 to 18 (the page is titled 'Become a Cadet (Ages 12-18)'). The page says your local squadron can answer eligibility questions.
how_to_apply: Find a local squadron. Contact it and visit with a parent. Go to about three meetings. Then apply. You can apply online if your squadron commander says you are eligible, or by mail or fax. Contact: pao@cawgcap.org.
notes: Prices on the California Wing cost page are from 2021 and 2022. Ask your squadron for current amounts. The Northern California Bay Area squadrons are listed on the wing site. The cost page says you must go to encampment to advance to Cadet Second Lieutenant.

who_can_apply: Youth at least 12 and not yet 19. U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters may waive for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Visit a squadron and attend at least three weekly meetings first.
how_to_apply: Find a local squadron with the Georgia Wing locator. Contact it and visit with a parent. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the application, or ask if you can apply online. Wing office: 770-428-9031, publicaffairs@gawg.cap.gov.
notes: The Georgia Wing page says cadets are not obligated to join the military. The national page lists military obligation for cadets as none. Dues vary by location and the national page says $25 to $50 per year, so ask your squadron for the exact amount. The Georgia Wing home page lists squadrons including Atlanta (GA109), Marietta, Roswell, Chamblee, Lawrenceville, Cumming and others.

who_can_apply: High school students at participating schools in 14 counties, including Sacramento and Yolo. Ask the FARMS coordinator at your school.
how_to_apply: Ask your ag or science teacher whether your school participates. Contact Mindy Cunha at mindy@landbasedlearning.org.
notes: Advanced FARMS tier (year-long research, job shadowing) also exists. Main office (530) 795-1520. CLBL headquarters is The Maples Farm in Woodland.

who_can_apply: Students at Luther Burbank High, Grant Union High and Sacramento Academic and Vocational Academy (SAVA).
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Ask a teacher or counselor at your host school, or contact the Center for Land-Based Learning: info@landbasedlearning.org or (530) 795-1520.
notes: Only at the three host schools. Grant Union students can earn college credit through a Sacramento State partnership (ACE program). Pay rate and hours per week are not posted. Paid job for a minor, so a work permit is likely needed.

who_can_apply: High school juniors. About 60 students are chosen for each class by the steering committee. The page lists no county or school rule.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps or link a form. Contact the Cobb Chamber: Katie Guice, 770-859-2334, kguice@cobbchamber.org.
notes: Costs money and is not a job. Ask about financial help. No application deadline is stated, so call early. The page says six evening programs but lists seven evening dates; the duration follows the dates.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21. You must be 14 and in high school to join. Need a 2.0 GPA or higher, a clean background check, physical fitness and good character. Gang or organized crime ties disqualify you.
how_to_apply: Go to three meetings in a row. Then pick up an application packet and turn in a detailed application. Last step is an oral interview with a panel of cadet officers and advisors.
notes: Meets at the Cobb County Police Training Academy, 2435 East-West Connector, Austell, GA 30106. Contact Officer Andy Higgins, (770) 528-8388. New members have a 6-month trial and get a uniform after 6 meetings in a row. Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Anyone 15 or older. People 18 and older must pass a background check first. The page does not say which roles teens can take.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Cobb County Public Library Volunteer Application. You can also contact the branch where you want to help to ask what openings it has.
notes: Library phone (770) 528-2326, contactus@cobbcat.org. Branches: East Cobb, Gritters, Kemp Memorial, Lewis A. Ray, Mountain View, North Cobb, Powder Springs, Sewell Mill, Sibley, South Cobb, Stratton, Sweetwater Valley, Switzer, Vinings, West Cobb.

who_can_apply: Cobb County School District juniors and seniors who are 16 or older. Your high school's Work-Based Learning coordinator can tell you the rules at your school.
how_to_apply: Apply through your high school's Work-Based Learning coordinator. All applications must be completed in full before they are considered. The district page lists a coordinator for each high school.
notes: District CTAE and WBL coordinator on the page: Sapph Espinoza. The job should relate to your career goals and CTAE coursework. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

who_can_apply: Cobb County residents ages 16 to 24 who meet income qualifications (decided at eligibility) and are in one of the program's target groups.
how_to_apply: Fill out the B.O.S.S. application inquiry form online (it asks if you live in Cobb County, are 16 to 24, and are in school), or call 770-528-4300 or email bossinfo@cobbworks.org.
notes: Funded through WIOA, so participants must meet eligibility rules. The same site lists a PowerUp! plumbing pre-apprenticeship and a Cobb County Fire P.R.E.P. Academy for young adults; ages are not stated, so ask CobbWorks. The main cobbworks.org site returned an error, so this entry uses worksourcecobb.org. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

who_can_apply: Concurrent enrollment: high school students in grades 9 to 12. Dual enrollment: students at CSM's partner high schools; talk to your school counselor.
how_to_apply: Create an OpenCCC account and apply to CSM online. For dual enrollment, meet with your high school counselor first, then register with the Dual Enrollment team. Questions: csmoutreach@smccd.edu.
notes: Dual enrollment is only through CSM's partner high schools. Concurrent enrollment is open to any high schooler but may need your counselor's approval at some schools. Skyline and Canada colleges run similar programs (not checked here).

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18, per the national Civil Air Patrol page. This is a composite squadron, which means it has both cadets and adult members.
how_to_apply: Email the squadron commander to ask about visiting a meeting with a parent. CAP's usual steps are listed on the Virginia and North Carolina wing pages. They are to go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the membership application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Squadron location: 6709 Corporal Frank Scott Drive, College Park, MD 20740. Commander listed on the page: Capt. Estelle Roche, estelle.roche@mdwg.cap.gov. The meeting time is from the squadron page; confirm before you go.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 and older. Spots are limited.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application link. Email megan.merchant@pgparks.com to ask how to apply before the March 1, 2027 deadline.
notes: Confirm first. The county page has no application link. It does not describe audition steps. Maryland Department of Labor says work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland. A permit is issued only after a job offer.

who_can_apply: Prince George's County residents ages 13 to 18. No grade is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It is free. It has a short essay and a piece of original artwork in your preferred genre, such as music, dance or visual arts. Contact: Shaiday Dancy, Teen Arts Specialist, 301-446-3252, shaiday.dancy@pgparks.com.
notes: Applicants could also be invited to be a Teen Arts Council ambassador. The stipend is not called a wage on the page. Paid work for people under 18 in Maryland needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=md for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 to 18 who pass the audition.
how_to_apply: Attend the audition on February 7, 2027 at 3 p.m. Questions go to megan.merchant@pgparks.com. The audition event page was not available when checked, so ask for audition details (what to prepare) by email.
notes: Maryland Department of Labor says work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland. A permit is issued only after the minor is offered a job. Confirm first. The page lists the audition but not what to prepare.

who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade in the fall. The page does not list a GPA or location rule.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with a one page personal statement. Email a recommendation from a STEM teacher and your official transcript to summerengr@umd.edu. Contact: Sandra Crespin Melgar, summerengr@umd.edu.
notes: Costs money. Price, dates and deadline above are from the 2026 page and may change for 2027.

who_can_apply: Students who go to high school in Maryland or Washington, D.C., or live there. You need a cumulative GPA of at least 3.5. You must show interest and skill in math, science or engineering.
how_to_apply: Online application with a one page personal statement (12 point, double spaced), an official high school transcript, and official PSAT or SAT scores if you have them. You must attend all sessions, orientation, and the pre and post tests. Contact: Ms. Aishah Briscoe, FutureEngineer@umd.edu.
notes: The page does not say whether the program is residential. Costs money but is low compared with most pre-college programs. Dates and the $400 price are from the 2026 page.

who_can_apply: Current 10th, 11th and 12th graders. You should be strong in school, like robotics and show initiative. You need a high school transcript and a resume to apply.
how_to_apply: Use the online application linked from the SPARC page (Apply Now). Include your high school transcript and resume. A parent or other authorized adult must sign you in and out each day. Contact: robotics-sparc@umd.edu.
notes: Very expensive and commuter only. Participation does not guarantee admission to UMD. The page banner says Apply Now with a December 1, 2026 deadline, but another line says applications for 'this summer' are closed, so confirm the application is open before you plan around it.

who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th graders who are thinking about majoring in engineering. The page says the programs are open to all students. Gender does not matter.
how_to_apply: The page gives no steps beyond saying the 2027 application opens in January 2027. Contact Jen Kuntz of the WIE Program at jakuntz@umd.edu or 301-405-0315. Scholarship and payment details are sent after admission decisions.
notes: Costs money. The program does not guarantee admission to UMD. Other UMD engineering pre-college programs are listed at https://eng.umd.edu/pre-college-programs/summer.

who_can_apply: Youth in or entering grades 6 to 12 who are at least 12 years old. High school students 18 or older must be returning to a traditional high school and may need a background check.
how_to_apply: Online VolunTeen application, first come first served by branch. If your branch is missing from the drop-down, it is full.
notes: Openings vary by branch. Current or recent youth volunteers should talk to the Summer Reading coordinator at their branch. The library also has School Help, Reading Buddies and Creation Station volunteer roles; the page lists the age rule only for the summer VolunTeen role. Ohio's work permit rules for unpaid public library volunteering are not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Most assignments are for ages 16 and up. Volunteers and Junior Volunteers ages 11 and over may help at Inniswood Metro Gardens; the Inniswood training is in March.
how_to_apply: Attend a Volunteer Information session and complete the volunteer application. A background check including fingerprints is part of the process.
notes: Slate Run Living Historical Farm lets children volunteer with a parent or supervising adult. Scouts can set up group service days by email. For Inniswood contact the volunteer coordinator at 614-895-6226.

who_can_apply: Columbus residents (or people who pay Columbus taxes) ages 14 to 23. Must pass a drug test; a background check applies at 18 and older. Required documents: birth certificate and/or Social Security card, plus a state or school photo ID.
how_to_apply: Apply during the winter application window listed on the program page. Questions: AJRP@columbus.gov or 614-724-2038.
notes: Work experiences vary and are matched to career interests where possible. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement. The page does not say how to submit the application beyond the schedule, so confirm the method with the program.

who_can_apply: City of Columbus residents (getting City trash and recycling service counts) entering grades 6 to 10 in Fall 2026 who keep a 2.8 GPA. Selected applicants interview with the program directors.
how_to_apply: Email the application, last school year's report card and a letter from a teacher, administrator or community leader to CBMcGhee@columbus.gov, or drop it at Blackburn Community Center (263 Carpenter St.). Selected applicants interview.
notes: Includes middle schoolers (grades 6 to 10). There is a mandatory guardian and youth orientation on Sept 19, 2026. You can miss no more than three meet-ups without an excuse. The page says applications began May 1, 2025. That looks like a typo for 2026.

who_can_apply: Age 15 or older with the swimming skills needed. Must finish the American Red Cross Lifeguard Training course (the City waives the course fee if you are hired). Completing the course does not guarantee a job.
how_to_apply: Submit the Lifeguard Interest Form, take the pre-course swimming skills test, finish the Red Cross course, then submit the employment application.
notes: The City also offers Red Cross lifeguard training classes for ages 15 and older. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement. The page is not dated, so check that hiring is open.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 19 (age range from the Urban League's Career Connect youth list). Other eligibility rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. The Youth Leadership Team is at 3443 Agler Rd., Columbus, phone 614-257-6300.
notes: Supported by the Franklin County Board of Commissioners and employer partners. A 2024 WRTU Fellows program began with 27 youth. The Urban League's other youth programs (for example I Am My Brother's Keeper, ages 14 to 18, and VLOG, ages 14 to 19) are listed on its Career Connect page. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

who_can_apply: Teens entering grades 8 to 12 who show leadership, animal knowledge, professionalism and emotional maturity.
how_to_apply: Online application posted on the Teen Volunteers page in early 2027.
notes: The page does not state the months, hours or any fee, so confirm with the Zoo. Season is listed as summer as a best fit but is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the CHM internships page to join the mailing list.
notes: CHM says it is not accepting Teen Program applications right now; the page gives no reopening date. Join the interest list to be told when it opens. Pay and length are not stated.

who_can_apply: Middle or high school students living in the US (citizenship not required). Solo or teams up to four. Half the team must live in the district.
how_to_apply: Register on the Student Registration page, then submit the app online.
notes: Any language or platform is allowed, solo or teams up to four. Check the Participating Districts page on the site to confirm your district takes part.

who_can_apply: Students at West Contra Costa USD, Leadership Public Schools, Griffin Technology Academies, or Middle College High School on campus. Requirements vary by school.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor. Questions: earlycollegecredit@contracosta.edu.
notes: Serves West Contra Costa County (Richmond, San Pablo). No deadlines are listed on the page.

who_can_apply: Summer Read: entering 8th grade or above, with parent consent. Computer Docent and Homework Help: age 16 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer interest form on ccclib.org/volunteer. You may be called for an interview. Forms stay on file for six months.
notes: Contact your branch to see if it is taking volunteers now.

who_can_apply: Students in the grades listed for each role.
how_to_apply: Click Apply for the role you want on the volunteer page. Questions about youth roles: Kevin, kwonch@cooklib.org. Questions about high school roles: Leah, lhotchkiss@cooklib.org.
notes: You need a library card for the adult volunteer jobs.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 and up. Accepted volunteers must attend three weekend training sessions.
how_to_apply: Online youth volunteer application during the August window, then an in-person interview (5:30 to 7:30 p.m.) at COSI.
notes: Candidates who cannot attend all three trainings are told to reapply later. COSI also lists one-day Quick Impact volunteer shifts; check each listing for its age rule.

who_can_apply: California high school students completing grades 8 to 12. Non-California residents and international students cannot apply. Selected on academic strength and interest in math and science. You pick one campus and cluster choices.
how_to_apply: Online application plus teacher recommendations and parent signature. Pay the application fee. If accepted, pay one-third by Apr 7, 2027 and the rest by Apr 16, 2027.
notes: Competitive. Residential, so you live on campus for four weeks. Financial aid is reviewed separately from admission and needs a parent income document; it has a hard deadline. Program session dates are listed as TBA. Pick UC Davis as your campus on the application. COSMOS runs on several UC campuses (UC Davis, UC Irvine, UC San Diego and UC Santa Cruz); this card is the Davis campus. See the UC COSMOS site for the others: https://jacobs.ucsd.edu/cosmos

who_can_apply: Students who have finished 8th grade. A parent must send a one-time consent form. Your high school principal signs the concurrent form.
how_to_apply: Apply online to OCC. Pick "Enrolling in High School and College at the same time." Then your parent sends in the consent form. You email the signed Concurrent Enrollment Form to dualenrollment@occ.cccd.edu. Only handwritten signatures count.
notes: The one-time parent consent form is also honored at Golden West College and Coastline College. After you graduate you must re-apply as a first-time college student. Help: fpr@occ.cccd.edu.

who_can_apply: The page does not state a minimum age. Ask the department before you apply, because lifeguard jobs and leader jobs often have different age rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the city's Parks and Community Services employment page.
notes: The city also runs free after-school teen centers for grades 7 to 12 and a Summer Teen Camp for grades 7 to 10, which are programs to attend, not jobs. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 (two separate groups).
how_to_apply: No steps are posted. Email MadisonLeeRosen@CosumnesCSD.gov, call the District at 916-405-5600, or fill out the General Volunteer Interest Form on cosumnescsd.gov.
notes: Meeting times, location and deadlines are not posted on the page, so ask the District. Other volunteer roles on that page (adaptive recreation, youth coaching) are 18 and older.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18, high school juniors and seniors, 2.0 GPA, and a physician-completed medical exam form.
how_to_apply: Email explorers@cosumnescsd.gov to get application details. Fire Admin phone: 916-405-7100.
notes: Serves the Elk Grove area. Needs a physician-completed medical exam form. Meeting schedule and any costs are not posted on the page.

who_can_apply: Chicago residents attending a Chicago high school or equivalent (graduating seniors can apply), ages 16 to 19 on the first day (June 22 in 2026), with a Social Security number or ITIN.
how_to_apply: Log in to Chicago Youth Works, finish that application, choose After School Matters under Opportunities, then search library positions (program name CPL or your branch) in the ASM application. Branch staff interview in May.
notes: Positions were offered at every Chicago Public Library location. You can apply to many branches but be hired for one. Work permit: Illinois requires one only for under 16 and the minimum age here is 16. Questions: teenservices@chipublib.org.

who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Chicago and attend a Chicago high school. Ages 14 to 19 on the start date of Jan 9, 2027. Teen Best Reads and Teen Media Lab are open to current 9th, 10th and 11th graders.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Chicago Public Library application form (not the After School Matters site). Answer the open-ended questions carefully; they decide who is interviewed. Virtual interview in Microsoft Teams for each program. Apply to as many as you like but accept one.
notes: You enroll with After School Matters during the first month, which needs a Social Security Number and parent or guardian information. Questions: teenservices@chipublib.org. Gamer's Guild sub-guilds meet at different library branches.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 and older. Some departments accept only people 18 and older. Junior volunteers under 18 need a signed parental consent form.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, then an in-person interview and a health screening. The background check applies to adults only. Questions go to cpmcvolunteer@sutterhealth.org.
notes: Read on the official Sutter Health listing 2026-10-07. Not stated on the listing: TB test or immunization requirements, application window, and pay (unpaid volunteer role). The health screening is required but its contents are not described on this listing. Sutter's separate CPMC student volunteer page could not be read from this environment, so no details from it are used here. The listing is a lobby role, so it fits teens 16 and older who want to try hospital volunteering; it is not a high school program.

who_can_apply: Chicago Public Schools students. 8th graders apply through GoCPS when they apply to high school; freshmen and 10th graders ask their school counselor.
how_to_apply: Rank CTE programs on your GoCPS high school application (8th grade), or talk to your counselor (9th and 10th grade). Email CTE@cps.edu for questions.
notes: Which pathways are offered differs by school; the CTE Matrix and Guide to CTE Programs on the page list them. CPS Work-Based Learning (internships, co-op) builds on these pathways. Contact: 773-553-2108.

who_can_apply: Current 10th and 11th graders at a district-run CPS school; priority goes to 10th graders. Must attend an information session and submit a recommendation from a trusted adult who is not a family member.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google application form, a signed Student and Parent Expectations and Consent Contract and a Recommendation Form, then email everything to ChicagoBuilds@cps.edu.
notes: It is an Illinois Works Pre-Apprenticeship site and offers the Master Builder program with City Colleges of Chicago. Classes meet during the school day in an AM or PM cohort. Contact: 773-534-0909.

who_can_apply: High school seniors at least 16 years old with a 2.0 GPA, excellent attendance and a counselor recommendation.
how_to_apply: Apply in 11th grade through your school; contact the citywide Cooperative Education coordinator (773-553-2108) for the process.
notes: Placement and training partners listed on the page include Genesys Works and Urban Alliance. Work permit: Illinois requires one only for under 16 and the minimum age is 16. Cutting school or work can cost credit.

who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled at a Chicago Public Schools high school, including home-schooled students per City Colleges. A 2.5 GPA and strong attendance are typical requirements. If your GPA is lower, the page says recommendation letters are accepted. Under 16 needs a principal recommendation and approval from the college president.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor, get approval from the dual enrollment coordinator at your City Colleges campus, complete the City Colleges application and pick classes. Do not pay for or enroll in a class before talking to the Early College team.
notes: Undocumented students are eligible (CPS page). Some courses need ACT, SAT or City Colleges placement scores; many courses have no prerequisites. Jumpstart Pathways and Runway 606 are related CPS options. Seven campuses; each has a dual enrollment coordinator.

who_can_apply: Sophomores who live in Chicago and attend a Chicago high school (public, private or homeschooled). A 2.3 GPA and 90% attendance are recommended. Needs 2 recommendation letters, a physical and a background check.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, a signed consent form, a copy of a school or state ID, 2 recommendation letters, a physical exam record and a background check.
notes: Takes up to 125 students each year. Contact: cpfta@cps.edu or 773-553-2486.

who_can_apply: California residents in grades 8 to 12. Up to 20 students from out of state and other countries may also be enrolled. Each department has its own assignments.
how_to_apply: Apply online by department. A full application has the form and two teacher references, not peers. It has an unofficial transcript and department assignments. It has the $20 fee. It has the financial aid request if you want aid. Students can apply to more than one department. Each needs a full application.
notes: Students who finish can get 3 units of college extension credit from the California State University system (per the FAQ). Not a job. The pages read did not name the 2027 campus, so check before planning travel.

who_can_apply: Students at NYC public high schools. Grade 11 and 12 with an 80+ GPA can take courses on the partner campus, and a 70+ GPA opens some courses. Grade 10 with a 70+ GPA can take non-credit college and career awareness courses only. College Now is geared toward NYC Public Schools 11th and 12th graders.
how_to_apply: Apply to a specific CUNY campus's College Now program. Talk to your school's College Now liaison if your school has a partner campus, or contact a campus program directly. Many programs are first come, first served.
