notes: Graduating seniors cannot join summer sessions. Students in Early College high schools can only join in summer. Costs beyond tuition (like textbooks) are not described on the CUNY page, so ask the campus.

who_can_apply: Cupertino residents who are incoming 8th to 11th graders. The city page says seniors are not eligible to apply.
how_to_apply: When recruitment is open, use the 'Apply to be a Teen Commissioner' form on the city page. The page also links a supplemental questions list. Questions about applications go to cityclerk@cupertino.gov.
notes: Meets monthly, September through May, at 6 p.m. on the second Wednesday. It meets in the Quinlan Community Center Conference Room (10185 North Stelling Road), with a teleconference option. Commission email teencommission@cupertino.gov. Staff liaison Sonya Lee, Recreation Manager, (408) 777-3121. Pay is not mentioned on the page, so it is listed as unpaid. The page says members may be in 12th grade during their term. The 8th-to-11th rule applies to applicants.

who_can_apply: Lifeguard Training: you must turn 15 by the last day of the course. Junior Lifeguarding: pass a swim skills check on day one (25 yards of front crawl and breaststroke, tread water 1 minute, and more). Junior Swim Instructor: no age or swim test listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Register for a course through City of Davis online registration (the page links to it). Questions: 530-757-5626 or csweb@cityofdavis.org.
notes: Training can lead to City of Davis aquatics work. Junior Swim Instructor is for teens who may want to work for Davis Aquatics later, with volunteer chances after the training. The page does not promise a job. Lifeguard certification needs full attendance and passing tests. Job minimum ages are set in each posting at cityofdavis.org/jobs.

who_can_apply: Age 15 or older to officiate or keep score, and 16 or older to coach. You need CPR and First Aid certification before the season starts and a working knowledge of basketball rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the City of Davis job page (NEOGOV). Applicants are screened on experience and may be interviewed.
notes: Temporary part-time with no benefits. Games are Saturdays at the Davis High School community gyms. Other City of Davis seasonal postings such as Parks Maintenance Aide (18 and older) and Pool Maintenance Aide (21 and older) are not open to teens.

who_can_apply: DJUSD high school students. The page does not list which schools offer which pathway. Ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Contact your school counselor to enroll in a CTE course. Internships are on the Student Internships tab. See the Internship and Career Development Course.
notes: Page does not say which schools offer which pathways, or give grade or age rules. DJUSD office: (530) 757-5300. Related: the Internship and Career Development Course and the Summer Apprenticeship.

who_can_apply: Davis teens ages 14 to 17. Up to 24 members. Needs a full school-year commitment.
how_to_apply: Fill out the TLC application on the Teens page. Questions: Micayla Valceschini, mvalceschini@cityofdavis.org.
notes: Meetings are at the Veterans Memorial Center, 203 E. 14th St. Up to 24 teens, and it is a full school-year commitment. The application closed Oct 2, so ask the city whether late applicants can still join.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in any California high school, grades 9 to 12 (rising 9th graders included). Needs permission from a parent or guardian and your school principal. No GPA requirement.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor, apply for admission, set up MyPortal, finish the Dual Enrollment overview, check prerequisites, submit the school permission form, then register. Questions: outreach@deanza.edu.
notes: Math and English classes need an assessment (usually based on your school transcript). Students can buy a VTA SmartPass for unlimited bus and light rail rides. Undocumented students can take part. Parents cannot see your college records without your written consent.

who_can_apply: High school students join through a school chapter and its advisor, or a school can start a chapter. Contact the DECA advisor at your school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school for a DECA advisor. DECA lists an Online Membership System for joining.
notes: DECA says it has about 317,600 high school members in 4,510 chapters. Not every school has a chapter. California-specific details were not on the page.

who_can_apply: DeKalb County youth ages 14 to 18 who are in school. You keep at least a C average and have good attendance and behavior.
how_to_apply: Get the DCFR Explorer application packet from the page. Send it in with 3 job references and your latest report card.
notes: Contact frexplorers@dekalbcountyga.gov. Not a paid job, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who live in DeKalb County.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application steps; check the library's Teens Get Involved page and volunteer page for the next cycle.
notes: Meeting dates were listed as coming soon. Members can miss a meeting by telling advisors through Slack or the pre-meeting survey. A search result also described a separate Teen Library Board Trustee seat, but that was not on the page read.

who_can_apply: Volunteers ages 16 and older. Adult volunteers also need a background check. The page does not list any other rule for teens.
how_to_apply: There are four steps. Fill out the Volunteer Application. Sign the Volunteer Waiver. Go to a short orientation, online or in person. Then start.
notes: Call 404-294-2838 or write to Monique Larkin at mllarkin@dekalbcountyga.gov. The page gives no direct link to the application. Other park volunteering lists no minimum age. Examples are clean-up days and nature programs.

who_can_apply: DeKalb County School District students, mostly juniors and seniors. You need a parent or guardian OK and at least a 2.0 GPA. You must be on track to graduate. You cannot have had any suspensions this year or last year. You need good attendance: 15 or fewer unexcused absences and tardies in both years.
how_to_apply: Apply to your school's WBL coordinator. The coordinator approves students based on grades, behavior and attendance. You must have room in your schedule. Your family must give you rides to the job. Students who do not meet the rules may qualify for the Great Promise Partnership WBL. Ask your coordinator.
notes: Only for DeKalb schools students. You must leave campus at the start of your first WBL class, even on days you are not scheduled to work. The district CTAE office is at 1701 Mountain Industrial Blvd, Stone Mountain, GA 30083.

who_can_apply: 2025 rules: DeKalb County residents ages 16 to 21 who pass a drug screening and background check. Interns were picked by random lottery.
how_to_apply: In 2025, online registration at dekalbcountyga.gov/dsyep. That address now leads to a registration form marked no longer active. For help the 2025 county release listed the Workforce Development Manager at (470) 572-8229.
notes: Confirm that a new cycle exists before planning around it. All dates, pay and rules here are from the 2025 county release. WorkSource DeKalb also lists youth ages 16 to 24 with barriers as a service group. It sends people to ATLworks.org to check eligibility. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18. If you are 14, you can start the application one month before your 15th birthday.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application for a role. The roles are Exhibit Host, Team Spark and Team Celebration. Email a resume and a letter from an adult who is not family. Send them to VolunteerLA@discoverycube.org. Then do an interview and a mandatory orientation.
notes: The museum is in Sylmar in the San Fernando Valley. The letter of recommendation cannot come from a family member. Questions: 818-686-2835.

who_can_apply: The page gives one age rule: if you are 14, you may start the application process one month before your 15th birthday. No grade level is stated.
how_to_apply: Online application form, a resume, a letter of recommendation, then an interview. The full application must be in before an interview is scheduled.
notes: Plan for the 60-hour minimum if you need verified service hours. Location: 2500 N Main Street, Santa Ana, CA 92705. Questions: volunteeroc@discoverycube.org.

who_can_apply: Davis Joint Unified high school students. Some sites have priority rules (Dignity Health for Patient Care pathway students; Ford ACE for Transportation pathway students).
how_to_apply: Talk to your counselor or contact Internship Specialist Alexha Contreras (alcontreras@djusd.net, 530-757-5400 x170).
notes: Many other 2026-27 host sites are listed on the page; some have priority rules (Mercy General: Patient Care pathway students; Ford ACE: Transportation pathway students). Credit needs weekly meetings, an evaluation and a reflection. The page is written for DJUSD students.

who_can_apply: Camp volunteers and general program volunteers must be at least 14 years old. Other roles do not list an age on the page. Everyone fills out a volunteer waiver. The page says teens to seniors can volunteer.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Lyman Woods application for the role you want. Also fill out the volunteer waiver. Program and camp volunteers send in an application and go to an interview and training. A criminal background check is only for program volunteers 18 or older.
notes: REAP restoration workdays need an RSVP. The park district also runs Counselor in Training (C.I.T.) camps for teens. They have a sign-up fee. The pages read did not list ages or the fee amount.

who_can_apply: Teens entering 7th grade or higher. Complete the online application; staff review it and then tell you how to register. The page lists separate fees for Dublin residents and non-residents.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application when it is open (closed for 2026). Staff review it and then tell you how to register at dublinrecguide.com. Questions: Dublin.Lead@dublin.ca.gov.
notes: This is a fee-based training and volunteer-style program run by the city, not a paid job. Families pay the registration fee; the city page does not say teens are paid. The page does not name a residency rule for applying. Shifts are not pre-assigned; participants pick their own shifts in the registration system.

who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Dublin and be enrolled in middle or high school (committee bylaws). The committee has 13 members and 3 alternates; at least 6 members must be high school students.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the city page we read. Call Parks and Community Services at 925-556-4500 or use the contact link on the committee page to ask when the next recruitment opens.
notes: Meets 7:00 pm, second Wednesday of the month, Dublin Senior Center, 7600 Amador Valley Blvd; July and August meet only as needed. Bylaws say members must stay enrolled in middle or high school, and a member is removed if they stop living in Dublin or stop being enrolled. Older (2020 and 2021) notices mention late-winter recruitment; that is last-cycle information and was not confirmed for 2027. Teens who want a seat should check the city page each spring.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors in 2026-27 who are at least 15 by June 1, 2027 and from the Research Triangle area. Needs a Social Security Number or ITIN to receive the stipend. Students must provide their own transportation.
how_to_apply: Online application plus a recommendation letter (links on the CeBA page). Applicants hear back in mid-April.
notes: The 2026 deadline is stated two ways. It is March 20 on the flyer and March 27 in the FAQ. The page says there is no housing or transportation help, so only local students are considered. The $2,400 is a completion award. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: High school students who are 16 or 17 (16 by June 24 in 2026). Students must attend both days at one site. Space is limited to 25 slots at each site.
how_to_apply: Student completes the online application and a parent or guardian completes the Participation Agreement (both on Qualtrics links on the page). No late or incomplete submissions.
notes: Both Duke pages are titled Junior Volunteer Program but describe this event for 2026. The application window was only 3 days, so watch the page in early April. Questions: DRHVolunteerServices@dm.duke.edu (Durham) or DRAH_VolunteerServices@dm.duke.edu (Raleigh). Duke University Hospital says it no longer offers a junior volunteer program for high school students.

who_can_apply: Durham City or Durham County residents between 14 and 24 as of June 30, 2026, per the Duke page. The Duke article describes participants as Durham-area high school students.
how_to_apply: Submit the Durham YouthWorks application and select the healthcare category (link on the Duke Community Affairs page). Contact: Kimberly Monroe, kimberly.monroe@duke.edu.
notes: Applications go through Durham YouthWorks (City of Durham), whose own page could not be read (blocked). The article says about 50 students were planned for the latest class. North Carolina requires a Youth Employment Certificate for anyone under 18 who works; the employer starts that process.

who_can_apply: High school students in current grades 9 to 12 who are at least 14 to attend. (The page also lists middle school programs for grades 6-8.)
how_to_apply: Join the information request list on the Duke Pre-College page to be told when 2027 dates and courses open.
notes: Courses, session dates and fees for Summer 2027 were not posted on 2026-10-09. Check back after the October 2026 announcement.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 and up at Dunwoody Nature Center (15 and up at Island Ford). Be mature, reliable, flexible and energetic. You must attend a pre-camp orientation, in person the first time.
how_to_apply: Write to the Junior Counselor Coordinator. Ask how to join and what the steps are. The email is juniorcounselors@dunwoodynature.org.
notes: Phone 770-394-3322, info@dunwoodynature.org. The first email link on the page goes to a different address, so use the one in the FAQ (juniorcounselors@dunwoodynature.org). Camp dates are not listed on the page. Unpaid, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Teen and adult volunteers: age 14 or entering high school. Junior volunteers: junior high school students.
how_to_apply: Junior volunteers fill out the online application, permission form and photo release. Teen and adult volunteers check openings on the museum volunteer page. They can also call Jessica Greenlaw at 630-637-8000 ext. 4640. You get a 2 hour training.
notes: Experience with kids is helpful but not required. Summer teen volunteering is not mentioned on the page, so ask. The minimum age for the junior program is not given, only junior high.

who_can_apply: One-time community events: ages 8 and up with an adult. Long-term roles are generally 18 and up, with limited openings for ages 13 to 17. Family roles are ages 10 and up with an adult.
how_to_apply: For long-term roles, apply online through the volunteer portal. Then meet with program staff for an interview. After that, go to orientation and training. For one-time restoration workdays, find a date on the events calendar and register.
notes: Getting started for a long-term role takes about 2 to 3 months. The FAQ page says background checks apply to people 16 and older in one place and 18 and older in another. Ask the Volunteer Services office what applies to you. Call 630-933-7233 or write to volunteer@dupageforest.org. The page does not list which long-term roles take people under 18.

who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 13, or have a guardian's permission to fill out the form. The form lets you pick the age group you want to work with, including teens 13 to 18.
how_to_apply: Complete the online volunteer form (skills, preferred age group, days and times, hours per week, emergency contact). Questions: Maker_STEAM@dconc.gov.
notes: Days offered are Monday to Saturday. Time options are morning, afternoon or evening. The page does not describe a teen-only volunteer track.

who_can_apply: The For Teens page says the program is for all tweens and teens in grades 6 to 12. The general volunteer page says all volunteers must be 14 or older.
how_to_apply: Contact the teen librarian at your preferred branch. The general volunteer page also says to fill out the volunteer application form (PDF) and bring it to your nearest library.
notes: The two Durham County Library pages disagree on age: the teen page says grades 6 to 12, the general volunteer page says 14 or older. Ask the teen librarian which applies. The library says it cannot currently host court-mandated community service hours.

who_can_apply: Not stated.
how_to_apply: The home page has a Sign Up button for volunteers, but the volunteer page it links to showed a 404 error on 2026-10-09. Contact EBAYC directly (offices in Oakland and Sacramento are listed on the home page).
notes: Read the home page on 2026-10-09. It says EBAYC has many volunteer opportunities and welcomes volunteer groups and student internships, but it gives no ages, dates or pay. The volunteer page linked from it (ebayc.org/volunteer/) returned a 404 error on Oct 7 and again on Oct 9, 2026. Confirm the minimum age with EBAYC.

who_can_apply: High school students in the EBMUD service area. For 2026 the East Bay program took students referred by partner groups. The Maintenance track (Stockton) required age 16 by June 24, 2026.
how_to_apply: In 2026 you could not apply to EBMUD directly for the East Bay program. Ask a partner to refer you: ACE Mentor, Biotech Partners, Eden Area ROP, Girls Inc. of Alameda County, Youth UpRising. Email internships@ebmud.com, (510) 287-0710.
notes: Referral only in 2026. Separate Mokelumne programs (Fisheries in Lodi, Ranger in Valley Springs, Maintenance in Stockton) ran in 2026 with rolling review.

who_can_apply: Gate Attendant (high school pathway): at least 16 and completed 10th grade. Other jobs have their own rules; check each posting.
how_to_apply: Apply on governmentjobs.com/careers/ebparks. HR: (510) 544-2154.
notes: The 16 minimum is from the Gate Attendant page; other roles (for example lifeguard) may differ. The park district says it hires hundreds of seasonal students each year.

who_can_apply: Students at participating schools: U-46 (Bartlett, Elgin, Larkin, South Elgin, Streamwood), District 300 (Dundee-Crown, Hampshire, Jacobs), District 301 (Burlington Central), District 303 (St. Charles East, St. Charles North, Compass Academy), Cambridge Lakes Charter and St. Edward Central Catholic. The tracks are for juniors, seniors, or juniors and seniors, depending on the track. Talk with your counselor.
how_to_apply: Talk with your parents and your high school counselor first, then use the online Dual Credit application (Apply Now). Independent enrollment also needs approval from the ECC Dual Credit office. Contact: DualCredit@elgin.edu or 847-214-7887.
notes: Accelerate College students may need to qualify for college-level courses and testing may be required. Each district publishes a Dual Credit Guide listing what its schools support. The ECC page also lists Upward Bound, Educational Talent Search and College and Career Readiness workshops.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 at certain schools. The middle schools are Abbott, Ellis, Kimball, Larsen, Carpentersville, Canton and Tefft. The high schools are Elgin, Larkin, Streamwood and Dundee-Crown. You must be a US citizen or permanent resident. You must show money need or be a possible first-generation college student.
how_to_apply: Send in the Talent Search application with your papers. You can do this online, by email to talentsearchtransition@elgin.edu, by mail or by fax. You can also get a paper copy from your school counselor. A guardian helps if you are under 18.
notes: Contact: 847-214-7764, Building K Room K102, 1700 Spartan Drive, Elgin. Only the schools named above are served.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at Dundee-Crown, Larkin or Streamwood High School who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents and are either potential first-generation college students or from a low-income household (U.S. Department of Education rules). If unsure, apply and staff will tell you if you qualify.
how_to_apply: Student and parent or guardian complete the online Upward Bound application. Counselors and teachers can fill out the Student Recommendation Form. Contact: upwardbound@elgin.edu, 847-214-7253, Building K, Room K102, 1700 Spartan Drive, Elgin.
notes: Only for students at the three listed high schools. The page does not mention a summer part or a start date, so ask staff. A web search snippet suggested Elgin High School is also served, but the ECC page itself lists only the three above.

who_can_apply: Berkeley residents ages 15 to 24, recruited through Berkeley YouthWorks.
how_to_apply: Apply through the City of Berkeley YouthWorks interest form (the Ecology Center sends you there). Contact alex@ecologycenter.org or 510-697-4808.
notes: Berkeley residents only. YouthWorks asks for an interest form and a 15 to 20 minute interview. Pay rate and exact academy dates are not posted.

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors attending high school in the Castro Valley, Hayward, San Leandro or San Lorenzo Unified school districts.
how_to_apply: Ask your home high school counselor to contact the Eden Area ROP career counselor at (510) 293-2973. Main office (510) 293-2900.
notes: Center is at 26316 Hesperian Blvd, Hayward. Cost, pay and ages are not stated on the page. Some pathways are offered only at certain high schools. Students outside the four districts are not listed as eligible. Work-based learning is mentioned (for example in education careers) but no formal internship structure is described.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 10 to 12 who are at least 15 years old.
how_to_apply: Download the application and email it to k12partnerships@middlesexcollege.edu, or call 732-906-2554 to schedule a virtual appointment.
notes: Separate Dual Enrollment: in participating districts, college courses are taught at the high school. Ask your counselor.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Registration required.
how_to_apply: Register on the library event listing (registration required). Meetings alternate between the Main Library and the North Edison Branch; members may attend at either. Main Library: 340 Plainfield Avenue, Edison, 732-287-2298.
notes: The page I read did not print a year for the October 14 session, and the library's own Young Adults page had no volunteer details. Confirm the meeting location when you register.

who_can_apply: Qualified students in grades 9 to 12 who can benefit from college classes. No age rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Do the Steps for Dual Enrollment each term you want to register. The steps are listed on a separate page. Call 310-660-3344 or email dualenrollment@elcamino.edu.
notes: Unit limits are not on this page. Dual enrollment uses Remind to post updates for students.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older and done with 8th grade. One-year minimum. Competitive, with limited spots. No summer-only option.
how_to_apply: Attend the annual application seminar, then apply. Info on the El Camino Health junior volunteer page.
notes: Hospital does not offer summer-only or programs shorter than one year. Locations are Mountain View and Los Gatos. Spots are limited (earlier check).

who_can_apply: Youth interested in the fire service. The page does not list an age range or other rules. Ask the coordinator.
how_to_apply: Go to any meeting on the schedule. Or ask the coordinator for an application. You can write to efdexplorers439@cityofelgin.org. You can also call 847-931-6175.
notes: The page says the program is very physical. Age limits are not on the page, so call before you go.

who_can_apply: Individuals, families and groups, including school and youth groups. No minimum age is listed. Volunteers 18 and younger need a parent or guardian to sign the waiver.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer preferences form and sign the waiver (a parent signs if you are 18 or younger). Questions: david.schoenknecht@elginil.gov or 847-531-7055.
notes: Wear long pants and closed toe shoes. Because no minimum age is listed, call to ask if there is one for your role.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 up to under 21. You live in Elgin or a nearby town and go to a local school. You have a C average or better. You have no past arrests or felony convictions. Special cases are reviewed one at a time. Boys and girls are welcome.
how_to_apply: Fill out and sign the application packet. It has the application, terms and a liability waiver. Then pass a background check and an oral interview.
notes: The program is linked to Boy Scouts of America. Boys and girls are welcome. The page says it serves youth in Elgin and nearby towns.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 19.
how_to_apply: Watch the event calendar and social media for each month's plan, then show up.
notes: Short page. It does not say how to sign up, where events happen or if there is a cost.

who_can_apply: Students in grade 6 and up can ask to volunteer or do community service hours. The Junior Teen Advisory Group is for grades 6 to 8.
how_to_apply: Contact Adelaide Rowe, arowe@egvpl.org, (847) 439-0447 ext. 252 about volunteering. For Jr. TAG, use the Apply Online link on the page or contact Tammy Wulf, twulf@egvpl.org, ext. 248.
notes: The page does not describe a program for older teens. It only lists volunteering and the Reading Program.

who_can_apply: Youth appointed by the Mayor with City Council approval (10 voting seats). The page does not list ages or grades. A city factsheet in search results reportedly said ages 13 to 18, grades 7 to 12, but that is unconfirmed. The City tries to balance seats by school and council district.
how_to_apply: When a seat opens, use the Apply to the Youth Commission link (City Clerk vacancies page). Questions: youthcommission@elkgrove.gov or (916) 627-3254.
notes: Age and grade rules were not on the pages read, so confirm with the City before applying. Appointed seats, so competitive. Sign up for vacancy emails on elkgrove.gov to hear when a recruitment opens. Re-checked on 2026-10-09: the City page returned HTTP 403, so it could not be read again and the card stays snippet-only.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18 as of June 1 of the program year (June 1, 2026 on the current page).
how_to_apply: Create a MyImpact account and complete the application, with student and parent signatures on four forms. Get a recommendation from a teacher or school counselor by the deadline and rank up to three hospital locations. Interview, health screening and orientation follow.
notes: The window was only 10 days in 2026, so watch for the 2027 posting in early 2027. Space is limited and waitlists happen. Health screening includes a TB test and proof of chickenpox and measles immunity. No shadowing, internships or clinical hours.

who_can_apply: High school students; the page says it serves current sophomores and juniors. Application needs transcript and recommendations.
how_to_apply: Choose a program and course, review costs, then start the online application (transcript, recommendations, $70 fee). After acceptance, complete the pre-arrival checklist and pay the $350 enrollment deposit.
notes: Expensive. The nearest deadline is the Pre-Med Institute on Feb 1, 2027 (deadline_iso shows the main May 3 date). Financial aid deadline was May 1 in 2026. Information sessions are in November and December 2026.

who_can_apply: At least 16 by the start date (June 8 in 2026) and a rising or graduating senior. In-person spots need U.S. citizenship or permanent residency; others may apply to a virtual-only option. You can live anywhere in the U.S., but there is no housing.
how_to_apply: Apply in the Summer Scholars application portal. Two teacher recommendation letters are required, and one must be from a STEM teacher. You cannot submit until both are in. You cannot edit after you submit. An unofficial transcript is fine.
notes: Competitive. Parents or guardians handle off-campus housing and care for students under 18. Dates shown are from the 2026 page. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit is required for minors under 16; this program starts at 16.

who_can_apply: High school students. Endeavor Health says most roles are for age 16 and up, but age 14 and up at Edward and Elmhurst hospitals. Health screening and orientation are required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Student application. The hospital will contact the people it picks about next steps. If you have questions, call Volunteer Services at 630-527-3034.
notes: Hours per week and the length of service are not on the pages read. Ask Volunteer Services. Background checks are only for ages 18 and up.

who_can_apply: High school students. Endeavor Health says most roles are for age 16 and up, but age 14 and up at Edward and Elmhurst hospitals. Health screening and orientation are required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen application. If the site has problems, call 331-221-3282.
notes: The Elmhurst application page had no hours or length details, so ask the volunteer office. Background checks are only for ages 18 and up.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17. A parent or guardian must know about the commitment. You must pass the health screening and complete online orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen application. You then need online orientation and the health requirements from Endeavor Health Employee Health. Getting an assignment is not guaranteed.
notes: Endeavor Health's main page says most roles need age 16 or older and a background check is only for ages 18 and up. Apply early and check back for summer openings.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17. A parent or guardian must know about the commitment. You must pass the health screening and complete online orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen application. You then need online orientation and the health requirements from Endeavor Health Employee Health. Getting an assignment is not guaranteed.
notes: Endeavor Health's main page says most roles need age 16 or older and a background check is only for ages 18 and up. Apply early and check back for summer openings.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17. A parent or guardian must know about the commitment. You must pass the health screening and complete online orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen application. You then need online orientation and the health requirements from Endeavor Health Employee Health. Getting an assignment is not guaranteed.
notes: Endeavor Health's main page says most roles need age 16 or older and a background check is only for ages 18 and up. Apply early and check back for summer openings.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. A parent or guardian must know about the commitment.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online High School Volunteer application. Plan on one 30 minute sitting. Then you do an interest interview and a volunteer orientation. You may need a background check. You must also meet the health rules.
notes: The form cannot be saved and finished later.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17. A parent or guardian must know about the commitment. You must pass the health screening and complete online orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen application. You then need online orientation and the health requirements from Endeavor Health Employee Health. Getting an assignment is not guaranteed.
notes: Endeavor Health's main page says most roles need age 16 or older and a background check is only for ages 18 and up. Apply early and check back for summer openings.

who_can_apply: Local teens. The page does not give an age range or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Get the application PDF on the page, or pick one up at the Youth Services Desk on the 2nd floor. When it is done, email the form to teens@escondidolibrary.org.
notes: Phone for the Teen Services Librarian: 760-839-4283.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14. Volunteers need fingerprinting and a background check. Review Crew and Teen Advisory Board members do not need them. You must have an interview with the Volunteer Coordinator. The library does not accept court-ordered community service.
how_to_apply: Go to the City of Escondido volunteer website. Fill out the application there. You can call or email the City Community Engagement Liaison with questions. The number is 760-839-4523.
notes: Some roles on the page are for adults only. They are shelver, Friends shop and literacy tutor. The Review Crew and Teen Advisory Board do not need fingerprinting or a background check.

who_can_apply: Evanston or Chicago-area high school students who love art. You can come to meetings on Wednesdays from 5:00 to 6:30 p.m.
how_to_apply: Apply. Then do a short interview, take a tour of the art center and meet current members. To ask about the current application, contact Catie Bryant at cbryant@evanstonartcenter.org.
notes: The page has no closing date, and its board photo is captioned 2023-24. Email before you plan around it.

who_can_apply: Mainly under-resourced high school students and community members. The city workforce page says ages 17 and older. The ASPIRE page does not list exact rules, so email to ask.
how_to_apply: Write to aspire@cityofevanston.org and ask how to join. The workforce page also has a Workforce Division Engagement Form.
notes: Started in 2022. The page says 260 participants, including high school students, have taken part. It is a partnership with Evanston Township High School, so ask your school counselor too.

who_can_apply: Students at Evanston Township High School. The page is written for ETHS students.
how_to_apply: Talk to the Early College and Career Experiences office in Room W220. Contact Abronia Young. Call 847-424-7735 or write to younga@eths202.org. You can also call the post-secondary counselor, Michelle Vazquez, at 847-424-7163.
notes: ETHS also has a Work Permits page. It says Illinois law requires minors under 16 to get a work permit before working. Permits are by appointment only, and students aged 14 to 15 in school-approved work-based learning programs do not need one.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18 who live inside Evanston Township High School District 202.
how_to_apply: Register online ahead of time for the winter job fair, then meet employers there. Employers use a separate job request form.
notes: Illinois law says workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate), per the Evanston Township High School work permit page. The page says the program began in 1992 and last year over 40 employers offered over 300 jobs. Pay and exact summer dates are not on the page. The registration link is the 2026 form; look for a 2027 form around winter.

who_can_apply: California students without a high school diploma or GED, with approval from your school counselor or principal. Adult school students in GED programs can also join.
how_to_apply: Submit the dual enrollment application, get your high school counselor or principal to approve, then enroll. Counseling: mycounselor@evc.edu, 408-270-6475.
notes: CCAP classes are closed cohort classes held at partner high schools, so ask your school if it has an agreement. The page does not state a grade or age rule. Textbook costs for non-CCAP students are not stated.

who_can_apply: 11th graders at high schools that EXP supports. The 2025-2026 list includes Carson, Gardena, Lawndale, San Pedro, Phineas Banning and Sato Academy. It also lists some Long Beach schools: Cabrillo, Jordan, Lakewood, Long Beach Poly and Wilson. Some schools in Orange County and Barstow are listed too.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply to the Port directly; placement goes through EXP. Ask your school counselor if your school is an EXP school, or email internship@expfuture.org.
notes: Only for students at partner schools. Phone: 424.368.7100. The Port of Los Angeles Summer Internship (10 weeks, paid) is college students only. The page does not mention work permits. California requires a permit for paid work under 18.

who_can_apply: The site lists Posts for ages 14 to 20 (and Clubs for ages 10 to 14). Whether you must be a Scout was not stated. Find a unit through the Council Locator.
how_to_apply: Use the Council Locator on exploring.org or joinexploring.org to find a unit near you.
notes: Exploring.org was only readable in part; fees, Scouting membership rules and California posts were not listed. The page names Learning for Life Corporation in its copyright line. apply_url is the joinexploring.org home page, which has an Enter ZIP Code box for Exploring posts and clubs near you. On exploring.org, the Council Locator heading links to the contact page, and the scouting.org Local Council Locator finds a council, not a unit.

who_can_apply: Local high school students. Past interns came from Davis Senior High, Dixon High and Natomas Pacific Pathways Prep.
how_to_apply: No application process is posted. Use the contact page on the Facciotti Lab site to email the lab with a short note about your interests.
notes: Informal opportunity with no posted process, pay, dates or contact on that page. The lab names a partner teacher at Davis Senior High and lists one current intern, so openings may be rare.

who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 15 at the start of the course. Must pass the lifeguard course and its swim prerequisites (swim 100 yards, retrieve a 10-pound brick, tread water without hands for one minute) and a criminal background check. No prior certification needed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form on the Park Authority Aquatic Certification page, then interview. Questions: FCPAJOBS@Fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: Employment is contingent on passing the course. Virginia rule (Virginia Department of Labor and Industry): 14 and 15 year olds need an Employment Certificate before working; the page read does not list a certificate for 16 and 17 year olds.

who_can_apply: The library's volunteer guide is for adults, youth ages 12 and over, corporate groups, and people who need to fulfill a service requirement.
how_to_apply: Contact the volunteer coordinator for your branch (the guide lists names and phone numbers) or use the Volunteer Login link in the library's volunteering guide.
notes: The guide does not spell out the sign-up steps for teens, so call your branch coordinator first. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24. You must be legally allowed to work in the U.S. You must be getting services from a referring group or the WIOA Youth Program. You must want to find work. You must be able to work at least 20 hours a week and go to the workshops.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply alone. A sponsoring group or the WIOA Youth Program picks you. Email DFSEYE@fairfaxcounty.gov or see vcwnorthern.com/eye-programs/ to find a referring organization.
notes: Referral only. The county page also lists a WIOA Youth program for ages 17 to 24 who are out of school or close to graduating. In summer 2026, 133 youth worked with 100 local employers. Virginia work permit rules were not checked.

who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th grade students. No coding, health care or technology experience is required.
how_to_apply: Applications are closed. Fill out the Future Programs Interest Form on the camp page to get updates. Contact: Maria Uriyo, muriyo@gmu.edu.
notes: This is a day camp at George Mason University's Fairfax campus, 4400 University Drive, Fairfax, VA 22030. Not a job.

who_can_apply: Virginia residents in a public or private high school, or home-schooled in Virginia. You need a GPA of 2.5 or higher. You cannot have attended the 2026 STEM Academy (VSA) or Leadership Academy (VLA). You cannot attend another VALHEN summer program in 2027. A recommendation is required. It should come from a teacher, counselor, coach or community leader. That person must not be related to you.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the application opens in February 2027. Essays must be your own work (no AI generated or third-party essays). Contact STEM Academy Director Kerin Hilker-Balkissoon at khilkerb@gmu.edu.
notes: The camps list at Mason describes this program for ages 14 to 16 (rising sophomores and juniors). The program page itself says rising juniors, so use the program page. Competitive: students are selected. It is statewide for Virginia residents but held in Fairfax. It may also be on a Virginia-wide list.

who_can_apply: High school age girls in Northern Virginia (public, private or home-schooled) entering grade 10, 11 or 12 in the 2026-2027 school year. Class size is limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the program application on the page when the new session is posted. If you need a ride, email Captain Deanna Weand when you apply. Questions: 703-246-3332 or CPA@fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: For girls only. Classes are at Fairfax County Public Safety Headquarters, 12099 Government Center Parkway, Fairfax. Participants are expected to go to all classes. Not a job.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 20 who like the idea of a career in law enforcement. There are four units. They are the Criminal Justice Academy (Chantilly), West Potomac High School, Annandale High School and South Lakes High School.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Public Safety Cadets interest form on the page. The page also links an application. It links a waiver. It links a recommendation form. Email fcpdpsc@fairfaxcounty.gov with questions.
notes: An older Fairfax County police page called these units Explorer posts. They had the same unit numbers. That page no longer loads. Ask the cadet email about the current rules, such as citizenship, grades and costs. The page links an application, a waiver and a recommendation form.

who_can_apply: Fairfax County high school age students (public, private or home-schooled) entering grade 10, 11 or 12 in the 2026-2027 school year. Class size is limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Police Academy application on the page when the new session is posted. If you need a ride, email Captain Deanna Weand when you apply. Questions: 703-246-3332 or CPA@fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: Classes are at Fairfax County Public Safety Headquarters, 12099 Government Center Parkway, Fairfax. Participants are expected to attend all classes. Not a job.

who_can_apply: Illinois high school students who will be seniors in 2027-28 or who graduate in 2027. Must be a U.S. citizen and have proof of medical insurance. No STEM prerequisites. Age and GPA are not stated.
how_to_apply: Online application in Fermilab's Workday portal, a supplemental questionnaire, a PDF list of your STEM courses uploaded in the Resume section, and one letter from a STEM teacher or STEM club advisor. You cannot upload missing items after you submit.
notes: The apply link only works during the application window. Recommenders get an email upload link. It is sent only on weekdays during business hours, so line up your letter writer early. A walkthrough video is on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school students in public, private or parochial schools, and home-schooled students with high school standing. Students attend in person. A physics course and two years of algebra help but are not required. A unique email address is required.
how_to_apply: Watch for the news in November. Then fill out the online application. If you have questions, write to saturdaymorningphysics@fnal.gov.
notes: Lectures are at Wilson Hall in Batavia. Some lectures may be off-site. Spring 2027 dates are not posted yet.

who_can_apply: Open to all high school students across Illinois. No science prerequisite. You must attend at least 8 sessions, with no excused absences.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page for the application. It opens in late fall 2026. If you have questions, write to Saturdaymorningquantum@fnal.gov.
notes: Classes are held at the Olive Harvey Learning Center, 3055 East 92nd Street, Chicago. The page gives no exact open or close date for applications.

who_can_apply: Enrolled in an Illinois high school JROTC program, and an Illinois high school junior, senior or recent graduate when you apply. Must be eligible to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Online application in Fermilab's Workday portal with an unofficial transcript, a resume and three short essay answers (under 200 words each). Then give contact info for one recommendation writer; the letter is due by the close date. Questions: Internships@fnal.gov.
notes: Only for cadets in an Illinois JROTC program. You cannot upload missing items after you submit, so gather everything first. Reference emails go out only on weekdays during business hours.

who_can_apply: Teens at least 13 by September 1 and no older than 17 by June 1. Volunteers who turn 18 during the year may finish it.
how_to_apply: Submit an online application, an essay written by the teen, and two reference forms. Selected applicants are invited to interview. Contact: FYI@FernbankMuseum.org or 404-929-6360.
notes: Described as very competitive; teens who are not accepted are encouraged to reapply the next year.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15. Space is limited. Register in WebTrac.
how_to_apply: Register through Folsom WebTrac.
notes: Source is the city's May 22, 2026 news post, which does not list a fee or the 2027 dates. Held at Oak Chan Elementary School. Check the Folsom Parks and Recreation site and WebTrac in spring 2027.

who_can_apply: Any current high school student in grades 9 to 12. Apply to Foothill, then submit the Special Admit form signed by a parent or guardian and your high school principal or administrator. Meet course prerequisites; talk to your high school counselor.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to Foothill, submit the Special Admit form (parent and principal signatures, plus an unofficial transcript if asked), register, and pay any fees. Admissions: (650) 949-7325.
notes: Foothill can give a free Clipper SmartPass for VTA buses and light rail. Undocumented students are welcome. Grades go on your permanent college record, and your parents cannot see college records. Partner-district options also exist: Middle College, College Now! (MVLA), Firebird Academy (Fremont Union).

who_can_apply: Open access and free. The page does not state an age minimum, so check the terms and the Minors privacy notice.
how_to_apply: Create a free account and pick a simulation at theforage.com.
notes: Good for a resume line, but it is not a job or an internship. The page has no age minimum and links a privacy notice for minors, so read the terms and ask a parent before signing up.

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older. Those 18 and over also pass a background check and need a valid Social Security number. You commit to 150 hours a year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the PDF application form and email it to the Volunteer Office. Then do an interview, an orientation, two TB tests and a flu shot.
notes: Volunteer Office: (714) 378-7000, Mon to Fri 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Patient Care Pavilion, 18111 Brookhurst St. The application PDF was not checked.

who_can_apply: The employment page says positions run from teens seeking a first job to skilled professionals. Minimum age is not stated on the page, so check each posting.
how_to_apply: Apply online for the job you want from the Join Our Team page. Applications are kept on file for one year. A background check is required if you get an offer.
notes: The district says it has about 1,200 part-time and seasonal workers at times of the year. Job fair dates are from old press releases, so confirm the next one. In Illinois, workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before they start. This comes from the Evanston Township High School work permit page.

who_can_apply: Students and school groups. The page does not list a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Use the link on the volunteer page to reserve a spot for an event. To adopt a park or trail, email Ivan Chambers at ichambers@fvpd.net.
notes: The district provides trash bags, gloves and a few litter grabbers for Adopt-A-Park groups. Ask the district if a parent form is needed for under 18.

who_can_apply: Eligible local teens. The page does not state the age range or other rules.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Teen Corps page when it reopens. Contact the Teen Corps Coordinator through the page.
notes: Run on a community garden and the Conservatory's Farmers Market. Ages, stipend amount and dates are not on the page, so ask the coordinator. Ohio needs a working permit for paid work at ages 14 to 17, but 16 and 17 year olds do not need one for nonagricultural, nonhazardous work during summer vacation. See permit.html?state=oh for the steps.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 15 years old and complete an application, a background check and an orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application, then complete the background check and orientation.
notes: Some outdoor roles run March to November and the Children's Garden runs April to October.

who_can_apply: Students at Fremont Unified middle and high schools. The page says limited English is not a barrier to joining career and technical education programs.
how_to_apply: The page gives no sign-up steps. Ask your school counselor or principal, or contact Leslie Heller, Director of Secondary Education, (510) 659-2513.
notes: The page is general. It lists 15 industry sectors and 58 career pathways. It does not list internship partners or work-based learning. Ask your counselor which pathways your school offers.

who_can_apply: The page does not state ages, grades or residency rules. Ask the Recreation Division.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Call the Recreation Division at 510-494-4300.
notes: Meets 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. on the first Monday of each month except July and August, at City Hall, 3300 Capitol Ave. The page lists 12 members.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Attend a Teen Advisory Board meeting or submit a book review. The page does not describe a sign-up form. Allow up to 7 business days after an activity for your credit to show. Call (714) 773-5719.
notes: Easy way to start earning service hours. The Teen Advisory Board page on the same site has more detail; it was not read.

who_can_apply: High school students age 15 and over. The hospital picks based on your application. It looks at whether you can keep the weekly commitment. It also looks at your school background and career interests. There is no job shadowing or internship.
how_to_apply: When applications open, contact St. Jude volunteer services at Stjudevolunteers@providence.org or 714-992-3000 ext. 2878. Questions should come from the student. Accepted volunteers must go to an orientation and get a health screening. This takes about one month in all.
notes: Questions: Stjudevolunteers@providence.org or 714-992-3000 ext. 2878. Questions should come from the student. Health screening and orientation are required (about one month).

who_can_apply: Any high school student who lives in Fulton County, GA. You need a computer, phone or tablet and Wi-Fi.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online enrollment form. Do it during the time when sign-up is open.
notes: Enrollment for 2026-27 closed Sept 28, 2026, per the enrollment page. Call the county at 404-612-4000 to ask about late spots. The enrollment page does not mention internships. Only the county page does. Contact: customerservice@fultoncountyga.gov.

who_can_apply: Youth under 18 may apply with a parent or guardian signature. The page does not state a minimum age, so ask Volunteer Services.
how_to_apply: Under 18: download and print the PDF application, sign it, get a parent or guardian signature, and return it to Volunteer Services by email, mail, fax or drop-off. Then attend orientation. Email vol.services@fultoncountyga.gov or call 404-613-0125.
notes: The page says the library is currently on hold for community service hour requirements, so students who need school hours must contact Volunteer Services early. Teen Advisory Boards exist at some branches; ask the Youth Services Librarian. Library Systems for DeKalb and Cobb counties are separate.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 to 16. You go to a Fulton County school, live in Fulton County or have a family member who works for Fulton County. No serious arrest or conviction record.
how_to_apply: Send in the application with a one-page essay. The topic is on the application. Add a letter of recommendation from a school administrator.
notes: The page still shows 2025 dates, so call to confirm the current year. Contacts on the page: FCMD.JuniorDeputy@fultoncountyga.gov, 404-612-4462 or 404-612-4147.

who_can_apply: Fulton County Schools students who are at least 16, in 11th or 12th grade, and following a defined career pathway. Individual schools may add rules. Students in Atlanta Public Schools use their own district.
how_to_apply: Print and finish the WBL Interest Form. Give it to your school's WBL coordinator. Students who meet the requirements are issued an application. Grades, attendance, discipline and related coursework are reviewed. You must follow up on job leads yourself.
notes: District contact listed on the page: Leslie McHann, 470-254-0466. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

who_can_apply: Fulton County residents in 9th to 11th grade. You must go to a school inside Fulton County lines.
how_to_apply: Apply online with a two-page essay. Also get a one-page nomination statement. It comes from a teacher, counselor, principal or community member who has known you for at least a year.
notes: Contact on the page: 404-612-7386 or the county line 404-612-4000. The length of a term is not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12. Bring an ID (school ID, driver's license or library card).
how_to_apply: 1) Fill out the online teen volunteer application. 2) Register for a one-time Teen Volunteer Orientation. 3) Sign up for open sessions on the teen volunteer calendar. Cancel at least 24 hours ahead.
notes: Grade 6 is under 13, so younger readers should ask about their grade. The library's Elgin Teens page also describes Studio 270, a high school teen space at 270 N. Grove Ave. (homework help, college readiness, job hunting help; phone 847-695-7577), but parts of that page look out of date, so call first. The volunteer page lists a contact email that is hidden in the page text; use the library's Contact Us page.

who_can_apply: Gwinnett County Public Schools juniors and seniors who are 16 by September 1 and have coursework that matches their career choice. The school reviews grades, attendance and discipline.
how_to_apply: Apply through your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator. Forms: electronic agreement, WBL application, recommendation form and job site information form. Forms are uploaded in the WBL class when the semester starts. Apprenticeships need a post-high-school plan.
notes: No home-office or private-residence placements. The program cannot guarantee a job. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

who_can_apply: Motivated rising high school seniors enrolled at a Genesys Works partner school. The Bay Area page says 100% of its students qualify for free or reduced lunch. No GPA is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, then interview if accepted, then get summer training details. Phone 415-442-0280, email gwba@ba.genesysworks.org.
notes: You must attend a partner school, and the lists of schools and counties were not on the pages read. Ask them whether your school is a partner. No 2027 dates or deadline are posted. Interns work for pay, so a California work permit applies if you are under 18.

who_can_apply: Geneva Public Library patrons in grades 6 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register as a Volunteen using the sign-up form on the page. Contact: geneva.library@gpld.org or (630) 232-0780, 227 S. Seventh St., Geneva.
notes: Service hours are flexible and are not listed as a set number. The page does not describe the registration steps beyond the sign-up form.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 8 to 18. Cloverbud programs for ages 5 to 7 exist in some counties only.
how_to_apply: Contact your local county UGA Extension office, or Georgia 4-H at 706-542-4444 or ga4h@uga.edu. The site has a 'Find Your Local Club' page.
notes: The home page lists teen options. They are Ambassador Program, Leadership in Action, Step Up and Lead, Senior Conference, State Council and State Congress. The pages read did not give dates or ages for each. Check with the county office.

who_can_apply: High school or home school students ages 15 to 17 at the time of application. Teens need their own transportation and a parent or guardian must join the info session.
how_to_apply: Register for one mandatory virtual information session (email volunteer@georgiaaquarium.org or use the page's Contact Us interest form). A parent or guardian must attend with the teen. If chosen, attend a group interview. Bring birth certificate and photo ID.
notes: Not every applicant gets an interview. No behind-the-scenes roles for teens and no court-ordered or school service hours. The page lists the group interview as both three hours and four hours, and its weekday names for the 2026 dates do not match the calendar, so confirm exact dates with the Aquarium. Last-year dates are shown for reference only.

who_can_apply: Male high school rising seniors. The home page says to contact your local American Legion Post or your Guidance Counselor for more information.
how_to_apply: Contact your local American Legion post or school guidance counselor. Chosen students then use the 'Request to Attend' form. They also use a permission form. Both are on the Georgia Boys State site. Questions: administration@dogboysstate.org or 229-938-9352.
notes: Boys only (Girls State is a separate program run by the Auxiliary). The program is not a paid job, so no work permit. The 2026 memo says the week includes an evening devotional, and families who object may decline the invitation. Delegates must stay all week.

who_can_apply: Students at a Georgia school with a DECA chapter. The state page does not list grade or age rules.
how_to_apply: The state page is written for school advisors. Chapters sign up and renew members online at deca.org. Ask a business or marketing teacher if your school has a chapter. A school can start one using the Start a Chapter page. The page says the Georgia DECA minimum is 15 members.
notes: Contact the state staff through the Contact Us page at gadeca.org.

who_can_apply: Georgia students interested in business careers. The home page does not list grade, age or dues.
how_to_apply: The page says 'Joining is simple!' and links a chapter finder to see which FBLA chapters are close to you. Students join through a local chapter.
notes: Ask your school whether it has an FBLA chapter. The page read does not list the state conference dates or dues.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in agricultural education classes at a Georgia school with an ag program. The membership page says every student in those classes becomes an FFA member.
how_to_apply: Sign up for an agricultural education class at your school. Ask your counselor or ag teacher. The state page says a student is expected to be in ag classes to join FFA.
notes: If your school has no ag program you cannot join through it. The state site links a 2026-2027 state agricultural education calendar for event dates.

who_can_apply: Girls who finished junior year. You need high moral character and above-average school standing. An American Legion Auxiliary unit must sponsor you. Another group that a unit approves can sponsor you too. Each high school is limited to 12 girls.
how_to_apply: Contact the unit president or Girls State Chairman of a local American Legion Auxiliary unit. This is how you get sponsored. A selection committee picks the girls. Then the application is completed online. The school checks that you are eligible before school ends. Email georgiagirlsstate@gmail.com or call 678-289-8446.
notes: Girls only. The site shows 2026 dates and the 'I Want In' page says last updated 12/3/2022, so confirm with your unit before relying on the dates. Not a paid job, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Skilled and talented high school sophomores and juniors. A Georgia public school district, independent school or state charter school must nominate you. Home school students go through their local school district.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply directly. Ask your school counselor or GHP Coordinator to nominate you. Nominees then complete an online application with a parent permission form, a recommendation and a transcript. GHP project manager: (404) 444-7062.
notes: Local nomination dates differ by school district and the page says they run August to early November, so move fast. Standardized test results are no longer required. The application page is marked updated 08/2026.

who_can_apply: Students at least 12 years old. The packet says there are no exceptions. A page is sponsored by the Lieutenant Governor or one Senator.
how_to_apply: The 2025 welcome packet says to contact your sponsoring Senator's office when you register. Staff contact: kim.campbell@senate.ga.gov or illana.burkhart@senate.ga.gov, 404-657-7004. The program web page needs a browser to load, so check it for the current form.
notes: Source is the official 2025 Senate Page welcome packet (the program web pages on legis.ga.gov only showed a loading screen to the reader). Under Georgia law cited in the packet (O.C.G.A. 20-2-692) page service counts as present at school. Dress code is business or business casual. Cell phones are not allowed while paging. The Georgia House has its own page program at legis.ga.gov/house/page-program, which could not be read.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors or seniors on track to graduate. You need a recalculated GPA of 3.0 or higher. You need test scores unless your GPA is 3.4 or higher. You need approval from your counselor and a parent. You also need proof of lawful presence.
how_to_apply: Submit the undergraduate application online. Send test scores if they are asked for. Have your counselor send your transcript through GA Futures. Perimeter College has its own application. It has five campuses.
notes: You must earn a C or better in every class to keep funding. The page gives two test score minimums. The lower ones are in the requirements list. The higher ones are in the step on test scores. Ask admissions which apply. Perimeter College lets dual students take 1000 and 2000 level classes at its campuses or online.

who_can_apply: Students in a Georgia high school or Georgia home school. You need a 3.5 unweighted GPA and ACT, PSAT or SAT scores. You need precalculus and two finished college-level courses (AP, DE or IB). You also need proof of lawful presence in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Submit the Georgia Tech Dual Enrollment application in the term window. Add your high school transcript and test scores. Add AP scores if needed and proof of lawful presence. Apply for state funding at GAFutures.org.
notes: Competitive. Funding can be denied if you used your 30 hours, your high school does not take part, the course is not eligible (on-campus), or you are not a U.S. citizen, eligible non-citizen or Georgia resident. Out-of-state tuition is $1,153.46 per credit hour. Decisions come about 3 weeks after the window closes.

who_can_apply: Georgia residents who are at least 16 years old by the program start. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application on the STEP page before the deadline. Questions: outreach@ae.gatech.edu.
notes: Read on the Georgia Space Grant Consortium page that hosts the STEP information; the Georgia Tech Aerospace page itself returned a 403 block. Other sessions listed for 2026 were in Augusta and Albany.

who_can_apply: Georgia residents who are rising 11th and 12th graders. You should like engineering, science, math or technology. The page does not mention a GPA rule.
how_to_apply: The page says sign-up is closed for 2026. It does not give application steps. Check the Georgia Tech College of Engineering K-20 initiatives page for the next session.
notes: The same page also describes a separate TryEngineering Summer Institute, a nine day residential program for thirty Georgia high school students at no cost, with no dates given. Georgia residents only.

who_can_apply: High school students, through their own school's Work-Based Learning coordinator. The state page lists no age or grade rules. Districts set their own (Gwinnett, Fulton County and Cobb above say juniors and seniors age 16 or older).
how_to_apply: Ask your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator or counselor. Internships can happen only after coursework related to the placement. Co-op students must be enrolled in a course directly related to the job.
notes: Youth Apprenticeship in Georgia is run through the Department of Education and local schools. The Georgia Department of Labor youth page covers work permits and child labor rules only. Georgia Work Ready was not researched. Georgia requires a work permit for students under 16 (see the Georgia Department of Labor work permit page).

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 who face barriers to education, training or employment. Both in-school and out-of-school youth are served. The page does not list the exact barriers or income rules.
how_to_apply: The state pages give no application steps. They give no list of local offices. Use the contact page at tcsg.edu or the WorkSource Georgia portal (worksourcegaportal.com). Find your local office there.
notes: The pages read do not say how to enroll. A call to your local WorkSource office is the real next step. The services page says the Occupational Skills part is for ages 18 to 24. So 14 to 17 year olds would use the other services. Atlanta area teens may also see the city and county programs listed separately in this guide.

who_can_apply: Sophomores and juniors currently enrolled in high school in Los Angeles County, who are at least 16 when the program starts and live within 25 miles of the Getty Center.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in early February. Questions: gettyteens@getty.edu.
notes: Supported by the Vera R. Campbell Foundation. The page calls it a paid summer internship but says only that interns receive a stipend. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Girls and young women in grades 9 to 12. Programs run at the Simpson Center in Oakland (year-round) and Cal State East Bay in Hayward (summer).
how_to_apply: Use the Contact Us page at girlsinc-alameda.org. Office: 510 16th St, Oakland. The site does not list application steps.
notes: Code the Game is a six week program (the page mentions a fall offering). Internship pay, hours and ages are not posted.

who_can_apply: Aimed at girls and young women in tech. The page does not spell out the rule for other genders, so ask. Clubs meet 1 to 2 hours a week; Pathways is virtual and self-paced.
how_to_apply: Use Get Started on girlswhocode.com/programs to find a Club or begin Pathways.
notes: The page lists no cohort dates. A separate program for ages 18 to 25 also exists.

who_can_apply: Current high school students. Dual Enrollment: students in Glendale Unified (GUSD) and Burbank Unified (BUSD) taking courses on the class offerings list. Jump Start: everyone else, for college credit only.
how_to_apply: Apply at OpenCCCApply. Then send the Annual Digital Form signed by a parent and your counselor. Find classes, clear any prerequisites and register in MyGCC. Email dual@glendale.edu or call (818) 240-1000 ext. 4767.
notes: Jump Start credit is not guaranteed to count toward high school graduation. A weekly Zoom help hour runs Tuesdays 3:30 to 5:00 PM.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 and in school. You have a disability or health condition, such as an IEP, 504 plan, ADHD or anxiety.
how_to_apply: One online Apply Now form covers all GYA programs. A case worker contacts you in 3 to 5 business days. STEP contacts: (818) 937-8005 or (818) 937-8057.
notes: The GYA page does not mention work permits. California requires a permit for paid work under 18.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24. The page lists it as a first job or summer job program. GYA serves youth from Glendale, Burbank and La Canada-Flintridge and the greater Los Angeles County area.
how_to_apply: One online Apply Now form covers all GYA programs. A case worker contacts you in 3 to 5 business days. Office: 1255 S Central Ave, Glendale; (818) 937-8073, Mon to Fri 8 to 5.
notes: The GYA home page shows funder logos but does not say which program they fund. The pay rate is not on the page, so ask the office. The GYA page does not mention work permits. California requires a permit for paid work under 18.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21 and low income. GYA serves Glendale, Burbank, La Canada-Flintridge and the greater Los Angeles County area.
how_to_apply: One online Apply Now form covers all GYA programs. A case worker contacts you in 3 to 5 business days. Contact for TEAM: (818) 937-8006.
notes: Funded by the Verdugo Workforce Development Board and WIOA grants. Income limits are not spelled out on the page.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

who_can_apply: Youth volunteers must be in grades 6 to 12. They live in Glenview or go to a school the library serves. Teen Advisory Board applicants must be in grades 7 to 11 and follow the same rule. Innovation Center volunteers must be in high school at a school the library serves.
how_to_apply: Fill out the youth volunteer application when it opens. The Teen Advisory Board form comes out in November. For the Innovation Center, write to innovationdesk@glenviewpl.org. For other questions, write to youthdesk@glenviewpl.org or call 847-729-7500.
notes: Returning volunteers do not need to apply again. Court ordered community service for teens must be 16 and older. It uses a separate form.

who_can_apply: High school and undergraduate students. Minimum age 15 by Jun 18, 2026 for remote or computer-lab internships and 16 for in-person wet-lab internships. No minimum GPA; transcripts are not requested.
how_to_apply: Online application with a personal statement; interested mentors interview strong candidates and offers go out in early April. Request a fee waiver code from cosassip@gmu.edu if needed.
notes: Labs are at the Fairfax campus, the Science and Technology Campus in Manassas, or Woodbridge; students arrange their own transportation and campus housing cannot be arranged for minors. This is a paid-by-the-student internship, not a job, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Exceptionally talented high school juniors and seniors. You need a non-degree application and fee. You need your official high school transcript. You need permission from your high school counselor or administrator. Non-native English speakers must meet the English proficiency rule.
how_to_apply: Complete the Non-Degree application. Send your high school transcript. Send your counselor or administrator's permission. Fairfax County Public Schools and Loudoun County Public Schools students can use the school partnership pages. These are for math and science dual enrollment.
notes: The Admissions Committee may ask for test scores or transcripts from other dual enrollment credits. The page also lists Youth Leadership Conferences and Educational Travel Programs, which were not read in detail.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24. The program is built for young people who face barriers to work, such as low income, foster care, homelessness, disability, teen parenting or a record. The page lists no formal rules.
how_to_apply: Email youth@ging.org. The page lists 404-420-9900 as the general Goodwill number, not a program line.
notes: Address on the program page: 2201 Lawrenceville Hwy, Suite 300, Decatur, GA 30033. Career centers listed: Athens, Cornelia, Decatur, Duluth, Oakwood, Smyrna and Woodstock. The page does not say which counties are served, so ask when you email. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit is required for minors under 16. This program starts at 16.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 by the first day of class. You must volunteer, since you cannot be forced. You must be credit deficient or at risk of dropping out. You must be a U.S. citizen or legal resident and a California resident. You must be clear of felony charges. You must live in one of these places: Santa Cruz, Santa Clara, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Monterey, San Benito, Kings, Tulare, Inyo, San Luis Obispo, Kern, Santa Barbara or Ventura County, or in Lancaster or Palmdale.
how_to_apply: Make sure you meet the rules to apply. Fill out the Interest Form on the site. Then watch the required virtual orientation video. It is a must for the application.
notes: Meant for teens who dropped out or are at risk of dropping out. The FAQ says each ChalleNGe program runs its own admissions. Call or write the academy (contact page on its site) about county rules. Many cadets can earn a GED during the residential phase (FAQ). Some counties on the site have no separate region tag in this guide. They are Santa Cruz, Madera, Fresno, Monterey, San Benito, Kings, Tulare, Inyo, San Luis Obispo, Kern and Ventura. Lancaster and Palmdale are in Los Angeles County.

who_can_apply: Georgia residents in a public, private, charter or home school in Georgia, in the class of 2027, 2028 or 2029, who are 16 by April 4, 2027 (no exceptions). Proof of U.S. citizenship or U.S. person status is required for most positions. You need your own transportation.
how_to_apply: Complete the online pre-application. It has a resume (PDF), a personal statement and a letter of recommendation. It must be 100% complete before it closes. You can join the 2027 contact registry for updates. Email support.hsi.stem@gtri.gatech.edu with questions.
notes: No weekend, after hours or remote work. Housing is not provided. Do not send unsolicited emails or calls to GTRI employees about internships. The page asks this. Finishing the pre-application does not guarantee a job. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit is required only for minors who have not reached their 16th birthday. This internship requires age 16 by April 4, 2027.

who_can_apply: Gwinnett County residents or students who go to school in Gwinnett County, ages 15 to 21. You must be 15 by the first workshop. You must be free for the whole paid internship program. You need a reliable ride. You cannot be a past Empower Gwinnett County Government intern. No grades or work experience are required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application during the posted window. A form link is on the program page. Human Resources picks applicants based on interests, career goals and department needs. No interview is required. Selected applicants get a conditional job offer. Some jobs may need a background check.
notes: A work permit is required if you are 15. The main page says the 2026 application is closed. It says the 2027 application period will be posted there. Questions: HREmployeeEngagement@GwinnettCounty.com.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who live in Gwinnett County and will be in 7th through 12th grade as of August. Everyone must pass an application process.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the program page to reach the youth academy application. The page does not describe the steps.
notes: The page names no season or week for the sessions and gives no age range. The only date given is the May 29, 2026 application deadline, so confirm the week before planning.
