Season is set to summer only because the deadline is in May. Unpaid program, so no work permit. Only the general county number 770.822.8000 is listed.

who_can_apply: You must be 15 to 18 years old and go to a Gwinnett County public school. Case by case, the program may approve school outside Gwinnett County. You must be in good standing in your school and community.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. The parent and the student both sign it online. Go to orientation. Turn in a recommendation from a teacher, a school leader or a community leader.
notes: The page does not say whether it pays, how long it lasts or what the exact opening date is. No essay is mentioned. County phone: 770.822.8000.

who_can_apply: Age 13 and up. The page says the minimum age is 13 with parental permission required. Homework help covers students in grades K to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form from the Apply Online button on the volunteer page. List the branches you want. If you are a GCPS student, use a personal or parent email, not a school email.
notes: The background check on the page applies only to volunteers 18 and older. Open spots vary by branch.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older to be a certified lifeguard. You can start the prerequisites (an in-water skills test) at 15. Lifeguard I or II jobs need a current lifeguard training certificate by hire date.
how_to_apply: 1. Contact a year-round aquatic center and schedule the In-Water Skills Test. 2. Get certified in lifeguard, first aid and CPR/AED through the American Red Cross course. 3. Apply for the position online at GwinnettCountyJobs.com.
notes: Course costs are not listed, so ask. Email Lifeguard@GwinnettCounty.com or call 770.822.8000. The page does not mention work permits. The season is listed as part-time seasonal, with no months given.

who_can_apply: The page and form do not list an age. The form asks for your school, grade and a parent or guardian signature, and asks about teen leadership training. Accepted aides must pass a background check and fingerprinting.
how_to_apply: Download the Summer Camp Aide Volunteer Application from the Day Camps page. Fill it out with a parent or guardian. Email it to CommunityServices@GwinnettCounty.com or Parks@GwinnettCounty.com, or drop it off at the camp site you want. Use a separate form for each camp site.
notes: Day camps are for children ages 5 to 13. The minimum age for aides is not stated, so call 770.822.8000 to check. Unpaid, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 20 who have finished 8th grade and have a clean record. Open to youth interested in law enforcement.
how_to_apply: Pay the sign-up fee and do an interview. Contact the Community Affairs Section to start.
notes: Sponsored by Learning for Life. Contact Cpl. Juan Reyes at 678.442.6520 or PDCommunityAffairs@GwinnettCounty.com. Community Affairs Section: 3125 Satellite Boulevard, Duluth, GA 30096. The page has no Explorer page of its own. Details come from the outreach programs page.

who_can_apply: Students who will attend a Gwinnett high school the next school year. No ages or grades are listed. You must get yourself to the Gwinnett Justice and Administration Center in Lawrenceville and other program sites.
how_to_apply: There is an Application link on the program page. The page does not describe the steps.
notes: The page does not list exact dates, ages or the application steps. Unpaid, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: The county page and flyer say the program is open to high school, undergraduate and graduate students. No ages or grade rules are listed in what was read.
how_to_apply: Find the listings and apply at VolunteerGwinnett.net. You can also call 770.822.7955. Or write to VolunteerGwinnett@GwinnettCounty.com.
notes: The VolunteerGwinnett.net listings page would not open because of a certificate error. So the open jobs, ages and hours were not read. Ask about the minimum age before you apply. The county page names Muriam Nafees as the contact for volunteer internships.

who_can_apply: Age 16 and up for construction sites, even with a parent or guardian. Ages 16 to 18 bring a signed minor waiver. Age 15 and under can help with fundraising, flyers or lunch for site volunteers.
how_to_apply: The page gives no online sign-up link; there is usually a volunteer kiosk on site. Call 866-450-4432 or email Volunteer@HabitatEBSV.org. Groups of 5 or more use the group pages.
notes: Hands-on building experience for age 16 and up. Specific build sites were not listed on the page; ask which are near you.

who_can_apply: At least 16 to volunteer on a job site. The page lists no age minimum for the ReStore and no special rules for 16 and 17 year olds. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Make a VolunteerHub account (sachabitat.volunteerhub.com), register for and attend a one hour HabiTour orientation, then sign up for shifts. Email volunteers@habitatgreatersac.org or call (916) 440-1215.
notes: Ask whether under-18 volunteers need a parent signature or waiver, since the page does not say. Group volunteering contact: gcabral@habitatgreatersac.org. Office: 819 North 10th St, Sacramento.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Free forever for teenagers.
how_to_apply: Join through hackclub.com and find or start a club.
notes: Free for teens. The page lists about 1,500 clubs and events such as game jams and a hardware hackathon in San Francisco.

who_can_apply: Open to everyone. The page does not state an age limit. In 2026, pull requests no longer count toward rewards.
how_to_apply: Sign in on hacktoberfest.com with MyMLH, or register for a local fest.
notes: The page states no age limit; check each local fest for age rules. Pull requests no longer count toward rewards in 2026. Earn three stickers to get a sticker pack by mail, and you must sign in with MyMLH and give an address.

who_can_apply: Monthly projects: filter the calendar by age to see which are open to you. HandsOn Tomorrow and the Youth Volunteer Council are for Bay Area high school students; the Council requires finishing HandsOn Tomorrow first.
how_to_apply: Use the Community Calendar at handsonbayarea.org/calendar and filter by age. Email info@handsonbayarea.org or call 415-541-9616.
notes: HandsOn Tomorrow, a 2-week summer program (up to 40 hours), is paused and is not running in summer 2026. The Youth Volunteer Council needs HandsOn Tomorrow first, so for now the monthly calendar projects are the way in. Age limits vary by project.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. Animal handling, public speaking or working-with-children experience helps. It is not required.
how_to_apply: Download the volunteer application, write a 1-page cover letter about your interests and goals, and send both by mail, email, fax or in person to 1300 Senter Road, San Jose. Selected applicants interview. Phone (408) 794-6425.
notes: Minimum 48 hours a year (about 4 hours a month). Not everyone is picked, but you can reapply the next season.

who_can_apply: The page says ambitious high school students, including rising juniors, may enroll. No age range or grade rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page of the Summer Session site. You send a registration application with a transcript and pay fees before the course starts.
notes: Costs money and the courses are college level. Check the site in winter for 2027 dates and prices.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 and up. Some jobs have their own age rules, listed on each opportunity. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the volunteer agreement.
how_to_apply: Create a volunteer profile, then register for a one-time event or submit an interest form for a service project. Service projects need a background check and TB risk assessment before starting.
notes: This page lists many volunteer roles, not one program, so each role's own age rule applies. Verification of service hours is emailed on request. Volunteers with court orders should follow the district process (info@haywardrec.org).

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. Library service hours cannot be used for community service required by a judge or court.
how_to_apply: Use the APPLY TO VOLUNTEER online interest form linked from the library page. Questions go to hpl.teens@hayward-ca.gov.
notes: The page says the roles are subject to change, so check the online interest form for current openings. The Just for Teens page describes its events for grades 9-12, while the volunteer page says ages 13-17; the volunteer page is the one used here. An older 2023 city notice describes a monthly Teen Advisory Group meeting (1st Wednesday, Downtown Library, ages 13-17, no commitment). That notice was not re-checked for 2026, so ask hpl.teens@hayward-ca.gov whether it still meets.

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 20 who live in the City of Hayward or within the Hayward Unified School District boundaries. Applicants under 18 need a parent or guardian consent form.
how_to_apply: Get the application and the Parent Agreement and Contact Information form from the City of Hayward website, or call the City Clerk at (510) 583-4400, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays. Applicants are interviewed by a panel.
notes: The official Youth Commission page returned 404. The newest notice read is from April 2025. The 2021 notice said meetings were on the first and third Mondays, so the meeting schedule may have changed. Confirm the 2026 cycle with the City Clerk before applying.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors. The page says interns are ages 16 to 18 in one place and 16 to 19 in another.
how_to_apply: Watch Hennepin County job listings (sign up for email notifications from the program page). Libraries hiring interns: Brookdale, Brooklyn Park, Franklin, Hosmer, North Regional, Roosevelt, and Cedar Riverside Opportunity Center.
notes: Training includes hands-on learning, group reflection and an adult mentor. Hiring dates and pay are not on the page. Confirm with the library before relying on it.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Only a limited number of teen volunteer spots exist at some libraries.
how_to_apply: Ask your local Hennepin County library about teen openings. If there is one, fill out the teen volunteer application (PDF), bring it to the library, and a staff member will contact you. Questions: Volunteer Services, 612-543-8633.
notes: Adult volunteers have a different process. The phone line is staffed Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

who_can_apply: Black male students entering grades 9, 10 or 11. No coding experience needed. Must commit to the full 15 months.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Immersion Program page on hiddengeniusproject.org.
notes: The immersion page still shows the old 2025 deadline. No 2027 date is posted, so wait for the new announcement. Oakland and Richmond are the East Bay sites.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors enrolled full time in high school for the program year. The group has 15 members.
how_to_apply: Send in the online application during the Feb 1 to Mar 1 window. Questions: HMATeenPrograms@high.org.
notes: No absences are allowed during the summer intensive. The High's Teens and College page also lists an Early College Program in Art History and Curatorial Studies with the Atlanta University Center for rising juniors and seniors, but it gave no dates or application details.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. Application, interview, orientation and hands-on training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Flight Teen application online, then expect a call to schedule an interview, attend volunteer orientation, and train with an active volunteer.
notes: Year-round, ongoing applications. Weekend shifts only. Interview timing and training length are not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 living in the City of Los Angeles. The checklist PDF we read (2024 version) lists the other rules on who can join. Check the current one.
how_to_apply: Create an application on the Hire LA site, then bring or upload proof of age, right-to-work (I-9) documents, City of LA residency and the family income form.
notes: Cycle dates are not confirmed, so check with EWDD before counting on a summer 2027 spot. The same city department runs 14 free YouthSource Centers for ages 14 to 24 (school help, job readiness, some paid internships); ask at your nearest center, for example Boyle Heights 323-526-5800 or South LA 323-903-6926. Under 18 you need a California work permit. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Local students ages 16 to 18. No grade level is stated.
how_to_apply: The page lists no application or interest form for this program. Call the Volunteer Office to ask when interest will be taken again.
notes: Not offered: summer, short-term, hands-on patient care, shadowing or observation. Volunteer Office phones: Newport Beach (949) 764-8264, Irvine (949) 517-3152. Specific weekly hours are not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Minimum age is 16. High school students use a separate application and must attend an in-person orientation. Needs a health screening (MMR, varicella, flu, TB testing) and availability to start within one month of applying.
how_to_apply: Submit the application form for high school students from the Holy Cross volunteer applications page, then complete a screening interview and orientation.
notes: Another site named holy-cross.com is Holy Cross in Fort Lauderdale, Florida; use holycrosshealth.org for Maryland. Background checks are required for volunteers 18 and older. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Students in health science or biomedical science programs, or interested in health careers. Join through a school chapter.
how_to_apply: Ask your health science teacher for the chapter advisor.
notes: HOSA reports over 200,000 members in 51 chartered associations. California chapter rules, dues and middle school eligibility were not on the page.

who_can_apply: On-site animal care volunteers must be 18 or older. Students under 18 can foster with a parent or guardian's support or make fleece blankets.
how_to_apply: Email volunteer@hssv.org or see the student opportunities page for fostering and blanket instructions.
notes: No hands-on shelter work until 18. Service hours: 2 fleece blankets = 1 hour (0.5 hour each); fostering is counted by care time. Email for a service hour verification letter.

who_can_apply: Restoration days are for ages 8 to adult. Kids under 14 need an adult with them. Age rules for long-term volunteer roles are not stated on the pages read.
how_to_apply: Come to a restoration day (wear closed-toe shoes and bring water) or sign up for the monthly volunteer training. A waiver form is on the volunteer page. Contact Kenny at 714-846-1114.
notes: The Conservancy internships are unpaid. They need a related degree or college enrollment, so they are not for high schoolers.

who_can_apply: Most roles are ages 13 to 17 (18-year-olds still in high school can also join). Teen Tech Volunteer is ages 15 to 17, Chess Club Volunteer is ages 15 to 18 in high school, and Helen Murphy toy cleaning is 13 and up. D&D Club volunteers must have attended a club meeting in the past six months.
how_to_apply: Use the online application for the role you want (several library roles share one application link, so check which one). Seats for club roles are first-come, first-served, and staff email next steps. The Main Street Branch also accepts a printed teen application dropped off at the branch.
notes: Contact: Teen Services Librarian Katelyn Wong (Katelyn.Wong@surfcity-hb.org) or the library at 714-842-4481. The page also lists other Huntington Beach volunteer groups for teens (Bolsa Chica Conservancy, Bolsa Chica Land Trust, Shipley Nature Center, OC Coastkeeper cleanups) with their own age rules, so read it for those. Some entries on the page look copy-pasted, so confirm details with staff.

who_can_apply: Local high school students. These are HB Union High School District students. They also include Huntington Beach residents who go to private school or are homeschooled.
how_to_apply: The page says applications are now available. It links the word Applications to its Notice of Vacancies page. No deadline is listed. For questions, contact the city staff liaison, Molly Uemura. She is at the Community and Library Services Department. The email is on the page.
notes: Application dates and the form are not on the page. Confirm with the city first.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 8 to 18 join a 4-H Club. Your age on September 1, the start of the 4-H year, decides how you join. Teen teams: Creative Collective Art Ambassadors is ages 14 to 18, and Illinois 4-H Influencers is for high school age youth. Other teams do not list ages on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form on the Join 4-H page with a parent or guardian. Your local Extension office then contacts you with next steps to register. Returning members renew in Zsuite.
notes: This is club membership and volunteer leadership, not a paid job. Cost, grades and teen team application steps are not stated on the pages read. Call Illinois 4-H at (217) 333-0910 or email Illinois4H@illinois.edu.

who_can_apply: Boys who have completed one semester of 11th grade and have at least one semester left after Boys State. Those who finished junior year get preference. A boy may attend only once as a citizen. Many are sponsored by a local American Legion post.
how_to_apply: Complete the online registration form; your local American Legion post will then contact you. Parents can also register eligible sons. Questions: info@illinoisboysstate.org or 309-663-0361.
notes: Boys only. Delegates must stay all week and may not drive or leave campus. The Samsung Scholarship application must be finished before arriving.

who_can_apply: Members must have an interest in marketing, management, entrepreneurship, hospitality and tourism or finance. A chapter needs a certified local educator as advisor. Grades and ages are not listed on the pages read.
how_to_apply: Ask your school for a DECA chapter and advisor. If your school has none, the Illinois DECA site has a Start a Chapter page. Membership runs through the DECA membership portal linked on ildeca.org.
notes: Not a paid job. Dues and conference dates come from the DECA Inc. page for Illinois. The state site ildeca.org did not repeat them. Mailing address on the state site: 2460 Dundee Road, Box 1001, Northbrook, IL 60065.

who_can_apply: High school girls who are current juniors. A principal, guidance counselor or home school administrator must certify leadership qualities, good character and U.S. residency. You must secure sponsorship from an American Legion Auxiliary Unit and attend an orientation.
how_to_apply: Complete the online registration form (name, school email, counselor name and email, school, hometown), get approval from your school official, find a sponsoring American Legion Auxiliary Unit and attend an orientation. Call 309-663-9366 or email info@alaigs.org.
notes: Girls only. The program is physically active with long walks; the registration page asks you to check with a doctor if you have limits. After the program you share your experience with your sponsoring Unit.

who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th graders who are Illinois residents. You need earlier research experience (a research program, course or science fair). If you do not have it, you must finish an online Research Fundamentals course first.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application form linked on the IMSA page when the portal opens. Questions go to Dr. Anita White at awhite@imsa.edu or 630-907-5949.
notes: Residential students live in IMSA halls and get all meals. Commuters get breakfast and lunch but must drive to the Aurora campus. Topics change each year.

who_can_apply: Students who are a sophomore, junior or senior at a charter or public high school in Illinois. You must be in that grade during the year you apply.
how_to_apply: Make a Submittable account with a personal email, not a school email. Then send in the online application. Finalists do a video interview. Returning members apply again. They skip the interview.
notes: The ISBE page is marked archived, so watch the page for the next call for applications. Next year's dates are not posted; the June 30 date is from the last cycle.

who_can_apply: You must be at least 12 years old and not yet 19. Members under 18 join a cadet or composite squadron, not a senior squadron.
how_to_apply: Find your local squadron with the unit locator or the Illinois Wing units page. Contact the unit to confirm a meeting. You usually go to about three meetings. Then you finish the membership application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. The national page says ages 12 to 18; the Illinois page says at least 12 and not yet 19. Illinois Wing HQ: 630-524-4400 or wa@ilwg.cap.gov.

who_can_apply: High school students. Legislative Assistant and Press Team are open to freshmen through seniors. Lobbyist and Attorney are for sophomores to seniors. Legislator is for juniors and seniors. Anyone can be a Clerk-Bailiff.
how_to_apply: Get the registration link from your local Delegation Advisor. A student and a parent or guardian both sign the code of conduct. You pick a preferred role and give your State Senator and State Representative. Contact the state office if you have no delegation.
notes: Not a job. State office: 1315 Butterfield Rd, Suite 218, Downers Grove, IL 60515, (630) 833-9622, ilyag@ilymcayg.org.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. No prerequisite courses.
how_to_apply: Use the sign-up link on the IMSA High School Online Programs page. To ask about cost and openings, email studentenrichment@imsa.edu.
notes: Asynchronous course with weekly office hours. The page said another cohort was added because of demand.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page does not list grades for this course. Spots are limited.
how_to_apply: Sign up online on the IMSA High School Online Programs page. Or apply for a need-based scholarship. Email studentenrichment@imsa.edu.
notes: IMSA does not provide a mentor or lab space in this course. Students must complete all assignments by the deadlines to earn the certificate and refund.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. You must find your own research mentor and lab space if needed. IMSA cannot provide them.
how_to_apply: Sign up online on the IMSA High School Online Programs page. Or apply for a scholarship instead. Do not pay if you apply for a scholarship. Email studentenrichment@imsa.edu.
notes: It is a hard program. Daily work is expected and you must meet firm deadlines. Failing three deadlines means removal without a refund. IJAS fair entries must be made as an IMSA RISE student for Region 5. Program is non-credit.

who_can_apply: Members must be in a business or marketing class now or have been before. The Indiana Department of Education must recognize chapters. They must have business courses. Grades and ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's business or marketing teacher. Ask about joining or starting a DECA chapter. Send state questions to the Indiana DECA advisor. Use indianadeca@gmail.com.
notes: Not a paid job. The state website listed on the page is indianadeca.org. This card is based on the DECA Inc. page for Indiana.

who_can_apply: The state page says in-school young adults ages 14 to 21 and out-of-school young adults ages 16 to 24 may be eligible. Eligibility rules beyond age are not stated.
how_to_apply: Connect with your local WorkOne Career Center (Lafayette office serves Tippecanoe County; schedule by appointment through the WorkOne West Central site). Ask about the young adult program.
notes: This is the state workforce agency's WIOA-style youth help, not a single job. The WorkOne West Central about page (older) says a youth program for ages 16 to 24 is offered; the newer state page says 14 to 21 in school. The Bloomington (South Central) WorkOne regional page was not read, so confirm locally. Call before going. Re-read on 2026-10-09: the state page says nothing about cost or pay, so the card is not in the paid group.

who_can_apply: To join FFA, you must be enrolled in an agriculture course at your school. The page does not list grades or ages.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or agriculture teacher about enrolling in an agricultural education class. The Indiana Agricultural Education site explains how to start a program if your school has none.
notes: Not a job. Your school needs an ag class and an FFA chapter. The page links the Indiana Agricultural Education program for how to start one.

who_can_apply: Boys going into their senior year of high school. No age limit is listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Registration opens January 11, 2027 on the Hoosier Boys State site. The application steps are not described on the pages read. Email info@hoosierboysstate.org or call 317-630-1301.
notes: The FAQ on the About page says the cost to attend is $400. The About page says a $50 non-refundable application fee is due, and the remaining $350 sponsorship fee is paid by a local American Legion Post or other community partner. Drop-off and pickup is at the MTI Center, 1215 Thunder Ave, Angola, IN. Not a job. The page links to a separate Girls State site (alahgs.org) that returned a 404, so no Hoosier Girls State card was written.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. You must be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (national headquarters may waive this for some non-citizens). Cadets can stay in until their 21st birthday.
how_to_apply: Find a cadet or composite squadron with the locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the application. Some squadrons take it online.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Indiana Wing office: 4760 Andrews St, Columbus, IN 47203, 877-350-8643, info@inwg.cap.gov.

who_can_apply: Hoosier students in 6th through 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Contact Shelby Lashbrook. Use shelby@indianaymcas.org or (317) 715-2145. Do this to join, start a delegation, volunteer or sponsor.
notes: Not a job. Office: 6610 N Shadeland Ave, Indianapolis, IN 46220, open Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

who_can_apply: Must be at least 16 by the start of the session, interested in a healthcare career, and able to attend every session date. Needs a 250-word written response, background check, TB screening, MMR, varicella and Tdap proof, an interview with a parent, an in-person orientation and photo ID.
how_to_apply: Register during the window through the 'High school students register here' link on Inova's student page. Spots are assigned by lottery, one entry per applicant, and the student handles all email.
notes: Mandatory student-and-parent info meetings are in mid-November 2026 and orientations in late December 2026 (dates differ by hospital; one of each is required). Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

who_can_apply: Students who are chosen as student reps from local high schools. The page lists 2026-27 reps from Beckman, Portola, Irvine, University, Northwood and Woodbridge high schools. It lists no grade or eligibility rules.
how_to_apply: The page says to look for HSYAT at your school through the Campus Clubs page. No application form is listed.
notes: The page lists no grade rules, application dates or phone number for this program. Check your school's Campus Clubs page.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 and over (program assistance and toy cleaning are ages 14 to 17). Teen Summer Reading volunteers are students in grades 8 to 11. Each library has up to 20 TAG memberships.
how_to_apply: Submit the Teen Volunteer Application on the library's volunteer system at www.volgistics.com/appform/337674493. A required orientation comes before the summer program.
notes: The page lists no library contact; it points to the volunteer coordinator, and the City of Irvine main number is 949-724-6000. The page writes the Teen Volunteer Application link as volgistics.com/appform/337674493 and links it over https, so apply_url uses https.

who_can_apply: High school students who will graduate in 2027 or 2028. The page also describes 11th or 12th grade in Fall 2026. You need an unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher in college prep classes. You need a strong reason to take one UCI course.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Enrollment Form. Send it to the Summer Session office. Add a copy of your latest high school transcript.
notes: This is real college credit and costs real money. The grade stays on a college record. The page names two grade groups (graduating 2027 or 2028; and 11th or 12th grade in Fall 2026), so check which one fits you. The fee page says 2026 Summer Session fees were pending the state budget and may change.

who_can_apply: Grades 9 to 12 need parent and principal consent. Grades K to 8 also need instructor approval. You must meet each class prerequisite. There must be open seats.
how_to_apply: Find a class in the IVC schedule, write down its CRN, then complete the General Enrollment Form steps with parent and school approvals. The Director of Dual Enrollment is listed on the page.
notes: IVC/IUSD Summer College is for grades 9 to 11 at seven Irvine high schools. These are Creekside, Irvine, Northwood, Portola, San Joaquin, University and Woodbridge. The Early College Pathway is for some students who are admitted before grade 9. It is at Beckman and San Joaquin.

who_can_apply: Students in Northern California; grade levels not stated. The center is not open yet.
how_to_apply: No sign-up steps yet. Call JA of Northern California at (925) 465-1070.
notes: Not open yet, and the page lists no registration steps or opening date. Watch for it in early 2027. The contact on the page is for sponsors and partners.

who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 18 (students in 6th grade or older). Boards meet at Central (1st Monday, 5 pm), Greene County, Louisa County, Nelson Memorial and Northside; Crozet is full and Gordon Avenue is not currently running.
how_to_apply: Use the Join a Teen Advisory Board page or contact your branch. The page does not say how to apply beyond that.
notes: Meeting times: Greene 1st Tuesday 4-5 pm; Louisa 3rd Thursday 3:45 pm; Nelson 2nd Thursday 4-5 pm; Northside 2nd Monday 7-8 pm. Gordon Avenue's entry on the teen volunteers page says its board is accepting applications while the TAB page says it is not currently running; call the branch.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 13 years old. Teen volunteers should be able to work independently. Branches include Central, Crozet, Gordon Avenue, Greene County, Louisa County, Nelson Memorial, Northside and Scottsville.
how_to_apply: Contact your local branch (Send a Message link) or email the Young Adult Services Manager through the JMRL contact form. The page does not list formal application steps.
notes: Volunteering can count toward school or club service requirements. At the time of reading, Gordon Avenue said all weekly positions were filled. JMRL's volunteer coordinator is listed as Acacia Rodgers, volunteer@jmrl.org, 434-979-7151 ext 6695.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. The national site says you must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated to succeed. The pages read do not explain rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Make a MyJobCorps account. Upload the documents that show you are eligible. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Brunswick center: 4401 Glynco Pkwy, Brunswick, GA 31525. Turner center: 2000 Schilling Ave, Albany, GA 31705. Neither center page showed a closure notice on 2026-10-09. The application asks for ID, Social Security number and proof of income. That is normal for this federal program, but only enter it on the official jobcorps.gov site with a parent or guardian. A parent should ask an admissions representative about the rules for 16 and 17 year olds. The Atlanta center is not listed here because its page could not be confirmed.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated. The pages read do not explain parent consent for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Make a MyJobCorps account. Fill out the application. Upload the papers that show you are eligible. Examples are proof of income and proof of citizenship or residency. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Address: 1480 Snelling Ave N, St. Paul, MN 55108. Job Corps is a training program, not a job. After applying, the national site says the review includes a background check (1 to 2 weeks) and a campus review (about 30 days).

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who are low income and meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules, plus background checks (per the national Job Corps site). Mostly fits teens who are out of school or want a different path. Housing is on campus.
how_to_apply: Apply at enroll.jobcorps.gov or call 800-733-JOBS (800-733-5627).
notes: Residential, so you live on campus at 3100 Meadowview Rd, Sacramento. The Sacramento page lists the trades (building construction, carpentry, cement masonry, Certified Nurse Assistant) but not the age or income rules, which come from jobcorps.gov. A federal settlement reported Aug 12, 2026 kept all 99 centers open, but that article does not name Sacramento, so confirm the center is enrolling.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated. The page does not explain rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Click Apply Now. Make a MyJobCorps account. Upload eligibility papers. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Or call 800-733-5627.
notes: The center page footer lists 2800 Airport Hwy 21 E, San Marcos, TX 78667. Job Corps is a training program, not a job. Texas has other Job Corps centers that are not covered by this card.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated. The pages read do not explain rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Click Apply Now. Make a MyJobCorps account. Upload the papers that show you are eligible. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Phone for Curlew and Columbia Basin: 877-763-0580.
notes: Addresses: Cascades, 2060 Powerhouse Drive, Sedro-Woolley, WA 98284. Curlew, 3 Campus St, Curlew, WA 99118. Columbia Basin, 6739 24th Ave NE Bldg 2402, Moses Lake, WA 98837. Job Corps is a training program, not a job. Each center page shows only a few of its trades; use See More on the center page for the full list.

who_can_apply: Local high school students interested in a healthcare career. Must be at least 14.5 years old, at least a second-semester freshman, with a minimum 3.0 GPA. Must attend a Saturday orientation with a parent or guardian and complete required training. Students apply through a partner high school, which interviews and screens its own candidates.
how_to_apply: Apply through your high school. Contact the career, college or community service office at a partner school listed on the page. The school interviews and screens its own student candidates.
notes: Read on the official John Muir Health page 2026-10-07. Not stated on that page: application window or deadline, TB test or immunization requirements. It is an unpaid volunteer role, so no work permit is listed. Region is east-bay because Walnut Creek is in Contra Costa County, not Oakland. The Auxiliary at Walnut Creek Medical Center offers selective scholarships to high school seniors and college students who volunteered in this program. A separate Concord Medical Center high school program is not onboarding this summer; its page says to check back in March 2027. An older third-party listing said seniors are not accepted, which conflicts with the official page; confirm with the program before applying. Minimum age is listed as 14.5 on the page, stored here as 14.

who_can_apply: High school programs are delivered through schools and teachers, who request them. The site does not list a way for a student to sign up alone, so ask your school or call JA.
how_to_apply: Ask your teacher or counselor to request a JA program, or contact JA at (925) 465-1070 or info@janorcal.org.
notes: JA reached 27,947 students in 128 schools in 2025-26, mostly through schools. JA Launchpad (Silicon Valley) is listed as opening early 2027. Job shadow and internship details were not on the pages read, so ask JA.

who_can_apply: Be 16 to 19 by June 1, 2027, live in a Northern California Kaiser Permanente service area, have proof of legal US work eligibility, and be free Monday to Friday about 8am to 5pm. Priority goes to juniors and seniors. Children of Kaiser employees or physicians cannot apply. The program aims at students who lack resources to explore health careers.
how_to_apply: Apply only on the KP LAUNCH online portal during the window (email submissions are not reviewed). You need a resume and a personal statement of up to 750 words. Questions: KP.LAUNCH@kp.org.
notes: Full-time hours, so no summer school or camp overlap. Competitive. A Kaiser story reportedly cited about 3,300 applicants for 318 spots, which is not confirmed here. Placement sites vary, so check that your area is offered. Kaiser may ask for COVID vaccine proof.

who_can_apply: Workdays are described as for all ages, individuals and families. No sign up needed unless you come with a group of 10 or more. Age rules for the longer volunteer roles are not on the pages read.
how_to_apply: For workdays, just show up 5 to 10 minutes early and sign in with the leader. For longer roles, fill out the volunteer application on the site. Volunteer Office: 630-762-2741, volunteer@kaneforest.com.
notes: Bring boots or sturdy shoes, a water bottle and gloves. Info on Eagle Scout and Gold Award projects is in the Resources section of the volunteer page. Questions about workdays: Stewardship Specialist, 630-200-1290.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who live in Kane, DeKalb or Kendall County. The page lists no income or other rules (federal workforce funding rules may apply, so ask the provider).
how_to_apply: Pick a provider on the page and contact them directly. Providers in Kane County include Elgin Community College and Business & Career Services Inc. Waubonsee Community College covers Kane and Kendall. Not sure where to start? Call 630-762-2085.
notes: Starts at age 16, so it fits older high schoolers. The page names one contact person but lists an email that does not match that name, so phone first. Funded by a U.S. Department of Labor grant per the page. Elgin Community College's own Future Workforce Leaders program is one of the providers.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not state ages; ask the teen librarian at your branch. Each board sets its own meeting schedule.
how_to_apply: Contact your local librarian (Teen Services Librarian). Or go to an open Teen Advisory Board meeting listed on the page. If your branch has no board, ask about starting one.
notes: KCLS serves King County outside the city of Seattle (its branches include Maple Valley, Lake Forest Park, Newport Way and Federal Way). The Seattle Public Library volunteer page showed no current volunteer openings when read on 2026-10-09. Washington L&I says its child labor rules 'only apply to minor employees, not volunteers.'

who_can_apply: Currently enrolled high school students ages 16 to 17. Must be 16 or older when you apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You need a self-portrait photo, proof of COVID-19 vaccination and a questionnaire. Recommenders email letters to volunteer@med.usc.edu by April 30. If accepted, you do an interview. Then you get a health screening with a TB test, an orientation and a tour. Phone (323) 442-8436.
notes: Check the page in January for the next year's dates.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19 and enrolled in high school or an equivalent program. Parent or guardian written permission is in the application. No drugs, underage drinking or gang ties, and you must pass a background check (a waiver may be allowed for past minor offenses). Cadets who join before 19 can stay until 21.
how_to_apply: Go to a weekly meeting. You learn about the program and meet the officer mentors. You can pick up an application there.
notes: Contact Officer David Buchanan, dbuchanan@kennesaw-ga.gov, 770-424-8274. Kennesaw Police, 2529 J O Stephenson Ave, Kennesaw, GA 30144. The page does not give a meeting day or time, so call first. Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Any high school student who wants to serve and lead. Clubs are set up in high schools or equivalent schools. Members are expected to do at least 50 hours of service a year.
how_to_apply: Use the Find a Key Club tool on keyclub.org, or follow the Start a Key Club steps if your school has none.
notes: Dues and local rules vary by club; dues amount not stated on the pages read. Key Club International phone: 800-549-2647.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

who_can_apply: Open to anyone. The site says its mission is a free education for anyone, anywhere. The page states no age rule.
how_to_apply: Go to the page, pick a course, and sign up for a free account if you want to save progress.
notes: The page loads slowly because it builds in your browser. Course list seen: Financial Literacy, Personal Finance, Entrepreneurship, Careers, College admissions, Career Exploration.

who_can_apply: Current students in grades 9 to 11 in the Naperville area. The page does not give a school or residency rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application when it opens. For questions, contact the KidsMatter Director of Programs. Call 630-864-3960 or write to sherilyn@kidsmatter2us.org.
notes: The page still showed the 2025-26 call when read. Check back in spring for the next one.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18; no prior experience required for the free onboarding programs. Camps run in several cities including San Francisco and Oakland, plus virtual.
how_to_apply: Use the sign-up form linked on the Kode With Klossy programs page.
notes: Free for all programs. Workforce development programs are for ages 18 to 26, not high schoolers. Camp dates and sites for summer 2027 are not posted yet.

who_can_apply: High school students of all levels. No ages or grades are listed.
how_to_apply: Register online when registration is open. In 2026 registration was closed and a waitlist form was on the page.
notes: Costs money, not a job. Contact doarch@kennesaw.edu. Kennesaw campus: 1000 Chastain Road, Kennesaw, GA 30144.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders for camps at the KSU Center. The Aerospace Engineering camp at the Marietta campus takes rising 6th to 12th graders.
how_to_apply: The 2026 sessions are over, though the page still shows Registration Open labels. For Summer 2027 updates, fill out the contact form on the page. No 2027 dates or registration are posted.
notes: Places: KSU Center, 3333 Busbee Dr NW, Kennesaw. The Marietta campus hosts Aerospace. Contact discoveru@kennesaw.edu or 470-578-6765. It costs money and is not a job. Confirm sign-up status with the team before you pay.

who_can_apply: Students going into 9th grade through college freshmen. The Dance Intensive is for intermediate to advanced dancers.
how_to_apply: Register on the pages for each program. They are linked from the main page. Sign-up starts November 1. Questions: arts@kennesaw.edu or 470-578-6742.
notes: Costs money, not a job. The Dance, Theatre and Arts and Design intensives list no exact dates on the main page. Scholarships are not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Rising public high school seniors (entering senior year in fall 2027) who attend a public high school in LA County and live or go to school within 10 miles of the worksite. Must be able to work legally in the U.S. and bring a school ID and proof of work eligibility. No age rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Apply for a listed internship when applications open in March 2027. Questions: BAI@arts.lacounty.gov.
notes: Schedule may change. You cannot be a current or former employee of the worksite or related to its staff. The 2026 internship positions list is on the Department's site. The page does not mention work permits. California requires a permit for paid work under 18.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 20 with at least a 2.0 GPA. You can read, write and understand training materials in English. You can work on a team.
how_to_apply: Send in the Explorer Program Interest Card to hear about the next cycle. Add the program's email to your safe senders. Then apply during open enrollment. Accepted applicants get a uniform fitting and a family meeting. They also go to a two-day orientation.
notes: The page lists 12 posts. They are Vernon, Carson, Whittier, Industry, Azusa, Lancaster, Fairfax, Santa Clarita, La Canada Flintridge, El Monte, Agoura Hills and Pomona. But its sign-up form lists Posts 1 to 22. Confirm your post with the department.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 9 to 17 in LA County. New participants must pass a 100-yard freestyle swim test (1:30.00 for ages 14 to 17). Cadets must be 16 or 17 as of July 1 with at least two years in the program, one as an A.
how_to_apply: Register online when the season opens, usually in February or March. New participants must pass a swim test. They must bring a birth certificate or passport. Cadet and Life Saving Team applications are separate. They are posted later.
notes: The page calls the $635 an estimated operating cost and says the fee schedule is under review. Costs money and is mainly for younger kids; teens 16 to 17 can reach Cadets. Not every beach offers afternoon sessions or Session 2. Refund rules and absence limits are on the page.

who_can_apply: Anyone 14 and older can volunteer. Teen Advisory Boards are open to teens at libraries that have one.
how_to_apply: Contact your local LA County Library branch to ask about volunteer openings and whether it has a Teen Advisory Board.
notes: This covers LA County Library branches (unincorporated areas and many cities), not the City of Los Angeles library system (see the LAPL card). Tasks vary by branch and season.

who_can_apply: LA County residents who are 14 to 24 when they enroll and have the legal right to work in the U.S. The county gives priority to youth with high needs, such as current or former foster youth, youth touched by the justice system, youth who are or were homeless, and LGBTQ+ youth.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Interest Form on the Youth@Work page. AJCC staff reach out within 48 hours to check eligibility and match you with an employer.
notes: The county released a Youth@Work Program Review and Redesign Report on August 25, 2026, so rules and pay for 2027 may change. Under 18 you need a California work permit before the first day. The pay figure is the 2025 summer rate from the county's own news release, not a 2027 promise. Long Beach youth can also use the City of Long Beach center (see the LBWIN card).

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. The 2026 council has 27 members from nine areas, including the San Gabriel Valley, Central Los Angeles and the South Bay. No other rules are listed.
how_to_apply: The page has no application. Use the update sign-up form, email metroyouthcouncil@metro.net or call 213.922.2852.
notes: Check the page for the next recruitment. The page does not say how often the council meets.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14 years old and able to finish the required training. No upper age limit is stated.
how_to_apply: Join the waitlist on the Zoo's volunteer page. When applications open, go to an info meeting and an interview. You are invited to these. Then finish online and in-person training. You must also pass a fingerprint background check.
notes: Applications were closed when this page was read. A negative tuberculosis test may be needed for some advanced roles. Phone: (323) 644-4200.

who_can_apply: Los Angeles County residents, 16 to 18, who will be juniors or seniors in the 2027 school year and are interested in art, museums or community events.
how_to_apply: Online application during the open window (last year July 1 to Aug 21). Questions go to teens@lacma.org.
notes: Next year's dates are not posted. Watch for a July opening. LACMA also offers NexGenLA, a free membership for LA County youth 17 and under (free museum entry plus one guest). Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Teens who are 14 to 17 years old on June 1 of the year they apply. Teens interested in any career field may apply. A parent or guardian must co-sign the online application. A teacher or mentor recommendation form is part of the process.
how_to_apply: Read the Zoo Teen Information Packet, apply online through the zoo's volunteer form (applicant and parent both e-sign), and submit the teacher or mentor recommendation form. Contact: zooteen@lafayette.in.gov, 765-807-1543.
notes: Opening date for 2027 is not posted; the page only says check back in January 2027. The page mentions sponsors that keep costs low for participants but does not state a fee amount. The information packet was not read, so shift length and total hours are not stated here.

who_can_apply: Minimum age is 9. Everyone under 18 needs a waiver signed by a parent or guardian. Ages 9 to 15 need an adult chaperone (1 adult for every 5 youths). Individual 16 and 17 year olds can volunteer without a chaperone. Groups of 16 and 17 year olds need chaperones (1 adult for every 10 youths). You must be at least 14 to volunteer at the Fresh Market.
how_to_apply: Create a VolunteerHub account (a parent or guardian creates the profile for a child), pick a shift on the volunteer calendar, and bring the signed waiver to your first shift. Questions: call 765-471-0062.
notes: Some shifts have their own age rules. A parent or guardian needs to make the account for anyone under 18. Court ordered community service hours need separate approval before you start.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 9 to 12. No other rule is stated on the camp page.
how_to_apply: Apply through Purdue's Summer College for High School Students (the camp page says the 2026 application was there). Questions: purdueag@purdue.edu.
notes: This is a camp, not a job, and it costs money. The Purdue ag summer programs index page describes the high school camp as a two-week experience. The camp page itself says one week. Confirm the length with purdueag@purdue.edu.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 (the Pulsar level). New students send an essay or other media about their interest. They also send two of these. One is a transcript with a 3.5 GPA in the talent area. Others are a test score of 120 or higher on an intelligence test and a 90th percentile achievement or aptitude test. A teacher or mentor letter counts. So does proof of involvement such as awards.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application through the Purdue conferences site (the Register Now link on the program page). Upload your essay or media and two supporting documents. Questions: geri@purdue.edu or 765-494-7210.
notes: Costs money and is a camp, not a job. The details on this card came from a summarized fetch of the program page. The raw page would not load for a second check. Confirm the Pulsar price, dates and application steps with geri@purdue.edu or 765-494-7210 before you plan. The page also lists other prices ($1,250 commuter and $1,495 residential per session). They may be for the younger levels.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors (Class of 2027 for the 2026 camp). Purdue recommends three years of high school math and one year of chemistry or physics by summer.
how_to_apply: Apply online. A complete application needs your PSAT, SAT or ACT scores and a transcript. Applications are taken until spots are full, then a waiting list. Questions: step@purdue.edu or 765-494-7217.
notes: Costs money and is a camp, not a job. Only for students going into their senior year. The page gives 2026 information, so check it for the 2027 cycle.

who_can_apply: High school students. Main page says ages 15 to 17. Application page: priority for GPA 3.30 or higher and at least 16 who have finished sophomore year, younger students may apply. Residential courses require being under 18 for the whole program. Course-specific rules apply.
how_to_apply: Online Summer College application: essay, high school transcript, up to three short-term course choices, $60 non-refundable fee. Admitted students first get one course; more are offered as space allows in late March to early April.
notes: Costs are summer 2026 and may change. Some courses were full for 2026 and some were canceled. The listed short courses include PREFACE and MITE, which are pre-college engineering workshops, with their own eligibility. The student pays; this is not a job.

who_can_apply: Teens who are 12 or older by May 31 of the program year. No grade rule is listed. The library's volunteer page is under its Teens section.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form linked on the library's Teen Volunteers page, then attend one volunteer training day. Questions: Youth Department, 765-429-0119.
notes: The page was last updated for the 2026 season, so the next cycle should open in spring 2027 but is not posted yet. Check with the Youth Department before applying. Unpaid volunteering, so no Indiana work permit question applies.

who_can_apply: Youth in grades 3 to 12 can join a 4-H club in Indiana. Enroll through the Tippecanoe County Extension office.
how_to_apply: Create a family account and enroll each youth in 4HOnline 2.0 (links are on the county enrollment page). Call the Extension office at 765-474-0793 with questions.
notes: The county page gives two enrollment dates (Jan 15 and Jan 1), so ask the office which one applies. The Extension office is at 1950 South 18th Street, Lafayette, IN 47905. This is a youth club, not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older. Those 18 and over also pass a background check and need a valid Social Security number. You commit to 150 hours a year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form (PDF on the page). Email it to the volunteer office, addressed to Julia Lieberman. Then go to a Volunteer Services orientation. You also need 2 TB tests and the required seasonal flu shot. The page does not mention an interview.
notes: Volunteer Office: (949) 452-3728, 24451 Health Center Dr, Laguna Hills. The application PDF is labeled an adult form; ask the office which form teens use.

who_can_apply: The library page says East Lansing High School students can log limited volunteer hours through the Teen Action Group. Ages are not stated.
how_to_apply: For more information, contact Rheanna Reeder or Zandra Blake.
notes: The detailed TAG description is from a May 2022 library post that the site marks as possibly out of date, so confirm meeting times and who can join with the library first. Page also says the library is not accepting general volunteers at this time. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

who_can_apply: Current high school students in the United States.
how_to_apply: Apply through the program page linked from the MSU Spartan Youth listing. Contact: Zach Constan, constan@frib.msu.edu or 517-908-7363.
notes: The FRIB program page (frib.msu.edu) did not load for me because the site blocks automated readers, so this card rests on Michigan State University's Spartan Youth Programs listing only. Confirm dates, the application link, cost and any extra requirements on the FRIB page before you plan.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. The listing does not state other rules.
how_to_apply: Use the program page linked from the MSU Spartan Youth listing. Questions: ping@frib.msu.edu.
notes: The FRIB program page (frib.msu.edu) did not load for me because the site blocks automated readers. So this card rests on Michigan State University's Spartan Youth Programs listing only. Confirm dates, the application link, cost and any extra requirements on the FRIB page before you plan. Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: All volunteers must be at least 14 years old.
how_to_apply: Register once through Volunteer Hub, then pick a shift from the schedule. Groups of four or more email the volunteer program manager.
notes: Not teen-specific, but open to teens 14 and up. Warehouse shifts are 9 to 11 a.m. and 1:30 to 3:30 p.m. Monday to Friday, with some late afternoon, evening and weekend shifts at Mobile Food Pantries. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 to 19 (the listing shows grades 6 to 12). The listing says to check with your county MSU Extension office about scholarship funds.
how_to_apply: The listing links to a program page for details and registration, which I could not read. Contact on the listing: Michelle Neff, hydemich@msu.edu, 989-539-7805.
notes: The program's own 4-H page did not load for me. The Michigan State University College of Agriculture and Natural Resources site blocks automated readers. So this card rests on Michigan State University's Spartan Youth Programs listing only. Confirm dates, price and how to register on the 4-H page. It is a statewide event held in East Lansing, so it may also be listed as a Michigan-wide card. Not a job.

who_can_apply: Co-ed. Open to U.S. and international students entering grades 10 to 12 in Fall 2027. You need a GPA of 3.0 or better in engineering core courses (math, sciences, technology). A transcript is required.
how_to_apply: Send an online application with your transcript. Payment by credit card is the last step. It is required before MSU reviews the application. If you are not accepted, the fee is refunded minus a $25 processing fee.
notes: Residential. Mentors supervise students in the dorms, and students cannot leave campus. Contact: future-engineer@egr.msu.edu or 517-353-7282 (from the college page). Check the year of the session dates against the application page when it opens.

who_can_apply: Co-ed, open to U.S. and international students entering grades 11 and 12 in Fall 2027 with a GPA of 3.0 or better in engineering core courses. A transcript is required.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcript. Payment by credit card is the last step and is required before review. If not accepted, the fee is refunded minus a $25 processing fee.
notes: Residential with dorm supervision. Contact: future-engineer@egr.msu.edu or 517-353-7282. Check the year of the dates against the application page when it opens.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 17 who can work independently, have reliable transportation to the zoo, and can work outside in all weather.
how_to_apply: Step 1: attend an information session. Step 2: complete the application you receive afterward. Step 3: attend orientation and the required training. Keep a journal and finish monthly prompts.
notes: The zoo's volunteer page says teens 13 to 18 use this separate program; the program page itself says 13 to 17, so confirm the upper age. The regular adult volunteer program is 18 and older. Returning teens (years 3 to 5, under 18) can apply for the Zoo Teen Leadership Council. Contact is on the program page. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

who_can_apply: Age 16 and entering junior year of high school. Some placements need volunteers to be 17, and the Radiology placement is for ages 17 to 18.
how_to_apply: Online application on the Volunteering at Sparrow page (or ask for a paper copy at Volunteer Services). Then onboarding (2 to 3 weeks), online orientation, and placement registration links sent to onboarded volunteers.
notes: Expect a criminal background check, proof of MMR, varicella and Tdap immunizations (or titers), and a flu vaccine Nov to March; teens wear a provided smock apron and closed toe shoes. Volunteers must attend at least 75 percent of shifts. Free parking for active volunteers. Volunteer Services phone is on the page. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

who_can_apply: Oakland youth ages 16 to 21, per the City of Oakland summer youth jobs partner table. You must live in Oakland for that program.
how_to_apply: Call (510) 533-8850 or 1 (833) 532-3674, or use the Contact Us form at lfcd.org.
notes: LFCD's own employment page does not describe this youth program. Ages, hours and pay come from the City of Oakland MSYEP page. Under-18 workers need a work permit.

who_can_apply: Teen Volunteer and Teens Leading Change are for ages 14 to 19. Teen Council is for ages 11 to 19. Volunteers fill out a Teen Volunteer Intake Form and a parent or guardian signs a waiver.
how_to_apply: Contact the Young Adult Librarian or Senior Librarian at your nearest library, then complete the intake form and parent waiver. Questions: Volunteer Engagement, 213-228-7490.
notes: LAPL hosts over 2,600 teen volunteers a year across 73 branches. Openings differ by branch. Some branches also have volunteer slots listed at volunteer.lapl.org.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the Youth Volunteer Waiver. Students must attend a Summer Youth Volunteer orientation. Some roles have extra rules: Summer Nature Camp requires the Counselor in Training (CIT) program, and Open Space Jr. Docents require age 16 or older.
how_to_apply: Create a LARPD volunteer account by submitting the General Volunteer Application (use a personal email, not a school email). Attend a Summer Youth Volunteer orientation at the Robert Livermore Community Center. Then sign up for shifts through MyImpactPage. Questions: volunteer@larpd.org.
notes: The 2026 cycle is closed. Watch larpd.org/volunteer and the orientation pages for the 2027 dates; the district's pages were not all updated to the same year. The FAQ says the opportunity list may change each year. The orientation and FAQ pages list volunteer@larpd.org as the contact. Not a paid job, so no California work permit is needed.

who_can_apply: High school students in partner districts: Dublin, Livermore, Pleasanton and Tri-Valley, plus San Ramon Valley USD (welding) and TUSD (fire safety training). Residency and citizenship rules apply; ask Admissions & Records.
how_to_apply: Sign the CCAP Dual Enrollment form with your school counselor. You sign it once for all of high school. Questions: lpc-dualenrollment@laspositascollege.edu.
notes: Offered during and after the school day. Ages are not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Grades 10 and 11. Public school students in Alameda, San Francisco and Contra Costa counties are prioritized; nearby counties are encouraged to apply. In person at Berkeley Lab at least 4 days a week for 6 weeks.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Berkeley Lab K-12 program page when it opens (the 2026 application ran through apply.mykaleidoscope.com).
notes: Whether students are paid is not stated. Finishing students can join later workshops and possible lab internships in following summers.

who_can_apply: Grades 10 to 12 in Northern California, at least 16 by the program start. Students within 30 miles of the lab are prioritized. You can do the program only once.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the window and pick your top three projects. Do not contact mentors directly. Oakland Unified students also fill out a supplemental application.
notes: The page still says 'at least 16 by June 16, 2025', so check the age date when it reopens. Some 2026 projects were hybrid or virtual. Under-18 interns need a work permit.

who_can_apply: English-learning, native Spanish-speaking bilingual students.
how_to_apply: Watch the Berkeley Lab K-12 high school programs page.
notes: Grades and ages are not listed on the page. The 2026 camp is over and no 2027 camp is posted, so it is not confirmed to repeat. Page says it can lead to summer internship chances.

who_can_apply: The center serves ages 14 to 30. Youth@Work is for ages 14 to 24 and WIOA Youth services are listed for ages 16 to 24. WIOA funding focuses on out-of-school youth with barriers such as low income, foster care, homelessness, juvenile justice involvement, parenting, or a disability. A Long Beach residency rule is not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Complete the Youth Interest Form on the city's Youth Services page. Partner agencies can also refer youth through the Unite Us platform.
notes: Because most WIOA funding targets youth facing barriers, a teen still in school may be steered to Youth@Work or a school-to-career program instead. Under 18 you need a California work permit for any paid placement. The city's Youth Opportunities page also lists teen volunteering at Long Beach libraries and at Parks, Recreation and Marine (ages 13 and up).

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. The page does not state a residency rule for volunteers.
how_to_apply: Use the Register to Volunteer link for the teen volunteer call on the League site, or email lov@lov.org. Phone (510) 793-5683.
notes: The teen call on the homepage is for summer 2026. Confirm with the League whether it recruits again for 2027. Serves the Tri-Cities (Fremont, Newark and Union City).

who_can_apply: California high school sophomores, juniors and seniors. A select number are chosen.
how_to_apply: Apply through the LegiSchool website application. Join their mailing list for contest, town hall and internship news.
notes: The application link and 2027 dates are not on the page. The stipend amount is not stated. LegiSchool also runs Town Hall meetings in downtown Sacramento. It also runs video and essay contests for California high school students.

who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade. You must be able to work full time all summer. You must go to May Saturday trainings.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Lawrence Hall of Science teen internship page when it reopens; questions to lhscamps@berkeley.edu.
notes: The page URL says 2024 but the content is the 2026 posting. The page says to apply next summer; 2027 dates are not posted. Mid-January is the 2026 pattern only.

who_can_apply: Entering 9th grade or older and age 14 by June 1 (2024 cycle wording); not a current volunteer. Own transportation to Berkeley.
how_to_apply: Check the Lawrence Hall of Science teen volunteer page; contact veronicau@berkeley.edu or 510-642-5132.
notes: The volunteer page now says it is not taking new adult volunteers and lists no teen program. Call or email to ask whether the redesigned teen program has launched. The age rules in who_can_apply come from 2024 wording, so the age fields are blank.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 10 and up. Anyone under 18 must have a parent or a named adult with them at all times during orientation training. Youth cannot handle animals.
how_to_apply: Create a volunteer account with the Become a Volunteer link on the page. Then go to orientation at a shelter with your parent or guardian.
notes: A parent or designated adult must be with you at all times through orientation. The page does not list the shelter addresses in the text read. A COVID-era section mentions remote projects for younger kids, but it may be outdated, so it is not listed here.

who_can_apply: Youths ages 12 through 20, preferably attending Livermore schools. Youth members who attend Livermore schools do not have to live in the city (Livermore Municipal Code 2.51.010).
how_to_apply: Not confirmed. Contact the City of Livermore to ask how to apply and when the next seats open.
notes: Confirm first. The membership and duties come from Livermore Municipal Code Chapter 2.51, read on the code publisher's page. The city's own teen page (livermoreca.gov) returned HTTP 403 to both our fetch tools, so the application process, term, and dates are not confirmed. The municipal code gives 15 youth seats and 3 adult seats; the code does not say how seats are filled. Re-checked on 2026-10-09: the City teen page returned HTTP 403 again, so it could not be read and the card stays snippet-only.

who_can_apply: High school students in 9th through 12th grade in the Inland Empire who are interested in health sciences. Students 17 and a half or older may be invited to an optional shadowing week.
how_to_apply: Submit the application form, a recommendation form from a teacher or clergy member, a 200-word essay on your interest in health sciences, and the $30 fee or a waiver request.
notes: Closed until the next cycle opens. Loma Linda University is a Seventh-day Adventist institution.

who_can_apply: Active middle or high school students who meet each course's prerequisites. No minimum GPA is listed.
how_to_apply: Apply free on OPENCCC. You get your Viking ID by email. Then turn in the High School Dual Enrollment Form with all signatures. Finish New Student Orientation with a score of 80% or higher on the final test. Then register once Admissions confirms your form.
notes: Students who stop attending for two main terms must reapply. Taking college classes does not affect Long Beach College Promise eligibility. To take extra units, file the Unit Max Petition.

who_can_apply: Two seats are for youth under 19 at the time of appointment. Each youth is picked by their district councilmember and appointed by the Mayor.
how_to_apply: The page has no application. Ask your district councilmember's office or the city contacts listed on the page.
notes: Only two youth seats exist. Meeting location was listed as to be decided. Contacts on the page include ashleigh.griset@longbeach.gov and erika.Medrano@longbeach.gov.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 17. Must be at least 15 by July 1, 2027. Capped at 15 cadets.
how_to_apply: Sign up with the Cadet Tryouts Sign Up form on the page. Bring a resume. Pass a physical tryout: a 1000m open water swim in about 20 minutes and a run-swim-run in about 10 minutes. Then do an interview. Questions: LBJG@longbeach.gov.
notes: Very physical. Tryout date and calendar may change, so email to confirm. LBUSD students with at least one year of cadet experience can apply for a separate LBUSD Cadet Internship (details not on this page). The page header says the tryout date is not set but lists April 26.

who_can_apply: People ages 13 and over.
how_to_apply: Use the online 'Apply to Volunteer' link. It is in the BetterImpact portal. For questions, call (562) 570-3226 or write to prmvolunteers@longbeach.gov.
notes: The page does not list hours or what each role does. Ask which sites take 13 year olds.

who_can_apply: Must be at least 16 years old. If under 18, you must have a valid permit to work.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Apply Here for Recreation Jobs' link, which goes to governmentjobs.com (search for recreation). Tech help: (877) 204-4442.
notes: Pay rates are as posted on the page (the page does not date them). Under-18 applicants need a valid permit to work. Ask the department which level a first-time worker starts at. Accommodation requests: (562) 570-3188.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Interest Form linked on the library's volunteer page. Questions: lbpl_volunteers@lbpl.org.
notes: Hours, locations and training are not listed on the page. Ask by email.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18 as of February 27, 2027, and living in the City of Long Beach during the program year.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You answer five short questions. You also send a CV of up to 4 pages, a bio of up to 100 words and 5 poems (up to 10 pages). Paper applications go to LS-YPL@longbeach.gov or Teen Services at the Billie Jean King Main Library. Info sessions are Saturdays, Dec 12, 2026 and Jan 23, 2027, 12:30 to 2:00 PM at the Main Library. To reserve, email LS-YPL@longbeach.gov. Walk-ins are welcome.
notes: Poets must also take part in the National Youth Poet Laureate program and attend most monthly workshops. Mailed packets must be postmarked by Feb 27, 2027. Prize is a scholarship, not wages.

who_can_apply: High school students enrolled in the 2026-27 academic year.
how_to_apply: Online Teen Docent Program application, linked from the museum site (closed for 2026-27). A 2024 article says selected applicants are called in for a brief interview.
notes: Phone 650.948.9427; the page gives no email address. Pay is not stated on the current official page, so we list it as unpaid based on a 2024 article; confirm with the museum. The lahstalon.org article is a 2024 news piece, used only for the interview and volunteer details. The museum's adult docent roles are separate and not for teens.

who_can_apply: At least 14 years old or already started ninth grade. Needs a parent or guardian signature and a recommendation from your high school principal.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor, pick the Los Rios college that offers the class, apply at that college as a dual enrollment student (parent signature and principal recommendation needed), then register.
notes: Credits go on a permanent college transcript. Whether you also get high school credit depends on your school, so ask your counselor. Your school does not need a CCAP agreement for you to take a college class. Application deadlines are by college term.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up can volunteer on their own. Ages 8 to 13 can volunteer with a caregiver.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application form on the page, clear a background check, interview (in person, Zoom or phone), attend orientation, then sign up for shifts on Sign Up Genius.
notes: Volunteer Coordinator: Tim Gruber, tgruber@madisonchildrensmuseum.org. Spots may be limited at any given time, so email before you apply.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 (the page says the high school programs serve grades 9-12). Other rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Contact the program: TEENworks Manager Trevor Moores or High School Manager Vernon Hill (608-204-8039), or the center at 608-241-1574, info@goodmancenter.org.
notes: Confirm pay, hours and whether enrollment is open by phone. If you are 14 or 15, Wisconsin generally requires a work permit for paid work (see the Wisconsin rules on this site). Address: 214 Waubesa St, Madison.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 at the start of the program. Residency is not stated. Teens need reliable transportation to and from the zoo.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application form (Google Form linked on the program page). Optional Zoom info sessions were held in February. Questions: education@henryvilaszoo.gov.
notes: The page still shows the Summer 2026 schedule, so the 2027 dates are a guess based on last year. The page's email link points to volunteer@henryvilaszoo.gov while the text says education@henryvilaszoo.gov, so check both. Phone on the page: 608-266-4732. Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 can volunteer on their own in many roles. Ages 10 to 14 can volunteer with a parent or guardian in some roles (gate greeters, goat yard, events, wildlife champions).
how_to_apply: Pick a role on the zoo's Volunteer Roles page and fill out the application at the bottom of that role's page. Join the volunteer email list through the Volunteer Inquiry Form to hear about openings and information sessions.
notes: If you need school-required hours, check with your school counselor first. The zoo does not currently support court-ordered community service hours.

who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from the Madison area who care about the arts.
how_to_apply: Not described on the page. Call MMoCA at (608) 257-0158 to ask when the next application opens.
notes: The page may be out of date (it mentions the 2025 group), so confirm by phone before planning around it. Small group.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 in the Dane County area. Juniors and seniors need a referral from their home school. MMSD applicants must be entering the fourth quarter of junior year before applying.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Legacy page (opens a Google Form). Seniors and juniors also need a referral from their home school.
notes: Free program. Staff mentor graduates for one year after completion. Phone (608) 244-4721, info@operationfreshstart.org, 2670 Milwaukee St, Madison. The program starts at 16, so the Wisconsin permit rule for 14 and 15 year olds does not apply to it.

who_can_apply: The form has an age category of '17 and under', and the page says teens can volunteer to complete school hours. A minimum age is not stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form (area of interest, availability, branch). Staff reply by email. A background check is required under City of Madison APM 2-44.
notes: On Oct 9, 2026 the page said Central Library had no openings and asked high school students needing hours (for example National Honor Society) to check back in fall 2026. Alicia Ashman, Hawthorne, Lakeview and Meadowridge listed no openings or a waitlist. Ask a branch before counting on hours.
