who_can_apply: Students finishing grades 9 to 12 from Wisconsin, across the U.S. and abroad. Admission usually looks at advanced coursework, a 3.2 unweighted GPA or similar, and essays. No age range is stated.
how_to_apply: Online application with two essays (about 500 words total) and an unofficial transcript.
notes: Full scholarship for Wisconsin residents who get free or reduced lunch; partial scholarship (up to 50%) with income paperwork; none for international students. Funds are limited. Contact info@precollege.wisc.edu or 608-890-3260.

who_can_apply: Students finishing grades 9 to 12. Admission usually looks at a 3.0 unweighted GPA or similar, coursework, interest in the course and essays. No age range is stated.
how_to_apply: Online application with two short essays (about 500 words total) and an unofficial transcript. Decisions come on the 2nd and 4th Monday of each month.
notes: Full scholarship for Wisconsin residents who get free or reduced lunch; partial scholarship (up to 50%) with income paperwork; none for international students. Funds are limited and first come, first served. Contact info@precollege.wisc.edu or 608-890-3260.

who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or permanent residents. Need at least a year each of algebra and geometry, a 3.0 unweighted GPA and a strong interest in math, science and engineering. Highly selective.
how_to_apply: Online application, a high school transcript and a recommendation form. Questions: esp@engr.wisc.edu.
notes: Students live in Dejope Hall with supervision from staff and undergraduate counselors. Laundry and vending cost extra.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 and up who can commit to at least one full semester.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Wisconsin volunteer application on the UW Health volunteer page when it opens. Onboarding takes several weeks: online trainings, health assessment, placement interview, caregiver background check.
notes: Health clearance is required: seasonal flu shot, MMR, varicella, Tdap and a TB blood test. The page says waivers and exemptions are not accepted. Volunteer Services: (608) 263-6046, volunteer.services@uwhealth.org. The same page also covers Illinois locations; this card is for the Wisconsin application.

who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 24 in south central Wisconsin (job centers in Dane, Sauk and Jefferson counties). Whether in-school youth qualify is not stated.
how_to_apply: Go to a free info session. It is listed on Eventbrite from the page. Or visit a Job Center, or call 608-249-9001.
notes: Eligibility rules (such as income) are not on the page, so call before you count on a paid placement.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors in participating Dane and Jefferson county school districts. Employers choose and hire apprentices.
how_to_apply: Contact your school district's School to Career Coordinator (the page lists a name and phone for each district, for example Madison Metropolitan: Annie Johnston, 608-663-5384). Register for an information night on the program page.
notes: One date on the page is shown as Jan 20, 2027 even though its registration link says 2026, so check it. Students interested in UW Health need the Feb 17 session. Main office 608-249-9001. Ask the coordinator whether your age needs a Wisconsin work permit.

who_can_apply: Rules differ by event. On the 2027 events list only one event (hackPHS in New Jersey) is marked High School. The Fellowship page gives no age or student rule. Read each event page.
how_to_apply: Browse the events list on mlh.com and read each event's age rule before registering.
notes: The pages read did not state a minimum age. Many MLH events are aimed at college students, so check before you plan travel.

who_can_apply: At least 14, in high school, and not yet 21. A 2.0 GPA or higher if still in high school. Must be a U.S. citizen, pass a background check, physical test and written exam, and have written parent approval if under 18.
how_to_apply: Email bmarshall@mariettaga.gov to RSVP for a meeting. Attend 4 monthly meetings in a row and fill out the welcome packet. Then you get a background check, interview and a 3-month trial.
notes: The web page says ages 14 to 21; the requirements sheet says applicants must be under 21. The web page says meetings run Thursdays 6 to 8 pm, while the requirements sheet says 6 to 9 pm, so confirm the hours.Meets at 240 Lemon Street, Marietta, GA 30060. Phone 770-794-5355 or 770-794-5300 (ask for the Community Response Unit). The sheet says the fee goes to Learning for Life, Scouts BSA. Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 17. You must be 14 or older by Teen Boot Camp.
how_to_apply: Turn in the full application when it opens. Incomplete ones are not considered. Then go to a group interview. Questions: volunteers@marylandzoo.org or 443-552-5266.
notes: 2026 timeline from the page: selections May 28, parent orientation June 10, Boot Camp sessions June 22 to 26 and June 29 to July 3. The page text is partly inconsistent about dates, so check it when it updates. The Teens menu also lists a Keeper-in-Training Camp that was not read.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 8 to 18 (before January 1) can join and take part in projects and competitions. Ages 5 to 7 join as Cloverbuds and do not compete.
how_to_apply: Contact your local 4-H office to learn about programs and get the New Member Enrollment Packet. Fill it out and return it. The office then tells your parent or guardian where to pay online or by check. Re-enroll through 4honline.
notes: A youth group, not a job. The Get Involved page still shows a 2022-2023 fee note, but the Membership page lists the $40 fee with a $120 family cap, so confirm the current fee with your local office.

who_can_apply: Girls who are finishing or just finished their junior year. You must be a U.S. citizen or legal inhabitant. Documents are needed at check-in. You need an interest in government, strong leadership and above average grades. A sponsor is needed.
how_to_apply: Find a sponsor (a Legion post, Auxiliary unit, school or other group). Once your sponsor sends your name and email, the site emails you the online registration form. If you have no sponsor, fill out the sponsor request form on the Registration Forms page.
notes: Girls only. You can also send in an optional bill to be considered by the mock state Congress. The program says it is run by volunteers. Email Director.massgirlsstate@gmail.com with questions.

who_can_apply: Boys who finished junior year and have at least one semester left. You cannot have gone to a Boys State before. Leadership, character, grades and service to your school are what count. A parent and a family doctor must sign a medical consent form.
how_to_apply: Fill out the program interest form on the site. You will be told when applications open (late 2026). The application has your information and a short response on what Boys State would mean to you. It also has a reference from a teacher or guidance counselor. You can also ask your local Legion post or guidance counselor.
notes: Boys only (Massachusetts Girls State is a separate program). You are expected to attend the whole week. It falls during many schools' finals, so ask your school about make-up plans early. The interest form link is the one on the home page.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.

who_can_apply: Students at a Massachusetts school with an FFA chapter. The state site lists the chapters (the list includes vocational, technical and agricultural high schools). It does not state an age rule.
how_to_apply: Find your school on the Massachusetts FFA Chapters page. The page does not say how to join, so ask your school how to sign up.
notes: The chapters page lists schools such as Bay Path Regional Vocational Technical H.S. in Charlton, Bristol County Agricultural High School in Dighton and Minuteman High School. Check the full list for your area. The site describes FFA as an intracurricular student group.

who_can_apply: Rising sophomores, juniors and seniors in high school, and seniors who just graduated. The Pre-Veterinary Medicine and Veterinary Technology programs are only for rising juniors and seniors.
how_to_apply: Sign up for updates on the Pre-College page now. Applications for 2027 open in January. They are reviewed on a rolling basis. Scholarship applications use the same online system.
notes: Expensive. This is a college course experience, not a job. The page also lists year-round college prep workshops (fall 2026 workshops are open).

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. Must be 16 by Sept 1.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the program page when applications reopen. The page suggests joining an information session. Questions: mya@mednet.ucla.edu.
notes: Fundraising cannot start until you are accepted. It cannot take place on hospital or clinic grounds. Two excused absences are allowed.

who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from San Diego. The page says the group draws teens from across San Diego County. Limited to 25 students.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application (one per student). Invited students get an acceptance email and onboarding documents. Questions: education@mcasd.org.
notes: Closed for 2026-2027. The program is supported in part by the California Arts Council.

who_can_apply: Applicants must be 13 or in 8th grade at the time of application. They can be up to age 17 or 18 and a senior in high school.
how_to_apply: Complete the Teen Advisory Board Interest Form on the MCPL page; someone contacts you after it is received.
notes: Unpaid volunteer role. The page says there will be more chances to volunteer at MCPL in the coming year.

who_can_apply: The Maryland 4-H pages read do not list an age range. Programs vary by county. Contact your local Extension office to learn which clubs and programs fit your age.
how_to_apply: Contact your local University of Maryland Extension office. Ask about clubs, camps and programs in your county. Then use the Enroll in Maryland 4-H link on the Join a Club page.
notes: Maryland 4-H Center: 8020 Greenmead Drive, College Park, MD 20740, 301-314-9070. The leadership page lists a 2026 Volunteer and Teen Forum in Ocean City in November 2026. It has workshops for adults and teens aged 13 and older.

who_can_apply: Boys who have finished their junior year of high school by the start of the session, in public, private or home school, with at least one semester left. You cannot have attended any other Boys State.
how_to_apply: Apply online using the Apply now link on the Maryland Boys & Girls State site. Accepted students usually hear back in 2 to 3 weeks.
notes: Students under 17 sleep in college dorms, usually two to a room. Phones, smartphones and smartwatches are not allowed. The site recommends against driving yourself because the week is tiring. Staff are mostly veterans.

who_can_apply: Students in a high school agricultural education program. The site says Maryland FFA has almost 3,000 student members in 50 chapters. Age and grade rules are not listed on the pages read.
how_to_apply: Ask your school whether it has an agricultural education program and FFA chapter. The Maryland FFA home page has a Join FFA button and a chapters page.
notes: The 2026 National FFA Convention and Expo is listed on the site for Oct 20 to 24, 2026 in Indianapolis. If your school has no FFA chapter, contact the Maryland FFA office through the Contact page.

who_can_apply: Maryland residents who are seniors at a Maryland public or nonpublic high school and are at least 16 years old. You apply through the school you attend, not where you live.
how_to_apply: Contact your county page coordinator. The page has a list. Get the county's application and find its deadline. The Maryland program page says the coordinator works with your high school.
notes: Each year 105 pages and 36 alternates are chosen from across the state. Program contact on the page: Tawana Offer, Tawana.Offer@mga.maryland.gov, 410-946-5120 (Student Programs). Paid work for people under 18 in Maryland needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=md for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Girls who have finished their junior year of high school by the start of the session, in public, private or home school, with at least one semester left. You cannot have attended any other Girls State.
how_to_apply: Apply online using the Apply now link on the Maryland Boys & Girls State site. Accepted students usually hear back in 2 to 3 weeks.
notes: Students under 17 sleep in college dorms, usually two to a room. The Girls State page lists a Samsung American Legion Scholarship presentation on the last day.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules. You must meet background rules. The pages read do not explain the rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Make a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Fill out the application. Upload the documents that show you are eligible. Then connect with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Center address: 10900 Old Court Rd, Woodstock, MD 21163. No closure notice showed on the pages read on 2026-10-09. The application asks for ID, Social Security number and proof of income. Only enter these on the official jobcorps.gov site, with a parent or guardian. A parent should ask an admissions representative about the rules for 16 and 17 year olds.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 10 to 17. Ages 10 to 13 must come with a parent or guardian. Ages 14 and up can volunteer on their own. A signed parent permission form is required for all youth.
how_to_apply: Click Register on the volunteer page to pick a session. Everyone must register before arriving. Groups of 5 or fewer register one by one. Larger groups fill out the group request form.
notes: The volunteer page does not name its work site. The only address on the contact page is the Decatur headquarters at 3240 Clifton Springs Road. Confirm the site when you register. MedShare does not host court-ordered or required community service.

who_can_apply: Students in high school grades 9 to 12. No age range is stated.
how_to_apply: Watch the page for the next application. Accepted students get an email. Then they send shot records (varicella, MMR) and a TB test within 6 months. They also go to a required orientation by invitation only.
notes: The page covers Long Beach Medical Center only. It does not mention an Emergency Room volunteer role or its age rule.

who_can_apply: Applicants should be in grades 7-12. The page does not state a residency requirement.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked from the library's Teen services page. Questions to David Jimenez, Librarian I, 650-330-2528 or djimenez@menlopark.gov.
notes: Meets the 1st and 3rd Thursdays, 4:30-5:30 pm, at Menlo Park Library (800 Alma St.), and the 1st and 3rd Wednesdays, 4-5 pm, at Belle Haven Library (100 Terminal Ave.). Members may attend one or both. The page is undated and is the only source; older M-A Chronicle articles describe pandemic-era activities and a different meeting pattern, so confirm the schedule with the librarian before the first meeting.

who_can_apply: Must be a City of Menlo Park resident and be entering grades 9-12 for the upcoming academic year and committee term.
how_to_apply: Submit the YAC application form and supplemental questionnaire to the Library and Community Services Department. Staff review applications, schedule interviews and make the final selection.
notes: Competitive, and closed now. Members must attend at least 75 percent of meetings. Contact Da'Shawn Williams, Recreation Coordinator, 650-330-2248. The page lists two email addresses (dlwilliams@menlopark.org and dlwilliams@menlopark.gov); confirm which is current. An older city notice said about 8 hours per month; the current page says about 6. The page does not mention pay, so we list it as unpaid; confirm with the city.

who_can_apply: The squadron welcomes all community members ages 12 to 18. They join its cadet program.
how_to_apply: Fill in the contact box on the squadron's Join Us page with your contact information and a short description of your interests. Email: christopher.ince@cawgcap.org. The squadron meets at 3515 Hardstand Ave, Atwater, CA 95301.
notes: Confirm first: the squadron pages do not list meeting times, dues or the first visit steps. The national Civil Air Patrol cadet page says cadets can join at ages 12 through 18.

who_can_apply: K-12 students. Ask your high school counselor if you are eligible. English C1000 is only open to eligible 11th and 12th graders. K-8 students need a written recommendation from their principal or designee. They also need current transcripts.
how_to_apply: 1) Apply for admission for the semester you want. 2) Turn in the Dual Enrollment Parent Consent Form once during high school, after you get your 7 digit Merced College ID. 3) Complete the K-12 Permit form for your school level. 4) Wait for the email that lets you register in the MC Portal. 5) Pay fees online or at the Student Fees Office. Phone for the Merced campus: 209-384-6000.
notes: This is the college's own concurrent enrollment page. Merced Union High School District also has its own dual enrollment partnership with Merced College (see that separate card). Kinesiology courses with a physical activity part are capped at 10 percent of K-12 seats.

who_can_apply: Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 21 (for example, youth without a high school diploma). Teens 16 to 18 qualify only if they are out of school.
how_to_apply: Use the Click here to apply form on the EMPOWER page, or call 209-381-5926. The office is at 658 W. Main Street, Merced.
notes: Prospero (the Merced County workforce board, formerly WorkNet) lists EMPOWER as its main youth program for out-of-school youth. Prospero Youth Team: 209-724-2036. Confirm first: the page gives no start dates or wage.

who_can_apply: High school students across Merced County. The page lists the ROP at Delhi, Dos Palos, Gustine, Hilmar, Le Grand, Los Banos and Pacheco high schools. It also lists Merced Scholars Charter School. It also lists Valley Community School in Atwater and in Los Banos. Grade rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to enroll. Ask your school counselor, or contact Dora Robles, Staff Secretary, at (209) 381-6684 or drobles@mcoe.org.
notes: Confirm first. The page does not list the courses, grades, cost or how to enroll. The MCOE college and career page also lists the EMPOWER program (see the separate EMPOWER card). It also lists Cal-SOAP for college and financial aid information.

who_can_apply: Students in good academic standing at a Merced Union High School District school (Atwater, Buhach Colony, El Capitan, Golden Valley, Livingston, Merced, Sequoia, Yosemite). Complete the Merced College application, a parent consent form and a High School Permit.
how_to_apply: Apply to Merced College, submit the parent consent form and High School Permit, and talk to your school's Pathway Counselor.
notes: College privacy law applies once you enroll: parents do not get progress updates from Merced College. A college GPA below 2.0 can affect future college eligibility and financial aid.

who_can_apply: Teens must be 11 or older. Volunteering is during the school year, with extra hours in summer for the Summer Reading Program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application and return it to the front desk. An application does not guarantee acceptance. Missing 3 shifts without notice removes you from the schedule.
notes: The page was last updated Nov 12, 2024, so call your branch to confirm. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Female high school students who will finish their junior year in spring 2027. You must have at least one more semester before graduation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online delegate application. The link is on the Michigan Girls State page and the 2027 flyer. Questions go to the Girls State chairman, Beryl Robbins, at berylrobbins1980@gmail.com or (313) 318-6845.
notes: Not a job. A closing date was not on the page or flyer, so apply early. The page also lists a Samsung scholarship and a government manual to read before attending.

who_can_apply: Males who have completed their junior year and have at least one year of high school left, with an interest in government and strong leadership, character and school or community service. Applicants must be a U.S. citizen. Anyone who already attended Boys State cannot attend twice.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on michiganboysstate.org (the 2026 brochure says to visit the website to apply). Pay the $25 application fee and find a sponsor for the $400 program fee. Office: (517) 371-4720 ext. 123 (site) or 517-220-2754 (brochure), legion@michiganlegion.org.
notes: Not a job. Dates, fees and the deadline above are from the 2026 brochure and flyer, so confirm the 2027 details with the office. The resources page still showed a May 1, 2024 deadline, so it is out of date. Office address: 212 N. Verlinden Ave., Lansing, MI 48915.

who_can_apply: Members must be enrolled in a marketing, management, finance, hospitality or entrepreneurship course. Grades and ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's business or marketing teacher about a DECA chapter. Send state questions to the Michigan DECA advisor, Dave Wait. His email is dwait@emich.edu.
notes: Not a paid job. The state website listed on the page is mideca.org. This card is based on the DECA Inc. page for Michigan.

who_can_apply: Students ages 12 to 21 who are enrolled in a state-approved agricultural education course. The page does not list grades.
how_to_apply: Use the chapters and regions page to find a chapter near you, then ask that school about its agriculture class. Questions can go to the state office.
notes: Not a job. The homepage says there are over 10,000 members in 137 chapters. State office: association@michiganffa.org or (517) 353-9221.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students from around the world. The cost page lists no grade rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Sign Up Now link on the Summer Youth Programs page and pay the $150 deposit at registration. Pathway programs have nothing due at application. Contact syp@mtu.edu or 906-487-2219.
notes: Extra costs can include lab fees, a $20 weekly parking pass and charter bus service. Check the Course Catalog and Scholarships pages on the SYP site for current offerings.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 through 18.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Contact it to confirm a meeting. Go to about three meetings before you finish the membership application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Wing HQ mailing address: 43401 N. Jefferson, Bldg. 825, Rm 317, PO Box 450048, Selfridge ANGB, MI 48045-0048. School comes first; the page says school-based squadrons may differ.

who_can_apply: In-school youth ages 14 to 21 who are low income and have at least one listed barrier (for example basic skills deficient, English language learner, homeless or foster youth, pregnant or parenting, disability). Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 with a listed barrier.
how_to_apply: Call Michigan Works! at 1-800-285-WORKS (9675). Or find your local agency by ZIP code at michiganworks.org. Then ask about WIOA Youth eligibility.
notes: Not open to every teen: eligibility depends on income and barriers, so a short call to the local agency is the real first step. The state page does not list a local application form or local youth contacts. Capital Area Michigan Works!' own site (camw.org) mentions WIOA and says 259 youth were served but does not describe its youth program in detail. Work experience for anyone under 18 in Michigan needs a work permit under the state's youth employment law.

who_can_apply: High school students (a separate middle school program exists). The pages read do not list grades. You join through a school or YMCA delegation.
how_to_apply: Check the map on the YMCA page to see if your school or YMCA has a delegation. If not, use the Contact us page to start one. Then register for the conferences your delegation attends.
notes: Not a job. The deadline_iso is the end of regular registration for the February Lansing conference. Fall conference sites include Marquette, Grayling, Allendale, Saginaw, Kalamazoo and Detroit.

who_can_apply: Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 who live in Middlesex County and meet additional eligibility criteria. Not for teens currently enrolled in high school.
how_to_apply: Email opportunityyouthprogram@middlesexcollege.edu to start. Office: 550 Jersey Avenue, New Brunswick, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
notes: The page does not name the funding source. Teens under 18 who are not in school should check eligibility with the office. Paid work for people under 18 in New Jersey needs working papers (online). See permit.html?state=nj for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Commissioners must be in grades 7 through 12 and live in Milpitas. Applicants also complete the Youth Advisory Commission supplemental questionnaire.
how_to_apply: Submit a commission application online, by email, by mail, or in person, with the Youth Advisory Commission supplemental questionnaire. Questions go to the City Clerk's Office at cityclerk@milpitas.gov or 408-586-3001.
notes: Regular meetings at 6 p.m. on the second Thursday of every month, Milpitas Teen Center, Rooms 140/141, 40 N Milpitas Boulevard. Founded April 1996. The page lists current members with terms ending September 2028. Pay is not mentioned on the page, so it is listed as unpaid. The supplemental questionnaire PDF could not be read, so its questions are not summarized here.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 17, entering 10th or 11th grade in fall 2026, and attending a San Diego County high school.
how_to_apply: Online application, then a mandatory in-person interview and group interview if advanced. Contact the museum's Education Specialist or see the program PDF on the page.
notes: Closed for the 2026-2027 cohort. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Minneapolis residents ages 14 to 21 who are not enrolled in college. The Foundations level is for ages 14 to 21; the Pro level is for ages 16 to 21 with previous work or volunteer experience.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the January window. Accepted students (notified by about Mar 10) complete a required in-person orientation in March and April, then are matched with an internship.
notes: Step Up Director phone 612-673-5041; program phone 612-673-5118. The page does not mention work permits. Not every applicant is matched with a paid internship.

who_can_apply: Anyone from kindergarten through one year past high school. Independent membership means you are not in a club. It needs 6th grade or older and at least two years of 4-H club experience. It also needs an adult 4-H volunteer as your mentor.
how_to_apply: Get in touch with local 4-H staff near you, or fill out the interest form. Then complete your enrollment online or with a paper form.
notes: Clubs and costs can differ by county, so contact your county 4-H staff first. This is a youth club and learning program, not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Young men who have just finished their junior year of high school. The Legion says picks are based on merit and ability. A sponsor, usually a local American Legion Post, chooses from students your school recommends.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or contact a local American Legion Post. Forms and delegate information are on mnboysstate.org. For questions, call 651-291-1800 or email jkelley@mnlegion.org.
notes: Boys State is for boys. The 2026 session was June 14 to 20 at Saint John's University. Girls State is a separate program run by the American Legion Auxiliary. The Boys State pages give no age number, only the junior-year rule.

who_can_apply: Students at a Minnesota high school with a DECA chapter. Chapters must have business and marketing courses and an advisor employed by the school. The official pages list no grade or age rule, so ask your advisor.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's DECA advisor, usually a business or marketing teacher. The advisor registers members online. If your school has no chapter, DECA lists six steps to start one. State advisor: Jacklyn (Jackie) Schiller.
notes: DECA's page lists 86 chapters in Minnesota (high school and college counts are not split). The state site mndeca.org lists phone 218-847-5355 and posts role play and judging information. It does not explain joining, so start with your advisor.

who_can_apply: You must be enrolled in an agriculture, food and natural resources (AFNR) course at a school with an agricultural education program. The page lists no age or grade rule. If your school has no program, the site links to how to start one.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or agriculture teacher and sign up for an agriculture course. Joining FFA goes through that class.
notes: The home page reports 218 agricultural education programs in Minnesota. Ask your counselor whether your school has one.

who_can_apply: Any Minnesota high school junior. You can go to a public or private school or be home schooled. Selection is competitive. The program tries to include students from all parts of the state.
how_to_apply: Download the 2027 Page Application PDF from the House Sergeant at Arms site. Email it to EducationalPrograms@house.mn.gov. You also need a 500-word essay. You need one letter of recommendation. It can come from a teacher, counselor or academic advisor.
notes: Participants stay together as a group each evening at the program-designated hotel. Questions: Sergeant at Arms office, 651-296-4860.

who_can_apply: At least 12 and not yet 19. You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (headquarters may waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). You must attend at least three squadron meetings first. Cadets can stay until their 21st birthday.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the Civil Air Patrol unit locator or the Minnesota Wing Locations page. Visit a meeting with a parent. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. Ask whether you can apply online.
notes: Example squadrons: Duluth (MN-016), St. Paul (MN-042), Alexandria (MN-135). Wing office: 6275 Crossman Lane, Inver Grove Heights, MN 55076. This is a youth program, not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Minnesota residents ages 13 to 19 who attend a middle or high school in Minnesota. Four representatives come from each of the eight congressional districts, plus at-large seats. Applicants should be active in their community and know the three branches of Minnesota government.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, then interview in spring. Selected applicants meet the Council director with a trusted adult in May and are sworn in. You may get a follow-up call or text.
notes: The apply page has a caption with an older appointment date from the last round, so trust the Feb 28 and Mar 31 dates above. Full Council meetings are usually one Sunday afternoon a month. Check the apply page again in January 2027.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. (Zoo Ambassador volunteers must be 18 or older.)
how_to_apply: Watch the Minnesota Zoo volunteer page in 2027 for the application. Questions go to the volunteer services email on the page.
notes: ZooTeens do not handle or care for animals; they work with campers.

who_can_apply: High school students prepared for college-level work. Students in 9th grade or below need special approval from the Director of Outreach and Student Development. English and math placement rules apply. No GPA rule stated.
how_to_apply: Apply through OpenCCC, do the placement assessment, submit the Dual Enrollment Form (parent and school counselor signatures, 2 to 3 business days), meet prerequisites, then register in the My Mission portal. Phone (408) 855-5007.
notes: Unit limits: up to 8 in fall or spring (non-MECHS students), 6 in winter, 9 in summer; more needs a petition. Undocumented students are welcome. Getting to campus is on you.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors. MOCA aims for a group with different school, area and arts-access backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Not open now. See mocateens.org and the MOCA Teens page for the next call.
notes: Competitive. Check the page in summer for the next cycle.

who_can_apply: The department says teens interested in seasonal part-time positions can apply. The page I read does not state a minimum age for these jobs. It lists 15 for TeenWorks and 14 for volunteers.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Search and Apply' link on the Recreation employment page to apply for seasonal part-time positions.
notes: Call or check the posting for the minimum age of each job (lifeguard and camp roles usually have their own age and certification rules). Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors in Montgomery County Public Schools with parent or guardian permission. Must be free weekdays Jun 21 to Jul 23, 2027, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.
how_to_apply: Register online (parent or guardian reads the Parent/Guardian Agreement first), choose your top three career areas and in-person or virtual preference. If accepted, attend a mandatory workshop on professional skills and financial literacy.
notes: Hours are set by each host. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer. See permit.html?state=md for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Montgomery County residents who are high school students and at least 15, can work for a full year, attend a mandatory information session, and have a parent or guardian's consent.
how_to_apply: Attend the mandatory TeenWorks information session, interview with the TeenWorks team, then complete the county employment application when the posting is available. Phone 240-777-8080.
notes: The 15 year minimum comes from the Recreation employment page, not the program page. The window dates have no year on the page, so confirm that the fall/winter window is still open. TeenWorks staff are seasonal county employees. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.

who_can_apply: Volunteers without a parent or guardian must be 14 years old. Some jobs have higher age limits. Younger children can volunteer with a parent. This is the Family Volunteer program. The adult must register separately.
how_to_apply: Open the SSL Opportunities list on the Montgomery Parks site. Pick an event approved for SSL hours. Then register. You log in or create a volunteer account. Email parksvolunteers@montgomeryparks.org with questions.
notes: If you need many SSL hours in a short time, the page says that is only sometimes possible. Contacts on the page: Montgomery Parks Customer Service (301) 495-2595, and Volunteer Services 301-495-2504 on the main volunteer page. Office: 2425 Reedie Drive, 12th Floor, Wheaton, MD 20902.

who_can_apply: Rising high school students with interest in STEAM, health or biomedical research and a 3.0 GPA or higher. The research option also needs your latest report card.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. For the research option, also send your report card, an essay about lab research and two recommendation forms. One must be from a science teacher. Some applicants are interviewed.
notes: Costs money. A session can be cancelled if too few students sign up. Contact on the pipeline page: Dr. Ryan Clark, 404-752-1843. Dates shown are from summer 2026.

who_can_apply: High school students who are 16 or older when they apply, in 10th to 12th grade, with at least a 3.2 GPA.
how_to_apply: Send an online application. Add your official high school transcript and one recommendation from a teacher or counselor. List your top three course choices. Test scores are optional.
notes: Costs money. The page also calls the group rising juniors and seniors in places. Confirm your grade with the Summer Academy (academicsuccess@morehouse.edu). Dates shown are from the 2026 summer.

who_can_apply: Teens entering 7th, 8th or 9th grade in the fall. Volunteers can return each summer through high school. After one year, you can move to Science Camp or Tree Monitor.
how_to_apply: Write to youthvolunteers@mortonarb.org and ask about the application. Ask about the deadline too.
notes: Weekday daytime shifts at most branches. Shift hours, fees and training are not listed on the page. The Arboretum's paid science fellowships are for college students, so they are not in the guide. Eagle Scout and Gold Award projects are taken by emailing volunteer@mortonarb.org.

who_can_apply: Teens; the page says age limits vary by program but does not list them. Minimum time: Junior Leaders 1 week, Junior Lifeguards 2 weeks, Deer Hollow Farm interns 3 weeks.
how_to_apply: Follow the application steps on the city page (online account, email, or mail/drop-off at Mountain View Community Center, 201 S. Rengstorff Ave). Questions: TheViewTeenCenter@mountainview.gov.
notes: Age limits are not listed on the page, so email The View Teen Center to check yours. Shifts are weekdays (Junior Lifeguards also Saturdays). Transport to Deer Hollow Farm is provided from the Community Center.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who represent Mountain View teens. The committee has fifteen members plus members-at-large. Residency or school rules are not spelled out on the page.
how_to_apply: Use the application link on the city YAC page. Questions: yac@mountainview.gov or 650-903-6331.
notes: Meets twice a month, August to June, at 4:30 p.m. in person at The View Teen Center, 263 Escuela Ave. Email to ask whether 2026-27 seats are still open.

who_can_apply: Local high school students. The page does not list a grade, age or GPA rule.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application form linked on the summer programs page. A flyer is also posted there.
notes: The same page lists three other programs (FIRE UP, CADET, SCREP) that are for college or graduate students, not high schoolers. The symposium is in person for all summer students. The application form link is the 2026 one.

who_can_apply: Rising juniors from the Metro Atlanta area with a 2.85 GPA or higher and an interest in a health career. An interview is required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Apply Now form. Teacher recommendations, grades and an interview help pick who is chosen.
notes: Costs money. The same page lists a separate college track, which is not for high schoolers. Contact on the pipeline page: Dr. J. Wesley Lockhart, 404-752-1197.

who_can_apply: Bay Area residents who attend a local high school, are at least 15 and have finished 9th grade before it starts. Parent or guardian permission is needed under 18. GPA is not considered.
how_to_apply: Contact Academy@BayAreaMetro.Gov or 415-778-5207. The page does not detail the application steps.
notes: MTC's older 'High School Internship Program' pages date to 2018. The high school program MTC lists now is this Academy. It is mostly virtual evening sessions. It is not a job placement.

who_can_apply: Youth volunteers ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Apply through the museum's volunteer portal (MyImpactPage) via the Learn more link on the Volunteer page. General museum volunteer steps listed: application, background check, new volunteer orientation. Questions: volunteer@lifeandscience.org.
notes: The camp-specific application page returned an error, so the camp schedule, requirements and deadline were not confirmed. The general volunteer perk is a free membership after 100 hours in a year (not confirmed for youth).

who_can_apply: Residents of Albemarle, Charlottesville, Greene, Louisa or Nelson who are at least 17 or entering 12th grade. High school applicants need a college admittance letter or a counselor letter showing they plan to attend college.
how_to_apply: Submit an application form, an essay of at least 300 words, transcripts with GPA, a resume, a college letter, and two reference letters from non-family members, to director@jmrl.org or to the Library Director, 201 East Market St, Charlottesville.
notes: The official source read is the 2026 program flyer (PDF) on jmrl.org; the library's other pages did not list this internship. An applicant cannot receive the award more than twice. Whether a Virginia Employment Certificate is needed for 14 and 15 year olds was not stated (applicants are 17 or entering 12th grade).

who_can_apply: Job seekers from high school students (ages 15 and up) to older adults. Free.
how_to_apply: Walk in. KidsMatter says no registration is necessary. You can try a mock interview, work on a resume and talk about financial literacy there. Questions: sherilyn@kidsmatter2us.org or 630-864-3960.
notes: The Park District says students can use the January fair to plan summer jobs. KidsMatter's 2027 page lists mock interviews, resume help and money skills. Last year's fair also had panels on the 7 Illinois career paths. Confirm what is offered in 2027. A news post from March 2025 also described a spring job fair for summer jobs. Illinois: the Evanston Township High School work permit page says workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before starting.

who_can_apply: Groups of 2 to 5 teens in grades 7 through 12 when the application is sent in.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application during the August 1 to September 30 window. The top three to five teams give a short in-person pitch, and one team is chosen to run its program.
notes: Programs cannot sell products. They cannot be about politics, medicine or religion. The idea has to be new to the library calendar.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be in 9th grade or above. You do not need a Naperville library card. TAG is open to teens in grades 6 through 12.
how_to_apply: Volunteers fill out the online volunteer application. For TAG, write to the teen librarians and ask how to attend. The email is teenlibrarians@naperville-lib.org.
notes: The volunteer coordinator's phone on the page is 630-637-2226.

who_can_apply: Up to 8 sophomores and juniors who live in Naperville. You must live inside the city limits. Freshmen and seniors cannot apply. Students who served on a board or commission cannot apply.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply button on any board or commission page of the city site. Answer yes to the Mayor's Chief of Staff question. Upload a resume or a note about your interest. Say that you are free all year.
notes: The news post does not say whether it is paid. Ask Rachel Pruneda (prunedar@naperville.il.us, 630-420-6018). A full job description is on the city boards page.

who_can_apply: Minimum age differs for each job. Check the age listed on the posting.
how_to_apply: Find a posting on the district job board and fill out the online application for that job. Mail, email or fax is not accepted. Apply for each job separately.
notes: Only applicants chosen for an interview are contacted. The page has a table of when each job is usually posted. Ages and pay are on each posting, so check them before you apply. In Illinois, workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before they start. This comes from the Evanston Township High School work permit page.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 and up can volunteer on their own. Kids' Night Out and Santa's Workshop are open at age 14 (high school freshman). Anyone 14 or younger who is not in those roles needs a parent or guardian with them. BINGO volunteers must be 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Application (17 and under) and approve a DCFS background check, at least two weeks ahead. Then email Becca (address on the Programs volunteer page) to sign up for a program. You cannot just show up, except at Nature Champion days.
notes: Volunteer hours can be confirmed by email, a signed letter or a school form.

who_can_apply: At least 14 years old, finished 8th grade, and not older than 21. Needs a C average or better, and no serious arrests or convictions.
how_to_apply: Download the cadet application and turn it in at the front desk, 1350 Aurora Ave. A committee checks references and does a background check and an interview. Questions: NPDCadets@naperville.il.us.
notes: The police internship on the same site is for college students, so it is not listed. The department points younger people to the cadet program.

who_can_apply: Students in high school or going into high school in fall 2026. You live in Naperville or go to high school there. You need parent permission and your own ride. You need good standing at school and no criminal contacts.
how_to_apply: Print and fill out the application and waiver at naperville.il.us/youthacademy. Send the signed forms to Sergeant Greg Rink at rinkg@naperville.il.us. Or drop them off at 1350 Aurora Ave.
notes: First come, first served and space is limited.

who_can_apply: Students who live inside Naperville city limits. You are a sophomore, junior or senior. Freshmen cannot apply. If you already served on a board or commission, you cannot apply.
how_to_apply: Click Apply on any board's page on the city Boards and Commissions site. Fill in the profile and the student rep questions. Upload a resume or a short statement. You can apply to up to three boards.
notes: 24 positions, two per board. Contact: Rachel Pruneda, prunedar@naperville.il.us, 630-420-6018. The dates come from an August 2026 city news post.

who_can_apply: Open to everyone, and no citizenship is needed. Age rules vary by project: some (GLOBE Observer, NeMO-Net) are marked kid friendly; Growing Beyond Earth is for middle and high school teachers.
how_to_apply: Browse the project list, pick one, and follow that project's own sign-up steps.
notes: Some projects need a telescope or other gear. Projects are free to join.

who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or permanent residents attending a U.S.-based high school; rising juniors, seniors, or college freshmen; unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher; at least one high school biology course; a computer with stable internet.
how_to_apply: Apply online with a PDF high school transcript when the window opens.
notes: The real NASA Ames option for high schoolers. NASA's main OSTEM internships are college-only. Acceptance was rolling through April 30, 2026, and the cap was 1,000 applications, so apply early. Needs a PDF high school transcript. No 2027 dates posted.

who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from Franklin County and surrounding areas.
how_to_apply: Register when the program reopens; contact HNHFWorkforceDev@nationwidechildrens.org.
notes: The hospital's student opportunities page also lists Project SEARCH (a 9-month internship for students with disabilities) and Upward Bound Math and Science. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 16 to 21. Participants must be at least 16 years old at the time of registration.
how_to_apply: Register online during the registration window. Questions: HNHFWorkforceDev@NationwideChildrens.org.
notes: Popular: the page says there is overwhelming interest, and about 108 young adults took part in 2025. Schedules are Monday to Friday starting at 9 or 10 a.m. All participants are 16 or older, and Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) lets 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer give proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement instead of a work permit; the hospital may still ask for paperwork, so confirm.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18 can join the teen programs. Age is counted as of January 1 of the program year. You join through your local county 4-H program.
how_to_apply: Find your county 4-H program. Then enroll through 4-H Online. That is the system for joining, renewing and signing up for events.
notes: The teen page was updated April 30, 2026. Clover Crew is listed as new in 2026. Programs differ from county to county. The pages read do not give a fee or the dates for the teen events.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 5 to 12 who belong to a school FFA chapter, which runs through a school agricultural education program. Homeschool students can join if they take an agriculture course and have an SAE project (for example through the NCSU Agriscience Academy chapter).
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor or agriculture teacher if your school has an FFA chapter. Take an agriculture class. The chapter advisor sends in the roster and dues. Homeschool families use the Homeschool FFA Membership Application on the page.
notes: The state office is at 4111 Beryl Road, Raleigh, NC 27606, 919-515-4206. The site says North Carolina has over 47,000 FFA members. If your school has no ag program, the page explains how a school can start one.

who_can_apply: High school students or recent high school graduates in good academic standing. Seniors may apply to take part the summer before college. College students are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Governor's Page application and send the online recommendation form to two people: a non-relative school staff or faculty member (unless homeschooled) and a non-relative adult who can speak to your fit. Applications without both recommendations are not processed.
notes: Founded in 1973. The work location is the Albemarle building, 325 N Salisbury St, Raleigh. Business clothes are required. Pages and their guardians arrange where to stay and eat in Raleigh. Office of the Governor phone: (919) 814-2000. The page does not list dates for page weeks. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: North Carolina residents in public or non-public schools. You must meet one of the GPA or course rules in the family overview, for example a 3.25 unweighted GPA. You cannot apply on your own. Your school or district must nominate you first.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or local Governor's School coordinator. Turn in the student application at your school, not to the state office. It has one essay or audition and a personal readiness form. Turn in two recommendation forms too.
notes: Competitive. The family overview says about 1,800 students are nominated and about 800 are picked in a typical year. Students must stay the whole session and may attend only once. The overview says you may not use AI on the application.

who_can_apply: Current high school sophomores, juniors and seniors in good school standing. A North Carolina House member must sponsor you. You must not have been a House Page before. School principal approval is needed if you serve during the school year.
how_to_apply: Ask your own House member to sponsor you (find yours with the Find Your Legislators tool). Then fill out the online application, which goes to that member. You can ask the House Page office, Room 1329, 16 W. Jones Street, Raleigh, for a paper copy.
notes: Very competitive and you can apply with only one member. The Speaker of the House makes the final appointments. Housing in Raleigh is up to your parent or guardian. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules. You must meet background rules. The pages read do not explain the rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Make a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Fill out the application. Upload the documents that show you are eligible. Then connect with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Centers: Schenck, 98 Schenck Dr, Pisgah Forest, NC 28768. Kittrell, 1096 U.S. Highway 1 South, Kittrell, NC 27544. Oconaluftee, 502 Oconaluftee Job Corps Rd, Cherokee, NC 28719. No closure notice showed on the pages read on 2026-10-09. The application asks for ID, Social Security number and proof of income. Only enter these on the official jobcorps.gov site, with a parent or guardian. A parent should ask an admissions representative about the rules for 16 and 17 year olds.

who_can_apply: High school girls in grades 9 to 12 who are enrolled in a North Carolina public, private, charter or home school. Rising 9th graders are not eligible. Open to girls from across the state, but all placements are in the Raleigh area.
how_to_apply: Apply when the application portal opens in early January 2027. The FAQ says to check the program website for current deadlines. Email your resume, cover letter and transcript to doa.youth.involvement@doa.nc.gov. Students who skip these documents are dropped from the process.
notes: Only 15 to 20 spots. You must get yourself to your job site every day; the program only gives rides to Wednesday and Thursday events. Contact named on the page: Jean McBride. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. The school calendar followed is Wake County's; the page does not say whether eligibility is limited to the Raleigh area.
how_to_apply: The page gives no step-by-step process. Staff contact is Lynn Cross (listed on the page).
notes: The page did not describe how students are picked.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders. The museum's general volunteer rule is 18 and older; under-18s join through the teen programs.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in mid-January 2027, then attend a group interview if invited. The page does not describe the application steps; contact the listed staff member.
notes: Teens may reschedule up to 3 of the 10 shifts. Other teen programs on the museum's Teens page (Climate Resilience Institute, Cafe Coordinators, Teen Science Cafes) were listed without dates or fees.

who_can_apply: Students in grade 10, 11 or 12 who are in good school standing. A North Carolina senator must sponsor you. If you serve during the school year, your principal must approve it first.
how_to_apply: Contact your senator and ask for an application. It is not online and not available from the Page office. Return the finished form to your senator.
notes: Competitive. Each senator can sponsor only a set number of students. The Senate President Pro Tempore makes the appointments. Business clothes are required. Bring money for lunch each day. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: High school (secondary) and college (postsecondary) students in career and technical education pathways.
how_to_apply: Ask your career and technical education (CTE) teacher about your school's chapter. Your advisor signs you up on the national SkillsUSA registration site. It is linked from the NC join page.
notes: Contacts on the site: information line 919-675-1241, info@SkillsUSAnc.org, P.O. Box 88, Oxford, NC 27565. The March 1 date is described as an annual national deadline, not tied to a named year.

who_can_apply: Academically talented North Carolina students in their second or third year of high school who want STEM careers. Applicants must complete the Residency Determination Service process. Students are picked by Congressional District.
how_to_apply: Apply through NCSSM Admissions. The application is on cfnc.org. Finish the Residency Determination Service step. Write the essays. Have your school send your transcript and teacher and counselor evaluations.
notes: 2027 campuses and dates listed: Appalachian State (June 20 to July 31, to be decided), East Carolina (virtual week June 27 to July 3, then on campus July 4 to 24), UNC Charlotte (June 20 to July 31, to be decided), UNC Wilmington (June 20 to July 17). Accepted students do an online Research Prep course in June. Contact: summerventures@ncssm.edu or 919-416-2747.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors in North Carolina, chosen by American Legion posts. The About page describes the program as for young men in North Carolina. No age or residency rule beyond that is listed.
how_to_apply: Applications open Nov 1, 2026. Local American Legion posts pick delegates. Find a post near you. The FAQ page links a post finder. Or email info@tarheelboysstate.org.
notes: Delegates must attend the full week. The FAQ page says graduates get an automatic $20,000 scholarship to Chowan University, spread over 4 years. The girls' program is a separate American Legion Auxiliary program (Tar Heel Girls State) and is not covered here.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18, per the national Civil Air Patrol page. Cadets join a local cadet or composite squadron, and you may join any one in the wing.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the NC Wing page. Then contact a squadron and visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the membership application and pay dues.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. NC Wing office: 3520 Alamance Road, Burlington, NC 27215, 336-290-7473, info@ncwgcap.org. The NC Wing site lists a 2027 summer encampment page.

who_can_apply: Start as early as age 16. You must be enrolled in high school or be a high school graduate, interested in a high-demand career field, and ready to do both on-the-job learning and classroom instruction.
how_to_apply: Find a Registered Apprenticeship opportunity on the ApprenticeshipNC site and apply by contacting the program sponsor or employer. Questions: apprenticeshipnc@nccommunitycolleges.edu or 919-807-6988. The page also mentions youth apprenticeship consortia that serve high school students.
notes: The NC Department of Labor says youth under 18 who work in North Carolina must have a Youth Employment Certificate, started by the employer once you have a job offer. Some jobs are off limits to people under 18 unless a supervised practice agreement is approved. Specific openings and employers change, so use the Find Apprenticeship Opportunities tool.

who_can_apply: Any high school student in good standing at a public, private, charter or home school in North Carolina. You do not need a legislator to sponsor you.
how_to_apply: The page says to complete the student application, but it shows no link. Contact the program coordinator, Erica Gallion, at (919) 301-1372. Ask for the application.
notes: The page does not say where the application is, what it costs or when it is due. Check the page again or call the coordinator before you plan.

who_can_apply: Open to rising sixth graders through recent high school graduates. For the Junior Wildlife Assistant role you must be in 10th or 11th grade when you apply, live within 90 miles of the zoo, and be able to lift 50 lbs and stand for 30 minutes. Other roles have their own rules on their pages.
how_to_apply: When recruitment opens, choose a teen role on the zoo's Teen Volunteers page. Send in that role's application. Junior Wildlife Assistants also do a 20 minute phone interview. They go to at least two Zoo Pathways events.
notes: Roles listed: Play Pals (middle school), Junior Wildlife Assistant (high school), Camp Crew (middle and high school), Zoo Futures (middle school). Zoo address: 4401 Zoo Parkway, Asheboro, NC 27205, 336-879-7001.

who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade (2026 page). Homeschooled, out-of-state and international students are encouraged to apply. Admission is based on academics (typically A's and B's in math and science) and interest.
how_to_apply: Online application: GPA, school and counselor info, and two short written answers (camp goals and a problem you would like to solve). Each applicant is placed in one workshop.
notes: All dates and the fee on the page are for 2026; 2027 terms were not posted. The Engineering Place also runs day camps for younger students.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. Anyone under 18 must come with a guardian, and you must secure an individual volunteer slot for both the adult and child.
how_to_apply: Register for a shift on the volunteer site linked from the page; a minor and the supervising adult each need their own slot. Questions: volunteer@elijahspromise.org or 732-545-9002 ext. 122.
notes: Wear closed-toed shoes and long pants; expect to stand for the whole shift. Only five people fit in the kitchen at once. Large groups are booked through January 2027.

who_can_apply: College-bound youth from urban communities in Atlantic, Camden, Essex, Hudson, Mercer, Middlesex, Passaic and Union counties, with a B or better GPA, top 25% of the class, and interest in volunteering to help 4-H with STEM programs.
how_to_apply: Online application on the program site (opens early in the year). About 60 students are accepted each year. Contact on the Rutgers 4-H STEM site: Chad Ripberger, ripberger@njaes.rutgers.edu.
notes: Only students in the listed counties qualify. Selected students start with an orientation in May and two short online modules.

who_can_apply: Current high school students ages 16 to 18 (must be 16 by the course start date) with at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA, who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents. Graduating seniors are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Online application plus unweighted transcript, a Parent/Guardian Permission Form and a letter of recommendation (teacher or anyone who knows your work). Reviewed first come, first served; decisions in 5 to 7 business days.
notes: Some courses need extra technology or prerequisite courses. Withdrawing after the add/drop period puts a W on a Rutgers transcript. Questions: summerscholars@rutgers.edu.

who_can_apply: Motivated high school students entering grades 10 to 12 who have completed at least one high school biology course.
how_to_apply: Online application only: about 250-word essay on your interest, high school transcripts or report cards, and your preferred session. Acceptance emails go out in the first week of April; pay within 2 weeks to hold the spot.
notes: Held at EOHSI, 170 Frelinghuysen Road, Piscataway. Questions: THED@eohsi.rutgers.edu. Expect the 2027 cycle to follow the same winter pattern, but confirm on the page.

who_can_apply: Mathematically talented high school students. No specific grade or age is listed. You must submit solutions to the Problems to Explore.
how_to_apply: Four parts: Student Information and Consent Google Form (with a parent), your solutions to the Problems to Explore, a teacher recommendation emailed directly, and a transcript emailed by your counselor.
notes: Residential; students go home on weekends. Page read was the Summer 2026 listing.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18 who have completed ninth grade. Weekday shifts are 4 to 6 p.m. for ages 15 and up, or 6 to 8 p.m. for ages 16 and up.
how_to_apply: Email the Volunteer Director (Jacob.Persily@rwjbh.org) with the teen's name, high school and current grade. Applications are not sent at a parent's request. Then comes orientation. Next is medical clearance. That is a health form from a doctor covering TB screening, immunizations and flu vaccine. Then a drug screen. Phone: 732-937-8507.
notes: Volunteers must be fully vaccinated and wear the provided uniform. The page says internships and shadowing are not offered. A newer and an older version of this page disagreed on hours (75 vs 100 a year); the page read on 2026-10-09 says 100.

who_can_apply: High school students who have completed a high school level biology course. No age or grade range is stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Online application posted on the WISE page; first come, first served. Pay the fee within 2 weeks of approval.
notes: In-person sessions are non-residential at the Waksman Institute on the Busch campus in Piscataway. The year-long Waksman Student Scholars Program (WSSP) is a separate, school-based program that starts with teachers.

who_can_apply: Youth in grades K to 13. The Rutgers 4-H homepage says it serves everyone in grades K through 13.
how_to_apply: Use the Join 4-H form on the New Jersey 4-H site, or find your county 4-H office on the Rutgers 4-H page.
notes: Not a job. It is a youth group. The Rutgers homepage has a Join 4-H form and a link to the New Jersey 4-H Camp. The pages read did not give fees, so ask your county 4-H office.

who_can_apply: Juniors who live or go to school in New Jersey and are legal U.S. residents. You must be fluent in English and able to attend the whole session. You must be willing to take part in nondenominational prayer, patriotic ceremonies, the Pledge and the National Anthem. An Auxiliary unit must sponsor you.
how_to_apply: Contact a local American Legion Auxiliary unit or a county chairperson to ask for sponsorship. The site lists contacts. You cannot apply without a sponsor.
notes: Girls only. Start asking local Auxiliary units in the winter. The 2026 site says sponsorships were already filled. A matching program for boys (Jersey Boys State) is run by the American Legion.

who_can_apply: High school juniors with at least one semester left. Posts pick students with school help, or you can apply on your own as self-sponsored.
how_to_apply: If a post sponsors you, your school staff recommend you. The local American Legion post interviews you. If you sponsor yourself, make an account on the ALJBS CampSite portal. Fill out the questionnaire. Add a 300 to 500 word essay, or a video or a counselor reference. Pay the $50 fee.
notes: Boys only (Jersey Girls State is a separate program). Post-sponsored and self-sponsored costs are in pay_detail.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.

who_can_apply: New Jersey residents who have finished their junior year at a public, private or home school. Applicants must be nominated by their high school (one nominee per 325 juniors). It is competitive. Fewer than 25% of nominees get offers.
how_to_apply: Get nominated by your high school, then submit the online application with essays (admission is based heavily on essays). Contact: njgset@soe.rutgers.edu or 848-445-4753.
notes: Residential at Rutgers School of Engineering, 98 Brett Road, Piscataway. The Application Instructions page on the program site still mentions the Summer 2023 application, so rely on the state page and director for 2027 dates.

who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 25 who do not have a high school diploma.
how_to_apply: Send the online services request form on the NJ Department of Labor page for general questions. The state page does not list sign-up steps, so ask for the site that serves your county.
notes: For teens 16 and up who left school without a diploma. Not for students still working toward a diploma in a regular school. It includes help getting a high school equivalency diploma or an adult high school diploma. It includes counseling and help moving on to college or jobs. Paid work for people under 18 in New Jersey needs working papers (online). See permit.html?state=nj for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 through 12. The page does not list an age rule or a residency rule; it describes students from New Jersey.
how_to_apply: Research a global issue and write a paper with a teacher or mentor, following the guidelines PDF on the page. Register and submit the paper through the World Food Prize website.
notes: The Rutgers page was read through a summarizing fetch tool because the site blocks plain page requests, so check the page itself for the 2027 date. It is listed on the New Jersey 4-H page as a program for high school students.

who_can_apply: Youth from kindergarten up to age 19. A kindergartner must turn 5 by January 1 of the 4-H year. A teen cannot enroll or re-enroll if they will turn 19 before January 1 of the new club year (club year runs Oct 1 to Sept 30). Counties can set their own details.
how_to_apply: Contact your county Cornell Cooperative Extension office. Join a club. If you cannot join a club, you can enroll as an independent member. You work on projects at your own pace with an adult helping.
notes: Not a job. The rules are for New York State 4-H as described by two county Cornell Cooperative Extension pages (Jefferson and Erie). The listed URL is the Erie County page. Your own county office has the sign-up steps and costs.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.

who_can_apply: Youth 14 to 17 can go to the weeks set aside for that age. Campers must be the minimum age by December 1 of the calendar year. The pages do not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Set up a family account in the DEC online registration system. Fill out the camper forms and waivers in the Document Center before registration opens. Then register for a week and pay online. If a week is full, join the waitlist.
notes: This is a camp for campers, not a job. The main camp page still mentions a March 2025 opening, so use the How to Register page for dates. Ask DEC about sponsorships early.

who_can_apply: Girls. Your local American Legion Auxiliary unit picks citizens and alternates, sometimes with interviews, essays or a nomination. The pages read did not list a grade or residency rule, so ask your unit.
how_to_apply: Contact your local American Legion Auxiliary unit. Ask your guidance counselor or email egsregistrar@gmail.com with your hometown, county and school. Join the local selection. Then use the login the unit gives you. Register online and pay the fee.
notes: Girls only. The site says there is a virtual orientation on Zoom in May or June. The program says it is not a sports camp or a recreational camp.

who_can_apply: Strong swimmers who meet the age and certification rules. Outside Long Island, the minimum age is 15 for pool posts and 16 for other posts. On Long Island the minimum is 17 (16 for pool posts only). You also need a background check, a medical form and an interview.
how_to_apply: Fill out the lifeguard job application and email it to the address on the page. Then sign up for a qualifier. Long Island has its own preregistration. After you pass, regional staff tell you the next steps.
notes: The minimum age depends on region (see who_can_apply). Confirm your age with the regional office. The New York Department of Labor page returned an access error. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Youth volunteers must be in 7th through 12th grade and age 12 to 18. The Young Adult Advisory Council (YAAC) is only for teens who live in Newport Beach.
how_to_apply: Teens fill out the online application themselves on the library's volunteer portal (application form number 2) and lead communication with staff. You must attend volunteer training before starting.
notes: Volunteers age 15 and up must complete fingerprinting and a background check. Applying does not guarantee a spot. Questions go to the library's Teen Services team through the email link on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Submit a Teen Leader Application. Qualified applicants may be interviewed and the top candidates are chosen. Selected teens pass a background check, register online and pay the fee. Contact Recreation and Senior Services at (949) 644-3151.
notes: This is a volunteer role with a fee, not a paid job. The same page lists the Mayor's Youth Council (an unpaid internship that runs October 2026 to August 2027, applications May 15 to Sept 4, 2026), but it does not state an age or grade, so it is not listed as its own card.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who live in or attend high school in Boyle Heights. A work permit and proof of authorization to work in the U.S. are required.
how_to_apply: Online application. The link and deadline are posted on the program page each February.
notes: Narrow: ten spots a year (eight new interns and two returning peer mentors) for Boyle Heights students. Transportation is provided.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 15 years old. The page does not list a minimum age for the part-time and camp jobs, so check the posting.
how_to_apply: For jobs, apply on NISRA's ADP Workforce Now site from the Employment page. For volunteering, use the Volunteer Opportunities link on the same page. Call NISRA at 815-459-0737.
notes: The City of Elgin is a member of NISRA. The city says NISRA offers programs at Elgin sites. The 15 week internship is for therapeutic recreation college students. Jobs need a reliable ride. Illinois: the Evanston Township High School work permit page says workers under 16 need a work permit.

who_can_apply: U.S. citizens who are a high school junior or senior at the time of application, with at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA on a 4.0 scale. You must be able to do the full seven weeks and live within 50 miles of the host campus. Families must provide their own housing and transportation.
how_to_apply: Watch for the SHIP job announcement on USAJOBS and follow the application page linked from the SHIP page. The page says to read the application process page for the full steps.
notes: The page lists two NIST campuses (Boulder, CO and Gaithersburg, MD); this card is for Gaithersburg. The 2026 poster session was held in Gaithersburg on Aug 6, 2026. The exact application dates for 2027 were not final on the page read, so check it again in late October.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. CTD uses levels based on test scores. Or it uses a school record and teacher recommendation. Check the course page and the CTD eligibility page.
how_to_apply: Apply online through MyCTD. For admission, you use test scores or a portfolio. The portfolio is your report card and a teacher recommendation. If you have questions, email ctd-admissions@northwestern.edu.
notes: Costs a lot and is for advanced learners. CTD also has many other summer and weekend courses for grades 6 to 12 that are not listed here.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16 years old. For Northwestern Memorial Hospital the age is 18, and it has no summer program. You must pass a health screening and an interview. You must also go to a virtual orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application during the window. Then do an interview. Onboarding includes a health screening and an orientation. Ages 18 and up also get a background check.
notes: Volunteer offices: Delnor, 630-938-2180. Central DuPage, 630-933-6207. Lake Forest, 847-535-6851. Call the one near you.

who_can_apply: Current high school juniors who will be seniors in fall 2027. The page says no exceptions.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form, write a 200 to 225 word essay, list your journalism activities and send up to three work samples. Pay the $55 fee. Your counselor emails your transcript, GPA and school profile to Prof. Roger Boye. Add the financial aid form and a parent tax return if you want aid.
notes: Questions: r-boye@northwestern.edu (email is best) or (847) 491-2069.

who_can_apply: Students rising into grades 9 to 12 the summer they attend. The page asks for a class rank near the top 30 percent and experience or interest in policy debate.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $60 fee. Then send extra materials such as a debate record, a letter of recommendation and your transcript. You need a laptop with a webcam, a mic and Microsoft Word.
notes: The 2026 program was online only. Check whether 2027 is online or on campus. Financial aid and scholarship page exists on the NHSI site but was not read.

who_can_apply: Students in their sophomore or junior year who will be rising juniors or seniors. The page asks for a class rank in or near the top 30 percent. It also asks for proof of special skill or strong interest in media arts.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $60 fee. Then send extra materials. These may include two essays, a resume, a letter of recommendation, test scores and your transcript.
notes: Competitive and costly. Travel is not included. Aid is need-based only. Not a paid program.

who_can_apply: Students in 10th or 11th grade who will be rising juniors or seniors. Juniors get priority. The page asks for a class rank near the top 30 percent and some theatre experience or strong interest.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $60 fee. Then send a resume, two essays, a letter of recommendation and your transcript. Test scores are optional. The Musical Theatre track needs a third essay.
notes: Competitive and costs a lot, but the program says need-based aid is given and does not offer merit aid. Travel is not included. Not a paid program.

who_can_apply: Attendants must be at least 14, lifeguards at least 15, cooks at least 16.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Apply Now' link under the position on the Waterpark Employment page (current listings: lifeguard at Atlantis and Pirate's Cove, water safety instructor at Great Waves and Ocean Dunes).
notes: Atlantis is at Bull Run and Pirate's Cove at Pohick Bay (Fairfax County); Great Waves is in Alexandria and Ocean Dunes is at Upton Hill in Arlington. Virginia rule (Virginia Department of Labor and Industry): 14 and 15 year olds need an Employment Certificate before working; the page read does not list a certificate for 16 and 17 year olds.

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24 who live in San Mateo County or Cupertino, Los Altos, Milpitas, Mountain View, Palo Alto, Santa Clara or Sunnyvale.
