High school students who live outside the area qualify if their school is inside it. In-school youth 17 to 21 need low household income plus justice involvement, unstable housing or foster care.
how_to_apply: Fill out the short interest form on the NOVAworks Young Adults page, then meet a Career Advisor. You can also email youngadults@novaworks.org, call 408-730-7640 or text 408-568-7776.
notes: Narrow eligibility. The FAQ says internships are 18 and up, so a 17 year old gets coaching and training first. Teens under 17 do not qualify. Most applicants need a documented barrier and income under the program limits.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18, permanent US residents, and able to commute daily. Nearly all sites are day programs with no housing.
how_to_apply: Check the NPS YCC page in late January or early February 2027 for the park list and contacts, then apply to the park you want.
notes: Applications are closed right now. Each park runs its own program, so check whether a park near you takes part. Contact the national office through the link on the NPS page with general questions.

who_can_apply: Any high school student in grades 9 to 12. No experience is needed. No grades, essays or recommendation letters are needed. A parent consent form is needed.
how_to_apply: Register on the ACE GNY website. Use the yellow button on the students page. Get a parent to sign a consent form. Pick a team from the map you get by email. Then wait for a confirmation email.
notes: Teams meet at host firms or universities. The page also links to a Summer Internship Program for alumni, which this card does not cover.

who_can_apply: High school seniors (12th grade) who live in one of the five boroughs. You must send a current transcript or report card that shows 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application form linked on the Apollo page. It includes an essay, a transcript or report card, and recommendations. All are due by the deadline. Late or incomplete applications are not read.
notes: The FAQ says accepted interns under 18 must give the Apollo a copy of their New York State working papers before orientation. Ask your school guidance counselor how to get working papers. The Apollo also runs a paid technical theater internship in the summer. The page text about length is not the same in two places. Confirm with the Apollo.

who_can_apply: Rising seniors going into 12th grade in September who live in the five boroughs of New York City. You like technical theater. You must come to the full program and a parent or guardian orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on Formstack before the deadline. The page says group interviews happen by appointment. Accepted teens and a parent or guardian go to an orientation on the first day.
notes: The Apollo Arts Administration internship page says interns under 18 must show New York State working papers. This technical internship page does not say so. Expect to need them for a paid job.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 11 who start in Tier 1 (9th grade), Tier 2 (10th grade or Tier 1 done) or Tier 3 (11th grade or Tier 2 done). No age or borough rule is stated. You do not have to share immigration status for Tiers 1 to 3.
how_to_apply: Apply online (account lets you save progress): short answers plus references, then a group interview. Apprentices must reapply every year. Two references use a separate online reference form.
notes: Tiers 1 to 3 are not employees. Tier 4 apprentices must be legally authorized to work and eligible under NYC Department of Labor rules, per the program page. Partial participation is not allowed. Questions: gap@bbg.org (shown on the page) or 718-623-7252.

who_can_apply: High school students who are U.S. citizens, permanent residents or in the U.S. for other than a temporary purpose, from a low-income household and/or first in the family to go to college. About 60 students are served each year.
how_to_apply: The Program Overview page says to click its apply link (a short link). Phone: 718-289-5855. Ask the program about this year's dates.
notes: The page says low-income means family taxable income at or below 150 percent of the poverty level. Two thirds of participants must be both low-income and first generation. One third must be one or the other. After-school tutoring runs 4:30 to 7 PM on weekdays when the host school does not offer it.

who_can_apply: New York City high school students ages 14 to 19. Twelve students are chosen for each session. The page encourages you to apply again if you were not accepted before.
how_to_apply: Fill out the free online application on the Bronx Museum event page for the session. Educators read the applications and pick 12 students. If you have questions, write to education@bronxmuseum.org.
notes: The fall 2026 application form is closed, so no apply link is listed here. Check the Teen Programs page for the next one. The museum is under renovation but stays open Wednesday to Sunday, 11 AM to 6 PM, at 1040 Grand Concourse. The pages do not say whether a work permit is needed.

who_can_apply: Rising seniors at a high school in any of the five boroughs. You need an interest in the arts, a GPA of 2.0 or higher, and an unofficial transcript.
how_to_apply: Use the Enroll button on the BAM BIAC page, which links to an online form. The page lists the Education Program Manager for questions. Include an unofficial high school transcript.
notes: Only 13 spots. After the program, BAM Education alumni ages 18 to 24 can join a separate paid Creative Career Collective (virtual, Oct to Dec). Pay amount and work-permit rules are not on the page.

who_can_apply: Students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade in New York City public schools.
how_to_apply: The page does not give steps. It says applications usually open at the end of the school year. Check the Youth Advisory Council page or ask the Borough President's office.
notes: The council is run with the Brooklyn North and Brooklyn South high school superintendents and Sadie Nash Leadership Project. The page does not say whether members are paid or where teens must live, so ask the office.

who_can_apply: High schoolers ages 14 to 18 who live in Brooklyn. BRIC picks students from groups with less access to media training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the class page. Attending every class is required to get the stipend.
notes: The class page says students under 18 need working papers from their school. Finishing the program makes you eligible for other paid BRIC work, per the page. The page says eight sessions but lists nine Tuesdays, and gives Dec 9 in one place and Dec 8 in another, so confirm the last date.

who_can_apply: NYC high school age teens. You can apply to only one of the two fellowships. The current page does not list exact ages; the 2023-24 page said NYC sophomores, juniors or seniors, or ages 15 to 19.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. You cannot edit it after you submit. Then you have a virtual interview. After that you get an offer and steps to start.
notes: Pay is called a stipend on the page. Working papers are not mentioned for the fellowships, but BRIC requires them for its bootcamps for under 18, so ask. BRIC also accepts youth under 21 for its film festival.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Beginners are welcome. You must attend every session; if you miss the first day your spot goes to the waitlist.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the class page.
notes: The class page says students under 18 need working papers from their school. Class is at Clarendon Library in Brooklyn, not at BRIC House. The page text says Mondays but its class-times list shows Thursdays (Oct 8 to Nov 26), so confirm the weekday.

who_can_apply: All ages can join. Teens under 16 must be with a parent or guardian the whole time, so teens 16 and up can volunteer on their own. Event volunteer roles are usually 18 and up.
how_to_apply: Make a Volunteer Profile with the Volgistics link on the park's volunteer page. Then pick events.
notes: Coastal Cleanup is best suited for ages 10 and up. Tasks happen outdoors on uneven ground. Ask staff about accommodations.

who_can_apply: Rising 10th, 11th and 12th graders who live in Brooklyn or go to school in Brooklyn. A strong interest in Brooklyn's past.
how_to_apply: The page does not give steps. It says the 2026 application is closed. Questions: CBHEducation@bklynlibrary.org.
notes: Confirm first: pay, exact dates and application steps are not on the page we read (it showed the 2026 application as closed). Ask CBH Education whether it is paid.

who_can_apply: Youth from across New York City. Most classes are ages 14 to 19; the Advanced Portfolio class is ages 16 to 24. You do not need to be an artist.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the Studio Programs page. Questions: Phoebe@groundswell.nyc or Brandon@groundswell.nyc (shown on the page), or call 718-254-9782.
notes: The page we read described the 2025-26 school year, so check the page for the 2026-27 session. Classes are at the Gowanus studio, in person.

who_can_apply: Youth. Ages, grades and how to join are not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the program page. Contact Groundswell: Office@groundswell.nyc or 718-254-9782 (shown on the site), or check the Youth section for application news.
notes: Confirm first. The page does not list ages, pay amount or how to apply. It says murals are made throughout New York City, and one project title mentions Queensbridge House.

who_can_apply: High school students in 11th or 12th grade, and college students, who like health careers. You must also be processed as a hospital volunteer. That means a form, a medical packet, an in-person interview and a 3-hour orientation.
how_to_apply: Send the intern application and the under-18 release form. Add a short essay (500 words max) on why you want it. Add proof of vaccination (COVID and flu) and two short recommendation letters. Then you have a 15 to 20 minute virtual interview. Questions: Volunteer@maimo.org or 718-283-3980.
notes: Unpaid, so no work permit. Students under 18 may only volunteer 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday to Friday, per the page. Check the page for the year of each deadline.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page says volunteers range in age from 14 to 90 but does not state a minimum teen age. All volunteers need medical clearance, references, an interview, a background check and orientation.
how_to_apply: Download the High School Student Application Packet from the volunteer page. Email it to Volunteer@maimo.org. Or mail it to Department of Volunteer and Student Services, 5014 Fort Hamilton Parkway, Brooklyn, NY 11219. Phone 718-283-3980. They send medical clearance forms after they get your application.
notes: Students under 18 may not volunteer outside 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday. The page says volunteering does not lead to a paid job at Maimonides. Some programs (Feeders, Summer Youth) go through partner schools.

who_can_apply: High school students entering their senior year. Strong essay needed. You must be free Monday to Friday for all four weeks with no vacation or summer classes.
how_to_apply: Email the form and an essay as one PDF to Volunteer@maimo.org. Put "Science Scholars" and the year in the subject line. Add a parent waiver form. If accepted, you also finish the hospital volunteer form, the medical packet and an in-person interview by May 20.
notes: Formerly named Women in Science. Led by the Chief of Colon and Rectal Surgery. Incomplete applications are not looked at. Accepted students also go through the hospital volunteer process. Ask whether it is paid.

who_can_apply: High school students who will be between 15.5 and 18 years old. U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or international students with a valid F-1 visa. All experience levels are welcome.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Pratt PreCollege form. It opens in November. Students are billed in mid-April and payment is due right away. Scholarship forms are separate. Email: precollege@pratt.edu (listed on the page).
notes: Scholarships go to students with strong art work and big money need. The FAQ says winners usually come from homes with income of $60,000 or less. Pratt also has shorter options. They include an Explore program, an online summer program, Saturday classes and one-day workshops.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 for the Teen Service Series. The Park Pitch In weekends are open to teens 14 and up, adults and groups. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Register online for each event through the Alliance volunteer page. Registration is required. Questions: (718) 965-8951. The phone number is listed under Contact Us.
notes: Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit. Some events have age limits, so check the age on each event. The Junior Volunteer Corps is for youth groups with children ages 4 to 13.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 or freshman year of college. The commuter option is for students who live in or near NYC. Academic strength is what the admissions team looks for.
how_to_apply: Online application. Columbia says applications are reviewed on the dates-and-deadlines schedule; early registration is cheaper to plan around.
notes: Expensive; the page says financial aid details are elsewhere and they were not read. The commuter page still shows a $95 application fee under a Summer 2026 cost heading while the cost page for Summer 2027 says $80. Free Columbia programs for NYC teens (Double Discovery Center, Freedom and Citizenship) exist but their pages blocked access, so they are not listed.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors based in the New York City area. You must come to every weekly meeting at the museum.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Smithsonian application system (SOLAA). The application has short answer questions, an essay and two references. The references are adults who are not related to you. A teacher or mentor works. You can save and finish later. A virtual info session was offered. See the page.
notes: Meets at 2 East 91st Street and some offsite places. The page says the demographic and citizenship questions are optional and not tied to your application. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed. Cooper Hewitt also runs free monthly Teen Drop-In workshops and a Design Career Fair.

who_can_apply: New York City public or charter high school students in grades 9 to 12. The page says students meet a mix of these: attend a school without a full visual arts program, qualify for free school meals, or come from a low or moderate income household. No art experience needed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online registration form on the Saturday Program page when it is open. No recommendation letter is needed. You get an email when you are accepted. Sign up for the mailing list on the page for the next opening. Office phone and email are on the FAQ page.
notes: Classes are at the Foundation Building, 7 E 7th Street, and 41 Cooper Square. The FAQ page still shows the 2024-2025 year in places, so trust the main page for current dates. There is a year-end show for families.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18. You are a rising sophomore to rising senior or the same level.
how_to_apply: Fill out the registration form and pay tuition to enroll. The page also links a scholarship section for the Jeffery and Paul Gural Merit Scholarship for NYC Public School Students. Questions: the program email is on the page.
notes: This is a commuter program on campus. The page does not give housing or college credit. The page lists the 2026 year; check the mailing list for the 2027 price.

who_can_apply: Current high school students who have finished 9th, 10th or 11th grade. Rising 9th graders are not eligible. Open to students from anywhere, but New York City students get priority for financial aid. Some courses need strong math or chemistry grades.
how_to_apply: Apply online when applications open on Dec 11, 2026. See the FAQs on the Summer STEM page for the aid process. The program is selective.
notes: Classes are in person at 41 Cooper Square. The page lists 2026 prices: $3,150 for a 3-week course and $5,150 for a 6-week course. Check the 2027 numbers when applications open.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 19 who completed 10th grade by the program start, live in the NYC area (or arrange a supervising adult and housing), and are U.S. citizens or permanent residents at U.S. curriculum schools. No interview or minimum GPA.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcript, two recommendation letters and short essays (250 to 300 words each). Contact: summer@tech.cornell.edu.
notes: Cost is not stated on the page read, so confirm the price and any financial aid with the program before applying. Selective. International students are not admitted at this time.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24 who are not in school and not working. You need at least a 5th grade reading level. The Advanced Training track needs a high school diploma or HSE.
how_to_apply: The page has no application form. Call DYCD Community Connect at 1-800-246-4646 to find a provider near you.
notes: The page lists these training areas: Healthcare, Construction, Transportation and Culinary Arts. It also lists Digital Marketing. Direct Service Professionals is listed too. It does not say if you need a work permit.

who_can_apply: 2025 FAQ: rising high school seniors or college students ages 16 to 24 who can legally work in the U.S. and have some prior paid or volunteer work experience.
how_to_apply: Fill out the SYEP application online at application.nycsyep.com and choose a Ladders community partner. Selection uses a personal statement, transcript and resume, then workshops, mock interviews and employer interviews (2025 FAQ).
notes: Competitive. Eligibility, pay and process come from the 2025 FAQ because no newer FAQ was found, so check the DYCD page when applications reopen. Interns under 18 need NYS working papers (NYS Department of Labor). Free to apply.

who_can_apply: NYC high school juniors and seniors who live in New York City, are low income (or meet an exception such as public assistance, foster care or living in a high-poverty area) and meet at least one other listed need. The page lists age 16 to 21 in one place and 14 to 21 in another, so ask a provider.
how_to_apply: Contact a Learn & Earn provider from the DYCD list, or call DYCD Community Connect at 1-800-246-4646. Providers check your eligibility.
notes: Income-based, with extra eligibility rules listed on the page. Teens under 18 need NYS working papers (NYS Department of Labor). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 who live in the five boroughs of NYC and are legally allowed to work in the U.S. Some options (school-based, NYCHA, foster care, homeless youth) have extra rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online at application.nycsyep.com or on paper with an SYEP provider. One application only. Community-based placements are picked by random lottery. Have ID documents ready (proof of age, identity, address, Social Security).
notes: Pay and hours above are the 2026 numbers and may change. Free to apply. NYS Department of Labor says anyone 14-17 needs working papers (employment certificate) to hold a job in New York State; ask your SYEP provider what they need from you. Teens in school-based (CareerReady) options apply through their school. You pay your own transportation and meals.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 16 to 24 who are not in school and not working. The page also lists a high school diploma or equivalent, U.S. work authorization, and Selective Service registration (for males).
how_to_apply: The page has no application form. Call DYCD Community Connect at 1-800-246-4646 to find a provider near you.
notes: The page says the program is for ages 16 to 24 who are not in school and not working. Target industries are Infrastructure, Healthcare, Technology, Media and Government. The page does not state the pay rate, the program length or whether a work permit is needed.

who_can_apply: NYC residents legally allowed to work in the U.S. who took part in the 2026 Summer Youth Employment Program as CareerReady (ages 16 to 19 in a CareerReady partner high school) or in Special Initiatives (ages 16 to 20, in high school or a high school equivalency program), as of Oct 26, 2026.
how_to_apply: Use the WLG online application (CareerReady or Special Initiatives link), or ask your SYEP provider for help. If selected, submit documents online or in person to your provider.
notes: Only for teens who were in 2026 SYEP through a partner school or Special Initiatives provider, so most teens cannot start here. Internet access is required. The application deadline has passed. Teens under 18 need NYS working papers (NYS Department of Labor).

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors attending a New York City high school. Not every accepted student is matched with a site.
how_to_apply: Online application with short-answer questions and a resume, then an interview with the Futures and Options team. Then they try to match you to a site. Use the interest form on the page to get a notice when it opens. Questions: programquestions@futuresandoptions.org.
notes: Pay rate, season and length are not on the page, so confirm first. Futures and Options is based in Manhattan but serves NYC students from every borough. It also runs Career Essentials workshops (the fall application closed Oct 7, 2026).

who_can_apply: New York City students who are about to graduate from high school. You like business, finance, government or public policy.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the program page. You will be told when the application opens.
notes: The page says 930 students have been ULF interns since 1996 and alumni have received $1.7 million in scholarships. Rate and dates are not stated.

who_can_apply: Driven high school juniors who are on track to graduate and allowed to work in the U.S. You can have a lighter class load in senior year for the internship. Students at partner schools apply in the fall or winter of junior year.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Genesys Works site and pick New York. If accepted you get an email to interview for a spot in summer training. You provide your own transportation to training and to the internship.
notes: The page says Genesys Works works with set schools, so ask your counselor if your school is a partner. The direct New York link on the location page gave a not-found error. Use the main Apply Now button or email info.nyc@genesysworks.org. Many schools give credit for the training and internship.

who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or permanent residents who come from a low-income household and/or are first-generation college students (neither parent has a bachelor's degree). The program checks income with tax papers such as a 1040. Grade levels and school lists are not stated on the pages read.
how_to_apply: Ask the program for the forms by email. You need the application and the recommendation forms. The Eligibility and Selection page lists who to write to: the Program Director or the Curriculum Coordinator. The form asks about you and your money. It also asks for a personal statement.
notes: This is a federal TRIO program that gets funding from the U.S. Department of Education. The pages do not say how many students are accepted or which schools it serves. Ask the program before you plan around the summer dates.

who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled in 10th or 11th grade. Not residential.
how_to_apply: Step 1: fill out the Program Registration Form. Step 2: pay with the Program Payment Form. Both steps are needed to confirm a spot. The contact is listed on the page.
notes: The page says to register early because the program has hit its limit in past years. Confirm that registration is open before you plan around it.

who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled in 10th or 11th grade. Not residential.
how_to_apply: Step 1: fill out the Program Registration Form. Step 2: pay with the Program Payment Form. Both are needed to confirm participation. The contact is listed on the page.
notes: Confirm that registration is open before you plan around it. The page also lists a free Summer Engineering Awareness Program. It lasts six or ten days.

who_can_apply: Any high school student.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Institute Registration Form to pick your weeks, then pay for each week with the Program Payment Form. Both steps are required to hold a spot.
notes: Contact details are on the page. The registration and payment forms are separate, and both are needed. The form link uses the old Manhattan College name. The form page did not load as text, so confirm it is open before you plan around it.

who_can_apply: Motivated high school students. The page lists students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Use the pre-college sign-up form linked on the O'Malley program page when it reopens.
notes: Manhattan University is in Riverdale in the Bronx. Check the page for 2027 prices and dates.

who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled in 10th or 11th grade who are entering their junior or senior year. You must stay in the residence.
how_to_apply: The page lists the School of Engineering contact for details. The phone is 718-862-7281. The email is deanengr@manhattan.edu. No sign-up form is linked for this program.
notes: Parents can come to the closing ceremony and final project contest. Other short summer engineering programs on the same page cost less or are free.

who_can_apply: Students now enrolled in 10th or 11th grade. The page says selection is based in part on strong math and science skills and interest in engineering.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application form. It says to complete the registration form, and the page lists the program director, Dr. Walter P. Saukin, at 718-862-7171 (Monday to Friday, 9:30 AM to 4 PM). Call to ask how to apply.
notes: The school is now called Manhattan University, formerly Manhattan College. The page says the program has run for over 40 years. The page lists a free program. It comes with a certificate and no fee to apply at Manhattan University. The page lists an email for the director that does not match the director's name, so call instead. Confirm the steps with the director.

who_can_apply: Students 16 and older. Some roles, such as Maternal Child Health, require 18. Montefiore also partners with SYEP. Its SYEP provider is Children's Arts and Sciences Workshop.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Summer Volunteer - High School posting on Montefiore's career site (linked from the volunteer page), then attend an orientation and interview. Interviews are first come, first served.
notes: Confirm first: the dates are from the 2025 posting. Contact: volunteerservices@montefiore.org (shown on the page).

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 15 or older. JuMP is for ages 15 to 17 and requires full availability for all six weeks. Unit Support is open to high school students. The emergency department and some other roles are 18+.
how_to_apply: Online application, one letter of recommendation from a non-relative, and a resume.
notes: Read through the fetch tool because direct downloads were blocked. The page says volunteers need a valid Social Security number (a hospital clearance rule on the official site) and pay for their own medical clearance. Other Mount Sinai campuses have their own pages and age rules that were not read.

who_can_apply: High school students interested in health care who can attend the full month. The page wants motivated, mature students with volunteer experience. Ten students are accepted.
how_to_apply: Watch the Lenox Hill volunteer page for the next call for forms. If you have a question, write to the Manhattan campus volunteer team. The email is manhattancampusvolunteers@northwell.edu.
notes: The page is out of date, so check with the volunteer team to see if there is a 2027 program. The regular junior volunteer program has different rules and needs working papers.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16 at the Manhattan hospitals. Junior volunteers (ages 16 to 17) hand in working papers and a parent consent form. All applicants are interviewed, then there is a six-month trial period.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the Lenox Hill volunteer page. There is an interview. There is a required orientation. You also need a medical clearance. Questions? Write to manhattancampusvolunteers@northwell.edu.
notes: The page says junior volunteers (ages 16 to 17) must submit working papers and a parental consent form. Orientation and medical clearance are required. Volunteers 18 and older must pass a background screening. The page asks for 100 hours a year. The page gives a minimum age of 16 and no maximum age.

who_can_apply: Grades 9 to 12. The application form says weekday internship options are only for Partnership School students, so check which options you can apply for.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application by the deadline. Complete applications get an invite to a group interview at the Children's Adventure Garden. Accepted teens attend orientation with a parent or guardian and 24 hours of training before starting.
notes: Questions: explainers@nybg.org. Intern tier is unpaid, so a work permit is not clearly needed there; the paid tiers are jobs and the page does not say what papers are required. The orientation date printed on the page shows the wrong year, so confirm it with NYBG. Late applications roll to the next session.

who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 16 (18 for some programs; check each campus). The Queens and Hudson Valley campuses do not offer Summer Only volunteering. Spots are limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application and choose Summer Only plus your preferred program and campus. A volunteer services representative contacts you for an interview if a spot is open.
notes: Many NYP roles (emergency department, palliative care and others) are 18+. Brooklyn Methodist also runs a Junior Volunteer Program that was marked full when searched; its own page was not read for details. This entry covers the system-wide Summer Only option only.

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old at the start of the program. Under 18 cannot volunteer during the school year. The year-round program is 18 and older.
how_to_apply: Online application, a group information session, full summer availability, onboarding, health clearance (TB test, MMR and varicella proof, flu shot) and a background check.
notes: The Brooklyn campus requires age 18+. Long Island has its own teen program (not read in detail). The FAQ page still shows old 2022 dates, so only the Manhattan page was used for dates. Med-career internships and research are handled separately through HRNTV@NYULangone.org. The Manhattan page and the volunteer page do not mention working papers, so the work permit answer is unknown.

who_can_apply: Full-time NYC residents who attend NYC schools, applying as 10th or 11th graders (rising juniors and seniors), with strong grades and interest in STEM. Students from groups underrepresented in STEM are encouraged to apply.
how_to_apply: Online application (optional recommendation due after), a group interview and lab tours to pick your placement.
notes: Selective with limited spaces. Funded by the Pinkerton Foundation. Students present at an AMNH poster symposium at the end. The two NYU pages differ slightly on grade wording (10th or 11th grade now versus rising juniors and seniors), which is the same group. The program name on a second page reads Applied Research In Science and Engineering. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Students in 10th grade at a New York City high school. You show strong effort in school. Most Fellows apply with a GPA of 87 or above. You come from an under-resourced community. Your household income (AGI) is under $125,000. You should not already have similar college and career help. You must commit to the whole program.
how_to_apply: Sign the interest form on the Apply page to get an email when the application opens. The online application takes a couple of hours. It needs your transcript, family facts and two recommendation forms. One is from a teacher. One is from a counselor or advisor. Chosen applicants are invited to group interviews. The page puts these in late March.
notes: Admitted Fellows must come to all days of the Summer Institute. A family member must come to an orientation. The application asks for household income. The program uses it to check the income limit. The pages do not say if a work permit is needed.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older by the first day of work. The test page said 16 by July 18, 2026. You must swim 50 yards and meet the vision rule.
how_to_apply: Register for a qualifying test on the Parks page when dates open (or join the notice list). Pass the swim and vision test, then do the training. A letter from an eye doctor can replace the on-site vision exam.
notes: The two Parks pages disagree on the swim time. The main page says 50 yards in 50 seconds or less. The test page says 50 yards in 40 seconds or less with proper form. Plan for the faster one. The pages do not say whether a work permit is needed for 16 and 17 year olds.

who_can_apply: Students entering high school in New York City. The program starts with career exploration in 9th grade, and college courses can begin as early as 10th grade. The page does not list entry rules for each school.
how_to_apply: The page says admission is unscreened (Educational Option method). Attend an information session, open house or high school fair, then rank a P-TECH school as a top choice on your high school application. Check each school's process on its website or at MySchools.nyc.
notes: This is a school choice made before 9th grade, so it fits 8th graders and their families. The page names five schools in Manhattan and the Bronx. Examples are Inwood Early College for Health and Information Technologies and Urban Assembly New York Harbor School. Check each listing to see how students get in.

who_can_apply: High school students who are seen as leaders at school, often through student government. Members are voted in at the borough meetings. Each year, two student reps are voted onto the Panel for Educational Policy.
how_to_apply: There is no open form on the page. Ask your school counselor or student government adviser how students are chosen for the borough council. Elections for the Chancellor's council happen at the borough meetings.
notes: There are six borough councils: one in each borough, with two in Brooklyn. The page does not list contacts or meeting dates. It is a leadership role, not a job.

who_can_apply: Students at least 14 and now in high school. You can be outdoors for 2 hours. You have your own ride to the site. You pass an interview. You come to 5 of 6 classes.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the internship page, then do a virtual interview. Contact: Erica Chow (email on the page).
notes: This is a learning internship, not a job, and it costs $200 unless you get aid. You must find your own transportation. Supported by Con Edison and other funders per the page. The page says 5 of 6 classes in its eligibility section but 6 out of 7 dates for spring and fall, so ask which applies.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 17. You must attend an interview and an orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Volunteer form on the volunteer page. Return it to the volunteer coordinator before the deadline. Then you have an interview and an orientation.
notes: The page lists deadline months, not the year. Popular program, so apply early.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students ages 12 to 18. Only the student should fill out the application, not a parent.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the form on the program page. Applications only, no walk-ins.
notes: Popular program with an acceptance step and a waitlist. Mostly outdoors, weather permitting. The museum is the Queens County Farm Museum.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. Junior volunteers cannot serve on weekends or late evenings.
how_to_apply: Call Volunteer Services at 718-670-5952 to book an in-person interview. No walk-ins. Bring a valid ID (state, school or passport), a working permit and one professional letter of recommendation. Then you need medical clearance (doctor form, urine drug screen, flu shot). You also go to a 4-hour orientation.
notes: The hospital lists a "Working Permit" as a requirement for junior volunteers. This may mean New York working papers. Ask the Volunteer Services office which work permit paper they accept. The page says volunteering does not guarantee a job. Hospital address: 4500 Parsons Blvd, Flushing.

who_can_apply: Teens, with a focus on BIPOC and other under-served Queens youth. The page does not list exact ages, grades or home address rules, so ask the museum.
how_to_apply: Send in the QTI 2026-27 form through the Submittable link on the Queens Museum announcement. Phone 718-592-9700. Email info@queensmuseum.org.
notes: This is the fifth year of the program. Ages, grades and work-permit rules are not stated on the announcement, so ask the museum.

who_can_apply: New York City residents who are currently in high school or college in New York City. You do not need to love science. NYSCI wants curious students who will try new things and practice public speaking.
how_to_apply: Online application form (linked from the page). You can also fill out an interest form to get a reminder and an invite to an info session. Questions: ebautista@nysci.org (listed on the page).
notes: NYSCI is at 47-01 111th St., Corona, Queens. The youth page lists "Young Adults, Age 14-24" in the site menu; the Explainer page itself does not state a minimum age, so confirm. The apply form link on the page showed as closed when read. Pay rate not stated. Work permit not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors with a cumulative average of 92 (no test scores needed), or an average of 90 plus an SAT of 1210 or an ACT of 25. An interview may be required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application with a parent consent form and an unofficial transcript. A counselor recommendation form and the official transcript come next. Contact: 718-990-7533. The number is on the page.
notes: Costs money and is for strong students. Check the page in spring for 2027 dates and price.

who_can_apply: Current high school juniors or seniors who are at least 16 when the program starts. Students from outside NYC and outside the Tri-State area may apply but get no help with housing or travel. No GPA minimum. Sophomores are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Online application plus a letter of recommendation and a transcript (to confirm you are in high school). Selected applicants get a Zoom interview.
notes: Very competitive (about 32 students a year). You must attend the entire program with no gaps. Minors cannot work with human patients. You may not use SSRP work in science competitions. The program page labels its glance box SSRP 2026 but lists the 2027 dates. Contact: program administrator listed on the page, 1230 York Ave.

who_can_apply: Young women and gender-expansive youth in 10th or 11th grade who live in New York City or Newark and can come in person once a week. No academic rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the link on the Leadership Scholars page. Questions: Charlie Ambrose, charlie@sadienash.org (listed on the page).
notes: The page lists the New York City office at 247 W 37th Street, Suite 705, New York, NY 10018. Stipend is based on participation.

who_can_apply: High school seniors who are women or gender-expansive youth of color and live in New York City or Newark. No academic rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the link on the Nash U page. Questions: Charlie Ambrose, charlie@sadienash.org (listed on the page).
notes: The apply page says you must identify as a woman or gender-expansive person of color. You must commit for the full internship.

who_can_apply: Young women and gender-expansive youth in grades 9 to 12 who live in New York City or Newark. You commit for the whole program. No academic rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the link on the Siblinghood Academy page. For questions, write to Cielito Pareja at cielito@sadienash.org. The page lists this contact.
notes: No more than 5 absences for the in-person version.

who_can_apply: Young women and gender-expansive youth enrolled in high school who live in New York City or Newark and have not done Summer Institute before. No grade or skill rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Apply Now page when the cycle opens, then join a group interview. Sign up for the opportunities email list to hear when it opens. Questions: nashers@sadienash.org.
notes: For young women and gender-expansive youth. The Brooklyn, Queens and other borough sites are part of the same program.

who_can_apply: New York City high school students ages 14 to 18 in grades 9 to 12. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the Apprenticeships page when it opens each March.
notes: Pay is not stated, so ask whether it is paid and whether working papers are needed. The site says the program has run for decades.

who_can_apply: Staten Island high school students in grades 11 and 12. The hospital does not take volunteers under 18 in its general volunteer program. So this is the program for younger students.
how_to_apply: Download the application. It is a PDF on the program page. Email the finished form to the program email on the page: Medicalscienceprogram@rumcsi.org.
notes: Session dates, start month and cost are not stated, so call or email to confirm before you plan. The general RUMC volunteer program requires age 18 or older.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors. No age rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Send the application form, a one-page essay (500 words max) about your goals, and a parent or guardian signature. You can apply online, by mail or by email. Contact: lifelong-learning@wagner.edu, 718-390-3221.
notes: Ask the office whether spring 2027 spots are open and whether the internship is paid.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 years old and older who are in high school. Adults over 18 join the regular Docent program.
how_to_apply: Use the Docent application form linked on the zoo volunteer and job page. Candidates must pass the 10-week course. Volunteers go through a background check.
notes: The 2026 class deadline had passed when we read the page. Check the page around late summer for the next class. Teens learn public speaking and animal presentation skills.

who_can_apply: Teens who are at least 14 years old. You must be able to work on your own and on a team and be available on a regular basis. Some roles (like animal diet prep) are adults only.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer application form linked on the zoo volunteer page. All volunteers go through a background check. The zoo cannot give status updates. It only contacts qualified candidates.
notes: Limited spaces. Volunteers in animal care jobs must show a negative TB test and proof of COVID-19 vaccination, per the page.

who_can_apply: High school-aged youth. No photography experience needed. To get the stipend you must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident or otherwise eligible to work in the U.S., and show valid working papers when accepted.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application (link on the Expanding the Walls page) by Nov 6, 2026. Show valid working papers when you are accepted. Questions: use the contact email on the page.
notes: Meets at 144 W 125th Street. The FAQ on the page still shows the 2026 dates in one spot; the headline dates for 2027 are Jan 9 to Aug 5, 2027. Public school holidays are observed. The page does not state an age range or whether you must live in NYC.

who_can_apply: Open to all NYC youth, including current students and recent graduates. No experience needed. The page gives no age range.
how_to_apply: Email youth@transalt.org with questions or use the RSVP link on the Youth Activist Committee page. Meetings are hybrid, and in person is encouraged.
notes: The page describes youth activism and does not mention a work permit. The page lists meetings on the last Friday of each month from 4:30 to 6 PM, and says meetings are hybrid. Confirm before you go.

who_can_apply: New Yorkers ages 14 to 18. The program page does not list other rules.
how_to_apply: Check the NYC Votes Youth Ambassadors page for the next call for applications.
notes: Run by the City of New York Campaign Finance Board. Past ambassadors registered voters at public events and with other city agencies. The pages do not say whether the work is paid or needs a work permit.

who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school, 15 years old by July 1 of the program year, eligible to work in the United States. You must be free on weekends and for the full 13 months (June to June). The 2026 page said June 2026 to June 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply to Wave Hill when applications reopen. Watch the ACES page for news. If you have questions, write to education@wavehill.org or youthprograms@wavehill.org.
notes: Wave Hill House, where this program meets, is wheelchair accessible. Interns travel off site for some field trips.

who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school, 16 years old by May 1 of the program year, a New York City resident eligible to work in the United States. The 2026 page asked for May 1, 2026.
how_to_apply: Apply to Wave Hill when applications reopen (watch the Forest Project page). Pay runs through SYEP, so you also need a separate SYEP application; for 2026 that was due before March 1. Wave Hill tells interviewed teens which SYEP provider to pick. Questions: youthprograms@wavehill.org.
notes: Fieldwork is hard physical work outdoors with heavy tools on unpaved ground. The Ecology Building has 28 stairs and is not wheelchair accessible. You must be ready to join all of the program.

who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school, 15 years old by July 1 of the program year, a New York City resident eligible to work in the United States. The 2026 page asked for July 1, 2026. You must be free for all 14 months.
how_to_apply: Apply to Wave Hill when applications reopen (watch the WERM page). Questions: youthprograms@wavehill.org.
notes: Courses are taught at Wave Hill and the University of Mount Saint Vincent. Fieldwork is outdoors on rough ground with heavy tools. The Ecology Building is not open to wheelchairs. The page names partners such as the American Museum of Natural History.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 22 at any of the five WCS parks. No borough rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form to be told when recruitment opens. Questions go to the park's volunteer email (discoveryguide@wcs.org for the Bronx Zoo).
notes: The apply link is the interest form, not the application. WCS also lists 30+ internships and paid jobs for ages 14 to 24 (WCS Career Lattice) and the Youth JIVE job and volunteer expo in early February. Those pages did not state ages or dates for individual internships, so only this program is listed.

who_can_apply: NYC high school students. YI Artists: grades 9 to 12. YI Arts Careers: entering grades 10 to 12. YI Introductions: entering grades 10 to 12 who are English Language Learners. YI Leaders: grades 11 to 12 who finished at least one semester of YI Artists or YI Arts Careers.
how_to_apply: Online form for each program (links on the Youth Insights page). YI Leaders is for teens who have already done another Youth Insights program.
notes: The page's closing note also lists YI Introductions graduates as eligible for Leaders. That conflicts with its Open to line. The page lists no program contact. Use whitney.org/contact. The Whitney also runs a separate Open Studio for Teens (free).

who_can_apply: NYC public high school students at one of the 130+ schools with CTE programs. Students who finish a state-approved program can earn a CTE endorsement on their diploma.
how_to_apply: Browse programs on NYC MySchools. Talk to your guidance counselor or a Family Welcome Center about admissions and enrollment.
notes: This is a school choice, not a job. Ask your guidance counselor or a Family Welcome Center how enrollment works for your grade. The CTE endorsement needs 44 credits, 5 Regents exams, a technical assessment and work-based learning.

who_can_apply: Students at participating NYC public high schools. Juniors apply for the apprenticeship.
how_to_apply: Ask your school if it participates. Juniors apply for apprenticeships through the program. The page does not list an application link.
notes: Only at participating schools; the page does not list which ones. Apprentices attend school mornings Monday to Thursday and all day Friday, and work Monday to Thursday afternoons. Apprenticeships are registered with the NYS Department of Labor. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12, per the page. The page does not list residency rules.
how_to_apply: Complete the application on the LETAB page. Questions: mhs@oppl.org.
notes: The page has an Apply now button and says questions go to mhs@oppl.org. It does not give dates.

who_can_apply: The page says boys and girls at least 14 years old are invited to learn new skills and gain work experience.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer form and waiver on the volunteer page. Volunteers also go through a criminal background check.
notes: The page says the volunteer background check applies to volunteers. Ask whether it applies to under 18.

who_can_apply: Open to job seekers. The page does not list minimum ages. Check the age on each job posting.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online job form. You can upload a resume and cover letter. Hiring supervisors review it. The district cannot talk about forms with anyone but the person who applied.
notes: The page does not say when seasonal hiring opens. Check it in winter. Inclusion partner jobs are handled by WSSRA, a partner group. Illinois: the Evanston Township High School work permit page says workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before starting.

who_can_apply: Must live in Oakland. No work experience needed. Free. Partner groups set their own ages (for example YEP 14 to 18, Youth UpRising 14 to 21, Lao Family 16 to 21).
how_to_apply: Pick a partner from the City list (YEP, Youth UpRising, Lao Family, Trybe, Rising Sun, Destiny Arts, Soccer Without Borders, YouthBeat, Alameda County Office of Education GCGI-GET) and apply on that group's site or by phone.
notes: City Council approved more than $3.1 million for 2026 and 2027 summer youth jobs, so a 2027 round is expected. Another City page lists ages 16 to 21, so check each partner's own age rule. Under-18 workers need a work permit (OUSD Linked Learning can help OUSD students).

who_can_apply: Oakland youth ages 16 to 21, per this City page.
how_to_apply: Contact Lao Family Community Development (510) 533-8850, Youth Employment Partnership (510) 533-3447, or Trybe (510) 985-9915. OWDB email: OWDB@oaklandca.gov.
notes: This City page is older than the MSYEP page (which lists partners with other ages, such as YEP 14 to 18 and Lao Family 16 to 21). Treat 16 to 21 as the safe range and confirm with the partner.

who_can_apply: Open recruitment for the City's recreation jobs; the page does not state a minimum age (lifeguards and many City jobs need 16 or older). Spanish, Cantonese and Mandarin skills are encouraged.
how_to_apply: Apply at governmentjobs.com/careers/oaklandca. Questions: parksandrec@oaklandca.gov, (510) 238-7275.
notes: The hiring process takes several months, so apply early. Check each posting for minimum age and pay. The governmentjobs.com/careers/oaklandca portal showed 0 openings on Oct 7, 2026. If you cannot find the posting, call (510) 238-7275.

who_can_apply: Teens who join through the library teen volunteer application: ages 13 to 17, or 18 and still in high school. The TAB page itself states no age rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application and choose 'leadership', or ask your branch teen librarian.
notes: Meets monthly at Main (TeenZone), 81st Ave, Asian, Cesar Chavez, Dimond and Rockridge. The same page also covers the Oakland Youth Poet Laureate program.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17, or 18 and still in high school. Also takes teens with court-ordered service hours.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen Volunteer Application, or stop by a branch.
notes: The library cannot promise a spot at a specific branch. About two thirds of library volunteers are teens, per the page.

who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade interested in animal care or environmental education.
how_to_apply: Online form with a cover letter (500 words max) and resume or transcript, then an interview.
notes: Up to 6 interns, so it is likely competitive. No stipend is listed; ask. Financial aid is available for the $50 fee.

who_can_apply: Must be 13 or turning 13 in the application season. Zoo page lists grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application, interview, then attend both mandatory training days.
notes: Unpaid, and teens pay a small fee (aid available). Must be 13 or turn 13 in the application season.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 for Teen Assistant (no experience needed). Paid Teacher and Administrative Intern roles are for grades 11 to 12 with previous camp experience and one letter of recommendation. All roles need at least 3 one-week sessions.
how_to_apply: Each role has its own online application (Volgistics link on the Oakland Zoo page). Interns also need one recommendation letter. A required training day is held in May.
notes: Great first step: be a Teen Assistant, then apply to be a paid intern. The 2026 info meetings were in March and the 2026 training was Sunday May 17; expect similar timing for 2027.

who_can_apply: You must be at least 16 to work at the annual OC Fair. Some jobs require 18 or older. Applicants 17 and under must provide a valid work permit, available through their school, unless they have already graduated from high school. You must show documents proving identity and work eligibility in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Read the Fair's jobs page, then contact Human Resources at (714) 708-1563 or humanresources@ocfair.com. The page lists no application link.
notes: The page does not describe an application link or a pay rate, so call or email HR to ask when summer 2027 hiring opens. Applicants 18 and older must pass a background screening.

who_can_apply: Teens are typically 12 to 17, but each branch sets its own age range, so check with your local branch. Court-ordered community service is not offered.
how_to_apply: Contact your local branch to confirm there is an opening. Once a spot is confirmed, fill out the OCCR Volunteer Registration Form, print it, and drop it off at the branch.
notes: The registration form is shared by several county agencies, so some questions may not apply to you. Ask your branch what it needs. Arrive on time and tell the branch as early as you can if you miss a shift. OC Public Libraries points teens who need court-ordered hours to the OneOC Court Referral Program.

who_can_apply: In-school young adults ages 14 to 21 who are low income (free or reduced-price lunch counts) and have at least one barrier: basic skills deficient or English learner, offender, homeless/runaway/foster, pregnant or parenting, or disabled. Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 who are not in school (adult education is allowed) and have a barrier such as dropout, offender, homeless/runaway/foster, pregnant or parenting, or disabled.
how_to_apply: Fill out the READY S.E.T. OC interest form (Interest and Eligibility Assessment) linked on the page. Services are delivered by a network of regional providers, which the page does not name.
notes: Federal WIOA program, so eligibility rules apply (income and barriers). Cost to the student is not stated on the page. Questions: County Directory Assistance 855-886-5400. Many teens will not qualify, so read the eligibility list first.

who_can_apply: Eligibility is based on age and grade as of January 1 of the project year. Any youth age 9 or older can do a project, whatever the grade. Eligibility ends December 31 of the year you turn 19. You must join an authorized Ohio 4-H club or group.
how_to_apply: Contact your County Extension Office to be connected with a club. Go to a first meeting. Pick a project. Then enroll in 4-HOnline with your club volunteer or the county office. Do it before the county deadline.
notes: Club membership, not a paid job. The site menu has a Just for Teens section that was not read. The ohio4h.org home page was down (503) when tried, so only the join page was read.

who_can_apply: Students who interview in their junior year for the next summer's program. That means incoming seniors from across Ohio. Local American Legion posts sponsor delegates. The pages read do not list other rules.
how_to_apply: Ask a counselor, administrator or history teacher if a Legion post is interviewing at your school. If not, use the Apply or Become A Delegate form on the site. The program will match you with a post. Chosen delegates go to an orientation.
notes: Not a job. Office phone is 513-529-3860. The site describes the program as drawing over 1,200 young men a year.

who_can_apply: Members must be enrolled in a career-technical education program approved by the Ohio Department of Education and Workforce. Grades and ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's career-technical or business teacher about a DECA chapter. State questions go to the Ohio DECA advisor, Drew Goldfinger, at Drew.Goldfinger@education.ohio.gov.
notes: Not a paid job. Your school must have an approved career-technical program with a DECA chapter. The state website listed on the page is ohiodeca.org.

who_can_apply: Students at schools with an Ohio FFA chapter. The membership page does not list grades or ages. Ask your chapter advisor.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's FFA chapter advisor to add you. Chapters submit membership through FFA.org. Schools with no program can contact Ohio FFA about starting a chapter.
notes: Not a job. The homepage reports 30,880 members in 345 chapters. State office phone is (614) 387-7575. The September 30 and November 30 dates are chapter deadlines, so a student should ask the advisor early.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. You must be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (national headquarters may waive this for some non-citizens). You must attend at least three squadron meetings first.
how_to_apply: Find a cadet or composite squadron with the unit locator. Visit with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the application. Some squadrons take it online.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Ohio Wing office: 6031 E Main Street, PO Box 301, Columbus, OH 43213, phone 614-338-8198.

who_can_apply: Middle school (6th to 8th) and high school (9th to 12th) students. You join through a local delegation run by a school or YMCA.
how_to_apply: Join or start a delegation at your school or YMCA in the fall. New delegations can email yg@ohioymcas.org or call (614) 407-4819. Students and advisors register on the State Assembly registration page.
notes: Not a job. The registration page still showed the 2026 assembly dates, so check it for the 2027 dates.

who_can_apply: Tutors are ages 13 to 18, love working with young kids, have a B or higher in high school math, and bring a laptop.
how_to_apply: Sign up to volunteer on the OneInMath site. Use the register-volunteer page.
notes: The pages read do not list chapter locations. The tutor page's library news mentions North Texas libraries, so ask the group which library near you has a chapter.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

who_can_apply: Students in high school, college, grad school or medical school who are interested in health care and innovation. You must be at least a high school freshman. You need to be on site 40 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Apply on the CHOC website when the form opens. Interviews are rolling, so apply early. You are admitted by form and interview.
notes: The page links to a CHOC volunteer page but does not state its age rule here. Hospital and outpatient shadowing rotations are 18 and up. Business casual dress is expected.

who_can_apply: Girls in 9th to 12th grade. The four-week externship is for 11th grade girls.
how_to_apply: The program page has a Contact Us link. Ask the Girls Inc. Programs Team how girls sign up.
notes: For girls only. Past host companies named on the page include PepsiCo, Edwards Lifesciences and Disneyland Resort. Confirm dates with Girls Inc. first. The 2026 host flyer says girls get a minimum of 50 hours of training; the page says up to 40, so ask Girls Inc. which is current.

who_can_apply: Current high school students. You need a parent consent form and one Dual Enrollment Release Form. Concurrent students also submit a Concurrent Enrollment Release Form from their high school every term. High school students cannot register for a college class without a valid release form on file.
how_to_apply: Apply to Golden West College (new students create an Open CCC account) and write down your CCCID number. Then turn in the consent forms and get your high school's approval. Dual enrollment classes are taught at your high school, so your counselor adds you to the roster. Concurrent students use a Concurrent Enrollment Release Form and register in MyGWC. Questions: dualenrollment@gwc.cccd.edu.
notes: The consent form also covers Coastline College and Orange Coast College in the same district. Only one parent consent form is needed for all high school years. The page says tuition is free, but students may still owe college fees and course costs. It offers a Foundation financial aid form and a possible fee waiver.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors from anywhere in Orange County. The 2025-26 group came from 9 school districts and was chosen from over 100 applicants.
how_to_apply: Application steps are not listed on the pages read. Email langsonteens@uci.edu to ask.
notes: The museum is named UC Irvine Langson Orange County Museum of Art on the page. Confirm dates and any stipend with the museum first.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 18, or 16 with parent permission. You must pass a background check and give at least 36 hours a year. The page does not give a separate age rule for OC Zoo roles.
how_to_apply: Complete the brief interest form linked from the OC Parks Volunteers page and tell them the work that interests you. Pass a background check and attend training. For short term opportunities, search the activity listing. Questions: volunteer@ocparks.com.
notes: Volunteers 16 and 17 need parent permission. The page lists historic docent, backcountry patrol and OC Zoo roles. It lists others too.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 who want to take their leadership to the next level. The page does not list other eligibility rules.
how_to_apply: Apply in spring. The page does not link a form, so email Nadia Khodadadi at OC Pathways (address on the page) to ask how to apply.
notes: Ask your school CTE teacher or counselor too. Confirm the spring dates with OC Pathways.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 with a 2.0 GPA or higher, no arrests or convictions, and fire-safe grooming. Anyone over 18 also does a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Cadet Interest Form on the OCFA site to join the interest list. Later, people on the list are asked to finish a longer form.
notes: OCFA serves many Orange County cities. Ask which cadet post is nearest to you.

who_can_apply: High school students, called special admit students. Students in grades K to 8 need approval from a Santa Ana College dean.
how_to_apply: Use the New Students page on the Dual Enrollment site. Contact the Dual Enrollment Office at dualenrollment@sac.edu or (714) 564-6931.
notes: If you go over the unit limit you pay the enrollment fee for all units, not only the extra ones. The office is closed on Fridays in summer.

who_can_apply: High school students (special admit students). Students in grades K to 8 need approval from an SCC division dean. High school students sign up through the SCC Dual Enrollment Portal.
how_to_apply: Apply to SCC. Make your dual enrollment profile in the portal with your SCC student email. Send a course request. Then confirm your enrollment. Phone (714) 628-4764 or earlycollege@sccollege.edu.
notes: SCC is phasing out the paper Special Admit Form for high school dual enrollment. It now goes through the portal.

who_can_apply: High school students and young creatives ages 14.5 to 19. No grade level is listed.
how_to_apply: Use Register Now on the Summer of Art page. Questions: soa@otis.edu or 310-665-6850. Scholarships have their own application.
notes: The page says ages 14.5 to 19; min_age is entered as 14 because the field takes whole years. Costs money. Prices shown are the 2026 numbers. In 2026 the early discount deadline was April 25. The April 16, 2027 date is the scholarship deadline, not the registration deadline.

who_can_apply: OUSD students (the page also says Alameda County high school students for the Peralta Summer Institute). Some internships are open to all; others go through your career pathway.
how_to_apply: Fill out the district Summer Internship Common Application. It is a Google Form linked on the OUSD page. For school-year internships, ask your pathway lead teacher or your school's work-based learning lead.
notes: The OUSD page still shows Summer 2024 forms, so look for a new form in January 2027. Not every internship is open to every student.

who_can_apply: OUSD high school students.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's Linked Learning or pathway coordinator, or call the district at (510) 879-8000. The office also processes work permits for students.
notes: The office handles work permits (needed for any paid job under 18). Check the pathways pages on the OUSD site to find work-based learning at your school.

who_can_apply: Current high school students who live in the Northeast San Fernando Valley. It is hard to get in. A parent or guardian must come to a required orientation.
how_to_apply: Not open now. If you have questions, write to aguau@pacoimabeautiful.org or call 818-899-2454.
notes: Pacoima Beautiful also lists Bee Wise, Agua Academy and YUTEP on its youth page. No details were posted for them.

who_can_apply: Current high school students in the Northeast San Fernando Valley with a 2.0 GPA or higher. Returning participants are not eligible. No age range is listed.
how_to_apply: Not open now. Selected students must provide a valid high school work permit. Questions: jfr@pacoimabeautiful.org or 818-899-2454.
notes: Classes run 8:00 AM to 2:30 PM and field days 8:00 AM to 1:00 PM. Dates may change each year.

who_can_apply: Students in the grades listed for each role. You must finish the volunteer application and have it accepted before you can sign up for events.
how_to_apply: Click Apply Now on the volunteer page and finish the form. Then sign up for service projects on the events calendar.
notes: Service projects sign-up opens two weeks before each event.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17. Morning or afternoon sessions.
how_to_apply: Register for a CIT or Lead CIT spot when Enjoy! summer camp registration opens on Feb 4, 2027. To get on the teen volunteer email list, email rebecca.passarello@paloalto.gov.
notes: Same page lists the Ceramics Apprentice Program (16 and older, 2 years of Art Center ceramics or instructor approval, 2 hours a week, one training session). Spots may fill fast once registration opens.

who_can_apply: Grades 8 to 12. Rising 8th graders can join in summer. You must live or go to school in Palo Alto, Menlo Park, Mountain View, Los Altos, Los Altos Hills, Portola Valley or East Palo Alto.
how_to_apply: Submit the TLAB volunteer application in Better Impact, finish the paperwork in Docusign, then go to an in-person Livescan fingerprint appointment. Contact libraryteens@paloalto.gov.
notes: Fingerprinting is required. Log your hours in Better Impact or the library cannot confirm them.

who_can_apply: High school students. Needs an online application, a letter of recommendation (returning members are exempt), an intro video and an interview with a nominating committee. Residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application, recommendation letter and intro video by the deadline, then interview with the nominating committee.
notes: Check the current deadline with Mitchell Park Teen Services (3700 Middlefield Rd, or @mpteenservices on Instagram and Facebook). Pay is not mentioned on the page; treat as unpaid until confirmed.

who_can_apply: High school students. Needs an online application, a letter of recommendation (returning members are exempt), an intro video and an interview with a nominating committee. Residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Online application, recommendation letter, intro video, then an interview with the nominating committee, once applications open.
notes: Pay is not mentioned on the page; treat as unpaid until confirmed. Term length is not stated. Contact Mitchell Park Teen Services (3700 Middlefield Rd).

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students. Dual enrollment is only at partner schools. These are in the Arcadia, El Monte Union (Rosemead High), La Canada, Pasadena, San Gabriel, San Marino, South Pasadena and Temple City districts. Grade and age rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Apply at OpenCCCApply. Pick courses with your counselor. Then send the Recommendation form. A counselor and a parent sign it. If you are under 18, send the Medical Consent form too. Send your latest unofficial transcript as well. Then turn on your LancerPoint account and register. Questions: outreach@pasadena.edu.
notes: Do not email documents to the outreach address; upload them as the page says. Check with your counselor which classes your school offers.

who_can_apply: Volunteer jobs are for ages 15 and over. Ambassador is open at 14 with a parent or guardian. Anyone under 15 must have a parent or guardian who also volunteers at all times.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a coming virtual orientation on the volunteer page. Then go to the training for each job you pick.
notes: The page does not say which roles are only for adults. Kids ages 6 to 14 have separate roles (Shelter Greeter, Boredom Busters). Those need a parent who volunteers too.

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 and up who live or go to school in Pasadena.
how_to_apply: Send your writing or art to the teen librarian (email on the page). To help with the magazine, fill out the library's Teen Volunteer Application. Limits: poetry up to 40 lines, short fiction up to 1,000 words, book reviews 250 to 500 words.
notes: The library page does not say the age rule for the Teen Volunteer Application, so ask the teen librarian. Teen librarian contact is on the page. The page does not say whether contributors are paid.

who_can_apply: K-12 students, through their school or district. The Pathful site lists logins for schools and does not describe individual student sign-up.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor whether your school has Pathful. Login pages are listed on pathful.com (app.pathful.com/login).
notes: The home page names Pathful and Pathful Junior and does not use the name Pathful Explore. It is a school-run tool; individual students likely cannot join without a school plan.

who_can_apply: Any child ages 5 to 18 who lives in Pennsylvania. Ages 8 to 18 (before January 1 of the current year) can join the program and take part in contests. Ages 5 to 7 are Cloverbuds. They do non-competitive activities.
how_to_apply: Look up your county 4-H program. Pick a club. Talk with your county educator. Then sign up in 4-H's ZSuite. If you cannot enroll online, ask the educator for help.
notes: A youth group, not a job. Ask your county educator what clubs and teen leader roles are near you.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in agricultural education at a school with an FFA chapter. All students in agricultural education are on the official roster. The page does not state an age rule.
how_to_apply: Sign up for agricultural education at a school that has an FFA chapter. Use the Chapter Locator on the Pennsylvania FFA site to find one near you.
notes: The state page says nearly 16,000 students are members, in four regions. Members compete at chapter, regional, state and national events. The National FFA Organization has its own listing in other cards. This one is the Pennsylvania state page.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 in Pennsylvania: public, private, parochial or home schooled. You need an adult sponsor (a teacher, parent or scientist). You must do your own research and your own presentation.
how_to_apply: Pick a research category. Find a sponsor. Use the Find Your Region page for your region's deadlines, forms and location. Turn in any required SRC/IRB approval forms.
notes: A science fair, not a job. Your project may need extra approval forms depending on your research field, so ask your sponsor or Regional Director early. Regional pages list the exact deadlines.

who_can_apply: Boys who live in Pennsylvania, have finished their junior year and have at least one semester of high school left. You cannot have gone to a Boys State before. Leadership, character and school service count.
how_to_apply: Register online on the Keystone Boys State site when registration opens. Posts also sponsor students; use the Legion post locator on the Pennsylvania Legion page.
notes: Boys only. A matching Girls State program is run by the American Legion Auxiliary, not this one. Check the Boys State site for the 2027 location and dates, because 2026 was at Messiah University.

who_can_apply: Girls in Pennsylvania. The pages read do not state grade, citizenship or cost rules, so check the application.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply tab on the Keystone Girls State site (the home page links an application for 2027). The old FAQ says to print and mail the form, then fill out a parent packet before camp. Check with a local Auxiliary unit for sponsorship.
notes: Girls only. The FAQ on the site is still from 2023, so confirm this year's dates, deadline and cost with the program before you plan. The national Auxiliary list shows June 21 to June 26, 2026 while the state site shows 20-25 June 2026.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18 at the start of the program. High school students. Crews are based in cities across Pennsylvania.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Student Conservation Association (SCA) website. The state page links to the current openings. It links to the application too. You can email paoutdoorcorps@thesca.org.
notes: Crew locations change by year; check the SCA page for this year's list. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: High school students from Oakland, Berkeley and Alameda. Needs counselor and parent or guardian signatures on the High School Special Enrollment Form.
how_to_apply: Meet your counselor, apply to a Peralta college, submit the High School Special Enrollment Form, give transcript and photo ID, meet a college counselor, then register.
notes: Peralta also runs a free Summer Institute for Bay Area high schoolers including incoming 9th graders (2026 dates were June 22 to July 31; no application deadline posted). The old OUSD page mentions a stipend; the Peralta page does not.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 24 in Prince George's County. Placements are by random lottery. The county's main SYEP pages were blocked for my reader, so residency and work-eligibility rules are not confirmed here.
how_to_apply: Apply online at syep.mypgc.us during the spring window. Eligible applicants are entered in a random lottery for a placement. Questions: syep@co.pg.md.us or 301-883-6200 (from the county release).
notes: Facts come from the County Executive's official March 1, 2026 bulletin; the county SYEP web pages returned Access Denied to my reader, so confirm at syep.mypgc.us. Highly in demand, so apply the day the window opens. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.

who_can_apply: Youth must reach the required age on or before May 31. It is 14 for Summer Playtime and 15 for Summer Day Camps. Youth cannot volunteer at a site where a younger sibling or child is a registered participant. Ages 15 and older need a criminal background history check.
how_to_apply: Sign up through the Volunteer Opportunities page of pgparks.com. Each youth may volunteer at only one Summer Playtime or Summer Day Camp site. Transportation is not provided.
notes: Dates for the 2027 season are not posted on the page. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: About 20 high school-age youth who live in Prince George's County. No other rule is stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Email your name, resume, school information and a list of extracurricular activities to the contact named on the page (301-446-3416 for questions).
notes: The same page lists other teen programs (Teen Arts Council, Teen Vocal Showcase for ages 10 to 18, Teen Nights for ages 10 to 17). Unpaid, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14 (library system rule). VolunTEEN is for grades 6 to 12. The Kids Achieve Club welcomes teens over 15. Volunteers cannot staff the Circulation or Information desks.
how_to_apply: Get a volunteer application from your local branch. Ask for the volunteer coordinator. For VolunTEEN, sign up through the Beanstack app.
