notes: The page says volunteers must be vaccinated and that the library is accepting volunteers; check with your branch for the current rule. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Minimum age is 14. The page lists no teen-specific roles; ask which positions accept teens.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked on the page, then email the Volunteer Coordinator at volunteers@ansp.org about specific openings.
notes: The page does not say which areas teens can join. Bird Safe Philly runs April to May and September to November.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors in Philadelphia. The page does not state an age range or residency proof.
how_to_apply: The program page gives no intern application steps. Contact info@philaculture.org or 215-557-7811.
notes: Pennsylvania's Department of Labor and Industry page says children need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer. The permit is not mentioned on the program page.

who_can_apply: Philadelphia residents ages 12 to 24. In-school youth get priority. You can apply to one program per cycle.
how_to_apply: Apply through the C2L-PHL Youth Portal (phila.gov/c2l-phl). Documents: photo ID, school records, Social Security card, birth certificate or passport, and a work permit. Not first come, first served. Help: C2LPHL@jevs.org or 833-750-5627.
notes: Application is English only; call for help in other languages. Roughly 8,000 city-funded slots a summer (per PYN's site). Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18. The Pennsylvania Wing page lists Become a Cadet as ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: The squadron page does not describe a visit process. Contact the squadron: cc214@pawg.cap.gov (squadron commander) or 215-531-2278. The wing's Join CAP page has the cadet steps.
notes: The Pennsylvania Wing lists five other squadrons in the Philadelphia area. They are Willow Grove, Liberty, Griffin, Gen Carl A Spaatz and Chester County. Ask the wing which is closest to you. The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors with a biology, chemistry or research background. Admission is competitive.
how_to_apply: Submit transcripts and two letters of recommendation. Contact camp assistant Ipatia Daigle (ied26@drexel.edu) or director Dr. Jed Shumsky (js52@drexel.edu).
notes: Drexel runs other Summer Institutes (arts and sciences, business, engineering, design, nursing, public health); their pages did not list grades, costs or dates when read.

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old who finished both high school biology and chemistry. Neither can be taken at the same time. Open to students in the Philadelphia Tri-State area. You can apply to a Philadelphia-only section.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google form application. It cannot be saved, so a PDF version is available to draft offline. Two letters of recommendation are required. One must come from a science or STEM teacher who has known you at least a year. Applications are blind reviewed. Then three committee members interview 20 to 25 applicants.
notes: The FAQ says the application launches in mid to late October, so it may open any day now. Check the page for the real dates. General Fox Chase number: 888-369-2427. A summer fellows track is funded by National Cancer Institute grants. Its pay and rules are not stated on the pages read.

who_can_apply: Students living in Philadelphia and surrounding areas who are entering 9th grade, interested in STEM, able to commit to four years, with a 3.0 GPA (per FAQ). Non-freshmen are rarely accepted.
how_to_apply: Online application, essay, transcript, two recommendation letters, then an interview with Youth Programs staff.
notes: The FAQ timing and the 'currently closed' message are not fully consistent, so confirm on the page. The sister middle-school program PACTS is for grades 6 to 8.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: the Philadelphia campus page lists transportation and no dorms. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

who_can_apply: Students now in high school or college from the greater Philadelphia area, including Camden, NJ. You must be able to prove you can work in the United States. No age or grade is stated. The committee gives strong preference to students from groups underrepresented in science.
how_to_apply: Use the MSAP Applications page on monell.org when it opens. Sign up for Monell's newsletter for updates. Questions: AcademicAffairs@monell.org or 267-519-4700. About 200 applications come in each year. 18 to 24 students are usually enrolled.
notes: Minors do not need working papers to apply. They must get them after they are admitted. They come from the School District of Philadelphia, per the Monell FAQ. The Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says minors under 18 need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer. Monell does not provide housing or meals. Students must commit to the full program with no vacations.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 22 at the high school sites. Ages 10 to 13 are served at middle school sites. A parent or guardian must sign and provide extra information before a youth under 18 can be enrolled.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Inquiry Form on the Mural Arts enroll page. It is not an application and does not confirm enrollment. An Art Education staff member follows up about classes near you. Contact: natalie.gearin@muralarts.org or (215) 685-0750.
notes: The pages say 3 high school sites and 6 middle school sites on the enroll page but 16 sites in total on the program page, so ask which site is near you. Mural Arts also has paid summer work experience through Career Connected Learning (see the C2L PHL card). Ask whether classes are free. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older to work as a city lifeguard; you can attend the screening at 15.
how_to_apply: Choose a pool and contact its supervisor, train with Aquatics staff to pass the screening, then finish the Red Cross certification and pre-employment steps. Contact: lifeguard@phila.gov.
notes: Free training is at Lincoln High School and Friends Select School. Pennsylvania's Department of Labor and Industry page says children need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer; workers under 16 also need a parent statement (Form LLC-75).

who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 14 to 24. Residency is not stated on this page (the parent C2L-PHL program requires Philadelphia residency).
how_to_apply: Not described on this page; positions come through C2L-PHL. Questions: PPRC2L@phila.gov or 215-683-3683.
notes: Check the C2L-PHL listing for the actual application. The page I read had not been updated after Summer 2025. Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says work permits are required for minors under 18 hired to fill a position; the Parks and Rec page itself does not mention permits.

who_can_apply: Students who live in Philadelphia. You must go to a Philadelphia public, Catholic, private or charter high school. You need a minimum GPA of 3.0.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page on the program site when it opens in January 2027. You will need a high school transcript with fall 2026 grades. You need a 250 word essay about yourself and your interest in the program. You need an up to date vaccine record.
notes: The two pages word the grade rule differently (currently 9th or 10th on the apply page, entering 10th or 11th in fall 2027 on the main page); they describe the same group. Office: St. Leonard's Court, Suite 110, 3819 Chestnut Street, Philadelphia, PA 19104; contact form at https://vpse.upenn.edu/smp/contact-us/.

who_can_apply: Current 9th to 11th graders (Pre-College: 10th to 11th).
how_to_apply: Online application from the student: essays (400 words each), transcript, recommendations. For the scholarship, say you attend a School District of Philadelphia school and fill in the scholarship section.
notes: There are no scholarships for the Pre-College programs. Contact hsprogs@sas.upenn.edu or 215-746-2309.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 18, primarily rising 9th to 12th graders. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Use Apply Now or the interest form on the page (name, contact, current grade, cohort, three career fields). Phone 267-502-3800 or info@pyninc.org.
notes: About 400 internship slots a year across cohorts. The city's large summer jobs program is C2L-PHL, a separate application. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: District high school students starting in 10th grade. Middle schoolers choose a CTE program on their School Selection application; high schoolers can join if their school has the program and space allows.
how_to_apply: Middle school: pick schools that offer your CTE program on the School Selection application. High school: talk to your school counselor.
notes: The page notes that students ages 14 to 17 need working papers to work. Which schools offer which programs is in the CTE Programs List.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. Positions are limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form on the camp page, including a one-page essay (why you want to volunteer as a CIT, experience with children, what you enjoy about nature).
notes: Camp is at 8480 Hagy's Mill Road, Philadelphia, PA 19128. The page's date line looks like a typo (June 15, 2025 to August 14, 2026), so confirm dates when the 2027 application posts.

who_can_apply: Clinic Support volunteers must be 16 or older (Animal Care requires 18+). Must attend a training session, sign the volunteer agreement and finish online ethics and safety courses.
how_to_apply: Complete the Wildlife Clinic volunteer Google Form. It is linked on the page.
notes: The general volunteer page says regular volunteers who work with children need Pennsylvania child abuse and criminal history clearances (free for volunteers).

who_can_apply: Students who are at least 16 by the program start date and have finished at least one high school science course. The program gives priority to students in the School District of Philadelphia. It strongly encourages Philadelphia high school students to apply. No grade level or residency rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Send an online application. It has a personal statement of one page, single spaced. It has two letters of recommendation. One from a science teacher is preferred. It has an unofficial transcript or list of classes with grades. Finalists have a 15 minute virtual interview in April. Participants and a parent or guardian go to a mandatory orientation in June.
notes: Contacts: Jason Diaz, 215-898-3803, jdiaz@wistar.org, or Cailey Bice, 215-898-3749, cbice@wistar.org. Absences of more than two days in a row cannot be accommodated. The stipend is not called a wage on the page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Email the zoo through the contact link on the volunteer page. No application link is listed.
notes: Separate options: Special Events volunteers (13+ for family events) apply through an online form; school groups of grades 9 to 12 can join Boo at the Zoo takeover shifts (those 2026 dates have passed). Docents must be 21+.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17 (must be 16 by June 1). A recent graduate can still apply if they are still 17 on June 1. Recent graduates who are 18 go to the college or adult programs. You need a 3.0 GPA or higher and interest in a health career.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Two or more recommendation forms (teacher, counselor, coach or boss, not family). Show you are immune to measles, mumps, rubella and chickenpox, and have a TB test. Send a headshot and parent signatures.
notes: You must go to the required orientation, or you can apply next summer.

who_can_apply: Piscataway residents only. Grades 6 to 12 and at least 12 years old; high school volunteers must be in grades 9 to 12 and at least 14. Must sign a Teen Volunteer Code of Conduct at training.
how_to_apply: High school: attend a library orientation session with a mandatory training video, then enroll if you meet requirements. Adopt-a-Shelf (grades 6 to 8): apply on the volunteering page when the session opens. Questions: teens@piscatawaylibrary.org (subject line Volunteer).
notes: Latecomers are not admitted to training sessions. Open only to Piscataway residents.

who_can_apply: Teens at Club locations that offer Workforce Pathways: Carnegie, Estelle S. Campbell (Lawrenceville), Shadyside, Downtown and McKeesport. The page does not give an age range.
how_to_apply: Use the Returning Teen or New Teen registration link on the Workforce Pathways page. Or use Register Now at bgcwpa.org/registration. Financial assistance is available. See the Financial Assistance page. Phone: (412) 782-5710. Email: contact@bgcwpa.org.
notes: Confirm first: ages, cost, schedule and whether any work is paid are not on the pages read. The Clubs also run two Club Teen Centers (Downtown and McKeesport).

who_can_apply: Natural History camps: teens 14 and older. Powdermill Nature Reserve camps: ages 14 to 19. Art museum camps: 16 and older. Each museum has its own application form.
how_to_apply: Use the museum's own teen camp volunteer application form. It is linked from the Carnegie Museums volunteer page. There is one form each for Natural History, Powdermill and Art. Questions: volunteers@carnegiemuseums.org or 412-353-4680.
notes: The apply link above is the Natural History form. The Art museum form is https://form.jotform.com/230685138792162 and the Powdermill form is https://form.jotform.com/230595011446148. The Natural History page also lists a Teen Advisory Board with an interest form (https://form.jotform.com/243505851081150); its ages are not stated. The Kamin Science Center teen volunteers are a separate card.

who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18. The Pennsylvania Wing page lists Become a Cadet as ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: The squadron page links a Google Form for people interested in joining and the wing's Become a Cadet page. It lists no squadron email or phone. The Pennsylvania Wing headquarters can be reached at 717-220-3517 or hq@pawg.cap.gov.
notes: The Pennsylvania Wing lists other squadrons in the Pittsburgh area. They are Golden Triangle, Jimmy Stewart, Washington, Beaver Falls and Butler. Ask the wing which is closest to you. The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 by the program start, in 10th grade when applying, and U.S. citizens or permanent residents with a green card. Meant for students who lack access or resources in computer science.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the CMU Pre-College application portal by February 1, 2027. Residential only; full participation required.
notes: Status is unconfirmed only because the application opening date is not posted; the 2027 deadlines are confirmed on the program pages (the apply portal could not be read). Limited spots. The admission page lists two different dates for this application (February 1 and March 1, 2027); the program page and the deadlines table both say February 1, 2027, so apply by then. Completers may be invited back to AI Scholars.

who_can_apply: High school students at least 16 years old by June 26, 2027 who are in 10th or 11th grade when they apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the CMU Pre-College application portal. The scholarship option is only considered under the February 1, 2027 deadline.
notes: Status is unconfirmed only because the application opening date is not posted; the 2027 deadlines are confirmed on the program pages (the apply portal could not be read). Expensive; shown so families know the cost and the scholarship route. The three fully funded programs (AI Scholars, CS Scholars, SAMS) cost nothing. Check the cost page again in November 2026 for 2027 prices.

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old by the program start who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents and in 11th grade when they apply. The program focuses on students underrepresented in STEM.
how_to_apply: The application opening date is not posted; apply online through the CMU Pre-College application portal by February 1, 2027. Residential only; scholars must attend the full program.
notes: Status is unconfirmed only because the application opening date is not posted; the 2027 deadlines above are confirmed on the program pages (the apply portal itself could not be read, it needs JavaScript). Competitive and limited spots. The page gives no application opening date. Scholars cannot take other summer programs that overlap. Questions: cmu-sams@andrew.cmu.edu.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Must be at least 14 by the application deadline. Late applications are not considered.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application (or download one to email or mail) during the window. Selected teens are interviewed and must complete an orientation.
notes: Teens accepted twice a year (summer and school year). The next summer window should open in January; confirm on the page.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 23 in Allegheny County and the City of Pittsburgh. Income and residency requirements apply (details on the application).
how_to_apply: Apply online through Partner4Work during the spring application window (new participants and returning participants use different links). A complete eligible application does not guarantee a placement, so apply early.
notes: Questions: summer@partner4work.org or (412) 932-2950. A separate Year-Round Learn & Earn (fall, winter, spring work sessions) serves ages 16 to 23 in the City of Pittsburgh but only for people who already finished a summer. The program page does not mention a work permit; the Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says work permits are required for minors under 18, so ask your school or the program how to get one.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 interested in animal-related careers (age counted as of June 1, 2026 for the 2026 session). Must commit to at least 8 of the 10 days in the chosen session.
how_to_apply: Submit the volunteer application when it reopens, attend an in-person group interview, and attend orientation with a parent or guardian.
notes: Questions go to the volunteer contact on the National Aviary volunteer page.

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 19 who have finished at least one year of high school. You pick one of two weekly groups (Wednesday or Thursday) and must attend all of the dates.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form on the Phipps page when the next group opens. Use the sign-up form on that page to be notified. Questions go to the high school programs coordinator at amule@phipps.conservatory.org or 412-622-6915 ext. 3804.
notes: The page lists two different dates for the final Youth Garden Summit, so confirm with Phipps. The stipend is not described as a job on the page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who enjoy working with children. You must be able to get Pennsylvania Act 33/34 clearances. Phipps pays back the fees.
how_to_apply: The page says the first step for volunteers is to fill out an application. Accepted applicants then go to an interview, orientation and placement meetings. The page does not give a form just for teens. Email the volunteer coordinator listed on the Phipps volunteer page to ask. That is Deb Knorr, dknorr@phipps.conservatory.org.
notes: Confirm first. The volunteer page gives no teen deadline or teen form. Ask Phipps for the current age rule and dates before you plan around this.

who_can_apply: Students from high schools in the Pittsburgh region who have completed one year of high school biology. The page does not state an age rule.
how_to_apply: The page says a link to the application will be posted when applications open. To get updates, join the email list by contacting Jess Robertson at jah99@pitt.edu. Questions: Dr. Becky Gonda, 412-383-5739, reg11@pitt.edu.
notes: No research experience is needed. Free PRT bus passes are available. The honorarium is not called a wage on the page. The page's dates (June 28 to July 16) are shorter than 'four weeks', so confirm the length. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Current 10th or 11th graders at a high school in the Greater Pittsburgh area or Western PA. You need a strong interest in science and a GPA of 3.0 or above. You must finish a biology class by the end of the school year. You must commit to the full four weeks.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It has two essays of up to 200 words each. A high school teacher must complete the recommendation form. It is uploaded at the end of the application or emailed to phsa@pitt.edu by the deadline. Incomplete applications are not considered. Applicants are told by email in mid to late March. They confirm by April 1.
notes: The main page says public high schools in one place and all high schools in another, so ask which applies to you. The award is not called a wage on the page. Applicants without a computer or reliable internet are encouraged to apply. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 17 (having turned 15 by June 1, 2026 for the 2026 program). Two non-relatives must complete a reference form. Needs proof of a negative TB test and a Tdap shot before orientation.
how_to_apply: Check the teen program page in early January for how to submit an inquiry. Questions: chpvolunteer@chp.edu or 412-692-5185.
notes: Very high demand and limited spots. The volunteer office does not handle shadowing, internships or research requests; contact departments directly for those. Adult volunteer program is 18 and older.

who_can_apply: High school students in good school standing. You must be at least 15 at the program start for the computational sites (CompBio, COSBBI, Surgery). You must be at least 16 for the other sites. There is no residency rule, but out of region students must find their own housing.
how_to_apply: Send an online application. It has two short essays. It has one or two references, who get an email. It has a resume and a high school transcript. It has parent or guardian contact information with a digital signature. It also has your top research site choices. PDF files are preferred. In person students may need proof of vaccination.
notes: Very competitive. Another page describes it as an eight week program, so confirm the length. Questions: hillman.academy@pitt.edu or Steven Jones, 412-624-5904 (from the program's Oct 2025 profile). The stipend is not called a wage on the page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Pittsburgh area teens ages 15 to 18 (high school students).
how_to_apply: Send in the online application by the deadline. Work samples are optional. Email teens@warhol.org with questions. Bus tickets are available for transportation.
notes: The 2026-27 deadline was 2026-10-09, so email teens@warhol.org to ask whether late applications are accepted. The Warhol also hires paid Student Assistants and runs a free Teen DJ Academy (ages 14 to 18, stipend) and School of Drag (ages 14 to 18); see the Teens page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 who are interested in animals and conservation (having turned 14 by June 1, 2026). Must commit to one day a week for at least 5 of the 7 weeks.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application when it opens. All applicants are interviewed in person before acceptance. Not all applicants are accepted.
notes: Volunteer role, so no pay. Contact the Volunteer Services Manager through the zoo volunteer page. The page's age requirement reads 'having turned 14 by June 1, 2026' even though it describes the 2027 program, so ask the zoo to confirm the age cutoff date. Confirm dates when applications open.

who_can_apply: No age or grade rule is stated. The program focuses on youth facing challenges such as hunger or homelessness and aims to keep them in school.
how_to_apply: Email your resume to jobs@plantingjustice.org. Or call the East Oakland Nursery at 510-756-6965.
notes: Ages, season and hours are not stated, so call and ask. Pay is from the program page and may change.

who_can_apply: Volunteers of all ages are welcome. The page says junior and senior high school students are encouraged to take part.
how_to_apply: Call Pleasant Home at (708) 383-2654. The Park District also asks volunteers to use the general Acorns to Oaks volunteer form and waiver.
notes: The same volunteer page lists the Oak Park Conservatory (call 708-725-2451). It also lists Cheney Mansion garden volunteers (call 708-383-2612). It does not give ages for those.

who_can_apply: Must reside within Pleasanton city limits. Seats are set aside by grade: middle school, 9th grade, and 11th grade (fall 2026 ad: 3 seats each).
how_to_apply: Apply online through the City of Pleasanton boards and commissions page (link at the bottom of the page, per the recruitment ad). Questions: Office of the City Clerk, 925-931-5027.
notes: The next recruitment date is not posted in the ad we read; deadline_confidence is last-year-pattern because the most recent cycle was fall 2026. The recruitment ad describes city commissions in general; the Youth Commission's own duties and term length were not on a page we could open, so what_you_do is based on the ad's general description.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 20 at appointment, enrolled in high school or college with a C average or better. Needs a valid government ID (CA ID, driver license or US passport), parent consent if under 18, and a background check.
how_to_apply: Email the completed application to joinsmpd@cityofsanmateo.org or call the Recruiting Unit at 650-522-7629.
notes: Training classes are on the 1st and 3rd Thursday, 5 to 7 p.m. Hours count toward school service requirements. You need a flexible schedule for weekdays and weekends. FAQ is at cityofsanmateo.org/4720.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19 (not yet 19 and a half), full-time student, 2.5 GPA, must pass a background check.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, or contact the coordinator at 510-293-5060 or Explorers@hayward-ca.gov.
notes: The page gives no closing dates, so check at the start of each window. Meetings are Wednesday nights 5 to 7pm plus training and some weekend events.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21, currently enrolled in school with a C average or better. No felony or certain misdemeanor convictions, no pending criminal cases, and you must agree to fingerprinting for a background check.
how_to_apply: Email the Explorer application PDF to MHPD_Explorers@morganhill.ca.gov, then complete an oral board interview.
notes: Free to join, but you may need to buy a uniform and gear. Financial help is available. Expected to attend all meetings, trainings and events. Meeting times are not on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students at least 14.5 years old, 2.0 GPA, average or better attendance and discipline, no felony or serious misdemeanor.
how_to_apply: Email Explorer Coordinator Officer Charles Stone at cstone@oaklandca.gov, or Oakland PAL (Officer Jumaal Hill) at 510-615-5758 or oaklandpal@oaklandpal.org.
notes: The page gives a minimum age of 14.5 and no upper limit. The page does not give meeting times or dates, so ask the coordinator. Oakland PD also runs the Police Activities League.

who_can_apply: Current 9th graders who live or attend high school in Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino or Ventura County. First-generation, low-income, or Geometry/Integrated Math II students are considered but not required. About 30 students are admitted each year.
how_to_apply: Online New Student Application, two essays (up to 500 words each), a current-year transcript and two recommendations (one from a core subject teacher). Some applicants are interviewed. Contact PAYS@pomona.edu or (909) 607-1810.
notes: The apply page mentions both 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 in places; the 2026-2027 deadlines above are the ones listed. Confirm with the program. Pomona College is in Claremont, next to Pomona.

who_can_apply: Students currently in 9th, 10th or 11th grade. The page does not list an age rule.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Click here to apply for high school volunteer opportunities' link on the page, or call the hospital volunteer office to confirm if high school applications are open.
notes: CONFIRM FIRST: the page offers a high school application link but also says only adult applications are being accepted right now. Scheduled Monday to Friday shifts.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 12 or older. The TeensTeach and TeensTable teen programs are for ages 13 to 19.
how_to_apply: Volunteers: create an account and submit the individual application, read the handbook, finish the online orientation and quiz, then sign up for training. Teen programs: submit an idea through the page. Staff pick programs that fit the museum's mission and email chosen applicants.
notes: Address: 29 Hubble, Irvine, CA 92618. Volunteer questions: volunteer@pretendcity.org or 949-428-3900. The page also links a Youth Leadership Board but does not describe it.

who_can_apply: Current high school students in grades 9-12 who live in the five boroughs, with parental consent and NYS working papers, and who register as library volunteers.
how_to_apply: Complete the Idea Submission questionnaire on the library volunteer site during a submission window. The Civic Engagement Team will contact you to get your idea library ready. Questions: volunteer@queenslibrary.org.
notes: A limited number of projects are accepted and a branch must agree to host. Other QPL pages list ages as 14-18 for this program, so check the age limit if you are 18.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 with a signed parent consent form. The page says some projects do not require NYS working papers, so check each project's description. Students at schools outside the country or the state may use a waiver.
how_to_apply: Get the parent consent form and NYS working papers (from your high school office), create a volunteer account, search projects and click Express Interest/Sign Up, then interview and get an offer letter. Questions: volunteer@queenslibrary.org.
notes: Library says some projects do not need working papers, so check each listing. Working papers take 1-3 weeks from your school, so start early. They are issued regardless of immigration status. Under-14s can only volunteer with a parent or guardian.

who_can_apply: Red Cross says the in-person Babysitter's Training is for ages 11 to 16, and its online Babysitting Basics course is designed for youth 11 and older.
how_to_apply: Pick a class on the Red Cross Babysitting and Child Care page, or buy the online course there.
notes: The old take-a-class/babysitting-training link no longer works, so the page address was updated. Red Cross says these courses do not qualify you for state-licensed child care. Casual babysitting in a private home does not need a work permit per the California child labor guide (2013 edition).

who_can_apply: Lifeguarding: at least 15 years old by the last day of class, plus a swim test (swim, tread water, timed event). Water Safety Instructor and Basic Swim Instructor: at least 15 by the end of the course.
how_to_apply: Use Find a Class on the Red Cross lifeguarding page to pick a pool or YMCA class near you, and check the fee.
notes: Final test is a 50-question exam with an 80% pass mark. Certificate lasts 2 years. Before the update this file said Water Safety Instructor needs age 16; the Red Cross page says 15. For lifeguard jobs, check each employer's page for pay and work permit rules.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15; you must be 13 by the first training day. Written application, then an interview if selected. At most 20 L.I.T.s per session. Redwood City camps.
how_to_apply: Download the L.I.T. application and email it to tbrent@redwoodcity.org by the deadline. If chosen you interview, then get camp placement and payment instructions. Phone 650-780-5929.
notes: Teens pay a fee to take part (2026: $88, $98, $98 or $49 depending on session). The fee is due after a successful interview. Placement depends on camp needs. A mandatory Saturday training is required. 2027 dates are not posted, so expect a similar April to May window and watch the page.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 or equivalent. You cannot enter ISEF directly; you must win at a Society-affiliated fair. Use the Find-a-Fair tool for California fairs.
how_to_apply: Use Find-a-Fair on the Society for Science site, then register with your school or regional fair.
notes: Projects can include no more than 12 months of continuous research. The 2027 ISEF is in California, which can lower travel costs for California finalists.

who_can_apply: Students in their last year of high school who live and attend school in the US or its territories, any citizenship. You need your own original research with real data, plus essays, a paper of up to 20 pages, recommendations and a transcript.
how_to_apply: Apply online at the Society for Science application portal (sciencetalentsearch.smapply.org).
notes: Seniors only, so juniors should plan for next fall. Test scores are optional. Homeschooled students may apply.

who_can_apply: Lake County high school students who like health care, science and research.
how_to_apply: Email campmed@rfums.org to ask how to apply.
notes: In person only. Ask when applications open.

who_can_apply: Lake County students. High school students who live near the Rosalind Franklin University campus come first.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for INSPIRE link on the pathway programs page. It is a Google form. It opens in December 2026.
notes: Check whether it pays. Students can come back every summer until they finish a bachelor's degree. To reach the program, write to Rachael Lange at rachael.lange@rosalindfranklin.edu or call 224-570-7325.

who_can_apply: Juniors in good standing with a GPA of 2.0 out of 4.0 or higher and an interest in nursing. Applications are for juniors at Cristo Rey St. Martin College Prep, Highland Park, North Chicago, Round Lake and Waukegan High Schools.
how_to_apply: Use the Learn More link on the Nursing INSPIRE page to find the form. To reach someone, write to Dr. Mosilda Asanji at mosilda.asanji@rosalindfranklin.edu.
notes: Only students at the five schools named can apply. The page looks about two cycles old (it shows 2024-25 dates), so ask the program for current dates. Parents join a session on financial planning for college.

who_can_apply: Local high school students. The page does not list a school list or grade rule beyond high school.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for Science Saturdays link on the pathway programs page. It is a Google form. It opens in December 2026. Contact: Rachael Lange, rachael.lange@rosalindfranklin.edu, 224-570-7325.
notes: Only about 25 students are chosen each year.

who_can_apply: Local high school and college students who like health care or science.
how_to_apply: Use the Register for the Virtual Mentor Program link (a Google form) on the pathway programs page. You must attend an orientation before being matched.
notes: Online, so you do not need to travel to North Chicago.

who_can_apply: Richmond youth ages 16 to 21. Must attend required workshops and training to be guaranteed an internship.
how_to_apply: Submit the online Work Experience Program application (2026-2027 form linked on the city page). The team contacts you for an intake. Phone (510) 412-2044.
notes: Must live in Richmond. Ask about the hourly wage and your start date at intake.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 24 living in Alameda, Contra Costa, Fresno, Merced, Madera, Napa, San Francisco, San Joaquin, Santa Clara, Sonoma or Tulare county. Must commit to four days a week.
how_to_apply: Apply through the links on the job posts at risingsunopp.org/jobs/. Phone (510) 665-1501.
notes: As of Oct 7, 2026 the jobs page lists only Central Valley coordinator postings, so no Bay Area summer posting was visible. Pay shown is the 2026 rate. The City of Oakland summer jobs list also includes Rising Sun.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 5 to 12 who live in River Forest. You must attend an orientation, and a parent or guardian must sign the release and waiver.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen/Tween Volunteer form or the Book Buddies form online. Or print it. Email the form to volunteer@riverforestlibrary.org or drop it off at the library.
notes: River Forest residents only. The page says both that Summer 2026 applications are closed and that they are open, so it is out of date. Ask the library when the next call opens.

who_can_apply: Teens at branches that have a board. The page states no age range, so ask your branch.
how_to_apply: Contact your local branch. The page describes no teen application; its online application is for adult volunteers.
notes: Not every branch has a board. The page gives no ages, hours or sign-up steps for teens, so call the branch first. Separate from the City of Riverside Public Library.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 14 years old who can pass a Department of Justice background check. The library cannot accept court-ordered volunteers.
how_to_apply: Create an account at riversideca.cervistech.com, find a Library opportunity, click 'Apply to participate', then wait for an email or call. If approved you book a processing appointment with Human Resources at City Hall and get cleared by background check.
notes: This is the City of Riverside library, not the Riverside County Library System. The page does not describe teen-specific roles; it applies to all volunteers ages 14 and up.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 and up. Spots are limited and not every applicant is chosen.
how_to_apply: Send the interest application and a letter of recommendation to Megan Eaton, meaton@roseville.ca.us, by the deadline. Selected applicants are interviewed, placed at a program site, then pay the course fee.
notes: The page does not say what day applications opened, only the May 5, 2027 deadline. You pay the course fee only after you are chosen. A separate LDP information sheet is linked on the page.

who_can_apply: Must be 13 or older.
how_to_apply: Complete the online Volunteer Form and a staff member will contact you. (916) 774-5221
notes: The page lists no parent permission rule, tasks, or hours. Call (916) 774-5221 or ask the staff member who contacts you.

who_can_apply: Students about to start their last year of high school (juniors). Seniors are not eligible. Open to US citizens, permanent residents and students from participating countries. Needs essays, recommendations, a transcript and test scores.
how_to_apply: Apply on the CEE site: essays, two or three teacher recommendations, official transcript, and PSAT, SAT, ACT or AP scores.
notes: Extremely selective (the FAQ says under 2.5% are accepted). Held in Cambridge, Massachusetts, so plan for travel. The older FAQ page mentions a $75 application fee with waivers and a minimum age of 16 by July 1, but it also lists a six-week program, so it may be out of date. Confirm with CEE.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 to 18. A Minor Volunteer Consent Form is also needed. Volunteers must meet health and vaccine rules. They must do an interview and an orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application and print and complete the Minor Volunteer Consent Form. If your interests match, they will schedule an interview and registration. Call (630) 978-4826.
notes: No shadowing or observation. The page still has older COVID-19 wording (vaccine proof, medical conditions list), so ask the office what applies today. The page says the process depends on the background check, TB testing, health screening and orientation dates. A background check is for ages 18 and up.

who_can_apply: High school students can volunteer only during the summer months. Applicants must live within 12 miles of the hospital. The page does not give a minimum age.
how_to_apply: See the list of current chances (PDF). Then fill out the online volunteer application. Questions: volunteerROPH_services@rush.edu or (708) 660-5684.
notes: No shadowing or observation. Applying does not guarantee a spot and does not lead to a job automatically.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 13 to 21. Membership is free.
how_to_apply: Register for an enrollment session at rysecenter.org/for-youth. Then watch each cohort's application. Phone (510) 374-3401.
notes: Per the cohort page: Food Justice, Public Health, Health and Wellness Career Exploration and STAY FLY TAY Law applications are listed as releasing December 2026; Mock Trial January 2027; Roots to RYSE (summer) Spring 2027; YOUTHBRIDGE internship May 2027. Pay and ages for each cohort are not stated.

who_can_apply: Age 12 to 17. Ages 12 to 15 must volunteer beside a parent or guardian who also registers and trains.
how_to_apply: Do the online orientation and sign the volunteer agreement, make an online account and fill out the volunteer application, attend the Shelter Basics 101 on-site training, then sign up for shifts.
notes: Log hours online and also sign in and out in the paper student binder. Cat shifts need extra training. Court-ordered hours use a separate page.

who_can_apply: Enrolled high school seniors who can get a work permit if under 18, are low income, and meet at least one barrier (for example disability, English learner, foster or homeless, justice-involved, parenting, or struggling academically).
how_to_apply: Download the application from the page and email or hand it in, or pick up a paper copy at Belle Cooledge Community Center (9:30 am to 4:30 pm). WIOA@cityofsacramento.org
notes: Only for low-income students with at least one listed barrier. You can qualify as low-income through free or reduced lunch, SNAP or TANF, or a qualifying ZIP code. Work experience must start at age 18 or younger.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 still in high school (16 by the end of the program) who live in Sacramento city limits. May complete up to two times.
how_to_apply: Make a parent or guardian ActiveNet account and register your teen for the next session. jrrecaide@cityofsacramento.org
notes: Only one absence allowed because of the stipend. Waitlist spots are filled until the second week. Classes are in person at a community center. Youth who are 18 must show proof of school attendance. The page says sessions are held throughout the year.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17 living inside Sacramento city limits. Interview and work permit needed.
how_to_apply: Apply online only during a recruitment window using the Apply link on the L&L page. Selected applicants get an in-person interview, then hiring steps including a work permit. landscapeandlearning@cityofsacramento.org
notes: Fills fast because the window closes at 350 applications. Applications are online only during a recruitment window. Hiring includes getting a work permit. The page also lists a Crew Leader job ($21.83 per hour) that includes driving city vehicles. It states no age rule, so do not assume it is for teens.

who_can_apply: Youth 13 to 18 who live in one of eight listed North Natomas apartment complexes (address checked in week one).
how_to_apply: Register through ActiveNet using the Register Here button when a session is open. NNworkforce@cityofsacramento.org
notes: Only for residents of the eight eligible apartment complexes (Atrium Court, Natomas Park, Terracina Gold, Terracina Meadows, The Lofts, Valencia Point, Westview Ranch, Willow Glen). You must meet the age rule by the session start date. Only one absence is allowed or you may lose the stipend. Only one session is open for registration at a time.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18, in middle or high school, living in Sacramento city limits. 18-year-olds need a school transcript. May complete up to two times.
how_to_apply: Make a parent or guardian ActiveNet account and register. Teen and parent must attend a mandatory orientation. PrimeTimeTeen@cityofsacramento.org
notes: Fall sessions are at Evelyn Moore (Mon and Wed) and Clunie (Tue and Thu) Community Centers, 4:30 to 7:00 pm. You must be 13 on the first day. Only one absence is allowed. Graduated high school seniors who are in college do not qualify.

who_can_apply: Teens can volunteer. A parent or guardian must sign the application before you start. The page does not state ages; ask your branch.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. Teens who need school hours can ask about drop-in volunteering at a branch.
notes: Many people apply, so a spot is not guaranteed. Drop-in is the quickest way to start; scheduled volunteering needs a longer onboarding. Court-ordered hours are not accepted.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 7 to 12. Academies are sorted into 7th to 10th and 9th to 12th grade groups.
how_to_apply: Choose an academy once the 2027 schedule is posted, then register online starting March 1, 2027.
notes: Offerings change each year; the page lists 2026 courses as examples. Some academies are online and some are in person, and the same course may have an online and an in-person section. Open to students entering grades 7 to 12.

who_can_apply: Current freshmen, sophomores and juniors who attend a Sacramento City, Twin Rivers or Natomas high school or live in Sacramento city limits.
how_to_apply: Use the Register link on the program page when the window opens. Email summeratcityhall@cityofsacramento.org with questions.
notes: Dates are tentative. The city also runs Semester @ City Hall, a 6-week spring and fall version open to any high school student who lives or goes to school in Sacramento city limits; its dates are not posted yet.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 22 at the time of appointment. You must live in Sacramento city limits or go to school there for your whole term. City employees cannot serve.
how_to_apply: Apply online for an open seat. The city clerk reviews it, then there is an orientation and a supplemental application. The Mayor nominates and the City Council approves.
notes: Appointed by the Mayor and City Council, so not every applicant is picked. The FAQ says the $50 stipend applies to the 1st and 3rd monthly meetings. No experience needed. Seats open at different times; check the Become a Commissioner page. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19, 2.75 GPA (proof needed), letter of recommendation, interview, $30 uniform fee, mandatory in-person training Jan 10, 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply online starting Oct 10, send a recommendation letter and proof of GPA, then interview with the volunteer coordinator.
notes: Mandatory in-person training Jan 10, 2027. The Summer Camp Counselor teen role (ages 15 to 19) is closed for 2026; check back next year. Animal Care Volunteers must be 18 or older.

who_can_apply: Age 10 and up. Ages 10 to 15 need an adult chaperone; ages 16 to 17 need parent permission (waiver emailed after sign-up).
how_to_apply: Sign up for a shift on the online calendar; groups of 5 or more email volunteer@sacramentofoodbank.org. Phone 916-456-1980.
notes: Closed-toe shoes that cover your whole foot are required. Full shifts do not appear on the calendar, so check back. People who received food bank services in the past 12 months cannot volunteer there. Groups of 5 or more email volunteer@sacramentofoodbank.org.

who_can_apply: The page says programs are typically ages 14 to 20 and often need a 2.0 GPA, high school enrollment and parent consent under 18. Each program has its own rules.
how_to_apply: Use the links on the Metro Fire page and contact each program directly.
notes: Details from the programs' own pages: Sacramento Firefighter Youth Academy is free, ages 14 to 17, 9 months of Saturdays 8 am to 2 pm starting end of July, 35 spots, applications open in spring. Cosumnes Fire Explorers are ages 15 to 18 (juniors and seniors), 2.0 GPA, and applications for next school year open in spring 2027.

who_can_apply: Regular volunteers must be 18. Students and scouts can do community service projects without direct animal care. The page states no youth age range.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Community Service Application, or take the online New Volunteer Orientation. Questions: rmaier@sspca.org, 916-504-2807.
notes: You can become a regular volunteer at 18. Court-ordered hours are not offered. You will not get a confirmation after you send the application; you may start a project any time.

who_can_apply: Sacramento County youth ages 16 to 24. Federal eligibility rules apply, so ask a Job Center whether you qualify.
how_to_apply: Visit a Sacramento Works Job Center (find one on the Sacramento Works site). Staff at each center help youth access services.
notes: Designed for youth with extra barriers. Work experience is one of several services in a case-managed plan, not an open job board. Ages 16 to 24 are served, so this is mostly for older teens.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24. The page gives no other rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Register buttons on the Programs page, call 916-248-1081, or use the contact form.
notes: Open Mon to Sat, 12 to 6 pm, at 1901 Del Paso Blvd. The Cafe Paso job training cafe is marked temporarily closed, so ask whether job training spots are open. Pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 14 years of age or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application (general, or the Reading Together and Homework Center form), pass a background check, and attend volunteer orientation and training. Opportunities are posted on Idealist. Volunteer Services: VolunteerSPPL@ci.stpaul.mn.us or 651-266-7432.
notes: Not a teen-only program; open to anyone 14 and older.

who_can_apply: Saint Paul residents who live in a cost-burdened household (for example, they receive SNAP or Section 8) or have a barrier to employment. YJ1: at least 14 by June 1 and no older than 19 by Aug 25. YJ2: at least 16 by June 1 and no older than 21.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online youth application in February (have your Social Security number, household income, a phone number and an emergency contact email ready; YJ2 needs a resume). Then attend pre-employment training in March, Career Exploration Day and interviews.
notes: Very competitive. About 2,000 people apply for about 500 YJ1 internships (FAQ). Contact (651) 266-6363 or RightTrack@ci.stpaul.mn.us. The overview text says ages 14 to 24 across all Right Track programs. The summer teen programs are 14 to 21. Unplaced teens can join an online professional development program.

who_can_apply: San Diego County residents who finished their most recent semester at a San Diego County high school, are 16 by June 14, 2027, have a 2.75 GPA or higher and have finished at least one high school biology class.
how_to_apply: Online application with a resume (PDF or Word), unofficial transcript and short-answer responses. Questions: community@salk.edu.
notes: Applicants under 18 must get a work permit from their school if hired. Preferred but not required: one high school chemistry class and your own transportation.

who_can_apply: High school students at least 15 years old who are starting 9th, 10th, 11th or 12th grade in the 2026-2027 school year. Spots are limited and applicants are interviewed.
how_to_apply: Online application when the window opens, then an interview. Contact Kimberly Morrow, Volunteer Coordinator, 909-579-6794 (8 a.m. to 4 p.m.).
notes: CONFIRM FIRST: closed now and the page lists conflicting dates. Non-graduating volunteers who finish 100 hours can return the next year.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 anywhere in San Bernardino County. LTLP is required for all teen volunteers at the county's 32 branches.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application and turn it in at your local branch library. Then attend one meeting a month at Apple Valley, Chino Hills, Crestline, Fontana, Hesperia, Highland, Phelan or Yucca Valley.
notes: Meetings are the 2nd Thursday of the month 4 to 6 p.m. or the 3rd Saturday 10 a.m. to noon; you pick any listed date and branch. Locations may change with participation. The County Library is separate from the City of San Bernardino Public Library.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 through 20. You must be enrolled in or graduated from high school. You need a 2.0 GPA or better. You must be a legal U.S. resident in good health and character. You can have no arrest or conviction record and no pending cases. Under 18 needs a parent or guardian to sign a liability release.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Sheriff's Volunteer Application Form and bring it to your local station or email it to the address on the form. Contact: volforces@sbcsd.org, (909) 252-4100.
notes: Members must keep current CPR and First Aid certification and finish Explorer Academy within a year. The page does not give meeting days or locations.

who_can_apply: San Bernardino County residents ages 16 to 24 by the start date, legally authorized to work in the U.S., with a valid California ID card. Under 18 needs an approved work permit before day one.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the county's job site when the window opens in March, upload proof of age and residency, attend orientation, then get matched to a job.
notes: Very fast: the 2026 posting closed after 800 applications. Check hr.sbcounty.gov/spark-syep/ in early March 2027 and have proof of age, residency and a California ID ready. The county page shows a PDF on how to apply.

who_can_apply: Eligible youth ages 16 to 24. Specific eligibility rules are given by each provider.
how_to_apply: Contact one of the providers listed on the county's youth page. Openings depend on each provider's capacity.
notes: This is the year-round option when the summer SPARK program is closed. Phone numbers for each provider are on the county page. The page does not say whether 16 and 17 year olds are paid, so ask the provider about work permits.

who_can_apply: People age 16 and up. You need two reference letters to apply and must commit to at least six months.
how_to_apply: Get two reference letters ready. Then fill out the online volunteer application. Training happens four times a year.
notes: No short-term or summer internship spots. Not good for a one-time service-hours project because of the six-month rule.

who_can_apply: Group volunteering (3 to 25 people) takes volunteers age 8 and up. The page does not give an age rule for individual volunteers.
how_to_apply: For one-time or individual service, email cabr_volunteers@nps.gov. Groups use the Group volunteering page on the park website.
notes: Ask the park about age rules for each repeat role, since the page does not say.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 30 who are enrolled in a school or training program (show proof). Priority goes to people from communities of concern. You must have the legal right to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Pick a posting on the City internship job site. Attach proof that you are enrolled in a school or training program. Then apply. The city strongly urges you to add a resume and cover letter. The job site says to consider unpaid internships too.
notes: Interns are City employees. Interns need a work permit, Social Security Number, background check and ID. The job site says to consider unpaid internships too. Funded by the state Youth Service Corps.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students ages 13 to 15 who can come to the meetings. You show interest in service and leadership.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online form linked from the City youth volunteer page. Questions? Write to workreadiness@sandiego.gov.
notes: Only for ages 13 to 15, so a 16 year old is too old. For older teens, see the City paid internships. Confirm the current cycle with workreadiness@sandiego.gov, the contact listed on the City page.

who_can_apply: Recreation Aide: at least 15 and a half years old. Pool Guard: at least 16 at the time of application, no certification needed.
how_to_apply: Apply for 'Recreation Aide' or 'Pool Guard 1' on the City's governmentjobs.com portal. The City then sends interview and skills-test details.
notes: Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 25 who live in or go to school in the City of San Diego. You must be able to serve a 2 year term and go to monthly in-person meetings.
how_to_apply: Apply on the City boards website. Choose Youth Commission and your seat from the Boards and Seats menu.
notes: Seats are nominated by the Mayor and each Councilmember (2 each). Contact is the Office of Child and Youth Success. The chair's bio on the About page says she first learned of the commission through the Employ & Empower internship.

who_can_apply: Teens, generally ages 12 to 17. The exact age range varies by branch, so ask your branch.
how_to_apply: Ask a staff member at your San Diego County Library branch how to sign up.
notes: Run by the County library system. It is separate from the City of San Diego Public Library. The page lists no teen requirements. The background check and medical exam it mentions are for adult volunteers. Confirm your branch's age range before going.

who_can_apply: Students now in high school, in at least 9th grade. You need high school approval and written parent approval before you apply. You can appeal if you do not meet every rule.
how_to_apply: Apply online to become a Cuyamaca student. Then get approval from your high school administrator. A parent or guardian must approve too. Do this every term, before you register.
notes: All classes make a permanent college record, so choose with care. Your high school district decides if the class counts toward graduation.

who_can_apply: At food handouts, volunteers must be 14 or older. Anyone 15 or younger needs a chaperone over 18. The Distribution Center takes volunteers who are 6 and up.
how_to_apply: Sign up for shifts through the volunteer page on the Feeding San Diego website. Shifts are posted one month in advance.
notes: Closed-toe shoes are required. Shifts are posted one month ahead.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 with at least a 2.0 GPA. The page does not name a city residency rule.
how_to_apply: To get on the waitlist, email sdfdcadets@sandiego.gov. Give your name and date of birth, and say that you want to join.
notes: Phone on the page: 619-643-2505. Pay is not mentioned, so treat it as unpaid until the department says otherwise.

who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 15 can volunteer with a registered adult (18+). Ages 16 and up can sign up on their own. School groups from middle and high school are welcome.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Food Bank volunteer site, then sign up for open shifts. Under 18 volunteers use the minor waiver, which guardians sign.
notes: Good for a first volunteer experience or school service hours. Shifts are at the Miramar warehouse and the North County site in Vista. Wear closed-toe shoes.

who_can_apply: Junior Conservatory is for students going into grades 8 and 9. Conservatory is for students going into grades 10 to 12. To get in, you send a form and two letters of support. You also do an audition.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Have two references send letters. Then go to an in-person audition at the Playhouse. A separate scholarship form is linked from the page.
notes: The page prints 2025 in a few date lines for the 2026 program, so check dates on the page. The Playhouse has a form to get a note when 2027 applications post.

who_can_apply: Any San Diego high school student who is a rising 10th to 12th grader.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen Council application form during the open window. Applicants were told the result by Sept 18 in 2026.
notes: The page still says applications are now open, but its own deadline of Sept 4, 2026 has passed. Questions: Gia Battista Figueroa (email on the page).

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: See the museum's main volunteer page and Volunteer Application link, or contact the museum at 619-232-3821.
notes: The page gives no application steps beyond pointing to the volunteer application. Ask the museum about the time commitment.

who_can_apply: High school students with approval from their high school district and a parent or guardian. Students under 16 also need each instructor to sign an Under 16 form. Home-schooled students need extra forms.
how_to_apply: Get approval from your high school district and a parent. Apply online to Palomar. Fill out the K12 Special Admission Approval Form once. Turn it in at Enrollment Services or email it to admissions@palomar.edu.
notes: Part-time (11 units or fewer) enrollment fee is waived. Everyone pays the mandatory Health Fee and Student Center Fee. The same page lists GEAR UP, Upward Bound and Educational Talent Search for some North County schools.

who_can_apply: Junior volunteers are 16 and 17 years old. A parent or guardian must come to the interview, orientation and TB test. You give a school counselor contact.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Junior Volunteer application online. A parent or guardian must attend the interview, orientation and TB test. Give a school counselor or advisor contact. Screening can take up to six weeks.
notes: The processing fee pays part of the TB screen and background check. It also pays for uniforms and badge parts. You can volunteer at one site at a time, so pick Poway or Escondido, not both. Volunteers in good standing can ask for a letter of recommendation.

who_can_apply: Minimum age is 13. Under 13 must come with an adult. Volunteers (including 13 to 17 year olds) who work with minors, seniors or people with disabilities must be fingerprinted and cleared by state law.
how_to_apply: Register on the volunteer sign-up page, then pick events or roles. Fingerprinting is by appointment (619-236-6686) for roles that need it. Wear closed-toe shoes and bring water, a hat and sunscreen.
notes: Not every role needs fingerprints. The page lists Tecolote Nature Center and Tri-Canyon among its chances.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21. You need to be a high school graduate or have at least a 2.0 GPA if still in school. You pass a written exam, a character interview and a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Then go to a recruiting meeting at Police Plaza (4020 Murphy Canyon Rd). Bring a government photo ID. The meeting can last up to three hours. It includes a 20 question test.
notes: The activities page describes some activities. One is minor decoy work with detectives. A parent should read the page. You must finish the Cadet Academy first. Then you can become a cadet.

who_can_apply: Teenagers only. The library's general volunteer rule is that volunteers must be at least 13. Annual volunteer training is required.
how_to_apply: Open the library volunteer opportunities link, pick the Teen Team Program Assistant listing, click the information icon, then 'Fill in an Application'. Sign in or create a MyImpact account and submit. If your branch has no listing, email LibraryVolunteer@sandiego.gov.
notes: Applies to City of San Diego library branches only. San Diego County Library is a different system (see the Teen Service Learner card). The page does not say how many hours a week. Background check and mandated reporter training are listed only for volunteers 18 and older.

who_can_apply: Students who go to school in San Diego County and will be the first in their family to graduate from a four-year college. You must meet the program entry rules and reapply each year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. You get a confirmation email and staff follow up with next steps.
notes: This is a college-prep program, not a job. It is a good fit for a teen who wants help planning for college and careers. First-generation means neither parent or guardian has a four-year U.S. degree.

who_can_apply: Southern California residents in grade 10, 11 or 12 who have finished a semester of high school. You are 16 by June 15 and have a 3.0 GPA or higher. You are college bound. You must come to the final poster session.
how_to_apply: Apply online (free). Mentors read applications and interview students. If you accept, you get a registration link and pay by the end of May unless you get a scholarship.
notes: The page calls it a volunteer internship. Pick project prerequisites carefully. Students may do only one REHS internship per summer. 2027 dates are not posted, so check the page in early 2027.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 11 who are at least 14, with a 3.0 GPA or higher and a written recommendation from a school counselor. The page says it is not accepting the class of 2028 now.
how_to_apply: Download and print the junior volunteer form. Fill it out and mail it to Volunteer Services. Then go to a 30 minute interview and a 2 hour orientation with a parent or guardian. You also do a TB test and health screening.
notes: The page accepts applications only from grades 9 to 11 and says it is no longer accepting the class of 2028. Call 619-740-4175 to confirm your class year can apply. Mail address is on the page (Volunteer Services, Sharp Grossmont Hospital, PO Box 158, La Mesa, CA 91944).

who_can_apply: The page has a separate high school student application. The minimum age and any GPA rule are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: When the form opens, submit it. Then go to an in-person info session at Sharp Memorial. After that there is an interview. Onboarding includes a background check and health clearances.
notes: Health clearances include MMR, chickenpox, Tdap, TB blood test, and flu and COVID vaccine or a declination. Check the page for when high school applications reopen.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. Entry is by application. The intro course (BE-BOAT) comes first.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You hear back 7 to 10 business days later. Payment is due within 2 weeks of acceptance.
notes: Costs a lot. Scholarships exist for some Research Scholars programs but the scholarship page did not list Bioengineering. Email precollege@ucsd.edu with questions.

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 and older. You need two reference responses from people who are not friends or family. You cannot serve where you or a family member has worked.
how_to_apply: Apply online and line up two references. They can be work or school contacts, not friends or family. Then do a virtual interview. Send vaccine records for measles, mumps, rubella and chickenpox. Get a TB test and pass a background check. Finish online training. Then go to an in-person orientation and tour.
notes: You may start 2 to 3 months after applying. Questions: volsvcs@health.ucsd.edu or 619-543-6370. Applications outside the summer window will not be considered for summer-only.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 who are at least 14 when the program starts. You finish one Tier 1 course before applying for Tier 2.
how_to_apply: Apply online when a term opens. Students are accepted on a rolling basis and pay within 2 weeks of acceptance.
notes: Price for Tier 2 and Tier 3 was not checked. Email precollege@ucsd.edu with questions.

who_can_apply: Free career centers. The page says it has helped thousands of 16 to 24 year olds and states no eligibility age, so ask.
how_to_apply: Complete the online program application (10 to 15 minutes). The team follows up about next steps.
notes: The programs page also lists GenAI, workforce support for in-school youth across San Diego County school systems, and EXCEL for in-school and out-of-school young adults in the South Bay; their ages and dates were not checked. Pay and permit rules for under-18 placements are not stated.

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors. The application needs an administrator recommendation, a teacher recommendation (core subjects), a parent questionnaire, a student questionnaire and an unofficial transcript, plus a 504 plan if applicable. The page does not say whether students outside San Jose Unified may apply.
how_to_apply: Deliver the application packet (administrator and teacher recommendations, parent and student questionnaires, unofficial transcript) to the Middle College office, Business Building B-107, San Jose City College. Questions: Lisa Canton, lcanton@sjusd.org, 408-298-2191 ext. 3996.
notes: Re-read the SJCC Middle College page on 2026-10-07. The SJUSD Middle College page it links to (https://www.sjusd.org/our-schools/middle-college/nav/) returns 404, so the district's application steps, deadline and selection rules could not be confirmed. Students are responsible for their own transportation. Students from SJUSD can still play sports and join clubs at their home high schools. Confirm the deadline and whether non-SJUSD students can apply with Lisa Canton before applying.

who_can_apply: Teens Reach is for ages 13 to 18. You need a strong interest in the library and must go to meetings and join in activities. The library does not list an age for Teen Book Reviewer on its volunteer page, so ask Volunteer Services if you are 12 or younger.
how_to_apply: Teens Reach: find your branch's Teens Reach sign-up on Better Impact (each branch has its own) or ask the branch. Teen Book Reviewer: search for it on Better Impact from the library volunteer page, and attend an orientation (on-site or virtual). Questions: volunteer.sjpl@sjlibrary.org or volunteer@sjlibrary.org, or call Volunteer Services at 408-808-2181.
notes: The volunteer page lists both Teens Reach and Teen Book Reviewer as teen roles, and links Teens Reach to its own page at sjpl.org/teensreach, so this one card covers both. Teens Reach meeting times differ by branch; check your branch's page. TeenHQ is at the King Library, 150 E San Fernando.

who_can_apply: San Jose residents. The paid work experience is for ages 14 to 18 who face barriers to employment. Job help (resumes, job fairs) is open to ages 16 to 29. Free to join.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Youth Application on the San Jose Works page. A staff member contacts you afterward.
notes: Pay rate and placement dates are not posted on the pages I read. The paid work experience is for youth 14 to 18 with barriers to employment; placement is not guaranteed. The FAQ says job help is free for San Jose residents 16 to 29. Under 18 needs a work permit.

who_can_apply: Youth Advisory Council: ages 13 to 19 who live in a San Jose City Council district. Youth Commission: ages 14 to 20. You must live in the district you represent. The term is two years (up to two terms). It meets 4th Monday at 6:30 p.m.
how_to_apply: Fill out the District Youth Advisory Application for the YAC. A Youth Commissioner contacts you within about two weeks.
notes: Page is hosted by the library. Some council districts are unavailable or paused. YAC members earn community service hours. Pay not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 9 to 12 who can commit to a regular weekly shift for at least 4 months. You must attend one orientation each school year.
how_to_apply: Apply online, attend an in-person orientation at the Main Library, sign the waiver, and commit to a regular shift. Returning volunteers must use their old MyImpact login.
notes: The page mentions both 2026 and January 2026 timing, so confirm the next cycle with the Teen Librarian. It also says a teen should handle their own emails, because the program is meant to prepare you for a first job.

who_can_apply: The page does not state ages or grades. Ask the Recreation office.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Call Recreation at 510-577-3462 or email SLRec@SanLeandro.Org.
notes: Meets at 6 p.m. on the first Tuesday of the month at the Marina Community Center, 15301 Wicks Blvd. Events listed for the 2025-2026 term include the MLK Celebration and the Cherry Festival and Parade.

who_can_apply: San Mateo County youth ages 14 to 21 can join. The county summer internship is only for members ages 18 to 21. You must attend a 1 hour job prep workshop before using the job board.
how_to_apply: Register as a student member on jobsforyouth.org, attend the 1 hour job prep workshop, then use the job board. For the internship you also attend a mandatory orientation.
notes: Teens under 18 can use the workshops and job board but not the county internship. Phone 650-599-7215, email jobsforyouth@smcgov.org. Must be a San Mateo County resident for the internship.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. Minimum commitment 6 months or one semester. A free background check is required at 16 and older (takes 3 to 6 weeks).
how_to_apply: Pick a branch and apply for a role on Better Impact through the library volunteer page, or email volunteer@smcl.org.
notes: The page did not list a Teen Advisory Board. Roles are set by branch, and there may be a wait for an opening. Apply for your own branch (13 locations).

who_can_apply: California high school students who are at least 16 at the mid-June start. Preference goes to students living in San Diego or Imperial County. A few spots are reserved for San Diego MESA Alliance students.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Request Info' form on the SPARK page, or contact Program Director Sanjeev Ranade, PhD at cirmsparkinternship@sbpdiscovery.org.
notes: Confirm the current deadline before planning; the official page lists none. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: People currently enrolled in high school who can get a work permit. The page does not give a minimum age or a city residency rule.
how_to_apply: Check the city job site for internship openings and apply there. If none are open, check back later.
notes: Pay and hours are not stated. The job list loads by script, so open internships could not be checked on Oct 9, 2026. Other levels on the page are for college students.

who_can_apply: Anyone age 12 and older. Under-18 volunteers use the minor waiver form. TB test results must be submitted as part of the application process.
how_to_apply: Fill out the forms in the Volunteer Handbook. Then send a volunteer form on the city volunteer page with the forms attached. Roles with children need extra forms.
notes: Ages 18 and up also do an online background check. Open roles were not listed on the program page.

who_can_apply: Santa Ana residents ages 16 to 24 who can work in the U.S. by law. The Youth Service Corps version serves ages 16 to 30 and picks Santa Ana residents first. You must meet two of several need rules, such as low income or out of school.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application and upload the required documents. Youth under 18 must submit a Request for Work Permit form. Selection is first come, first served and spaces are limited. Call (714) 565-2600 or email SAYEmployment@santa-ana.org to confirm.
notes: Two city pages describe the same program with slightly different rules. Call (714) 565-2600 or email SAYEmployment@santa-ana.org to confirm which one fits you. The interest form is for a reopening notice. The main page says applications are open. The interest page says the program is closed to new applications.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 12 years old with an adult, or 15 years old on their own. Zoo Buddies is for ages 12 to 14, who must volunteer with a parent or guardian age 18 or older, and both complete the requirements together.
how_to_apply: Long-term volunteers and Zoo Buddies apply with the online volunteer application on the zoo page. Short-term volunteers contact the zoo through its Contact Us page. The zoo does not accept walk-up volunteers.
notes: Short-term needs the City of Santa Ana one-time volunteer waiver. Long-term needs the city volunteer application, a TB test and a background check. The City of Santa Ana volunteer page says volunteers under 18 must complete a minor waiver form. The Santa Ana library teen volunteer program was not listed because the only page found was from 2021.

who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: Contact the squadron to set up a visit (the page says to let them know you are interested so they can schedule one). Meetings are at 629 Firestone Rd # B, Goleta, CA 93117. Phone: 805-822-4817. Email: Tyler.Epley@cawgcap.org (Deputy Commander for Cadets).
