notes: Confirm first: the squadron pages do not list dues. The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.

who_can_apply: Volunteers 16 and older. Volunteers 15 or younger are welcome with an adult partner. This is a parent or guardian volunteer who goes to training and works next to them.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application for the role you want (dog, cat or clinic) and pick an orientation date and time. Outreach applications go by email. Main phone: 805-964-4777, or use the contact form on the page.
notes: Confirm first: the dog and cat roles were full when checked, and the page gives two different time commitments. Younger volunteers need a parent or guardian to volunteer with them.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18 interested in art or working with children. The program is competitive.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here links on the museum page for each class or camp. Email communityprograms@sbma.net or call 805-884-6457.
notes: The museum also runs a free SBPL x SBMA Teen Art Party for grades 7-12 (next: Jan 22, 2027 and Apr 16, 2027, Fridays 4-5:30 PM).

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. Uniform shirt required: $20 (waived for teens with SNAP/Cal Fresh EBT).
how_to_apply: Fill in the online CIT application form. Contact Haylee Rosso at hrosso@sbnature2.org or 805-682-4711 ext. 170.
notes: Dates shown are the 2026 cycle. The page says summer CITs are invited back for fall, winter and spring break camps.

who_can_apply: Students currently in 8th or 9th grade with at least a 2.5 GPA who can give 20 hours a month in the school year and 25 hours a week in summer, and have reliable transportation to the Museum and Sea Center.
how_to_apply: Online application, then an in-person interview. Contact Teen Programs Manager Haylee Rosso at hrosso@sbnature2.org or 805-682-4711 ext. 170.
notes: Only 8th and 9th graders can apply, so start early. Summers are intensive. Dates shown are the 2026 cycle; expect a similar early-spring deadline next year and check the page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17 who can work a two-hour shift on Saturdays or Sundays during Museum hours (10 AM to 5 PM). Teens must buy a Museum Store shirt as a uniform; the cost is waived for teens with SNAP/CalFresh EBT.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online VolunTEEN application. Contact Haylee Rosso at hrosso@sbnature2.org or 805-682-4711 ext. 170.
notes: Dates shown are the 2026 cycle. Expect applications to reopen around April 1, 2027 (the page did not say).

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Use the Register button on the Teens and Early Adults page.
notes: The same page also lists a Job Apprentice Program and a free Arts Alliance mentoring program; those pages gave no ages or pay, so they are not listed.

who_can_apply: Eligibility varies by position. Some need experience or certifications (for example lifeguard); others are for first-time workers. Camp Recreation Assistants need no experience. Minimum ages are set in each job posting and were not read.
how_to_apply: Apply to open positions on the City's NEOGOV job site (Parks and Recreation). Lifeguard jobs include a tryout.
notes: The City has offered a reduced-cost lifeguard certification course for ages 15 and up (March 2024 notice, $50 for residents); check sbparksandrec.santabarbaraca.gov for the current course. Under-18 workers need a work permit from their school district. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 9 to 12. Parents and guardians are welcome. No registration needed for the fair; the interview workshop needs registration.
how_to_apply: Just show up. Sign up separately for the Teen Interview Skills Workshop.
notes: 2026 employers included the Museum of Natural History and Sea Center, MOXI, Santa Barbara Museum of Art, Santa Barbara Zoo, City Parks and Recreation, and the Postal Service. More than 200 teens attended in 2025.

who_can_apply: Teens. Book reviews are for grades 7 to 12. The Teen Advisory Board is for high school students and requires a Library Services Orientation for Teens first. Volunteers ages 16 and over are welcome to complete an 8-hour training.
how_to_apply: Teen Volunteer Time: pre-register to guarantee a spot, or drop in. Advisory Board: send in the application and go to the orientation. Book reviews: send them through the library form.
notes: The apply link is the Teen Advisory Board form. Service-hour sign-off requests go to the Teen Services Librarian and take up to 3 business days. The library cannot sign court-ordered community service.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 with strong communication skills, an interest in coding or robotics, and the ability to work well with teens and children. No experience needed. Limited spots for highly motivated teens.
how_to_apply: Online application form (linked from the library news post).
notes: Meets at Central Library, 40 E. Anapamu St. Posted October 4, 2026, so the deadline is close. Supported by a federal library grant.

who_can_apply: High school and home school students. High-school-based courses are for Santa Barbara and Carpinteria Unified students only. Some courses are restricted. Complete the SBCC application and the dual enrollment steps first.
how_to_apply: Apply to SBCC through CCCApply, then follow the Steps to Enrollment for your course type. Contact dualenrollment@sbcc.edu or 805-898-8170.
notes: Your school counselor or College and Career Center can help choose courses.

who_can_apply: Anyone age 11 and up. Volunteers 11 to 13 must volunteer with a parent or guardian. Aquarist volunteers must be 14 or older and have done 48 hours of service first. Commit to one shift a week for at least four months.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online volunteer application, interview, then attend mandatory training. Contact scvolunteer@sbnature2.org or 805-962-2526 ext. 110.
notes: Counts for the community service hours needed to graduate from high school in Santa Barbara Unified (per the Museum). Shifts are 9:45-12:45, 12:30-3:30 or 3:00-5:00.

who_can_apply: High school students in 10th or 11th grade with a weighted GPA of at least 3.80. Students must attend the whole program and cannot take other courses or programs at the same time. No English test is needed for international applicants.
how_to_apply: Online application with a transcript that includes fall 2026 grades, AP scores if any, a 500-word personal statement, short answers, and the $75 fee. Tick the box on the application if you want to be considered for a scholarship. An optional info webinar is offered.
notes: Competitive. Costs shown are the 2026 figures because the 2027 cost page was not updated. Residential students live on campus and housing is billed by Summer Discovery. Contact: precollege@summer.ucsb.edu.

who_can_apply: High school students in 9th, 10th or 11th grade with a weighted GPA of at least 3.60. Students must attend the whole program and cannot take other courses or programs at the same time. No English test is needed for international applicants.
how_to_apply: Online application with a transcript that includes fall 2026 grades, a 500-word personal statement, short answers, and the $75 fee. Tick the box on the application if you want to be considered for a scholarship. An optional info webinar is offered.
notes: Costs shown are the 2026 figures because the 2027 cost page was not updated. The younger, shorter and cheaper of the two UCSB pre-college programs. Contact: precollege@summer.ucsb.edu.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 19. Of 15 members, 8 must live in the City; seats are set aside for SBUSD high schools, alternative and private high schools, and at-large. Members serve two-year terms from July 1.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the City's advisory group application. Youth Council applicants interview with both the City Council and the current Youth Council. Contact Recreation Specialist Nicole Morgan, 805-897-2582.
notes: The City's recruitment page lists Youth Council interview dates but this check did not confirm which seats are open this round, so call Nicole Morgan. The City also has a one-year Youth Intern seat on some boards and commissions (nominated by a high school principal).

who_can_apply: Most of our job opportunities are open to applicants 14 years and older; some positions require that an applicant be at least 16 or 18. You must be able to present proof of citizenship or legal right to work in the United States. Most positions require some related experience and/or an educational background in a related field. Students with no prior work experience: 'We will consider your application for our entry level positions.'
how_to_apply: Apply online for a specific opening on the Zoo's Employment Listings page. Send one application per job.
notes: The Employment Listings page was not read, so check whether any openings are posted now. Under-18 workers need a work permit from their school district. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Current junior high or high school students. Junior Camp Counselors give at least 3 weeks of summer Zoo Camp (about 100 hours). Leaders in Training give 4 summer weeks (about 130 hours). Special-event volunteers can be 13 or older.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply links under Teens on the Zoo volunteer page. They are for the junior camp counselor application plus a reference letter. Call or email the Zoo to confirm before you plan.
notes: Confirm first. The Zoo says no internships are available at this time. The Zoo held a Job and Volunteer Fair on February 22 (year not on the page).

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18 who live in Santa Clara County.
how_to_apply: Join the waitlist form on the Teen CERT website or email scctcert@gmail.com. Paperwork drop-off happened before the last academy.
notes: The March 2026 flyer said ages 13 to 17 and the website says 13 to 18, so check your age with them. Cost is not stated; the last academy was at Los Altos Hills Town Hall. Santa Clara County residents only.

who_can_apply: Santa Clara residents ages 12 to 19. You cannot be employed by the City of Santa Clara.
how_to_apply: Apply during the yearly recruitment. Call the Youth and Teen Center at 408-615-3760 or email youthcommission@santaclaraca.gov to ask when it opens.
notes: Meets the second Tuesday of the month at 6 p.m. at the Youth and Teen Center, 2446 Cabrillo Ave. The page was last updated 2026-09-30.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 7 to 12. No age range is stated. New members are always welcome.
how_to_apply: Use the Volunteer/TAB Sign Up link. It is at santaclaritavolunteers.com. Or contact a volunteer coordinator. They work at the Old Town Newhall library. They also work at the Canyon Country Jo Ann Darcy library and the Valencia library.
notes: Meeting dates are on the TAB Schedule calendar linked from the page. Branch coordinator emails are on the page.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 18 who get CalWORKs benefits, or current and former foster youth ages 16 to 24. Open to year-round employment services.
how_to_apply: Call 408-758-3797 to begin your application, or use the Register/Refer form on the page.
notes: Only for teens who get CalWORKs benefits or who are/were in foster care, so most teens do not qualify. Under 18 needs a work permit. Positions are across the county.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 14 or older.
how_to_apply: Apply through the volunteer page at sccld.org/volunteer. Or ask a local library.
notes: Serves the library district branches, not every city in the county (San Jose has its own library). Hours, training and schedule are on the volunteer page. See the separate homework-help tutor card (Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteer Tutor) for a similar after-school tutoring role.

who_can_apply: High school student (regular, alternative vocational, or working toward equivalency), enrolled or graduated within 6 months, legal right to work in the US, overall GPA of at least 2.5. Application plus transcript and proof of enrollment. Under 18 needs a work permit (from your counselor or EDD). May need Live Scan and a physical.
how_to_apply: Subscribe to alerts for the Student Intern Level I posting on the county jobs site and apply with your transcript when it opens. You can also email departments, or the coordinator at studentinterns@esa.sccgov.org.
notes: Interns can be hired any time of year depending on department needs, so keep the alert on. Some departments (District Attorney, Behavioral Health, Public Health, Parks) run their own internships; contact them directly.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older, free one afternoon Monday to Thursday from 3:30 to 6pm for a whole semester, and about 7 hours of training.
how_to_apply: Fill in the volunteer application on the library's volunteer page.
notes: The page lists these libraries: Campbell, Cupertino, Gilroy, Los Altos, Milpitas, Morgan Hill and Saratoga. Check that your branch is included. Training is online (about 7 hours). The broader card (Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteers) also includes after-school tutoring of a kindergarten to grade 6 student.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18 who live within the Schaumburg Township District Library service area. Grade level is not stated.
how_to_apply: The page invites eligible teens to apply but does not describe the method. Watch the library's Student Trustees page or ask the Teen Department.
notes: Board meetings are the third Monday of each month at 6:00 p.m., plus monthly meetings with the Teen Department. The next-cycle timing is a guess from this year's August 9 deadline.

who_can_apply: The page says the Volunteer Squad is open to students entering grades 8 to 12 in fall 2026. No age or residency rule is listed.
how_to_apply: The page does not say how to apply. Check the volunteer page in spring or ask the library.
notes: The contact email on the page was a blank placeholder. Call or visit the library.

who_can_apply: Minimum ages are not stated on the pages read. Check each job posting.
how_to_apply: Go to a job fair. Or apply on the district's online job board (BambooHR). Questions: Alex Khodan, Supervisor of Aquatics, alkhodan@parkfun.com.
notes: Pay figures for lifeguards are from the 2025 post, so check the current rate. In Illinois, workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before they start. This comes from the Evanston Township High School work permit page.

who_can_apply: Not stated on the page. Which classes you can take depends on your school district. Ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Ask your school counselor and look at the SCOE CTE course catalog. Contacts listed: Michelle McIntosh (Director), mmcintosh@scoe.net; Raelynn Sharp (Project Specialist), rsharp@scoe.net.
notes: The pages describe CTE (career technical education, 15 industry sectors) and list staff contacts. They do not list eligibility, enrollment steps, dates or work-based learning details. Treat this as a starting point and call SCOE. Age and grade are not stated, so ask your counselor.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 15 years old. Teens apply through the same process as adults; there is no separate teen program on the page.
how_to_apply: Submit one online application and choose one site. If chosen, you complete an interview, show proof of required immunizations and attend orientation. Onboarding takes about 6 to 8 weeks.
notes: Drop-in or on-call volunteering is not available; you pick a regular weekly shift. The portal opens on the first business day of each month and closes when a site is full, so apply early in the month. Only submit one application.

who_can_apply: Age 15 or older. You must give one 4-hour shift a week for at least six months in a row and at least 100 hours. They cannot take summer-only or school-break-only volunteers.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application and a volunteer reference form, then interview, attend a 2-hour orientation, pass a background check and health screening.
notes: The health screening asks for proof of vaccines, a flu shot, immunity to measles, mumps, rubella and varicella, a Tdap shot, and a TB test within the last 3 months. Ask your parent to start gathering records early. Questions: vmcvolunteer@hhs.sccgov.org.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page gives no narrower age or grade range. Space is limited to 12 teens.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application on the Teens page. Only completed forms are considered. Questions: outreach@sdmart.org.
notes: Closed right now. Check the page around late summer 2027 for the next application.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in grades 9 to 12 in a high school, Running Start, GED or homeschool program when they apply. Tides is the easiest level (any high school-aged person); Currents is the hands-on volunteer level.
how_to_apply: Attend a required online info session, then complete the application, then interview. Accepted teens do training before starting shifts. Questions: YOA@seattleaquarium.org.
notes: The page says its timeline is rough and may change. Washington L&I says its child labor rules 'only apply to minor employees, not volunteers.'

who_can_apply: People 16 and over for some positions and 18 and over for others. You must meet the minimum age when you apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online during an open period (you have one hour to finish), complete online training and forms within 2 weeks, do a 1-hour virtual group interview, then accept a placement. Onboarding includes a Washington State background check, an in-person health screening and a 90-minute orientation. Email VolunteerServices@seattlechildrens.org or call 206-987-4655.
notes: The youth service projects page (for ages under 16, such as donation drives or junior guilds) still carries a COVID-era notice, so it may be out of date. Nearly all shifts are weekdays starting between 9am and 2pm. Washington L&I says its child labor rules 'only apply to minor employees, not volunteers.'

who_can_apply: High school students entering senior year who are 16 or older by the program start. You need strong science interest. You must live in Greater Seattle or nearby. Out-of-state and international students are not accepted. You must be free for all eight weeks and able to do a Zoom interview.
how_to_apply: Online application with short essays, email addresses for two references (they get a recommendation link after you submit), a PDF transcript and a PDF resume. Applicants must be able to attend a Zoom interview with the selection committee.
notes: Highly competitive and designed for students without much research experience. Fred Hutch does not provide or arrange housing, and interns arrange their own transportation. In Washington there is no permit the teen carries: the employer must hold a minor work permit endorsement, and a parent/guardian (and the school during the school year) signs a parent authorization form (Parent Authorization for Summer Work if hired during summer break only) before the minor starts.

who_can_apply: Seattle Parks summer jobs are open to ages 16 and up (18 and up for some positions). Lifeguards need a current American Red Cross Lifeguarding, First Aid and CPR/AED certification. The Red Cross course requires you to be at least 15 on or before the last class. You must also pass a swim test.
how_to_apply: Get Red Cross certified. Then apply on GovernmentJobs.com when a listing is active, or email an Aquatic Application (or resume and cover letter) to parksaquatics@seattle.gov, or give it to the Aquatic Center Coordinator at any Seattle indoor pool. Hired lifeguards pass a background check, a physical and the NW Lifeguard Test. Call 206-684-4078.
notes: Red Cross certifications last 2 years. The cost of the Red Cross course is not stated on the Parks pages. Seattle Parks is a municipal employer; Washington L&I says state and municipal governments are not subject to Washington's child labor rules (federal rules still apply).

who_can_apply: Pre-Employment Training is for ages 13 to 18, and you can take it once every 2 years. It is the prerequisite for Parks paid internships (Teen Late Night, Summer, Community Learning Centers), which are for ages 15 to 21.
how_to_apply: Email PKS_Teen_Employment@seattle.gov (phone 206-684-4575) for details and to apply. The page also lists career readiness workshops (resumes, mock interviews, food handler permit help) at Teen Life Centers and community centers.
notes: Youth may do one paid internship at a time. Seattle Parks is a municipal employer; Washington L&I says state and municipal governments are not subject to Washington's child labor rules (federal rules still apply). The page also mentions free college tours for Seattle Public Schools students in grades 9 to 12.

who_can_apply: Washington state residents enrolled in a Washington high school in 10th or 11th grade. No coding experience needed. The program aims to include economically disadvantaged and future first-generation college students; the home page says it is open to all rising juniors and seniors at Washington state high schools.
how_to_apply: Apply online by the deadline (every application submitted on time is reviewed equally). Questions: cic@cs.washington.edu.
notes: Students must be able to get to the UW campus on their own. Absences are limited: after four absences students are dismissed. The stipend is described as a stipend, not a wage. Paid work for people under 18 in Washington needs a parent and school authorization form (the employer holds the Minor Work Permit). See permit.html?state=wa for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: High school students (page lists rising 10th, 11th and 12th graders and graduating seniors; no age range stated). No business experience required.
how_to_apply: Apply through partner Summer Springboard's online portal (Apply now link on the program page). Program questions go to the program contact listed on the page.
notes: Expensive paid pre-college program from a real university. The page says students can attend both experiences during a single extended stay, but it does not name a one-week Business Startup Bootcamp.

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 10 to 12. No prior experience required. The teen page does not state a minimum age; 15 teen volunteers were taken in 2026.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application by the deadline. Email teenambassadors@zoo.org for help. Sign up for recruitment updates at zoo.org/volunteer.
notes: The zoo's general volunteer program has its own rules (at least 16, one-year commitment, applications opening January 2027); those do not appear on the teen page. Applicants who identify with autism or ADHD can get application and interview support from Canopy Neurodiversity Foundation. Paid work for people under 18 in Washington needs a parent and school authorization form (the employer holds the Minor Work Permit). See permit.html?state=wa for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Age 16 to 24 at the start of the program (you can apply at 15 if you will be 16 by the start date). You must live in Seattle or attend Seattle Public Schools or Seattle Colleges, and household income must be at or below 80% of Area Median Income (for example $81,700 for 1 person, $116,650 for 4).
how_to_apply: Create an account and complete the online application at youthconnect.powerappsportals.us (the page links a help guide). The 250 internship spots are chosen by lottery. Pathways requires finishing SYEP Foundations or passing the Assessment of Skill.
notes: Proof of authorization to work in the U.S. is required for the internship, and an SSN or ITIN is needed to receive stipends and take part. The SYEP page does not mention work permits. Placements include City departments, which Washington L&I says are exempt from state child labor rules ('Public entities, including state and municipal governments, are not subject to Washington's child labor rules'; federal rules still apply), and private businesses and nonprofits, which are not exempt, so ask your placement about the parent/school authorization form. Questions: SYEP@seattle.gov or 206-386-1375.

who_can_apply: Students ages 6 to 18. Many students join through partner schools; some workshops allow direct sign-up.
how_to_apply: Check the calendar on the 826 Valencia site or contact a Writing Center.
notes: All 826 Valencia programs are free, and most students join through partner schools. The stipended Youth Leadership Advisory Board (grades 8 to 12) and Black Literary Achievement Club are listed on the SFPL page; the stipend amount is not posted.

who_can_apply: Any current high school student (grades 9 to 12). Preference goes to current Breakthrough students and current or former Breakthrough volunteers.
how_to_apply: Fill in the notify form on the BLP page to hear when the summer 2027 application opens.
notes: Breakthrough's separate Teaching Fellow job is a paid summer teaching residency with housing for people from outside SF and does not say it is for high schoolers, so it is not listed here. Located at 350 Masonic Ave.

who_can_apply: Current 9th or 10th graders at an SFUSD school, with a 2.5 GPA and a C or higher in science and math, authorized to work in the US, able to commit 2 to 3 years through high school, and able to get to the Academy after school and on Saturdays.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in February 2027. Contact CiS@calacademy.org.
notes: SFUSD students only. Sign up for the Academy's Youth Programs mailing list to hear when applications open. Questions: CiS@calacademy.org.

who_can_apply: SFUSD high school students, through a partnership with City College. Talk to your high school counselor about which classes are offered. Non-SFUSD students, or SFUSD students who want a class their school does not offer, use the Concurrent Enrollment page.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor. Questions: dualenrollment@ccsf.edu. Non-SFUSD students use the CCSF Concurrent Enrollment page.
notes: Classes can be at your high school or at a CCSF location. A permission consent form for high school students is linked on the page. Grade and credit rules are not stated on the page, so ask your counselor.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24. Register with the Google Form on the DCYF listing.
how_to_apply: Register using the form linked from the sf.gov youth opportunities page. Bring a resume if you have one.
notes: The page does not list which employers will attend. It is a free event, not a job offer.

who_can_apply: San Francisco high school students. No prior experience needed.
how_to_apply: Watch the Department of Elections high school programs page for the next application. Questions: hsp@sfgov.org or 415-558-6100.
notes: Same page: if you will be 16 by the next Election Day you can apply to be a high school poll worker, with a stipend up to $245. A poll worker application for the November 2026 election was due to be posted there in mid-August.

who_can_apply: High school age students, 15 to 18 for first-time Explainers (up to 20 for returning ones). Must be able to get a work permit, attend all training dates and work the whole school year or summer session. No science background needed.
how_to_apply: When open, apply on the Exploratorium Current Openings page under the job title High School Explainer. Questions: hsesupervisors@exploratorium.edu.
notes: About 130 paid positions a year across two cohorts. The Current Openings list did not show on my read, so check it for a live posting. A separate PACE program serves ages 17 to 21.

who_can_apply: Cadets must attend high school in San Francisco (or equivalent) or live in the City and County of San Francisco. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page on the academy's website.
notes: The site does not list an age range or application dates, so ask the academy. It is a project of the SF Black Firefighters Association. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 and in high school. The page says teens on Heart&Sole teams must identify as female, and males are welcome on Girls on the Run teams. Needs a completed reference, a signed waiver (parent signs if under 18) and the Junior Coach application. Background check at 18.
how_to_apply: Complete the Junior Coach application on the Girls on the Run Bay Area site. Email admin@gotrbayarea.org or call (415) 863-8942 to ask about late spots or the next season.
notes: The Oct 12, 2026 date on the sf.gov listing is for adult coaches (18 and up), not Junior Coaches. Teams meet at least once a week.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 (high school). Priority goes to youth underrepresented in tech, students at high schools with few or no computer science classes, and girls and LGBTQIA+ youth. Online classes are for San Francisco students only.
how_to_apply: Pick a class. Then register on the Mission Bit Classes page when registration opens.
notes: Mission Bit's Tech Start career prep is ages 18 to 26, not for most high schoolers. College Connections (Nov 7, 2026, 10:30 a.m. to noon at Chase Center, grades 9 to 12) closes registration Oct 27, 2026 per sf.gov.

who_can_apply: San Francisco youth ages 14 to 17 (the DCYF newsletter lists grades 9 and 10 for this round). Apply through the JCYC Workhub.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the JCYC Workhub (jcycworkhub.org). Ask the YMCA contact on the program page about your neighborhood site.
notes: Pay rate is not stated on the pages read, so ask your site. Contact the Buchanan YMCA ((415) 931-9622) about eligibility.

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24. Aimed at 'opportunity youth' who are out of school or not working.
how_to_apply: Apply on the New Door intake portal linked from their site. The application link is on the official page.
notes: Mainly for 17 year olds and older who are not in a regular school path; not the usual fit for a student who is in school. Pay is not stated on the pages read.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 24 who live in or go to school in San Francisco (that is the only rule on the OFA page).
how_to_apply: Create an account on the JCYC Workhub, complete the application and submit before the spring deadline.
notes: JCYC runs the applications. B2SF and the OFA fellowships share an application with other youth programs. Your interests decide where you are placed.

who_can_apply: California residents ages 16 and 17 who are US citizens and not in prison for a felony or ruled mentally unable to vote by a court.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online form at registertovote.ca.gov (linked from the Secretary of State page).
notes: Not a job or internship, but a real civic step. Your registration becomes active when you turn 18. Citizenship is required.

who_can_apply: San Francisco high school students (there are separate college tracks). The application page says details are coming soon.
how_to_apply: Use the High School Internship application page. Questions: sfprojectpull1996@gmail.com.
notes: The pages do not list age, pay or a deadline yet. Check the application page in early 2027.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 in San Francisco.
how_to_apply: Email yep@sfgov.org or call Yuri Ugarte at 415-452-3863.
notes: This page replaced the older Workreation name on the department site. An older listing says applicants need work-permit papers and no citizenship is required.

who_can_apply: No minimum age is listed for youth volunteers; if a branch is not on the application form it cannot take volunteers right now.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online volunteer form at https://on.sfpl.org/yva
notes: FOG Readers tutoring takes select volunteers age 15 and up (6 month commitment, needs fingerprinting). The same page lists paid teen jobs: YELL (summer, applications open each March) and the Youth Advisory Board (applications for this year closed Sept 14).

who_can_apply: High school students from San Francisco's southeast neighborhoods; internships start after junior year.
how_to_apply: The SFPUC page does not list an application. It says SFUSD students are referred through SFUSD's Career and Technical Education office, so ask them or the SFPUC workforce team.
notes: Narrow neighborhood focus (southeast San Francisco). The same SFPUC page also lists YouthWorks and Project Pull.

who_can_apply: Nature Trail: ages 12 to 14. Junior Zoologists: ages 15 to 17. Leadership Fellows: entering grades 10 to 12 in fall 2026 (ages 15 to 17 per the zoo's volunteer page).
how_to_apply: Each track has its own page. Nature Trail and Junior Zoologists include an online interview. Questions: naturetrail@sfzoo.org (Nature Trail), izvolunteer@sfzoo.org (Junior Zoologists), luked@sfzoo.org (Leadership Fellows), or (415) 753-7080.
notes: Located in San Francisco (a long trip from Sacramento). Applications were closed when checked. The Leadership Fellows page gave 2026 dates, so check for 2027 dates.

who_can_apply: Bay Area high school students who may have limited opportunities to engage with biomedical research, per the page. Grade range and other rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Email the program first, through the Contact Us link on the ImmunoX site, because the page is out of date. The page links a Google Form for 2026 camper applications.
notes: Re-read the ImmunoX page on 2026-10-09. It is still titled ImmunoExplore - Summer Camp 2025. It says 2026 Camper Applications are now open and links the Google Form. It posts no grade range, camp dates or deadlines, so none are listed here. Confirm dates and grades with ImmunoX before applying.

who_can_apply: Current juniors at an SFUSD high school or an SF public charter school, no exceptions. Grades and science background are not used to pick students; low-income and first-generation college students are encouraged.
how_to_apply: Fill in the interest form to hear when the application opens, then submit the online application. About 50 students are interviewed for 25 spots; results come by email in April.
notes: The SEP high school programs page says 2025-26 is the final year of a program and that there will be no summer internship for 2026; it is not clear which program that means, while the intern page invites 2027 interest. Confirm with SEP at 415-364-8077.

who_can_apply: Mainly public high school students in San Francisco. Programs are free.
how_to_apply: Call (415) 574-8137 or email info@youthartexchange.org.
notes: Also runs summer camps for grades 3 to 5 and classes for adults. The page does not mention paid internships or exact ages.

who_can_apply: 11th or 12th graders (rising juniors, rising seniors and graduating seniors) who live in or go to school in San Francisco and can get a work permit. Youth Leadership Team members must have finished a full YouthWorks session.
how_to_apply: Create an account and apply through the JCYC Workhub portal. Expect a short application and an interview step.
notes: Interns work in City departments such as the SFPUC, the Library and SFO. Former interns can return as paid Youth Leadership Team members. Ask JCYC about work permit help.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 through 11, at least 14 years old, who have finished 8th grade and have a GPA of 3.0 or higher. Seniors are pointed to the college or adult program after graduation.
how_to_apply: Use the 'High school volunteers (junior volunteers)' online application during the window. A follow-up email asks for your transcript and parental consent, then teacher referrals, an interview and orientation.
notes: The hospital calls this program highly sought after and competitive, and says onboarding can take up to three months. Health requirements after acceptance include MMR, varicella, Tdap, COVID, flu and TB testing. Contact scv.volunteers@sharp.com or 619-502-3606. The two official pages differ by one day on the close date; use Nov 12 to be safe.

who_can_apply: High school students can register for summer classes through Open University without being admitted to SJSU.
how_to_apply: Register as an Open University student using the first-time or returning student steps on the SJSU Summer registration page. Questions: professionaled@sjsu.edu or 408-924-2670.
notes: You pay college tuition. The page does not state age, grade or approval rules for high schoolers or the cost, so ask Summer Session. For fall and spring the page points to the Dual Enrollment Program (dualenrollment@sjsu.edu).

who_can_apply: Middle school, high school and college students in career and technical education, in a school chapter. Virtual chapters exist for students without a classroom chapter.
how_to_apply: Ask your CTE teacher, or use the 12 Steps to Start a Chapter or Virtual Chapter on skillsusa.org. Phone 844-875-4557, email customercare@skillsusa.org.
notes: Most useful if your school has a trades or tech CTE pathway.

who_can_apply: Current high school students in grades 10 to 12. The page describes it as an opportunity for Los Angeles teens.
how_to_apply: Closed now. Email youthprograms@skirball.org or use the inquiry form on the Skirball youth programs page.
notes: The same page offers TeenTix LA. It is a free pass for teens to visit museums and culture events across Los Angeles (la.teentix.org).

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who are 18 or younger and either live in Skokie or attend a Skokie school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Service contact form to join the email list. Or email teenteam@skokielibrary.info. You can also come to an upcoming teen volunteer event.
notes: Some opportunities are only on school breaks or days off. If you need hours for a ticket or a court order, the page says to email the teen team with your name and school.

who_can_apply: High school student teams registered by a coach or teacher. Team size and cost are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: A teacher or coach pre-registers the team on the National Science Bowl coach site (apps.orau.gov/nsb-coach). You do not need all team details for step one.
notes: Needs a school team and coach. Volunteer sign-up info is due to be shared by December 2026 (no experience needed). Event is at SLAC, 2575 Sand Hill Road, Menlo Park.

who_can_apply: High school students from all backgrounds. The page lists no age, grade or residency limits. Apply on the Kaleidoscope platform.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Kaleidoscope platform when the next cycle opens. It is linked from the SAGE site.
notes: The page says the camp is free. Whether it is overnight, and the 2027 dates, were not on the page I read. Check the SAGE site in February.

who_can_apply: Students in grade 10 or 11 with a 3.0 GPA and strong math scores. You must be at a public or scholarship-funded private high school. You need a strong interest in computer science. Bay Area schools within the radius are preferred.
how_to_apply: Join the interest list on smash.org/programs and watch for the application. Contact devo@smash.org.
notes: Based in Oakland (2148 Broadway). SMASH Virtual is a separate online option for a national audience; its cost is not stated. SMASH Morehouse is for males and SMASH Spelman for females.

who_can_apply: Students at partner high schools: Jefferson Union HSD, San Mateo Union HSD, South San Francisco USD, Sequoia Union HSD and Gateway charter school. Need a C or better to get college credit.
how_to_apply: Sign up through your high school (talk to your counselor), submit the Skyline application on CCCApply, then attend an enrollment workshop to register and get parent approval.
notes: Grades become part of a permanent college record and can affect financial aid and college admission. Contacts on the page: hendrieg@smccd.edu or fuentesa@smccd.edu. Canada College and College of San Mateo run their own dual enrollment pages, not checked here.

who_can_apply: 16 or older (by June 2 in the 2026 cycle), current junior or senior, 2.5 GPA or higher, attends an eligible school in the service area, no relatives who work for the internship host, own transportation.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Sacramento Works site before the deadline. Steps: application review, document check, computer random drawing (55 candidates), work readiness workshops and video interview, manager review, in-person interview. Up to 25 interns are chosen.
notes: Questions: SacramentoWorksFor.Youth@seta.net. Random drawing means even qualified students may not be picked. Check the school list on the Sacramento Works SMUD page. Age rule and school-area details come from the 2026 posting; confirm for 2027.

who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 14 to 24, in or out of school. Residency and income rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Use the Sign Up Here form. Or contact a job coordinator in your area. Or call the Inglewood office at 310.680.3700.
notes: Teen Centers for ages 13 to 17 (Inglewood Mon to Thu 3 to 6 PM, Hawthorne Mon to Fri 3 to 6 PM) are listed too but are not job programs. Bridge to Work is for foster youth only. The page does not mention work permits. California requires a permit for paid work under 18.

who_can_apply: Female high school students who are ready to start exploring college. Parent or guardian permission is required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer Programs Interest Form now for news. Then apply in the online portal when it opens Jan 29, 2027.
notes: Costs money. Applying is not an application to Spelman and does not promise admission. The Mar 29 closing date is on the main summer programs page; the CPI page itself says only that late submissions are not accepted.

who_can_apply: Female high school students in 11th grade with a 3.0 GPA and at least a 3.0 in English and science. Parent permission is required. One page also says juniors and seniors, so confirm your grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer Programs Interest Form for news. Then apply in the online portal when it opens Jan 29, 2027.
notes: Costs money. The Mar 29 closing date is on the main summer programs page; the ECP page itself does not give a due date.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. St. Charles Public Library cardholders and returning volunteers come first. Under 18 needs parent or guardian permission.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. It takes about 10 minutes. Answer every question. Applying does not mean you get a spot, because openings are limited.
notes: For summer, enter the grade you are going into. List dates you cannot volunteer. Contact details are behind a hidden email on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students, per the page. The page does not state age, grade range, residency or citizenship rules.
how_to_apply: Apply when the application opens on Nov 10, 2026 (the page does not describe the form). Attend the free info session on Nov 10, 2026, or RSVP through the page. Questions: aimi-hs-programs@stanford.edu.
notes: Re-read the AIMI page on 2026-10-07. The dates are for the Summer 2027 program. The page does not state pay or cost, length, detailed eligibility or whether the program is in person, so the pay and work-permit answers are not confirmed. Confirm those with aimi-hs-programs@stanford.edu before applying. The Summer Health AI Bootcamp is a separate program on the same site and is not covered here.

who_can_apply: Rising sophomores, juniors and seniors who are at least 14 and can commute daily to the Palo Alto campus. You need a laptop.
how_to_apply: Sign up for application announcements on the CARE page; email carehighschoolprogram@stanford.edu.
notes: Pay-to-play. Day program, about 9am to 3pm on weekdays. No housing or transportation provided; lunch and snacks included. No application fee waivers in 2026.

who_can_apply: Teens. Start with an online orientation, then a scheduled interview; eligible teens get the application link after the interview. Age and schedule rules are given in the orientation.
how_to_apply: Start with the online orientation on volunteer.stanfordchildrens.org, then interview. Questions: volunteerservices@stanfordchildrens.org.
notes: Minimum age is not stated on the page. Ask the volunteer office.

who_can_apply: Live in Alameda, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara or Santa Cruz County; 16 or older by the start date; unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher; some biology, chemistry or programming background.
how_to_apply: 2026 process: email essays, transcripts, resume, science course list and one recommendation letter to grips-program@stanford.edu by the deadline.
notes: Decisions in 2026 came mid-March to mid-April. The 2027 timing is a guess from last year; check the page in December.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Inpatient unit roles need 18. Needs 6 to 8 hours of online training, a background check, a health screening (including a TB test), and orientation within 30 days of selection.
how_to_apply: Apply on volunteer.stanfordhealthcare.org. Questions: VolunteerResources@stanfordhealthcare.org or 650-723-7424.
notes: Stanford says this does not count for school clinical-hour needs and has no shadowing.

who_can_apply: 16 by start; strongly suggested to have taken high school biology. Needs transcripts, resume, test scores, essay and a STEM teacher recommendation.
how_to_apply: Create an account and apply through the MEDCSI SlideRoom portal when the new cycle opens. Needs transcripts, resume, test scores (if available), essay and a STEM teacher recommendation.
notes: Pay-to-play and expensive. Fees shown are 2026 prices. No stipend or work experience. The program also admits undergraduate pre-med students.

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors, 16 or older, unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher, living in and attending high school in San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Marin, Alameda, Contra Costa or Santa Cruz County. You must live with a family member or legal guardian; housing and transportation are not provided.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the PIPS portal when the next cycle opens. Check the PIPS page for the next cycle.
notes: About 35 to 40 students are admitted. The page says in person, with some remote work possible. The 2027 timing is a guess from last year.

who_can_apply: Currently in grades 8 to 11 and between 13 and 19 years old during the program dates. Domestic and international students may apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online with unofficial transcripts and the application fee; rank up to three courses. Financial aid is a separate form due about a week after the deadline.
notes: Pay-to-play. Prices and dates are from 2026. The page says to join the mailing list for future dates. Age wording on the admissions page is 'between 13 and 19'.

who_can_apply: Juniors or seniors now (classes of 2027 and 2028), 16 or older by June 2027, living in and attending high school in the U.S., and a U.S. citizen or green card holder. Local Bay Area students are strongly favored. You must live with a family member or guardian.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcripts and recommendations. In 2026 the decision date was Apr 10.
notes: Very competitive. Housing and transportation not provided. Fee and decision date shown are from the 2026 cycle.

who_can_apply: Current high school juniors who are low-income and first-generation college students living in Northern California. About 24 students are admitted.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the SlideRoom link on the SMYSP page when it opens. Contact: smysp-team@stanford.edu.
notes: The 2027 timing is a guess from last year.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 for 2026-27 who attend a high school inside the City of Stonecrest. A parent or guardian must register you and send one proof of school enrollment. You must commit to regular attendance.
how_to_apply: A parent or guardian fills out the Stonecrest NextGen Program Application Form on the program page and sends proof of enrollment. Spots are first-come, first-served.
notes: Only 30 spots. City Hall: 3120 Stonecrest Boulevard, Suite 190, Stonecrest, GA 30038, 770-224-0200. Write to Nicholas Ivey at nivey@stonecrestga.gov. Unpaid, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: The library accepts volunteers age 13 and older. VolunTEENs is for ages 13 to 18. The district serves Sugar Grove and parts of Montgomery and Aurora.
how_to_apply: Fill out the library volunteer form from the circulation desk. For short projects, use the Service Hour Project form. Contact Nichole at 630-409-1589. Or contact Christine Edison, Adult and Teen Services Manager, at 630-409-3131.
notes: The apply link is the Service Hour Project form for ages 13 to 18.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 and a half to 18 (must turn 16 before the end of the residential phase and not turn 19 before the start). U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident. At risk of dropping out or behind in credits. Never convicted of a felony or under indictment. Must be willing to be drug free, able to do the program (sports physical), and must volunteer; it cannot be court ordered.
how_to_apply: Register for and go to an in person orientation. This is the first step. You get the application there. Then you send in documents. You do a one on one interview of up to an hour. You go to an invited roll call. Phone 562-936-1759, call or text (916) 639-2260, or email admissions@SunburstYouthAcademy.com.
notes: The eligibility page lists documents to submit including a California ID, birth certificate and Social Security card, so go with a parent or guardian. The pages read did not say which counties are served. The eligibility page still shows the earlier class dates (January to June 2026).

who_can_apply: Age 13 and up. Most roles require volunteers 18 and older to be fingerprinted and cleared first, so ask which roles take teens.
how_to_apply: Fill one application: general, library, or recreation and senior center. Volunteer Resources: 408-730-7533.
notes: Official page read directly. Fill out only one application.

who_can_apply: The pages read do not list rules on who can join. Shadow Days require your home school counselor's approval. Ask your counselor or call SVCTE about enrollment.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor about enrolling in SVCTE courses. To visit, apply for a Shadow Day through the SVCTE site (your counselor must approve it). Phone (408) 723-6403, Monday to Friday, 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. The site lists Milthon Marquez as Post-Secondary Planning Coach.
notes: Re-read the SVCTE home page and the Shadow Days, Dual Enrollment, Internships and Post-Secondary Options pages on 2026-10-07. The homepage lists 22 career technical courses (the old file said more than 24 pathways). Dual enrollment courses are taught by college professors at the high school campus. Shadow Days: after talking to your home school counselor, submit interest on the site; the counselor must approve it, and you get a confirmation 7 days before the visit. Eligibility, costs, deadlines and enrollment dates are not stated on the pages read.

who_can_apply: Students at a participating Georgia high school or approved home study program. 11th and 12th graders and returning 10th graders can take any approved course. New 10th graders take career courses, or core courses with the required SAT or ACT score. 9th graders can join but get no state funding.
how_to_apply: Get approval from your high school and parent or guardian, apply to the college, and apply for dual enrollment funding at GAfutures.org. Atlanta Tech asks for PSAT, SAT, ACT or Accuplacer scores (a 2.6 HOPE GPA can be used for 11th and 12th graders).
notes: Atlanta Tech funding rules on its page: 15 funded hours per semester, a 30 hour total, and funding ends after two course withdrawals. Atlanta Tech high school contact: hsadmissions@atlantatech.edu or 404-225-4511. This is a course program, not a job, so no work permit applies. The TCSG page sends students to GAfutures.org. The GAfutures Dual Enrollment Application Procedure page says students must apply to the college first, then complete the online Dual Enrollment Funding application; its Apply Now button opens secure.gafutures.org, which shows a GAfutures sign-in page first.

who_can_apply: Teens who are 14 or older by Nov 21, 2026.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the official page (vhub.at/TeenVolunteer). Questions: volunteer@thetech.org or 408-294-8324.
notes: The Oct 7 card said applications open Oct 9 to Oct 23, 2026. On Oct 9 the official page no longer shows that window, and the apply hub page shows no dates in its HTML (its content loads with JavaScript), so the status is unconfirmed. Re-check the official page for a new window. The page lists three mandatory 3.5-hour orientation and tour sessions on Saturdays Nov 14, Nov 21 and Dec 5, 2026, 9:00 AM to 12:30 PM. Applications are reviewed after the deadline by availability and answers. The page gives no year for Jan 3. The page's email addresses are encoded and could not be re-read on Oct 9; the email is kept from the Oct 7 read.

who_can_apply: Must be at least 14 and live in or near Los Angeles. You can start from fall of 9th grade through fall of 11th grade. Seniors and second-semester juniors are not accepted. Training and shifts are in person in West LA.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Then go to every training, interview and orientation session. After you are accepted, show a negative TB blood test from the last 12 months. To hear about the next round, join the Prospective Teen Line Volunteer interest list on the page.
notes: Serious role that handles hard topics. Hotline runs every evening from West LA, no remote option. Training is 65+ hours per the volunteer page (the main Teen Line page says over 100). The page lists no pay and the role earns community service hours.

who_can_apply: Youth in 3rd through 12th grade, ages 8 to 18. Each county sets up its own program.
how_to_apply: Contact your County Extension Office. Find a club. It needs at least five youth from three families. Choose at least one project. Then enroll online in 4HOnline.
notes: The October 31 date is the price cutoff, not a closing date. Counties customize their programs, so call your county Extension office first. This is a club and leadership program, not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Male high school students who finished their junior year. You need at least one semester left. You must never have been to Boys State. School officials must recommend you. You need a parent or guardian's permission. The sponsoring American Legion Post must certify you. You must sign the Texas Boys State Pledge.
how_to_apply: A school official nominates you. That can be a principal, teacher, coach or counselor. A local American Legion Post certifies and sponsors you. Ask your counselor or contact your local Post. The program's site is texasboysstate.com.
notes: Boys State is for boys. Girls State is a separate program. The site says the program asks for one or more boys nominated from each accredited public or private high school. Top delegates may be picked for Boys Nation. Confirm the 2027 dates and fee with your local Post.

who_can_apply: Female students now in their junior year at any Texas public or private high school. An ALA Unit may sponsor a home school student who meets the rules. You can attend only once. A student whose religion does not allow her to pledge allegiance to the U.S. flag is not eligible. You must be able to take part in all activities.
how_to_apply: You do not apply on your own. A school nominates you through faculty and a school official, and a local ALA Unit, the school or a community group reserves the spot. Ask your counselor or a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit early in the spring. Questions: GirlsState@alatexas.org or 214-733-7945.
notes: Girls State is for girls. Texas Boys State is a separate program run by the American Legion. Students chosen must attend the whole session to earn the certificate and pin.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 15 and a half to 18 who are U.S. citizens and Texas residents and are physically and mentally able to take part fully. The program is for youth who are currently disengaged from school.
how_to_apply: Go to an information briefing with a recruiter. Send the application packet and documents. Do a virtual interview with a case manager. Have a mentor fill out a mentor packet. Then a review board decides. Main line: 877-822-0050.
notes: This is for teens who are off track in school, not a job program. Campus: 600 HWY 3013 West, Eagle Lake, TX 77434.

who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 15 by June 1 of the program year and enrolled in high school for the next school year. The flyer describes the program as ages 15 to 17.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, upload two recommendation letters from two different references, and upload your most recent report card. Accepted volunteers must show vaccine records (MMR, varicella, Tdap) and a negative TB test, and attend mandatory orientation on the first two days.
notes: The flyer calls the program prestigious and highly sought-after, so expect competition. Up to two absences are allowed. There are no weekend or make-up shifts. Questions: ATXNCVolunteerServices@texaschildrens.org or 737-229-3388. Check the Texas Children's volunteer pages for the 2027 flyer.

who_can_apply: Students at a Texas high school with a DECA chapter. Texas DECA members must take part in a career and technical education (CTE) program. Chapters must offer business or marketing courses. The official pages list no age or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's DECA advisor, who registers members through DECA's online system. If your school has no chapter, DECA lists six steps to start one. State advisor: Josh Shankle, shankle@texasdeca.org. State office phone: 817-900-8037.
notes: DECA's page lists 352 Texas high school chapters. The state website does not explain joining step by step, so start with your school's advisor.

who_can_apply: Students who sign up for an agricultural science class at a school with an FFA chapter. The FAQ says the grade depends on the district and that home-schooled students are not covered by the program. Junior FFA needs age 8 and 3rd grade.
how_to_apply: Your first contact is your local agricultural science teacher. Sign up for an agricultural science class.
notes: Junior FFA is a state-only membership at $9 a year, says the membership page.

who_can_apply: Secondary students in a state-approved Health Science program, or who plan a career in the health professions. Middle school students in grades 6 to 8 who like a health career path can also join. Membership goes through affiliated school chapters.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's health science teacher or chapter advisor about joining the chapter. State office: texashosa@texashosa.org or 1-877-728-0150.
notes: State office: 201 W. Hillside Road Suite 26, Laredo, TX 78041. Ask your advisor for the fee amount and conference dates.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. Anyone under 16 must come with a parent or guardian. Everyone under 18 needs a parent or guardian's signed permission, and a parent signs the liability waiver. Each opening can add its own requirements. Minors cannot do some kinds of work.
how_to_apply: Search openings in the TPWD volunteer portal and apply online. Or contact a park's volunteer coordinator. TPWD checks your application and matches you to an opening. Questions: Volunteer@TPWD.Texas.gov or 512-389-8674.
notes: Park host jobs are long RV-based stays and are not a fit for most teens. The page lists Buffalo Soldiers, State Park Ambassadors and Texas Outdoor Family as special programs, but this card does not cover their age rules. Volunteers 18 and older in ongoing roles must pass a yearly background check.

who_can_apply: High school students who finished at least one high school chemistry course before the summer. The pages give no grade, age or residency rule. You need a recommendation from a high school chemistry teacher. Selection is merit based and space is limited to 20 students.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, which includes a short chemistry research statement. The form sends a request to your chemistry teacher for the recommendation. Questions: tamu_react@tamu.edu.
notes: The program ran for the first time in 2025 (July 14 to 25). The fee and rules above come from the 2026 pages, so check them again when the 2027 application opens. The program site is a Google Sites page run by the department.

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 22 (and under 22 as of September 1 of the previous year) who get special education services under IDEA or have a disability under Section 504, and who are in an educational program. That includes secondary school, home school and other recognized programs.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Texas Workforce Solutions Vocational Rehabilitation Services office. Counselors refer current VR participants. Students who have not applied for VR but meet the disability rule may also be candidates. Statewide contact: 512-936-6400 or vr.office.locator@twc.texas.gov.
notes: Only for students with disabilities. Texas child labor hour limits for 14 and 15 year olds still apply. The pages read do not give a posted 2027 timeline.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 through 18. You must be in school or a graduate with a satisfactory record. You must be unmarried (except marriage under 18) and not on active duty. You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (headquarters may waive). You must be of good moral character. Cadets who join before age 19 can stay until 21.
how_to_apply: Pick a local squadron from the Texas Wing unit listing. Go to three squadron meetings as a trial. The squadron and higher headquarters must accept you. Call Wing headquarters at 936-205-9013 with questions.
notes: Meeting times differ by squadron. This is a youth program, not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Students or recent high school graduates who want to learn about skilled trades.
how_to_apply: Fill out the student intake form on the Student page. Parents can email info@thetradecollective.org.
notes: The page does not list specific internships or pay. It says the group is forming partnerships with high schools, colleges and universities. Address on the site: 1910 Greenwood Street, Evanston.

who_can_apply: Must be 14 to 18 (14 by April 1) and in middle or high school, and must live and/or attend school in Travis County. Teens with disabilities can apply up to age 22. Other factors such as household income may also be considered.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application (Jotform) and upload a Social Security card and a school ID or recent report card. Eligible applicants are invited to a mandatory job readiness training, then matched to a host site if space allows. Applying does not guarantee a placement.
notes: Phone 512-854-4590. Pay rate, hours and program length are not stated on the page. The page does not mention a work permit. Texas rules for 14 and 15 year olds limit hours (see Texas Workforce Commission child labor page).

who_can_apply: No age limit. Minors need a signed parental consent form. Volunteers 15 and under (the FAQ says under 15) need an adult chaperone age 21 or older, one adult per 10 young volunteers.
how_to_apply: Sign up for an event on the TreePeople events calendar. The confirmation email has the waiver and parent consent forms. Groups must email volunteer@treepeople.org first.
notes: TreePeople's jobs page lists only an 18+ fellowship, so this is the way in for teens. The page gives two versions of the chaperone age rule (15 and under vs under 15), so confirm by email.

who_can_apply: Teens who are in high school or about to start, and at least 14 as of May 1.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the link is posted. You must finish every step. These are a required Challenge Day, a required volunteer tree planting and an interview.
notes: Competitive. Not everyone who applies gets a job. Returning members can apply for outside study spots with partner groups. 2026 dates are shown. Watch the page for the 2027 schedule. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit (employment certificate) is required for minors under 16, so 14 and 15 year olds need one. A school issuing officer or the county school superintendent gives it.

who_can_apply: High school students in Dublin Unified, Livermore Valley Joint Unified or Pleasanton Unified school districts.
how_to_apply: Sign up through your high school's regular class registration; your school's College and Career Specialist finishes the ROP signup. Phone (925) 455-4800.
notes: You must arrange your own transportation to off-site classes. Classes run at six high schools and Las Positas College, during the school day and after school.

who_can_apply: Current rules are not posted. Older postings (2022) said 16 and up with photo ID; confirm with the program.
how_to_apply: Call (510) 985-9915 or email info@oaklandtrybe.org. Trybe also has a Jobs/Internships page on its site.
notes: Trybe's free summer camp is for kids 0 to 14; the paid youth internship is separate and the summer page shows only a flyer with no details. Call to ask about 2027. Do not confuse oaklandtrybe.org with trybe.org.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors who live in the City of Tucker.
how_to_apply: Use the online application on the city's Youth Council page. Members may reapply at the end of their term.
notes: The page lists no direct phone or email; it links to the city's Contacting the City page. The page does not post the next application date. Unpaid, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 at the start of the summer program. You must be eligible to work in the United States. The page states no school or residency rule beyond the Twin Cities base. If you join through Step Up or Right Track, those programs have their own rules.
how_to_apply: Look for open positions on the Corps Join page (filter for youth programs) or call the youth program staff at 651-209-9900. Step Up and Right Track applicants apply through those programs.
notes: 2026 home bases were Tamarack Nature Center (White Bear Lake), Harriet Alexander Nature Center (Roseville), Mississippi Gateway Regional Park (Brooklyn Park) and Minnesota Valley National Wildlife Refuge (Bloomington). Do not mix this up with the Summer Youth Corps, the live-in camping crew. That program is not active in 2026 and the Corps is rethinking its youth programs.

who_can_apply: Youth in grades 8 to 12 who like STEM, from across the Twin Cities. The University of Minnesota summer camps page says students entering grades 8 and 9 are eligible to apply. The page describes a pro-girl program. It does not say whether boys can join.
how_to_apply: Use the Eureka! online application or the PDF application on the program page. Do this when registration opens. The PDF comes in English, Spanish or Somali. Contact: girlsinc@ywcampls.org or 612-215-4369.
notes: Described as a pro-girl program (Girls Inc.), so ask whether it is for girls only. Interns are treated as volunteers by the worksite because the stipend comes from Girls Inc., not the worksite. Minnesota work permit rules were not checked.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18. The page does not list other rules.
how_to_apply: Watch the Youth Employment and Training Initiatives page and the Park Board temporary jobs page (minneapolisparks.org/jobs/temporary_jobs/) for the next application.
notes: Pay, season and hours are not stated on the page, so ask the Park Board before you plan. The same page lists Minneapolis Park Corps for ages 18 to 24 as paid training (not for teens). The Park Board teen page also lists Youthline, a mentorship program for ages 12 to 17. Minnesota work permit rules were not checked.

who_can_apply: Youth leaders ages 14 to 17. Members serve a two year term.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Contact Adrian Waters at Awaters@minneapolisparks.org or 612-849-9048 to ask when the next group is chosen.
notes: The teen programs page calls it a select group. Confirm how to apply and whether it is paid before you plan around it.

who_can_apply: High school students entering grade 11 or 12. Priority goes to students who have not been in Discover STEM before. Admission is competitive, and the program especially encourages applicants from underrepresented communities.
how_to_apply: Apply online, or by mail on request. Send an unofficial high school transcript and personal statement answers. Do not send the application in pieces. Those are not reviewed.
notes: The camps page for the college also lists other high school options, such as the Run the World AI Explorers Camp (grades 11 and 12) and a Summer Computer Academy for girls in grades 6 to 12. Not a job.

who_can_apply: Teens from across the Twin Cities. The page does not state an age or grade range.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application steps. Applications for 2027-28 open in spring 2027. Follow @walkerteens on Instagram for programming info and updates.
notes: The Walker also offers free Teen Maker Break art sessions, monthly on the third Saturday from 2 to 5 p.m. (materials and snacks provided). Ask the Walker whether WACTAC members are paid and what ages can join.

who_can_apply: Must be 16 by the program start (June 15 in 2026). Two references (at least one from a school mentor), signed parent consent form, English fluency, proof of MMR, varicella and Tdap shots, and TB testing. The page names no upper age limit.
how_to_apply: Register in the UC Davis Health VolunTEEN portal, finish all health clearance items, and submit references. Questions: 916-734-2401 or volunteer.services@health.ucdavis.edu.
notes: Located at the Sacramento medical campus (Davis II Building, 2420 Stockton Blvd). Health clearances (MMR, varicella, Tdap, TB test) take time, so start early. Spots are limited and filled first come, first served.

who_can_apply: Students in career programs at Davis Senior High, MLK Jr. High, Da Vinci Charter Academy and Esparto High (2025 cohort). Through DJUSD, students are matched to internships by the Internship Specialist.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's CTE teacher or the DJUSD Internship Specialist (Alexha Contreras, 530-757-5400 ext 170). The DJUSD list shows a UC Davis Center for Valley Fever internship in spring.
notes: Based on a July 2025 UC Davis Health news story and the DJUSD CTE internship list. There is no UC Davis application page. Confirm that it runs in spring 2027.

who_can_apply: High-achieving high school students. No minimum GPA. Admission is first come, first served once your application is complete. No academic credit.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, two short-answer questions, and pay the application fee. Transcript and personal statement are optional but helpful.
notes: Expensive. The program moved to a new website (discoveryprograms.ucdavis.edu), and the fee page still shows 2025 numbers, so confirm the 2027 price and deadline. Age rule differs between UC Davis pages: other UC Davis pages say ages 16 to 18. A $1,500 deposit is due at enrollment. The apply page says a decision takes about 10 business days after your application is complete.

who_can_apply: High school students at partner schools in Sacramento, Solano, Shasta and Siskiyou counties who are low income or whose parents did not attend college.
how_to_apply: Get an application from the Upward Bound advisor at your school (Shasta County students ask the GO Center). Send student info and a short essay, a parent-signed eligibility form and two recommendation letters back to the advisor. Questions: eduadvising@ucdavis.edu or 530-752-5887.
notes: Only available at partner schools. Federally funded TRIO program for low-income or first-generation students. No fee or stipend is listed on the pages read, so ask.

who_can_apply: Rising junior or senior. Must be 16 by the first day and not turn 18 before the last day. Must be a permanent US resident living and attending school in the US. Two teacher references needed (one must be a science teacher).
how_to_apply: Apply in the YSP portal between Jan 1 and Mar 1. Submit grades, activities, essays and two teacher references. Ask for fee reduction by the deadline if you need it.
notes: Very competitive (about 40 students). Residential, so you live on campus. Late and incomplete applications are not accepted. Application fee waivers are given on request. Contact ysp@ucdavis.edu.

who_can_apply: High school students looking to get ahead or recover credit. The site mentions free options for California public schools and scholarship applications for eligible students.
how_to_apply: Enroll from the courses page, ask your school counselor about school-paid seats, or call (408) 450-4962.
notes: This is coursework, not a job. Included because many teens use it to free up schedule time for jobs and internships.

who_can_apply: California high school students in grades 8 to 12, per the COSMOS application site. A GPA of 3.5 or above is typical.
how_to_apply: Online application with a personal statement, teacher recommendation(s), transcripts and a parent or guardian e-signature, plus the application fee. You choose one campus and cluster. Pay one-third of tuition by Apr 7, 2027 and the rest by Apr 16, 2027 if accepted.
notes: Competitive. About 160 to 200 students join per campus. UCI says the 2027 application will be available in January 2027. Watch for info sessions in December. Students must live on campus for the full program. COSMOS runs on several UC campuses. This card is the UC Irvine campus.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 and over. Selection looks at your application, your ability to keep the weekly schedule, past community service, and your education and career interests.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the application steps. Email ucimcvolunteer@uci.edu or call 714-456-5541 to ask when applications reopen.
notes: Requires a physician-signed medical clearance with immunity proof (measles, mumps, rubella, varicella), Tdap, hepatitis B series, COVID-19 vaccine with booster, flu shot in season, and a negative TB blood test within 90 days of your start date. Also a three-hour orientation.

who_can_apply: Must be 16 by June 1. Grade and residency are not stated. A government photo ID and immunization proof are required.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a required Zoom info session. You get the form by email. Send it back with proof of shots (varicella, MMR, TB test). Then go to one required in-person orientation. Email studentvol@mednet.ucla.edu.
notes: Info sessions fill fast. Every slot showed FULL or CLOSED when read. The page also points to the Mattel Youth Ambassador program as another option. Santa Monica and West Valley campuses have their own student pages.

who_can_apply: High school students. The Summer Precollege Focus Series requires being at least 15 by the first day of Summer Sessions, and some programs set older ages. Regular summer courses must come from a pre-approved high school list.
how_to_apply: Apply or enroll through each program page on summer.ucla.edu. California students in grades 9 to 11 can apply for Summer Scholars Support (need and merit scholarships), and 10th and 11th graders from under-resourced California communities can apply for BASE, a free 6-week online course with a UCLA mentor.
notes: Out-of-state and international students cannot receive UCLA Summer Sessions financial aid. Exact program prices were not found; use UCLA's fee calculator before applying.

who_can_apply: Students at participating schools. Upward Bound: freshmen or sophomores at Moreno Valley, Perris, Rubidoux, Banning, Norte Vista, Ramona, Bloomington, Colton or Eisenhower High School. Talent Search: Arroyo Valley, Indian Springs, Pacific, San Bernardino or San Gorgonio High. Both need a 2.5 GPA, U.S. citizenship or permanent residency, low income and/or first generation, and interest in college.
how_to_apply: Upward Bound: fill out the interest form on the page to receive an application. Talent Search: fill out the ETS application and give it to your school's ETS contact or email ets@ucr.edu; phone (951) 827-7863.
notes: Only students at the listed schools qualify. The page does not list grade levels for Talent Search.

who_can_apply: Motivated students completing grades 8 through 12 with strong interest and achievement in math and science. In 2026 the in-person program was limited to California residents. Students can attend COSMOS only once.
how_to_apply: Online application through the COSMOS portal: choose UCSD, rank two clusters and write an essay for each, one or two online recommendations from a math or science teacher, current and prior-year transcripts, and the application fee.
notes: 2027 dates come from the statewide COSMOS site; the UCSD page still shows 2026 dates. Fees shown are for 2026. 2026 rules asked for proof of COVID vaccination and a negative test; check whether that still applies. If admitted, a non-refundable deposit of one third of tuition holds your spot.

who_can_apply: Incoming 11th and 12th graders with a cumulative GPA of 3.3 or better who are interested in sports medicine. No application is needed; you enroll directly.
how_to_apply: Enroll directly on the Extended Studies registration page. Add the course to your cart. No application or essay is needed. Questions: precollege@ucsd.edu.
notes: Earns 3 to 6 UC pre-college units. UCSD's Research Scholars also offers life sciences and marine science courses; its older Academic Connections summer program was canceled for 2026. Marine science fall 2026 application closed Sept 17, 2026.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. You must be 18 to volunteer in pediatric inpatient units or the Emergency Department. Minimum 6 months, one 3 to 4 hour weekday shift each week.
how_to_apply: Attend a virtual info session, in-person group interview, online training and health clearance (background check if 18+). Volunteer Services (415) 502-9888.
notes: The Oct 13 opening is for Parnassus and Mt. Zion or Mission Bay programs in San Francisco, not Oakland. UCSF says it cannot take new volunteers for other roles right now. Under 18 needs a parent at the health clearance visit. No high school summer program was found on the official pages.

who_can_apply: High school students who finished sophomore year and are 16 by the program start date. You must have taken one high school lab science course and one semester of algebra. You should be interested in ag, food and environmental science. First time participants only.
how_to_apply: Send an online application with short essays. Pick a campus (Athens, Griffin or Tifton). Add two recommendation letters from science or math teachers. Upload an official transcript.
notes: Not residential. You must arrange your own housing and transport, and travel to the campus daily. Contacts on the page: Athens 706-542-2713, Griffin 770-228-7264, Tifton 229-326-4663. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit is required only for minors who have not reached their 16th birthday. This program requires age 16.

who_can_apply: High-achieving high school students from across Georgia who are going into their senior year. No other rules are listed on the pages read. In 2026 exactly 50 students were chosen from 664 applications.
how_to_apply: Apply through the UGA Admissions application portal when it opens. Ask the Office of Academic and Community Engagement (oace@uga.edu) about future cycles. Admissions phone on the application page: 762-400-8800.
notes: Very competitive: a UGA news story dated Sep 3, 2026 says the program got a record 664 applications for 50 spots. Exact 2026 dates and application requirements were not on the pages the reader could open.
