who_can_apply: Rising 12th graders with at least a 3.2 GPA and no C's in math or science, who finished Trigonometry, Chemistry and Pre-Calculus with a B or better, want to study engineering at UMD, and can attend full time for all 4 weeks.
how_to_apply: Online application with an essay and resume, two teacher recommendations (one math, one science), and a virtual interview with the student and a parent or guardian.
notes: The page says taking part does not guarantee admission to UMD. No housing is offered. A free program, not a job, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Page lists rising 10th through graduating 12th grade; minimum age 13 and the 3.0 GPA rule are not stated on this page.
how_to_apply: Pick a course and the campus or online option, then apply online with a transcript, health insurance card and card payment for the application fee and deposit. No essays or recommendations.
notes: Costs shown are the 2026 prices; 2027 prices are not posted. Commuter program: no campus housing except the business course BMGT262. The grade posts to a UMD college transcript. Not a job, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: The page title says ages 12 to 15 (the University youth programs list says 12 to 16). Applicants attend a February info session, interview, and a mandatory one-day orientation in June.
how_to_apply: Attend the free virtual info meeting in February, get the application, sign up for an interview, pay the fee if accepted, then attend orientation. Call 612-301-1210 for questions.
notes: Good first leadership experience for younger teens. Volunteer hours can be logged.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 10 to 12 with an interest in automotive tech, manufacturing, engineering, planning or robotics. Space is limited to 20 students.
how_to_apply: Application steps for 2027 are posted early in 2027 on the camp page.
notes: Competitive: 20 spots. Day camp; the page does not mention transportation.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 7 to 9 with a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0, who have completed or can enroll in pre-algebra and are interested in engineering, science, transportation or technology.
how_to_apply: Application information for 2027 is posted early in 2027. Selection process details are on the camp's admission decisions page.
notes: For younger teens. The University's youth programs list shows ages 13 to 16 for this camp.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in fall 2027, at a high school or homeschooled. Not open to 8th grade or below or to graduates.
how_to_apply: Pre-register online (interest form on the Explore@UNC pages). Pre-registering improves placement chances. Payment details come after placement.
notes: Families must have a local trusted contact. A temporary drop-off pass is $25 for the week and all-day parking is the family's cost. UNC also lists dual enrollment as a visiting student for rising seniors (see summer.unc.edu/dual-enrollment/); its cost was not read. Questions: explore@unc.edu.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 who live in or go to school in Union City.
how_to_apply: Submit an application between February 1 and April 1, then interview in April.
notes: Follow @UCTeens on Instagram for events, per the city page. The program runs out of the Kennedy Youth Center.

who_can_apply: US citizen (the Senate application guide also mentions permanent residents; ask the office) with a Social Security number. Must be 16 or 17 at appointment, a junior (semester) or rising junior or senior (summer), with a 3.0 GPA and health forms. Needs a Senator's sponsorship. Senator Padilla sponsors California residents only.
how_to_apply: Send a cover letter, resume, recent transcript and two recommendation letters to Senator Padilla's office at Page_Program@padilla.senate.gov. Other Senate offices have their own rules; the central Page Program does not take applications.
notes: Only about 30 positions in the whole Senate. Pages pay their own travel to and from Washington, DC. The job is in DC, so a California work permit likely does not apply; ask the office. Moving to DC for a semester is a big step for a family.

who_can_apply: High school juniors or seniors holding an elected or appointed leadership office this school year, such as student body or class officer. Must be a US citizen or green card holder and live in California. Get the application from your principal, counselor or social studies teacher, or the state contact.
how_to_apply: Ask your principal or counselor for the application, or email the California coordinator at ussyp@cde.ca.gov (California Department of Education, Sacramento).
notes: Very competitive. Clubs, debate, Model UN, jobs and self-made groups do not count as qualifying offices. The CDE page was blocked by a bot check, so the coordinator name and contact are from the USSYP site only. If you are a junior now, plan for next fall.

who_can_apply: High school students who have completed ninth grade by the start of the program and are pursuing a rigorous curriculum. Domestic and international students may apply.
how_to_apply: Online application with the $85 fee. Email summer@usc.edu with questions.
notes: Expensive. The admissions page read does not describe financial aid, so ask summer@usc.edu. The prices and dates above are the 2026 numbers and may change for 2027.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 8 to 11 in 2026, rising grades 9 to 12. Active MESA, Mission Science and Engineering Transformer students come first. So do students at STEM Center schools. All students are considered.
how_to_apply: When it is open, send a student form and a teacher recommendation. You can use the online form or the PDF. Forms that are not complete are not considered. Contact k12summer@usc.edu.
notes: The program page says in person at USC main campus. The USC Viterbi summer programs list calls it virtual. Confirm the format before you count on it.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 and up for aircraft restoration, ship restoration, radio, community outreach and visitor services (16 and 17 year olds work with an adult). Collections: 18 and up. Docents, events, security: 21 and up.
how_to_apply: Apply at volgistics.com/appform/1737643431 or call (510) 521-8448 ext. 243.
notes: Ship work involves climbing ladders and tight spaces. Another museum page lists overnight programs for groups, but no teen intern program.

who_can_apply: Current high school sophomores or juniors who are 16 by July 5 of the program year, interested in STEM, and U.S. citizens. Past SEES interns cannot repeat.
how_to_apply: Apply online at spacegrant.net/apps/sees: essays (maximum 250 words per response), a short intro video (submit the link), an unofficial transcript or report card, and a recommendation form. Travel scholarships are available and do not affect your selection.
notes: Very competitive: about 2,000 applications and 215 accepted in 2024 (FAQ). It is an educational internship, not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Students entering 8th or 9th grade. A panel reviews applications (not first come, first served), and students who attend schools without engineering or STEM offerings are encouraged to apply. Houston and San Antonio sessions are by invitation only.
how_to_apply: Register through the camp page; you are notified by email by mid-May. Questions: cseoutreach@utexas.edu.
notes: For younger teens (about 13 to 15). Both 2026 Austin sessions are listed as full.

who_can_apply: Current high school juniors with a strong interest in engineering, science or math who live in the United States. About 50 students per session are chosen by holistic review. Students from low-income backgrounds or with limited STEM access are strongly encouraged to apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the MITE page. Questions: cseoutreach@utexas.edu.
notes: Selective. The page does not list a financial-aid policy; ask cseoutreach@utexas.edu if the $200 is a barrier.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors in good standing with a minimum 3.5 GPA in a college prep curriculum, age 15 or older on the first day and 18 or younger on the last day.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcripts, one teacher or administrator recommendation uploaded by the recommender, and a 350 to 500 word essay. Financial aid materials are due by March 1.
notes: Residents live in an air-conditioned residence hall with a 10 pm curfew. Travel, books, laundry and spending money are not included. Questions: UVaAdvance@virginia.edu, 434-243-2241. The Cost and Payment page was not read.

who_can_apply: High school youth ages 14 to 18. Students must attend a mandatory virtual information session with a parent or guardian and an all-day orientation on the first day of the program.
how_to_apply: Submit the online interest form, attend a mandatory virtual information session with a parent or guardian, then interview if selected. Two references must complete the online reference form before the interview.
notes: The program page mentions a lottery. Cost and immunization rules for juniors were not stated on that page; UVA Health's general volunteer page lists a health assessment, vaccination requirements, background check and training for volunteers. Questions: 434-924-5251.

who_can_apply: 4-H participants are youth ages 5 to 19. Community 4-H clubs are for ages 9 through 18. You join by contacting your local Virginia Cooperative Extension office.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Virginia Cooperative Extension office and ask about the 4-H program.
notes: The page also lists a 4-H State Congress, camps, maker education, shooting education and youth leadership opportunities. Details such as dates and fees for those were not on the page read.

who_can_apply: Boys who have finished their junior year and have at least one semester of high school left. You and your parents must live in Virginia. Home-schooled boys can apply if they meet the home school rules on the site. You cannot attend Boys State twice.
how_to_apply: Your high school counselor suggests candidates. Local American Legion post members interview them. Find your district chairperson on the Apply page. Ask about how your district does it.
notes: Delegates stay in university dorms. A delegate who turns 18 before the last day must pass a background check. It costs about $16, and the program refunds it. Two delegates go to Boys Nation in Washington, DC. The site lists a 2027 page, but no 2027 dates were found on the pages read. The apply page lists the fee as a $600.00 application fee per delegate. It says individual or parental sponsorships are not permitted. Registrar: registrar@vaboysstate.org.

who_can_apply: Girls who have finished their junior year and have at least one semester of high school left. Public, private and home school students can apply. Must be a U.S. citizen or legal resident of the United States (proof is needed).
how_to_apply: Delegates are selected by local American Legion Auxiliary units by interview, whenever possible. If your school has not been contacted, find your district on the map and email your district registrar for help. Online registration opens in spring 2027 for chosen delegates.
notes: The 2027 director listed is Cheryl Shine, director@vagirlsstate.org. Delegates must stay until 3:00 PM Friday to get program credit. The pages read do not say the cost, so ask your district registrar.

who_can_apply: Virginia youth who will be 13 or 14 years old on January 13, 2027. You must be in good school standing. Your school must agree to the long absence.
how_to_apply: Use the online application portal linked on the Capitol Classroom Page Programs page. Verify your date of birth. Create an account. Finish every part of the application. Ask your principal, teachers and counselor first, since you will miss school. Questions: HousePageInfo@house.virginia.gov or (804) 698-1502.
notes: The Speaker of the House picks the pages. Pages live in a residential setting with other pages. They have a mandatory evening study hall. Incomplete applications are not considered, so check that your application shows as complete. This is a separate program from the Senate Page Program.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 (18-year-olds must be enrolled in high school). Based on the 2024 flyer; check the current year's rules.
how_to_apply: 2024 flyer: application with parent signature, a 1-page essay, an availability schedule, and a virtual orientation. Contact the VA Center for Development and Civic Engagement, vhalomyouthprogram@va.gov.
notes: Closed now. The age, hours and application steps come from the 2024 flyer because the current page only says 2026 applications are closed. The 2024 flyer also required COVID vaccination or an exemption; check the current policy.

who_can_apply: Virginia residents who are 13 or 14 on the first day of session (the second Wednesday in January), with no exceptions. You live with a parent or guardian. You go to an accredited school or a qualifying home school. You should have an A or B average.
how_to_apply: Use the Application for Admission page of the Prospective Senate Page Portal during the open window. Questions: pageinfo@senate.virginia.gov or (804) 698-7410.
notes: Pages stay at a designated hotel Sunday night to Friday noon each week, and the hotel room is billed to the Senate Clerk's Office. Admission counts as an excused school absence. Cell phones are turned in during work hours. Rates are listed as subject to change. The overview page lists a $50 activity fee in recent years and does not list uniform or binder costs.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 through 17. You must be at least 14 by June 1, 2027, must not turn 18 before the session ends, and must still be in high school the fall after the program. You need your own email, bank account and photo ID.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Crew Member application on the program page. Two professional or academic references must turn in their forms by the deadline. Chosen applicants join a group interview. They also go through a background check.
notes: Competitive. The page says it gets many more applications than spots. About ten crew members live at each host park with three to four adult crew leaders. Crews are split into male and female groups. Cell phones, laptops and other devices are not allowed during the program. Contact: vspycc@dcr.virginia.gov. Virginia's labor department says 14 and 15 year old workers need an Employment Certificate before working. Its page does not mention this program. Ask the program if one is needed.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters may waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens).
how_to_apply: Use the unit locator to find a cadet or composite squadron. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the application. Or apply online if your squadron says you can.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Virginia Wing HQ: 7401 Airfield Drive, Richmond, VA 23237, 804-454-7356. The wing site lists squadrons in Blacksburg, Charlottesville, Herndon, Springfield, Richmond and other towns.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18, attending high school in Santa Clara County and living in the county. Able to give up to 5 hours a month for 2 years, and attend quarterly Wednesday evening meetings in person.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Commission interest form. To apply you need to know your Valley Water board district (find your home address on the map on the page).
notes: Meetings are at Valley Water headquarters, 5700 Almaden Expressway, San Jose.

who_can_apply: Teens aged 13 to 15. Applicants send a portfolio of 10 images in all. It has 5 to 7 finished works and 3 to 5 sketchbook images. They also send a letter of intent of 500 to 1,000 words.
how_to_apply: Use the APPLY NOW link on the page to submit the portfolio and letter of intent. Questions: submissions@artsumbrella.com or 604-681-5268.
notes: Scholarship-funded learning program, not a paid job. Canada, so British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.

who_can_apply: Students aged 15 to 18, or entering Grades 10, 11 or 12 in fall 2026.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Emily Carr University Continuing Studies website (Apply Now link on the page). Questions: teens@ecuad.ca.
notes: Paid-for arts program, not a job. Canada, so British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.

who_can_apply: Grade 12 students in BC and the Yukon. From Fall 2026, Grade 11 students are not eligible even if they take Grade 12 level courses. Students in grades 8 to 11 can use the Self-Directed program instead, which offers recorded sessions.
how_to_apply: Register online. You give your contact details and a sponsor teacher's name and email. You give a signed Participant Agreement Form. You give three answers of 150 words or less. After the deadline, students are picked by random draw. Priority goes to First Nations, Inuit and Metis students and to students from different schools.
notes: Registration for the 2026 round is closed. Watch the program page for the next round. In person sessions are at 950 West 28th Avenue, Vancouver. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them.

who_can_apply: Grade 11 and 12 students in BC and the Yukon. No research experience needed. Limited to the first 1,000 students who apply.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for your name, contact details, grade and school. It asks for a parent or guardian's contact. It asks for one answer of 150 words or less. Say why you want to attend.
notes: Online talks only, not a job or hands-on lab work. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. The institute says it does not offer any formal placements for students who want to volunteer, job shadow or gain work experience. The application form link is on the program page.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 30 who need to find work. The page does not list other eligibility rules.
how_to_apply: Click an event under Upcoming Events on the page to apply. Central office: 604-879-6554 or info@bgcbc.ca. Seats are limited.
notes: Canada, so British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet. The page did not say where the workshops are held.

who_can_apply: High school students in BC, grades 10 to 12 on the research institute page. A teacher must first register the school with the Canadian Medical Hall of Fame. The organizers encourage schools to consider students who are Indigenous, Black, a person of colour, or from rural or lower income backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Ask a teacher to register your school on the Canadian Medical Hall of Fame website (cdnmedhall.ca/discoverydays). The teacher then gets the student sign-up steps. If you cannot find a teacher, email cmhf@cdnmedhall.ca. Give your city, high school and the event.
notes: One day event, not a job. The Medical Hall of Fame page does not name the city, but the research institute page says the event is at 950 West 28th Avenue, Vancouver. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. Grades come from the institute page only.

who_can_apply: Core volunteer program: at least 16 years old, 100 hours minimum. High School Work Experience: Lower Mainland students in Grades 11 and 12; teachers sign students up.
how_to_apply: Check the volunteer page for the next intake. For the work experience placement, ask your teacher to sign you up.
notes: The Science World Teen Advisory Group (ages 16 to 18) is on hiatus and not taking applications (page read 2026-10-09). Volunteer role in Canada; British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.

who_can_apply: Must be 14 years of age by June 29, 2026. If accepted, you submit a criminal record check and complete training.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application, attend one in-person interview, then complete in-person or online training. Returning volunteers can apply as Lead Volunteers by email.
notes: SFU Camps says it is not a registered non-profit; check with your teacher that your school accepts these hours for service or work experience credit. Top volunteers are encouraged to apply as paid instructors later (2026 instructor wage $27.05 to $28.50 per hour, CAD); the minimum age for instructors is not stated on the page. Volunteer role in Canada; British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.

who_can_apply: Teens age 16 and older, and adults. No other rule is stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the "Volunteer with us" form linked on the Space Centre careers page. Questions can go to careers@spacecentre.ca.
notes: Age 16 and up, so 13 to 15 year olds cannot apply. The pages do not give shift length, hours or a start date, so ask before you plan. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. The details came from a summarized fetch of the Space Centre pages (the raw pages would not load for a second check).

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 17 can join EcoStewards, DIRT, Nature House Hosts, EcoRangers and EcoCamp Assistants. Ages 12 to 16 can join EcoStewards with adult supervision. A parent or guardian must sign the youth consent form.
how_to_apply: Register and sign up through Better Impact. If a role is closed, fill in the Volunteer Interest Form. Email vols@stanleyparkecology.ca with questions.
notes: Volunteer role in Canada. British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet, so work permit is marked unknown. Most other roles on the site are for volunteers 16 and older.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18 who have completed grade 10 or equivalent. UBC recommends about a 78% average, 3.5 GPA, B average or IB 5. Students still learning English should have IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL 80 or higher. Open to students from other countries.
how_to_apply: No application, transcripts or proof of English are needed. Check that you are eligible. Add a course or mini school to your cart. Have a parent or guardian create a Family Account. Pay the deposit at checkout. Then finish the information package within 48 hours.
notes: Costs money, and it is a camp-style university course, not a job. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. The fee table is labeled 2026 and still shows a 'due May 1, 2026' date next to the 2027 sessions, so check the 2027 fees before you plan. An online version also exists (3 week courses); this card covers the on-campus version.

who_can_apply: First Nations, Inuit or Metis students going into grades 9 to 12. Week 1 is for students going into grades 11 or 12. Week 2 is for students going into grades 9 or 10. The pages do not state an age rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer Science application online (UBC form). Or send it by email to summer.science@ubc.ca, or by mail. A reference letter of about 200 words is recommended. It can come from a teacher, coach, mentor or community leader.
notes: Only for Indigenous students (First Nations, Inuit, Metis). It is a camp, not a job. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. The program page still shows 2025 dates, so check the newest page before you plan. The application page lists the 2026 deadline of June 15, 2026.

who_can_apply: High school students. Applicants must apply by the posted deadline, attend a short interview and orientation, and commit to at least 25 service hours.
how_to_apply: Apply by the posted deadline, then interview and attend orientation. Contact Anna Deater-Deckard, anna@vadm.org, 434-977-1025 x104.
notes: The museum is a small children's museum for infants to age 8, so the work is with young kids. Weekday and Saturday shifts are available.

who_can_apply: Open to rising high school juniors and seniors. The pages I read do not state a Virginia residency rule for this program (WEE VT has one).
how_to_apply: Send the joint application with WEE VT and UPWARDS. Rank your choices. Write short essays of 120 words each. Add a grade transcript and a parent financial statement for scholarships. You get an offer to only one camp.
notes: Not a job, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Rising high school students in the grade band for each camp. No GPA or residency rule appears on the pages I read.
how_to_apply: Register through the camp application link on the College of Science camps page; apply for a scholarship inside the form. Cancellation refund minus a $30 fee until 4 weeks before camp.
notes: Explore Science rising 9-10 camp was listed as full in 2026. Questions: explorescicamp@vt.edu. Not a job, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors who are Virginia residents.
how_to_apply: Joint application with the C-Tech2 and UPWARDS summer programs: rank your choices, add short essays (120 words each) and a grade transcript, and a parent completes a financial statement used for scholarships. You get an offer to only one camp.
notes: The page tells families not to let the cost stop them from applying because of scholarships. Not a job, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: Virginia high school juniors and seniors who are at least 16, Virginia residents, and U.S. citizens or permanent residents. A 2.7 GPA is required. You also need a teacher recommendation and a school counselor letter. NASA security rules usually allow only citizens and permanent residents at the summer academy.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Then ask a teacher and a school counselor to send their letters through the online system. They get an email from notices@spacegrant.net. Letters sent any other way are not accepted. Contact: Regina Delzer, rdelzer@odu.edu.
notes: Closing soon. Statewide for Virginia, so it may also appear on another Virginia list. The page says 180 top scholars who finish the course attend the summer academy. The application link is on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students at partner schools. Schools join by filling out an interest form and talking with a VEI Regional Director.
how_to_apply: Ask your school or counselor about the program. Contact info@veinternational.org or 855-740-6555.
notes: Not an individual sign-up; your school must be a partner. Cost to schools is not posted.

who_can_apply: High school students age 16 or older (the page covers ages 16 through the summer after graduation). Needs a Social Security Number or ITIN and Occupational Health clearance. Apply to only one location: Raleigh Campus or Cary Hospital.
how_to_apply: Review the current junior-eligible openings, then submit the online application for one campus during an open window. Selected students interview, give two references, finish medical screenings and attend orientation.
notes: Not first come, first served. Processing takes about 3 to 5 weeks. Required Occupational Health clearance includes flu, MMR, Varicella, Tdap and TB. Not for court-ordered community service. The page describes volunteer service, not an internship or job shadowing.

who_can_apply: Middle school students, high school students and adults can apply. Students under 17 need a parent to say yes. The library cannot give drop-in volunteer work. It also cannot give court-ordered community service.
how_to_apply: Fill out the student volunteer application (a PDF from the volunteer page) or pick one up at the Welcome or Information Desk. Contact Laura Stone, Volunteer Coordinator, (847) 244-5150 ext. 3059, lstone@wnpl.info. For TAG, complete the registration form on the TAG page.
notes: Adults who apply must agree to a background check for crimes. The page says TAG is a good way to earn volunteer hours for National Honor Society and other service rules.

who_can_apply: Youth starting at age 5 up to those who have not yet reached their 19th birthday on October 1 of the current 4-H year. Clubs run through your county WSU Extension office.
how_to_apply: Choose your project or projects. Find a club through your county WSU Extension 4-H office. Or start one if none exists. Talk with local staff, then enroll through 4-H Online. Then go to meetings and events.
notes: Fees, clubs and projects differ by county. This is a youth club and leadership program, not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Washington state residents who are high school juniors (per the 2025 WAS FAQ: 'Scholars must be a Washington state resident and be a current junior in high school'). No math or science prerequisites are listed on the program page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the WAS 2026-27 Program Application linked on the program page. Questions: WAS@museumofflight.org or 206-768-7214. Phase 2 invitations use a lottery. It is among students who meet the Phase 1 requirements.
notes: Deadline is very close. Graduates can apply for Museum scholarships. Participation in Phase 2 is not required for Phase 1. Students who are not juniors yet can fill out the Program Interest Form on the page to be contacted when they are eligible.

who_can_apply: Students in a business or marketing class taught by a CTE certified teacher at a school with a DECA chapter. The official page lists no age or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's DECA advisor, who registers members through DECA's online system. If your school has no chapter, DECA lists six steps to start one. State advisor: Lori Hairston, lori@wadeca.org.
notes: DECA's page lists 187 chapters in Washington. The state site is wadeca.org.

who_can_apply: Any high school junior, typically a 16 or 17 year old finishing 11th grade. No political experience is needed. The program is for both boys and girls.
how_to_apply: Apply yourself with the online application at ebgs-wa.org/apply. Or ask a teacher, counselor or local American Legion Post to nominate you. They use the program's nomination form. After screening, the program helps find a sponsor if you need one.
notes: The site describes a 7-day, 6-night leadership experience. Confirm the 2027 dates on the main page of ebgs-wa.org.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Seniors are told not to apply because onboarding is long (a college program exists).
how_to_apply: Email volunteer_services@washingtonhealth.com with your name, grade, school, phone and email. They contact you only when an info session is scheduled. Phone 510-818-7465.
notes: No GPA rule or fee appears on the current page (older versions listed a GPA rule and $20 fee). Openings are limited. Office: 2500 Mowry Ave, Fremont.

who_can_apply: At least 14 years old and not yet 17. You need a parent or guardian's permission and a teacher's recommendation.
how_to_apply: Apply online when applications open on the Page Program page. Pick the weeks you can do with care. Senate contact: SenatePageProgram@leg.wa.gov, 360-786-7498. House contact: 360-786-7889.
notes: The page lists no closing date, so apply soon after Nov 1. Check the Page Program page for the current application link. Paid work for people under 18 in Washington needs a parent and school authorization form (the employer holds the Minor Work Permit). See permit.html?state=wa for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors in Washington. The SBCTC page does not list other requirements; contact the college's Running Start coordinator.
how_to_apply: Contact the Running Start coordinator at the college you want to attend (the SBCTC page links a coordinator list) and your high school counselor.
notes: Work hours tie-in from Washington L&I: 16 and 17 year olds enrolled in a bona fide college program, such as Running Start, may work non-school week hours during the regular school year (employers should ask for proof such as a college transcript).

who_can_apply: Ages 12 through 18 (national Civil Air Patrol page). The Washington Wing pages read do not list other rules. Ask a squadron about citizenship and school rules.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron on the Washington Wing Locations list or the national unit finder. Visit a meeting. Ask the squadron for the application. Wing office: 253-982-7774 or wa@wawg.cap.gov.
notes: The Washington Wing join page links to separate Youth, Adults and Educators pages, so the age and cost figures come from the national page. This is a youth program, not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Washington residents who are U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents, ages 15 and a half to 18 at entry (the main page says 15 to 18). You must be behind in school, have dropped out, or be at risk of not graduating. No felony charges or pending court cases. You must choose to attend, stay drug free and be able to take part.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Send the doctor and dentist forms and other documents (WYA.Applications@mil.wa.gov or fax 360-473-2623). Then do an interview and final review. Phone: 877-228-8947.
notes: This is for teens who are off track in school, not a job program. Campus: 1207 Carver Street, Bremerton, WA 98312.

who_can_apply: Students at East Aurora High School or West Aurora High School only. The pages read do not list income or first-generation rules, so ask the staff.
how_to_apply: Fill out the new student application (from your counselor, Room 201 at East or A104A at West, or the website). Staff then set up a family interview, and new students do a 10 to 60 day trial period. Email upwardbound@waubonsee.edu.
notes: The form asks for copies of your transcript and birth certificate. It also asks for your Social Security card and a parent tax return. Give these only to program staff at the school or the Sugar Grove office.

who_can_apply: Individuals and groups. People under 18 need a parent or legal guardian to sign the forms. No minimum age is listed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Agreement Form. A parent signs it if you are under 18. Email it to efallon@waukeganparks.org. Phone: Elizabeth Fallon, (847) 782-3626.
notes: Park projects: contact Bryant Brown. Bryant is the Park Services Supervisor. The phone is 847-360-4756. Read the Volunteer Requirements and Expectations document before you start.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 12. Right now the library does not take volunteers who must do court ordered community service.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen Volunteer form. Or visit the Youth and Teen Department during normal hours.
notes: The library's Maker Space (3D printer, laser engraver, sewing machines) is open to teens ages 16 and up, which is a good way to build skills. Hours and training are not on the pages read.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 15 or older. If you are under 15, you can volunteer with an adult who is 18 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Volunteer Application. You get a confirmation email, then a call or email after approval. Contact Lisa Snow, 630-681-0962 ext. 548, lisasn@wdsra.com.
notes: WDSRA also hires part-time program staff (the volunteer page does not give a minimum age for them). The jobs page lists openings and how to apply.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18 who are interested in a health care career. Spots are limited and competitive.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Send shot records (MMR, DPT, Varicella). Have your school counselor fill out and sign the School Records Release. You can email, fax or mail documents to Volunteer Services. If you are picked, there is a short 15-minute interview.
notes: Volunteer Services: 3950 Austell Rd, Austell, GA 30106, (470) 732-3767. Picks use a finished application and the required documents. They also look at time commitment, past volunteering, GPA and leadership. They look at speaking skills and interest in health care too. Unpaid, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. Picks are based on the full application. They also look at whether you can keep the time commitment. They look at past volunteering, GPA, leadership, speaking skills and interest in health careers.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the window. Email your shot record as a PDF. It needs 2 MMR, 2 Varicella or proof of the illness, and 1 Tdap. Your school counselor fills out and signs the recommendation form and emails it. The interview is in March and the orientation is in April. After you are accepted, you get TB test steps.
notes: Accepted students may keep volunteering in the school year if Volunteer Services says yes. It is competitive. This is an unpaid volunteer role, so no work permit.

who_can_apply: High school students aged 16 to 18. You need shot records, a school counselor form and an interview.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online VolunTeen application. Email your shot record (2 MMR, 2 chickenpox or proof you had it, 1 Tdap) as a PDF. Have your school counselor sign the recommendation form and email it. Then you are called for an interview.
notes: Spots are limited. Not everyone is accepted. Picks look at past service, GPA, leadership and interest in health careers. Students accepted for summer may keep volunteering in the school year with approval.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 16, eligible West Sacramento residents. Needs proof of the hepatitis B vaccine series, fingerprinting and a background check.
how_to_apply: The page does not give application steps. Call the Club West Teen Center at (916) 373-5877 or ask City of West Sacramento Parks and Recreation.
notes: Page has no year or dates, so ask when applications open. Vaccine proof may take weeks to collect. Runs in summer.

who_can_apply: Concurrent enrollment: grades 9 to 12. Middle College: juniors and seniors from LGSUHSD and CUHSD. Dual enrollment on high school campuses: CUHSD (Campbell Union High School District) students only.
how_to_apply: Start at the college's high school students page and apply through the admissions portal; the page also covers assessment, orientation and registration.
notes: Ask the college about unit limits and your counselor about credit.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12 can earn service hours. There are separate Teen Library Council groups for middle school and high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Interest Form. Or fill out the Teen Library Council form. Questions: teenread@wheatonlibrary.org.
notes: You can also earn hours by making cards. Four cards earn 1 volunteer hour. You can also write book reviews. Each review earns 30 minutes of service hours.

who_can_apply: Open to almost anyone, even without logging in. The page links to guidance for younger editors but states no minimum age.
how_to_apply: Start editing, or make a free account (not required). Try The Wikipedia Adventure tutorial.
notes: Protect your personal info; do not share your school or address.

who_can_apply: The program is for teens in grades 9 to 12. Kids ages 11 to 13 can apply to serve as library helpers for certain youth programs with parent or guardian approval.
how_to_apply: Go to the volunteering page. Fill out the volunteer form there. If you have a question, write to teenvolunteers@wilmettelibrary.info.
notes: Summer jobs run June to August. Krista Hutley is the teen librarian. Eti Berland is the school engagement librarian. They are the teen volunteer coordinators. The Studio program has its own info sheet.

who_can_apply: Students entering their senior year of high school next fall. You must be from a Wisconsin high school or home-schooled in Wisconsin.
how_to_apply: School staff such as counselors or the social studies department often help choose students. You can also email info@badgerboysstate.org to say you want to attend. Include your name, high school, phone number and email.
notes: Not a job. The 2027 session is the 83rd. Office: 2930 American Legion Drive, Portage, WI 53901, phone 608-745-1090.

who_can_apply: Young women in their junior year of high school in Wisconsin. The page does not list other rules.
how_to_apply: The page says to speak to your high school counselor if you want to become a delegate.
notes: Not a job. A tuition sponsor is needed, usually found through the school or the local American Legion Auxiliary. Dates for the next session come from the program site.

who_can_apply: Wisconsin DECA strongly encourages members to also be enrolled in a marketing or business course. Chapters need an advisor with a marketing or business educator license. Detailed rules are not listed.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's business or marketing teacher about a DECA chapter. For eligibility and deadlines, contact the Wisconsin DECA advisor, Tim Fandek, at Timothy.Fandek@dpi.wi.gov.
notes: Not a paid job. The state website listed on the page is wideca.org. This card is based on the DECA Inc. page for Wisconsin.

who_can_apply: Wisconsin students interested in the outdoors. It is best suited to high school students and younger students may apply. Some DNR volunteer tasks are only for ages 16 and up. You can take part through the summer after senior year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the YCC application and parent consent form from the DNR YCC page. Or contact the YCC Coordinator, Kyle Zenz, at kyle.zenz@wisconsin.gov or 715-299-0925.
notes: Volunteer program, not a job. A parent or guardian must sign the consent form. It can count toward school service-learning or independent study credit if your school agrees. The packet's example activities are from 2025, so check this year's schedule.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors. The applicant page lists no GPA, age or residency rule. You also need an employer to hire you.
how_to_apply: Pick a career area. Talk with your counselor and parents. Contact your local YA Regional Coordinator and apply. Then interview with employers. After you are hired you go to orientation and safety training.
notes: Wisconsin's youth apprenticeship page says work permits are no longer required for 16 and 17 year olds. The Wisconsin work permit page says 14 and 15 year olds still need a permit ($10 fee, repaid by the employer by the first paycheck). A 15 year old junior is possible, so ask your coordinator. Student learner status does not override minor employment laws. DWD phone (608) 266-3131.

who_can_apply: Students in a school agricultural education program that has an active FFA chapter. The Affiliation program page says grades 5th to 12th. No age limit is listed.
how_to_apply: Contact your school's ag education teacher. If your school has no program, contact the state ag education staff. Ask about starting one.
notes: Not a job. The site has a Local Chapter Locator that links to Find a Program. Your school must have an ag program and an FFA chapter. The Affiliation fee is based on enrollment. The page does not say who pays it, so the claim in pay_detail that the school pays is not confirmed by this page.

who_can_apply: The Wisconsin Wing site labels the cadet program as ages 12 to 19. The national CAP cadet page says between 12 and 18. The interest form lists grades 6 through 12 and high school graduates.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Cadet Interest Form on the Wisconsin Wing site. The wing aims to pass your info to a local unit within 48 hours, and the unit should contact you within 48 hours after that. If you hear nothing in four days, email Major Todd Mandel at todd.mandel@wicap.us.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Ages differ between the Wisconsin page (12 to 19) and the national page (12 to 18), so confirm with the squadron. Wing address: 2400 Wright Street, Madison, WI 53704.

who_can_apply: Students who join a delegation near them. The page read does not list grades. Media spots are by application and may be limited.
how_to_apply: Find a delegation near you on the Wisconsin YG site. Then register at wiyg.org/register before the closing date for your role. Use the Contact Us page if you need help starting a delegation.
notes: Not a job. Legislative and Media materials are due in January and Judicial materials in February.

who_can_apply: Current high school students who have finished 8th grade. Partner high school classes are arranged through your counselor. Tuition is free for 11 units or fewer.
how_to_apply: Explore with your counselor, apply on CCCApply, set up your student account, submit the CCAP or High School Non-CCAP form, then register.
notes: Students may pay for books and materials. Check your counselor for term deadlines. Davis High was not on the CCAP list I saw, so a Davis student would use the non-CCAP route. Charter and homeschool students may need grade verification.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Register online through the Woodland Community Services registration portal (linked from the Teen Programs page) or call (530) 661-2000. Email: WoodlandCSD@cityofwoodland.gov.
notes: The page gives no hours, dates or fees. Call Community Services to ask how it works and when to start.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 7 to 12. Teens should limit in-person volunteering to no more than two events a month.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a teen volunteer event on the library page. Or send a book review of at least 5 sentences through the form. Questions: askus@woodridgelibrary.org.
notes: If you register and cannot come, cancel so someone else can take the spot. Some events have waitlists.

who_can_apply: Santa Clara County residents ages 16 to 24 who are low-income and have at least one barrier to employment or education.
how_to_apply: Call the San Jose Job Center at 408-794-1101 or the Gilroy center at 408-758-3477 and ask about the young adult program.
notes: San Jose Works, a partner program for ages 14 to 29, is also listed on the page. Income and barrier rules apply. Job centers may be open by appointment only.

who_can_apply: Eligible young adults ages 17 to 24. The page does not list other rules or say which counties qualify.
how_to_apply: Click Apply Now or Get Started at worknetdupage.org/job-seekers/get-started/, or call 630-955-2030. Career Center: 2525 Cabot Drive, Suite 302, Lisle.
notes: Starts at 17, so it fits only older high schoolers. Spanish-speaking services are available. The Get Started page was not read, so check eligibility there.

who_can_apply: City of Atlanta residents ages 16 to 24 who are WIOA eligible. In-school youth are generally 16 to 21, must meet income and other criteria, and may have a barrier such as disability, English learner, foster care, homeless, justice-involved or parenting. A WorkSource Atlanta Eligibility Specialist makes the final decision.
how_to_apply: 1) Finish the online youth orientation. 2) Create a profile in the WorkSource Georgia portal and save your SID number. 3) Upload your documents. 4) Book an eligibility appointment, or email WSAYouth@AtlantaGa.Gov with subject Ready to RISE. 5) Take the My Next Move career assessment. 6) Eligibility review.
notes: Eligibility is income and barrier based, so not every teen qualifies. The document list includes a Social Security card and proof of address; this is the official city workforce board, but upload documents only through the portal named on the page. Under 18 using parent documents: proof of relationship and shared address is needed. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

who_can_apply: DeKalb County residents ages 16 to 24 who face barriers to work. The page does not define barriers.
how_to_apply: Apply online at ATLworks.org. Send everything it asks for. An eligibility specialist reviews it and replies within 7 business days. Then you meet the specialist and make a career plan.
notes: The page does not mention work permits. Contact 404-371-2000 (Mon to Fri, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm) or 311CCC@dekalbcountyga.gov.

who_can_apply: Fulton County residents ages 16 to 24 who are interested in employment or training and meet low-income guidelines and/or have significant barriers to education or employment.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe an application. Visit the youth center at 4405 Mall Blvd., Suite 400, Union City, GA 30291, or call a career center: South Fulton 404-613-6800 (5710 Stonewall Tell Rd., Suite 160, College Park) or North Fulton 404-613-4480 (7741 Roswell Rd., Suite 205, Sandy Springs).
notes: A March 2026 county news release says WorkSource Fulton also offers the Career Compass Academy, a five-week paid virtual work readiness program for ages 14 to 24 that is income based. Teens signed up at the county's Summer Teen Hiring Fair on April 11, 2026; next year's dates are not posted. If you live inside the City of Atlanta, also look at Youth R.I.S.E. and ask which office serves your address. The county's older Summer Youth Job Training and Summer Youth Internship pages return errors now.

who_can_apply: Washington Unified School District high school students who are 16 by the first day. River City HS students need a Career Technical Education course; Yolo HS and Washington Middle College students need a teacher or counselor recommendation. Everyone attends one online info session.
how_to_apply: Go to the Internships page, attend the info session, send the recommendation form if needed, then apply and interview with employers.
notes: Employers have included Center for Land Based Learning, Elica Health Centers, City of West Sacramento and others. The 2026 calendar on the page is an image, so ask for 2027 dates: wshomerun@cityofwestsacramento.org or (916) 617-4500.

who_can_apply: Incoming 9th to 12th graders.
how_to_apply: Register online for the day camp or residential option; a separate summer program scholarship application is available. Questions: summerprograms@xavier.edu.
notes: Xavier's Summer Programs page also lists other high school options: Summer in Cincy (one-week residential pre-college), D'Artagnan Summer Business Academy (rising juniors and seniors), CSI Forensics Camp (grades 10 to 12) and STRONG eXplorer Career Camp. Check each page for 2027 prices. High school students who attend may get a $500 to $1,000 award if they later enroll.

who_can_apply: Students in Yolo County. Start through your school College and Career Center or counselor, or email CCR@ycoe.org. Age or grade limits were not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Tell your school College and Career Center or counselor, or email CCR@ycoe.org.
notes: B-Unbound is the online platform for finding opportunities (interviews, tours, job shadowing, projects, internships). Placement depends on available mentors, so ask early. The stipend is paid after you finish the requirements. Email: CCR@ycoe.org. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Oakland youth. YEP's job training serves ages 14 to 24. The City of Oakland's summer list shows YEP's summer program for ages 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Use the application links on yep.org/how-you-join, or call 510-533-3447 or visit 2300 International Blvd, Oakland.
notes: The YEP page does not give pay rates. Age 14 to 18 for summer comes from the City of Oakland table; the 19 to 24 programs are for older youth.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. Leaders Club requires being a Y program member or facility member; the page states no membership rule for Changemakers. A Jr. Leaders Club exists for grades 6 to 8.
how_to_apply: Use the Register Now link on the teen community page. Changemakers uses the Teen Clubs sign-up. Or ask at a local YMCA branch.
notes: Leaders Club can include travel to conferences and leadership events. The page does not say how many community service hours a club gives. Which branch runs a club and when is not stated, so ask your local Y. The Y's teens page lists a Legacy Leaders college scholarship for active teen members, with a last day to apply of Sunday, September 13 (year not stated).

who_can_apply: Ongoing volunteers must be at least 16. Teens 14 and older can volunteer at many special events. Volunteers under 18 need parental consent.
how_to_apply: The page has no general form. Open roles link to postings (examples: Tustin Expanded Learning Volunteer, Youth and Government MUN Volunteer, Sports Volunteer at Laguna Niguel). Questions go through the contact form at ymcaoc.org/contact-us/.
notes: All ongoing volunteers complete an online orientation, child abuse prevention training and role training. Screening includes an application, waiver, ID copy and background check, with extra checks for higher-responsibility roles. Court-ordered community service is not accepted. The YMCA of Orange County Model Legislature and Court page describes the statewide YMCA Youth and Government program, so it is not listed separately.

who_can_apply: The page lists the program for ages 14 to 24 and older. Grade level, residency and other rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. The page says to contact the Workforce Development team. Phone numbers listed: Urban Services YMCA (415) 561-0631; Bayview Hunters Point YMCA (415) 822-7728; Chinatown YMCA (415) 576-9622.
notes: This is an umbrella page for several branch programs. Season, wage, hours and deadlines are not stated, so call a branch before a teen applies. The ymcasf.org/teens page lists teens ages 13-18 across programs, but it gives no details for Workforce Development. Contact emails on the page are obfuscated and were not confirmed, so none are listed.

who_can_apply: Must be at least 15 years old, in 10th grade or higher, and in good academic standing. A High School Authorization Form must be signed by members of your school. No prior training is required, according to the FAQ.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application through the Learn More and Sign Up link, get a High School Authorization Form signed by members of your school, and watch email for further instructions. The page recommends applying at least two weeks before your session dates.
notes: Camp Campbell is at 16275 Highway 9, Boulder Creek, CA 95006, per the cabin-leaders page. This is an unpaid volunteer role, so no work permit is needed. The same YMCA's Youth and Government program is already in ymca-youth-and-government-ca.json. Leaders in Training is also listed on the leadership page, but its age and details are not stated, so it is not a card.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students. Chapel Hill-Carrboro YMCA also requires a nomination form, an application and a handbook review. The page does not say which listed branches are in Raleigh or Durham.
how_to_apply: Register online through the link on the page, attend an interest meeting, or contact your branch's Teen Director.
notes: Branches listed: A.E. Finley, Alexander Family, Chapel Hill-Carrboro, East Triangle, Kerr Family, Kraft Family, Northwest Cary, Poole Family and Taylor Family YMCAs. The page does not explain the difference between Member and Participant dues.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 12. Locations are shared directly with participants.
how_to_apply: Register through the program's online registration page. Questions: yo.sobha@ymcatriangle.org.
notes: Achievers may earn certified community service hours and may receive partial scholarships as seniors. The page does not say which cities host groups.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 from anywhere in California. Join a local delegation. Cost and sign-up steps are not posted on either page.
how_to_apply: Two ways to reach the program. Southern California: contact the program director at (626) 604-4210 or use the inquiry form on the YMCA of Orange County site. Silicon Valley area: click 'Sign up for more information' on the YMCA of Silicon Valley Leadership Development page, which opens the YMCA sign-up form. Neither page describes the application steps.
notes: Over 1,300 teens in more than 60 California delegations. The YMCA of Orange County page (Southern California) lists no Northern California contact. The YMCA of Silicon Valley lists the same statewide program and links a sign-up form for the Silicon Valley area. Ask the director which delegation serves your area, and ask about cost and scholarships. The YMCA of Silicon Valley Leadership Development page also lists other teen groups and a Model UN program for middle school students; they are not part of this entry.

who_can_apply: Youth in Yolo County. The page does not list ages. Fee waivers are available.
how_to_apply: Find a community club, attend a meeting, complete online enrollment and pay the fee. Office: bbrinkhoushatch@ucanr.edu, 530-666-8703.
notes: Teens can take leader and ambassador roles. The fee is non-refundable. A fee waiver or reduction form is available. Returning members update their online enrollment and send health forms to their club.

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24, living in Yolo County, and not in school right now, per the program page. The page names foster care, homelessness, disabilities, parenting, leaving high school, and justice involvement as challenges the program serves.
how_to_apply: Contact the Workforce Development Program Manager at the Administrative Offices, (530) 757-5558, or drop by free office hours on Wednesdays from 3 to 6 p.m. at 2455 West Capitol Ave, #118, West Sacramento, CA 95691.
notes: Only the 17-year-old end of this guide's 13 to 18 range is covered. Older YCCA posts mention up to 300 paid hours; that figure is not on the current page and is not used here. Narrower and competitive: it is aimed at young people facing barriers and out of school. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

who_can_apply: Opportunities are limited and differ by branch. The Mary L. Stephens Davis Branch is not accepting applications right now. The page does not list a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Download the Youth Volunteer Application (PDF) from the volunteer page and email it or drop it off at the branch you want.
notes: Call the branch first (main number 530-666-8005). The page said the Mary L. Stephens Davis Branch was not accepting volunteer applications when checked.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 15 must be with an adult or a supervised group. Ages 16 to 17 can volunteer alone with parent permission (youth waiver).
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Yolo Food Bank volunteer site. Use the Youth Volunteer Waiver for ages 12 to 17. Then sign up online for events. Email volunteer@yolofoodbank.org.
notes: Wear closed-toe shoes and gloves at events. You log your own hours in your volunteer account. Ages 12 to 15 must be with an adult or a supervised group.

who_can_apply: For the Service Award: students in grades K to 12 who live or go to school in Santa Clara or San Mateo County. High schoolers need 100 hours within 12 months. Other programs list no clear age rule.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Do Service platform at volunteer.youthcommunityservice.org. Phone 650-858-8019 or email ycs@youthcommunityservice.org.
notes: Also offers a scholarship and one-day service pop-ups. Based at 780 Arastradero Rd, Palo Alto.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 25 in the greater Chicagoland area. Services are free.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the sign-up page. Current clients can talk to their career coach about a Paid Work Experience. Phone (847) 864-5627, 1114 Church Street, Evanston.
notes: A Chicago-area nonprofit that has worked with young people for over 40 years. Text YJCNEWS to (224) 253-6233 for updates. Ask the staff about work permits if you are under 16. In Illinois, workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before they start. This comes from the Evanston Township High School work permit page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form linked on youthradio.org.
notes: The page describes training and mentoring, not a formal paid internship. Ask whether it is paid. It is not on the City of Oakland's 2026 summer jobs list.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 25, low-income or homeless youth (per the Berkeley Public Library jobs page).
how_to_apply: Call (510) 858-7229 or email community@youthspiritartworks.org (both on the home page) and ask about job training. The Berkeley Public Library jobs page lists jobtraining@youthspiritartworks.org.
notes: Read the home page on 2026-10-09. It says YSA serves transitional age youth 14 to 25 at 1740 Alcatraz Ave, Berkeley, with free drop-in hours, workshops and events; some workshop series pay a $300 stipend for full participation. The home page does not describe a job training program or its pay, so the 15 to 25 age range, the paid jobs and the jobtraining email come from the library page and are unconfirmed. The FAQ says YSA is not actively accepting applications. Ask before you plan around a job. Not on the City of Oakland's 2026 summer jobs list.

who_can_apply: East Oakland youth. The City of Oakland list shows YU summer jobs for ages 14 to 21. YU serves ages 13 to 24 overall.
how_to_apply: Call 510-777-9909 or visit 8711 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. The site gives no online form.
notes: YU's own site has no summer job details, so the ages and hours come from the City of Oakland's 2026 list. Also a referral partner for EBMUD's high school internship.

who_can_apply: Oakland middle and high school students. The City summer jobs list shows Media Careers for ages 16 to 21 (June to September).
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page at youthbeat.org/apply, or call 510-922-0060 or email youthbeatmedia@gmail.com.
notes: YouthBeat's own page does not state exact ages; 16 to 21 comes from the City of Oakland's list. Address is a PO box in Oakland.

who_can_apply: One high school senior who lives inside School District U-46 lines. You show leadership. You plan to go to college or higher education.
how_to_apply: Submit the scholarship application and essays when the call opens. The page lists writing help resources, and in 2026 offered free one-on-one feedback on up to two drafts.
notes: Recent winners came from Larkin, Bartlett and Elgin high schools. Contact YWCA Elgin at 847-742-7930 or info@ywcaelgin.org.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 17 years old by June 1, 2027 who are enrolled in high school (or equivalent) for the coming school year.
how_to_apply: Online application plus an essay of 2 pages or less written by the teen alone (AI-looking essays are rejected), and one recommendation from a non-family adult. Selected teens interview in person in March and attend orientation with a parent in April.
notes: Staff review in February, notification of next steps by March 1. A current TB test is needed each year by June 1. Shifts are A.M., P.M. or full day. The page does not print a year beside Jan 1 and Jan 31; the year is read from the 2027 program-year details.

who_can_apply: Open to volunteers online. The pages read state no age rule; check the user agreement.
how_to_apply: Go to zooniverse.org, pick a project, and make an account if the project asks.
notes: The home page and FAQ do not state a minimum age. Projects span arts, biology, climate, history, language, medicine, nature, physics, space and social science.
